Chapter 1

Lee Hyun had rarely thought of himself as unhappy.

He had lived into his forties without any real relationships or dreams he wanted to pursue. Even so, he was not dissatisfied with his life.

He had once worked at a mid-sized company, but after quitting because of the stress, he took irregular jobs that earned little more than pocket money. He had some savings, and since he hardly spent anything, he managed well enough.

He almost never went outside. The world had reached a point where buying groceries, ordering meals, and purchasing anything else he needed could all be done over the internet.

Bringing in a package left outside his front door was more than enough of an outing for the day.

That did not mean he was the sort of shut-in who lived with his room buried in garbage. He cleaned up as soon as he finished eating, took out the food waste on time, had never fallen behind on his taxes, and had never disturbed his neighbors by making noise late at night.

Lee Hyun considered himself a thoroughly harmless person.

Someone who was not much help to the world, perhaps, but did not harm it either.

He figured that was good enough.

The one thing he was diligent about was brushing his teeth. Cavities hurt too much, and going to the dentist was terrifying.

On the other hand, he could not be bothered to get the free health screenings offered by the government. A screening might uncover an illness, and if an illness was found, he would have to go to the hospital.

He did not exercise either.

Watching online streams, playing games, watching dramas, and reading novels were more than enough to make a day pass quickly.

Lee Hyun was easily entertained.

If some new ramen he had bought tasted better than expected, if a YouTuber he regularly watched started playing a different game than usual, or if a new chapter of a novel he was following came out, that alone was enough to make it a pretty good day.

He could even find a certain amount of entertainment in pouring water into a pot and watching the bubbles form as it came to a boil.

That day was no different.

He opened the refrigerator, but there was nothing in particular he felt like making. In the end, too lazy to bother, he pulled a packet of ramen from the cupboard.

While waiting for the water to boil, he sat on the edge of his bed and looked at his phone. A replay of the stream he had fallen asleep watching the night before was playing.

It was a day exactly like any other.

So when his chest started to feel tight, he did not think much of it at first.

Maybe it was indigestion. The thought made little sense since he had not even eaten the ramen yet, but he figured moving around a little might help, so he stood up.

He had not even taken two full steps when the center of his chest clenched tight.

“Ugh...”

Lee Hyun grabbed the table.

It felt as though someone had wrapped a fist around his heart and was twisting it. He could barely breathe, and cold sweat instantly broke out across his forehead and back.

By the time he realized something was wrong, the strength had already gone out of his knees.

He collapsed to the floor and struck his head hard against the corner of the table. Yet he barely felt the pain. The agony radiating from his chest was far worse.

‘Could this be a heart attack?’

His phone was on the bed. It looked close enough to reach if he only stretched out his hand, but his body refused to obey him. He tried to move even if he had to crawl across the floor, but he could not properly move so much as the tips of his fingers.

The water was boiling on the induction stove.

Lee Hyun stared past the table leg toward where the pot should be and remembered that he had not put the noodles in yet.

‘It won’t start a fire... right?’

It was a remarkably pointless thought to have at the moment of death.

But nothing else came to mind.

He did not particularly regret never marrying, never making friends, or never going on a proper trip. Nor did he think he should have lived more diligently. If he had, life would undoubtedly have been more troublesome than it already was.

Still, he felt a little cheated. If he had known he was going to die this suddenly, he would at least have ordered something expensive to eat beforehand.

His vision slowly darkened.

The first thing he saw when he opened his eyes was a wooden ceiling.

The blackened planks were covered in old stains, and there were even cobwebs hanging between the rafters.

Lee Hyun blinked and stared at the ceiling for a while.

There was no way this was a hospital. No matter how run-down a rural hospital might be, they would not let spiders build webs on the ceiling.

So was he alive?

He touched his chest, but there was no pain. He could breathe easily, and his body actually felt lighter than before.

Lee Hyun carefully sat up.

The rough cloth covering him slid down. The first thing that caught his eye was a slender hand. The palm was callused, but it looked nothing like his own hand had after he passed forty.

Looking around the room, he spotted a cracked water bowl. Lee Hyun staggered over and looked down at the face reflected in the water.

An unfamiliar young man stared back at him.

Sun-darkened skin, tangled long hair, cheeks slightly hollow from starvation. He looked no older than twenty at most. His face was ordinary, neither particularly handsome nor ugly.

When Lee Hyun opened his mouth, the young man in the water did the same.

“Ah...?”

Lee Hyun crouched in front of the water bowl and stared blankly for a long while. Every sensation was far too vivid for him to deny reality.

It hurt when he pinched his cheek, and warm sunlight streamed in through an opening too small to properly be called a window.

He went back to where he had been lying and lay down again.

He hoped that if he slept a little longer and woke up, he might return to his original world.

But when hunger became too much to bear and forced him to open his eyes again, the wooden ceiling and cobwebs were still there.

There were almost no memories left in this body.

Only a faint sense of having starved lingered. He had no idea who his parents were, where he had lived, or why he had been lying in this dilapidated thatched cottage.

Not long afterward, an old man who had come to check on the house discovered that Lee Hyun had awakened. He introduced himself as the village chief.

According to the village chief, Lee Hyun had been found collapsed on a mountain path several days earlier. A villager gathering medicinal herbs had discovered him, and the village chief had laid him down in this empty house.

“You must have injured your head badly. You remember nothing except your name?”

The village chief asked with concern. Lee Hyun thought for a moment, then nodded.

“Yes. I don’t remember anything.”

This was White Wood Village, a small settlement in the western part of the Great Yan Kingdom.

The only houses with tiled roofs belonged to the village chief and a few relatively well-off families. Most of the villagers lived in homes made of mud walls and straw. When the sun rose, people went out to the fields, and when it set, they returned home.

At first, Lee Hyun thought he had fallen into a world resembling some period of Chinese history.

He could naturally speak the language here, but he assumed that was probably thanks to his transmigration.

To survive in this place, he needed to find work.

Farming was the first thing he ruled out. Farming required a great deal of cooperation among the villagers, such as maintaining irrigation channels together and sharing seeds.

He did not want to go into trade either. That would mean having to talk to customers.

Hunting was out of the question. He did not know how to properly shoot a bow, and even the thought of encountering a wild animal in the mountains frightened him.

In the end, he chose to become a woodcutter.

He climbed the mountain, cut suitable trees, split them into firewood, and sold only as much as he needed to in the village. Lee Hyun's body was young and sturdy, and his palms already had the calluses of someone who had handled an axe before. At first, his entire body ached, but as time passed, he grew fairly used to the work.

With the village chief's permission, Lee Hyun repaired a small abandoned cabin at the foot of the mountain.

There, he began living alone again.

Compared to his past life, everything was inconvenient. There was no electricity, running water, or gas, and food spoiled quickly.

To conserve firewood, whenever he lit a fire, he had to use the same heat to cook rice and boil water. In summer, insects swarmed everywhere, and in winter, it remained cold no matter how many layers of blankets he piled over himself.

The hardest thing to endure was the absence of the internet.

For the first few months, Lee Hyun suffered from crushing boredom. Once the sun set, there was nothing to do, and oil and candles were too expensive to keep a light burning all night.

Only then did he realize how much comfort he had enjoyed in his past life.

Eventually, Lee Hyun began pulling stories from his memories and rewriting them in his head.

Paper was expensive, so he could not actually write anything down. Instead, he reconstructed the novels and games from his past life in his imagination. He changed endings he had disliked, made characters from different works meet one another, and sometimes turned a favorite villain into the protagonist.

Whenever he had time to spare, he carved wooden figurines. He made knights in armor, horned demon kings, and even robots whose exact appearances he could no longer remember.

They were not things he intended to show anyone, so it did not matter if they were ugly.

And so Lee Hyun lived in White Wood Village.

Life was less convenient than in his past life, but once he grew accustomed to it, it was not unbearable.

Lee Hyun was someone accustomed to finding small pleasures wherever he was. Sitting under the eaves and listening to the rain was pleasant enough, and on days when the wild greens he added to his soup tasted better than expected, that alone was enough to put him in a good mood.

He intended to live quietly enough here until he grew old and died.

One spring day, Lee Hyun was tying bundles of firewood.

Suddenly, the village dogs began barking frantically, and shouts from the villagers soon followed. Everyone rushed out of their homes and stared up at the sky.

Lee Hyun looked up without thinking.

A ship came flying through the clouds.

A blue cloud emblem was painted on the white sail of the wooden vessel.

When the ship stopped above the village, figures in long robes glided down through the air. Beneath their feet floated swords, leaves, and round discs.

“They’re Immortal Masters from the Azure Cloud Sect!”

At someone's shout, the villagers all prostrated themselves on the ground.

Lee Hyun took his cue from them and bowed at the waist.

That day, the people from the Azure Cloud Sect tested the village children for spiritual roots.

One by one, the children placed their hands on a transparent orb. Most produced no reaction, but beneath the hands of a few children, red or blue light appeared.

They said children with spiritual roots could enter a sect of Immortals and cultivate the Dao.

The parents hoped their children would be chosen, yet when the time actually came for those children to board the ship, they shed tears.

As Lee Hyun watched, he finally realized what kind of world he had fallen into.

‘So this was a xianxia world.’

His heart did not race with excitement. Instead, cold sweat broke out across his skin.

Lee Hyun had read quite a few xianxia novels in his past life. The settings differed from one story to another, but they all had one thing in common.

Most of those worlds were brutally dangerous.

A protagonist in a novel might overcome countless crises and eventually rise to become the strongest, but Lee Hyun was not optimistic enough to think he was the protagonist.

The village chief suggested that he get tested as well.

“Who knows? You might have a spiritual root too.”

“I’ve already been in this village for several years. Aren’t the Immortal Masters looking for young children?”

“That is true. I suppose you may already be too old to enter the sect.”

Entering a sect meant cultivating. It meant competing with others, and he might even be dragged into secret realms or sent on missions. To Lee Hyun, who only wanted a quiet life, none of that sounded remotely appealing.

After the Azure Cloud Sect's ship departed, Lee Hyun returned to his old way of life.

The years passed without incident.

In spring, mist gathered over the mountains. In summer, the streams swelled. In autumn, the leaves turned red, and in winter, snow piled softly atop the cabin roof.

The children who had once run around the village with runny noses eventually married, while wrinkles appeared on the faces of the young men who had once been around Lee Hyun's age.

The villagers occasionally joked that Lee Hyun's face hardly seemed to change. Whenever they did, he brushed it off, figuring this body must simply have naturally youthful features.

Lee Hyun did not pay much attention to his appearance.

He had no mirror, nor any reason to study his own face closely. When his hair grew long, he roughly cut it or tied it back, and when his beard grew out, he shaved it off with a sharpened blade.

He realized something was strange one day, twenty years after arriving in White Wood Village.

Lee Hyun had gone down to the village to sell firewood when he encountered an unfamiliar man standing in front of the village chief's house.

The man stopped when he saw Lee Hyun's face. A moment later, he approached with a startled expression.

“Are you Uncle Lee Hyun?”

Lee Hyun did not recognize the man.

His face seemed familiar, but Lee Hyun could not remember where he had seen him before. When he hesitated to answer, the man pointed to his own chest.

“It’s me, Zhang San. When I was little, I used to follow you around, and you’d give me wooden figurines...”

Only then did Lee Hyun remember.

He had been the little boy who sniffled as he followed Lee Hyun along the mountain paths. Lee Hyun had carved him a wooden bird once, and after that, the child had come by almost every day, pestering him to make something new.

“So you’re Zhang San. You’ve grown so much I barely recognized you.”

Lee Hyun spoke with a smile, but the delighted expression disappeared from Zhang San's face. Zhang San stared intently at Lee Hyun.

Only then did Lee Hyun feel a sense of foreboding under that gaze.

“What is it?”

“Uncle...”

Zhang San lowered his voice.

“You look exactly the same as you did when I was a child.”

Chapter 2

That day, Lee Hyun returned to his cabin without selling his firewood.

He fetched water from a nearby stream, poured it into a basin, and peered down at the surface with growing unease.

The same face he had seen when he first awakened in this body twenty years ago stared back at him.

Aside from his sun-darkened skin and slightly longer hair, nothing had changed. There was not a single wrinkle around his eyes, and his hair was still pitch-black.

No matter how he thought about it, remaining completely unchanged after twenty years was not normal.

Had some glitch appeared in the laws of the world when he transmigrated? Or had the original owner of this body not been an ordinary human?

Lee Hyun rose to his feet and cautiously spoke into empty air.

"Status window."

Nothing happened.

"System."

A bird chirped outside the window.

"Open."

This time, the wind blew, making the cabin creak.

"What is this..."

Not aging was not a bad thing. But it frightened him.

If word spread that an ordinary person did not age, Lee Hyun would be as good as dead.

This was a xianxia world where cultivators existed. Why did they risk their lives cultivating? Was it not precisely to gain limitless lifespans and overwhelming power?

But what if a mere mortal who had not even entered Qi Refining already possessed a body that did not age? If that fact became known, the consequences would be beyond imagination.

'If word gets out, I'll suffer something worse than death... They'll steal my body, use me as an experimental subject, or refine me into a pill!'

Starting the next day, Lee Hyun grew out his beard and rubbed dirt and ash over his face. He even deliberately hunched his back whenever he walked.

But it was already too late.

Whatever Zhang San had said, word had gotten around. Whenever Lee Hyun came down to sell firewood, the villagers subtly studied his face. No one asked him outright, but their gazes held a mixture of fear and curiosity.

In the end, Lee Hyun decided to leave White Wood Village.

...

It was the cabin where he had lived for twenty years, but packing did not take long. An axe, a knife, a shovel, a hammer, a pot, and a few sets of clothes made up all his belongings. He wanted to take the wooden carvings he had spent so long whittling, but they were too heavy, so he left them behind.

Even after packing everything, Lee Hyun did not leave immediately.

He walked around the cabin and deliberately knocked down the fence. He carefully gouged scratches into the door so they resembled claw marks from a beast, then made a mess of the surroundings.

Next, he killed a mountain rabbit caught in a trap he had set several days earlier for food, then crudely splattered its blood across the cabin floor and threshold. He was making it look as though the place had been attacked by a ferocious beast such as a bear or tiger.

"Ugh... Sorry."

He was still not used to killing animals.

He looked back one last time at the cabin he had grown attached to.

He was reluctant to leave, but there was nothing else he could do.

Lee Hyun crossed the mountain before dawn.

The second place Lee Hyun settled was a remote mountain hamlet hundreds of li (1 li is about 400 m) from White Wood Village.

This time, he changed his name as well.

He introduced himself as Li Mo and claimed to be a wandering woodcutter who had fled from wild beasts. The villagers found him somewhat suspicious, but they showed little interest in a solitary wanderer.

Lee Hyun built a cabin near a cliff some distance from the village, then immediately began digging into the ground.

At first, he only intended to make a small cellar for storing food. There were many wild animals in the mountains, and if he kept food inside the cabin, they often followed the smell and came looking.

Once the cellar was finished, he carved out a space large enough for one person to hide.

Then it occurred to him that the entrance might become blocked, so he began digging a passage leading out the opposite side.

Digging through soil was manageable enough, but whenever he struck rock, he would struggle with it for days. He lit fires to heat the stone, splashed cold water over it to make it crack, then chipped it apart bit by bit with a small hammer.

As he dug the tunnel, Lee Hyun installed wooden support beams at intervals.

Lee Hyun did not hurry.

He had nothing in particular to do, and time was something he possessed in abundance. After twenty years as a woodcutter, he had grown skilled enough at the work to gain more free time, and he came to enjoy extending the tunnel little by little whenever he had a spare moment.

If he dug one ja (about 30 cm) today and got tired, he could simply continue tomorrow. After all, he had neither a deadline nor anyone waiting for him.

Several years passed like that, and the small cellar grew into a fairly long tunnel.

The end of the passage emerged beneath a thicket in the forest on the opposite side, and from outside, it was difficult to tell that an entrance existed at all.

To prevent animals from entering through the exit, he temporarily blocked it from the inside with piled stones and earth.

Lee Hyun stored food and firewood in the cellar, and on nights when the cries of mountain beasts sounded close, he simply slept inside the tunnel. It was damp and dark, but he felt safer there than in the cabin.

He also dug a small room deeper inside the tunnel, spread a thick layer of dry grass across the floor, and placed a water jar and dried grain there. It was preparation so that even if the entrance collapsed, he could survive for several days.

...

Time continued to pass as unfailingly as ever after Lee Hyun settled near the second village.

Another ten years passed.

Lee Hyun still had not aged.

He could no longer dismiss it as coincidence or imagination. His body was undeniably different from that of an ordinary human.

Then, one summer night, a tremendous boom rang out from the sky.

Lee Hyun woke from his sleep and initially thought it was thunder. But the next crash came from much closer than any thunderclap, and even the ground shook.

When he stepped outside the cabin, red and blue lights flashed across the night sky.

Two cultivators were fighting in the air far away.

One wore a long red robe, and enormous flames coiled around him like a dragon. Opposite him, a blue-robed man had dozens of blue flying swords arrayed in the air.

Every time the two gestured, streaks of light shot across the sky.

A blue beam grazed a mountain peak, and with a deafening roar, one side of the mountain collapsed.

The cultivator wielding the flames burst into laughter and hurled an enormous mass of fire.

Immediately afterward, part of the fireball was severed by the blue-robed man's flying swords and crashed into the mountainside. Dozens of trees erupted into flames at once, while earth and stone blasted upward as if exploding.

Lee Hyun stared at the scene with his mouth hanging open.

It looked more impossible than anything in the movies from his past life. Yet the scorching wind against his skin and the vibrations rumbling beneath his feet made it painfully clear that this was reality.

Then one of the fireballs came hurtling toward Lee Hyun.

"...!"

Lee Hyun dashed inside the cabin and yanked up the floorboards.

He threw himself straight into the cellar, shut the entrance behind him, and crawled deeper into the passage. His elbow scraped against a stone in the wall, but he had no attention to spare for the pain.

A moment later, the world turned upside down.

With a thunderous crash, the entire tunnel shook, and dust and fragments of stone rained from the ceiling. Lee Hyun flattened himself against the floor and covered his head.

Smoke and heat surged into the passage.

'I could die.'

Only then did Lee Hyun truly understand that agelessness was completely different from deathlessness.

Even with a body that did not age, there was no way he could survive an attack powerful enough to blast a mountain apart. If the tunnel collapsed, he would be crushed to death. If the flames reached him, he would burn to death.

He crawled all the way to the exit on the opposite side, moved enough stones aside to make a small air hole, then lay there catching his breath.

The battle continued until daybreak.

Lee Hyun lay near the exit, trembling without daring to move. He did not know who was fighting, why they were fighting, or who had won. The only thing that mattered to him was that while those two cultivators fought, a mountain that had nothing to do with their battle was collapsing and an equally unrelated forest was burning.

...

Only three days later did he make his way through the passage and return to the cabin side.

More than half the cabin had collapsed, and the surrounding forest was charred black. Black smoke was still rising from the direction of the village.

'Have I been thinking about this wrong all along...?'

Becoming a cultivator was dangerous. But staying a mortal was no guarantee of safety either.

Lee Hyun had no interest in power or fame. He had even less reason to cultivate for the sake of extending his lifespan. He already possessed an ageless body, after all.

Still, he found himself wanting to become a little stronger.

Strong enough not to be mauled to death by a mountain beast. Strong enough to escape if he encountered bandits. Strong enough to survive at least one stray blast if he were caught in a battle between cultivators.

That would be enough.

'Besides, I'm bored anyway... There's hardly anything fun to do in this world. Maybe cultivation would give me something to do?'

He still did not know whether he possessed a spiritual root, but Lee Hyun began to think that joining a cultivation sect might not be a bad idea.

Once inside, he could learn a cultivation method or two and, if possible, also learn how to grow spirit herbs or refine pills.

Then, when the time was right, he could secretly slip away from the sect, dig a tunnel somewhere deep in the mountains where no one would ever look, and hide there. Who would bother searching for an insignificant disciple like him?

Even if the sect branded him a traitor, he could simply remain hidden until everyone who remembered him grew old and died.

In the novels from his past life, spirit herbs became more potent the longer they were grown. Conveniently, time was one thing Lee Hyun had plenty of.

If it took ten years, he would wait ten years. If it took a hundred years, he would wait a hundred. There was no need for him to risk his life entering a secret realm in search of a thousand-year-old spirit herb like everyone else. He could simply plant seeds somewhere secluded and tend them at his leisure.

And so, partly to relieve his boredom, Lee Hyun decided to join a cultivation sect.

...

Even after deciding to join a sect, Lee Hyun saw no reason to rush. He repaired his collapsed cabin and continued his leisurely daily life. It was not until five whole years later that he finally chose which sect he would join.

During that time, he picked up stories from merchants at the marketplace and listened for rumors dropped by travelers at taverns.

After that long investigation, Lee Hyun chose a sect called Qinghe Valley.

Qinghe Valley was a fairly well-known sect in the southwestern region of the Great Yan Kingdom. It was not especially large, but it had a long history and a decent reputation among the surrounding people.

Most importantly, it specialized in growing spirit plants and spirit herbs.

Most of its disciples tended spirit fields and grew medicinal herbs, and it was said that there were also alchemists within the sect who refined pills. There were no rumors of conflict with other factions either.

It was the sect that came closest to what Lee Hyun wanted.

Two years later.

Hundreds of people had gathered below Qinghe Valley's Mountain Gate.

They ranged in age from children around ten years old to youths who looked nearly twenty. Some were family scions dressed in silk, while others were barefoot children in rags.

Including the applicants' families and servants, there were more than a thousand people present. The area below the Mountain Gate was as noisy as a marketplace, and throughout the crowd came the voices of parents holding onto their children and giving them final words of advice.

Lee Hyun mingled among them as he climbed the mountain path.

He had discarded the name Li Mo when he left the second village. At Qinghe Valley, he had decided to use his original name, Lee Hyun.

...

The first procedure was the spiritual root test.

An applicant placed a hand on a transparent orb, and the attribute and quality of their spiritual root were determined by the color and intensity of the light that appeared within it.

For most people, no light appeared at all. Anyone whose orb glowed even faintly was allowed through the Mountain Gate, while those whose orb remained dark descended the mountain with disappointed expressions.

Lee Hyun's turn approached.

Sweat beaded on his palm.

He carefully placed his hand on the orb.

A moment later, three colors of light blossomed inside it.

Blue, red, and yellow.

The Qinghe Valley disciple administering the test peered into the orb and said,

"Wood, Fire, and Earth. A triple spiritual root."

'I actually have a spiritual root?'

"Go through the Mountain Gate."

Following the instructions, Lee Hyun passed through the Mountain Gate.

Beyond the Mountain Gate, a curtain taller than a person screened off an enclosed area. The applicants who passed the spiritual root test entered behind it one at a time.

When his turn came, Lee Hyun stepped behind the curtain. Another Qinghe Valley disciple was waiting there with a bronze mirror in hand.

"I'll check your bone age."

Lee Hyun's expression stiffened.

"My bone age?"

"People occasionally lie about their age. Anyone over twenty-five is only accepted as a menial disciple unless they possess exceptional talent."

Light poured from the bronze mirror and swept over his body. A warm sensation seemed to flow along his bones, and then characters appeared across the mirror's surface.

The disciple administering the test read the result indifferently.

"Bone age, nineteen. Pass. Go out the other side."

'I really haven't aged!'

When Lee Hyun froze in surprise, the Qinghe Valley disciple waved a hand irritably.

"Didn't you hear me? The test is over. Move along."

Lee Hyun came back to his senses, stepped out through the other side of the curtain, and entered Qinghe Valley.

Chapter 3

Stepping out from behind the curtain, Lee Hyun found himself facing a broad clearing.

The applicants who had passed the spiritual root test had gathered in small groups.

Hundreds of applicants had originally assembled below the Mountain Gate, but by Lee Hyun's rough estimate, fewer than fifty had made it this far.

"Everyone, quiet."

A voice came from the front of the clearing.

A middle-aged man in a gray robe stood on a raised platform. Blue waves and medicinal herb patterns were embroidered together on his chest.

The noisy applicants fell silent.

The middle-aged man slowly swept his gaze over the newcomers.

"I am Wang Jin, an Outer Gate steward. Those whose names I call, come forward."

Soon, the four applicants with the best spiritual roots were called out. There was one boy dressed in silk, two young-looking girls, and one barefoot, scrawny child.

"You four are inner disciple candidates. Follow him."

While the four children rejoiced, low sighs of disappointment spread among those who remained in the clearing.

Lee Hyun, on the other hand, breathed a sigh of relief.

Since the sect poured so many resources into its inner disciples, it would naturally scrutinize their cultivation progress just as strictly. There was also a good chance their bodies would be examined in detail during the process.

For Lee Hyun, who needed to conceal his ageless body, there could hardly have been a worse position.

After the inner disciple candidates followed one of Qinghe Valley's disciples away, Steward Wang Jin spoke again.

"I'll make this clear first, in case any of you are under the wrong impression. You are not yet official disciples of Qinghe Valley."

One boy cautiously raised his hand.

"Didn't we pass the spiritual root test?"

"Having a spiritual root is not the same as being able to become a cultivator."

Wang Jin answered indifferently.

"From this moment on, your status is that of an outer disciple candidate. Within the next one hundred days, you must accomplish Drawing Qi into the Body and reach Qi Refining Stage 1. During that time, you must also learn the sect's rules and how to carry out the work assigned to you."

"What happens if we fail to succeed within one hundred days?"

"You will either be sent down to the Menial Labor Compound and given another chance, or you will have to leave through the Mountain Gate."

The atmosphere in the clearing grew heavy.

"Even after reaching Qi Refining Stage 1, you will not immediately become an outer disciple."

Wang Jin continued.

"We will also judge your conduct and performance over those one hundred days. Anyone who bullies fellow disciples just because their cultivation is a little faster, or helps themselves to sect property, will not be accepted."

Wang Jin pointed to a stack of wooden tokens beside him.

"Come forward and receive your identity tokens."

The applicants stepped forward one by one.

When Lee Hyun's turn came, Wang Jin looked down at the register.

"Lee Hyun. Triple spiritual root of Wood, Fire, and Earth. Bone age, nineteen."

"Yes."

Wang Jin handed him a wooden token about the size of his palm.

The words Qinghe Valley were engraved on the front, while Lee Hyun's name was carved into the back.

"Don't lose it. You'll need it for entering and leaving, meals, and collecting supplies."

"Understood."

Lee Hyun examined the identity token carefully.

He had yet to develop qi sense, but after spending decades as a woodcutter and handling every kind of timber imaginable, he could tell that this identity token was no ordinary piece of wood.

Its grain was clearly visible, yet it was as heavy as stone, and even pressing a fingernail into its surface left no mark.

Even an identity token handed out to outer disciple candidates was unlike anything made by mortals. As expected of a cultivator sect.

...

Qinghe Valley was, just as its name suggested, a sect nestled within a valley.

Several peaks rose along the valley, which was wreathed in blue mist.

There was Qinghe Peak, the main peak where the Elders and inner disciples resided; Medicinal Field Peak, covered in tier upon tier of spirit fields; and Alchemy Furnace Peak, where smoke rose day and night. Off to one side stood the Scripture Pavilion, where the sect's books were said to be kept.

The outer disciple candidates' quarters were at the foot of Medicinal Field Peak.

Simple houses with earthen walls and tiled roofs lined the slope. Two people were assigned to each room.

Lee Hyun set down his belongings in front of the room he had been assigned. His roommate was a sixteen-year-old boy named Wang Shao.

"Brother, how old are you?"

"Nineteen."

"You're older than I thought."

'Nineteen is old?'

Lee Hyun was momentarily at a loss for words. If he included his previous life, he had lived for nearly eighty years.

"Brother, what spiritual root do you have? I have a triple spiritual root of Earth, Metal, and Water. The Steward said that if mine were just a little better, I might've had a shot at becoming an inner disciple..."

"Mine is Wood, Fire, and Earth."

Wang Shao started chattering before he had even finished unpacking.

"I'm definitely going to become an inner disciple. I heard that if an outer disciple performs exceptionally well, they can be promoted to an inner disciple. What's your goal, Brother?"

"Well... I was thinking I might learn how to grow spirit herbs and make pills."

"Come on, a man should dream bigger than that."

As they talked, Lee Hyun sorted through the items he had been issued. There were two gray robes, a pair of shoes, a thin blanket, wooden tableware, a brush and ink, and one blank booklet.

...

That evening, the outer disciple candidates were each given three thin books.

《Qinghe Valley Outer Gate Code》, 《Introductory Guide on Cultivation》, and 《Qinghe Qi-Drawing Art》.

Of the three, the most important was the Qinghe Qi-Drawing Art.

It was Qinghe Valley's most basic qi-drawing art. Since it was attributeless, anyone could practice it regardless of what spiritual root they possessed.

After reaching Qi Refining Stage 1, they would be allowed to choose a proper cultivation art suited to their spiritual root and assigned work.

Lee Hyun carefully turned the pages.

The locations of the meridians were marked alongside illustrations, and the book explained how to breathe and guide spiritual qi into the dantian.

...

Basic instruction began the next day.

Before sunrise, the newcomers gathered in a broad lecture hall and sat in the lotus position.

Wang Jin and two other outer disciples sat at the front.

"The first step of cultivation is sensing the spiritual qi scattered throughout heaven and earth."

Wang Jin spoke.

"Do not try to see it with your eyes, and do not try to seize it by force. Steady your breathing, clear your mind of stray thoughts, and wait for the moment when the energy outside your body comes into contact with your spiritual root."

The candidates closed their eyes.

Lee Hyun also breathed according to the instructions written in the Qinghe Qi-Drawing Art.

He slowly drew in a long breath, paused for a moment, then exhaled.

At first, he felt nothing.

All he could focus on was the hardness of the floor and the breathing of the person beside him.

Before long, his legs went numb.

His back hurt too.

'I have to do this for several shichen (each shichen is about two hours) every day?'

Cultivation was harder than he had expected.

In the novels he had read in his previous life, the protagonist would sit in the lotus position, close his eyes, and somehow several days would pass before he knew it. Now that Lee Hyun was trying it himself, enduring even half a shichen was no easy task.

Still, thanks to the stamina he had built up through years of logging, Lee Hyun straightened his back every time his posture began to sag.

He felt nothing on the first day.

The second day was the same.

On the third day, one of the children sitting in the front row suddenly opened his eyes, his face lighting up.

"I felt it!"

An outer disciple examined the child and nodded.

"You haven't succeeded in Drawing Qi into the Body yet. Don't get excited. Concentrate again."

By the fifth day, three people had sensed spiritual qi.

After ten days, more than twenty had sensed it.

Wang Shao, who shared Lee Hyun's room, was delighted after sensing spiritual qi as well.

"It was like tiny specks of light floating around. I couldn't grab them with my hands, but they were definitely all around me."

"I see."

"Brother, you still haven't felt it?"

"Not yet."

"Don't worry. There are still ninety days left."

"Right."

Lee Hyun was not particularly worried.

Still, it would be somewhat troublesome if he failed to succeed within those ninety days.

If he was sent to the Menial Labor Compound, there was no telling what kind of work he might be assigned. If he ended up in a mine or a spirit beast enclosure, it seemed unlikely that he would be able to learn the spirit herb cultivation techniques he wanted.

Even after instruction ended, Lee Hyun sat on his bed and continued practicing the Qinghe Qi-Drawing Art.

While the other candidates asked about one another's backgrounds or wandered around exploring the sect, he remained in his room.

...

It was the night of his twentieth day in the sect.

As usual, Lee Hyun sat on his bed, regulating his breathing.

A cool breeze blew in through the open window.

At that moment, Lee Hyun sensed something extremely faint mixed into the wind.

At first, he thought it was his imagination.

His eyes were closed, yet he could vaguely picture tiny dust-like motes drifting around him.

There was a warm energy like an ember, another that felt heavy like earth, and a faint vitality that reminded him of a newly sprouted shoot.

Recalling the mnemonic formula of the Qinghe Qi-Drawing Art, Lee Hyun focused his mind on the energy that felt closest to him.

It was the faint energy that reminded him of a sprout.

The hazy energy drifted into his body and reached his chest.

At that moment, his concentration faltered, and the energy scattered without a trace.

Lee Hyun tried again.

The second strand disappeared near his shoulder.

The third reached below his navel but dispersed before touching his dantian.

He lost track of how many times he failed as the sky beyond the window gradually began to brighten.

At last, a thread-thin strand of energy reached his dantian.

A faint warmth appeared in his lower abdomen.

Lee Hyun did not try to seize the energy. Following the mnemonic formula, he slowly circulated it within his dantian.

After three circuits, the energy became slightly more distinct than before.

He had not reached Qi Refining Stage 1. He had merely succeeded for the first time in sensing spiritual qi and drawing it into his body.

'It really works!'

Lee Hyun felt a rush of accomplishment and joy. Cultivation might suit him better than he had expected.

...

From that day onward, Lee Hyun gradually gathered spiritual qi in his dantian.

It had taken him a long time to sense spiritual qi in the first place, but once he had learned the feeling, finding it again was not difficult.

His progress, however, was slow.

Drawing in a single strand of spiritual qi left him mentally drained. If he forced himself to continue, his head began to ache and nausea churned in his stomach.

Wang Jin warned newcomers who experienced such symptoms not to overdo it.

"If you get greedy while your meridians are still unopened, you will only injure yourself. The one who starts earliest is not necessarily the one who reaches Qi Refining first."

In fact, the child who had sensed spiritual qi after only three days became too eager, coughed up blood, and was carried to the Infirmary.

After seeing that, Lee Hyun decided to proceed carefully.

...

At dawn, one month after he entered the sect.

The moment the spiritual qi accumulated in his dantian passed a critical point, the previously calm flow suddenly began to rotate, forming a vortex.

A thin current started in his lower abdomen and rose through the meridians inside his body.

It felt as though scalding water were coursing through his blood vessels.

Wherever the energy passed, his blocked meridians were forcibly pried open. Pain swept through his entire body, as though needles were scraping along beneath his skin.

"Ugh...!"

Lee Hyun gritted his teeth.

The energy passed through his chest and shoulders, spread all the way to his fingertips, then returned to his dantian.

His fingertips felt as though they were swelling, and then, in an instant, all his senses sharpened.

He could even hear Wang Shao grinding his teeth in his sleep. In the faint dawn light, he felt as though he could make out every single mote of dust drifting through the room.

His body trembled lightly as something that had been blocked inside him finally seemed to break open.

Following the final passage of the Qinghe Qi-Drawing Art, Lee Hyun circulated the energy through another circuit.

During the second circulation, a surge of searing heat rose through the pain.

The moment he completed the third circulation, an invisible shell shattered into pieces.

Boom!

Inside Lee Hyun's head, a thunderous roar rang out as if a massive dam had collapsed. The spiritual qi gathered in his dantian spread throughout his entire body, then rushed back like a violent wave. The energy that had previously been as thin as a strand of thread had now become a clear, distinct current.

Lee Hyun's eyes snapped open.

Even with nothing but the faint light of dawn, everything in the room appeared sharply defined. He could see the grain of the wooden chest, the tiny cracks in the wall, even a single strand of hair that had fallen onto Wang Shao's blanket.

Inside his body, an energy incomparably stronger than before pulsed with life.

Lee Hyun clenched his fist.

Even with the simple motion of curling his fingers, the muscles in his arm and shoulder felt as though they moved as one. Every part of his body responded instantly to his will.

'So this... is what it feels like to be a cultivator!'

Chapter 4

Lee Hyun was certain that he had entered Qi Refining Stage 1.

Of course, compared to those he had once seen fighting in the sky, he was probably worth less than a speck of dust.

But that did not matter. He was stronger than he had been yesterday.

If he encountered a wild beast in the mountains, he felt he would no longer have to flee blindly as he had before. If he lost his footing on a mountain path, he probably would not be injured so easily, and even if several ordinary grown men came at him, he felt he could defend himself.

More than anything, unlike the ageless body he had obtained by sheer chance, this achievement was something he had accomplished himself after sitting in lotus position every day, reciting the mnemonic formula, and failing countless times.

A deep sense of accomplishment and satisfaction welled up from within him.

When he exhaled, it felt as though the turbid qi that had accumulated inside his body was leaving along with his breath.

Then a horrible stench assaulted his nose.

“Ugh.”

Lee Hyun reflexively covered his nose and looked around the room for the source of the smell, only to lower his gaze to his own arm a moment later.

Blackish-yellow, oily grime was seeping out through his skin, and sticky filth was oozing from his neck, back, and face as well.

Startled, Lee Hyun hurriedly checked his pulse, but his heart was beating more strongly than before, and there was nothing wrong with his body. If anything, he felt cleaner and lighter than ever.

Only then did he remember what he had read in the 《Introductory Guide on Cultivation》.

It said that after successfully achieving Drawing Qi into the Body, spiritual qi would wash through the meridians, expelling some of the turbid qi and impurities accumulated within the body.

When he had read it, he had imagined it would amount to nothing more than sweating a little. He had never expected something like rotten mud to pour out from his entire body.

“The smell...”

Beside him, Wang Shao shifted in his sleep and wrinkled his nose.

Lee Hyun thought Wang Shao might wake up if he stayed like this, so he quietly climbed down from the bed.

Whoosh.

The instant his foot touched the floor, his body shot forward.

“...!”

He had thought he was simply taking a step with the same amount of force as usual, yet he nearly went flying. Lee Hyun hurriedly braced himself with his toes and stopped, then grabbed a spare robe and quietly slipped out of the room.

...

A short distance downhill from the Outer Gate residences was a stream flowing down from the mountain. The sun had yet to rise, so no one else was around.

The stench grew even worse when he took off his robe, and the sticky filth clung to his skin like a thin shell.

“This is a bit much...”

He grimaced and stepped into the water.

The streamwater flowing down from the mountain was cold enough to chill him to the bone. Even so, when he moved a little spiritual power in his dantian, warmth spread throughout his body and drove away the cold.

Lee Hyun scrubbed himself vigorously from head to toe.

The filth dissolved into the water and washed away, but one rinse was nowhere near enough. Only after scrubbing several times at the residue that had worked its way beneath his fingernails and between the strands of his hair did his natural skin finally emerge.

Lee Hyun submerged his head one last time, then surfaced and let out a long breath.

His breath turned into white mist and dispersed into the dawn air.

His body felt astonishingly refreshed.

It was as though years of accumulated fatigue had been pulled clean out from between his bones and muscles. His vision was clear, and he could hear the water flowing through the valley and even sense beasts moving in the distant forest.

Lee Hyun looked down at his face reflected in the water.

It was still the plain face of a young man around nineteen. However, his previously dull complexion had grown a little clearer, and his eyes were noticeably brighter than before.

He looked at a stone by the stream about the size of his head.

Normally, it was large enough that he would have needed to crouch down and lift it with both hands.

Lee Hyun cautiously gripped the stone with one hand.

It came up with ridiculous ease.

“Oh?”

Almost without thinking, he raised his arm, and the stone rose all the way above his head. It was not weightless, but he did not even need to grit his teeth.

When he set it down, it landed with a thud, gouging a deep depression into the soil beneath it.

This time, he looked up at the steep slope beside the stream. Normally, it was steep enough that he would have needed to use his hands while climbing.

Lee Hyun put strength into his legs.

His body sprang lightly upward.

Once, twice.

After reaching the top of the slope in only a few steps, he looked back down the way he had come. He was not even slightly out of breath. His legs were still brimming with strength.

‘This is fun.’

Lee Hyun came back down and began scrubbing the robe he had taken off in the water, only to discover something surprising. The grime had not soaked into the fabric at all. Once he submerged it fully in the flowing water, swished it around, then pulled it out and shook it off, it immediately looked as good as new, and even the moisture soon vanished.

‘As expected! Even the clothes in a sect of immortal cultivators are different.’

...

When Lee Hyun returned to the room, Wang Shao was still asleep.

Lee Hyun lay down on his own bed. His body was not tired, but as soon as he closed his eyes, perhaps because the tension had finally left him, he quickly fell asleep.

...

That morning.

“Lee Hyun.”

“Yes.”

Wang Jin studied him for a moment.

“You achieved Drawing Qi into the Body at dawn today.”

Soft exclamations rippled through the lecture hall.

Wang Shao stared at Lee Hyun with his mouth hanging open.

“Yes.”

“The seventh, is it... Not bad.”

Wang Jin spoke in a tone that neither particularly praised nor dismissed him.

“For the time being, focus on adapting to your body. There was even an idiot who got so excited after entering Qi Refining Stage 1 that he kicked a wall and broke his ankle.”

Several of the youths struggled to hold back their laughter.

“I will keep that in mind.”

Wang Shao leaned closer.

“Brother, when did you succeed?”

“At dawn today.”

“Then why didn’t you tell me?”

“You were asleep.”

“You should have woken me up!”

Even after cultivation ended that day, Wang Shao kept peppering him with questions.

He asked how much lighter Lee Hyun’s body felt, whether he could break stones, what spiritual power felt like, and whether Wang Shao himself showed any signs of an approaching breakthrough.

Lee Hyun answered as best he could, and Wang Shao immediately climbed onto his bed and sat in lotus position.

“I’ll break through today too.”

“Don’t push yourself.”

“Don’t worry. Mine is an Earth, Metal, and Water triple spiritual root. We both have a triple spiritual root, Brother, so I’ll succeed soon too!”

Several days later, before dawn, Wang Shao finally succeeded in Drawing Qi into the Body.

If not for the stench of the impurities oozing from Wang Shao’s body, Lee Hyun might have congratulated him a little more enthusiastically.

...

Time passed quickly.

By the fiftieth day after entering the sect, those who still could not sense anything even while sitting in lotus position could be counted on one hand.

Those who had broken through to Qi Refining Stage 1 earlier repeatedly practiced controlling their spiritual power with the Qinghe Qi-Drawing Art under Wang Jin’s instructions.

They gradually became accustomed to controlling their strength as well. Lee Hyun found the process quite enjoyable.

...

On the ninetieth day after entering the sect.

When Lee Hyun entered the lecture hall, he discovered that its arrangement had changed.

A folding screen had been set up on one side of the hall, and the three people who had yet to enter Qi Refining Stage 1 were sitting in lotus position behind it under the guidance of an outer disciple.

Their faces were filled with anxiety.

There was still some time left before the hundred-day mark, but it could not have been easy to watch everyone else move on to the next stage.

Wang Jin walked behind the long table at the front of the lecture hall.

Stacks of books lay upon it.

“Starting today, those of you who have entered Qi Refining Stage 1 will learn the basic cultivation arts commonly used in the Outer Gate.”

A murmur passed through the lecture hall.

“The Qinghe Qi-Drawing Art is a cultivation art meant for Drawing Qi into the Body. It is not suitable for advancing to Qi Refining Stage 2 or higher.”

Wang Jin looked over the disciples.

“You must choose a cultivation art with your spiritual roots and the work you will take on in the future in mind. Before Qi Refining Stage 3, it is possible to switch cultivation arts, but you will have to disperse most of the spiritual power you have already accumulated. Do not take this lightly.”

He picked up the book on the far left.

“The Verdant Wood Vitality-Nourishing Art. Those with a Wood attribute spiritual root can cultivate it. Its speed at drawing in spiritual qi is average, but its nature is gentle, and injured meridians recover quickly. It also helps with sensing the vitality of spirit herbs, so it is suitable for those who wish to work at Medicinal Field Peak.”

Lee Hyun’s interest was piqued.

The reason he had chosen Qinghe Valley in the first place was to learn how to grow spirit herbs.

Wang Jin picked up the next book.

“The Crimson Flame Art. A Fire attribute cultivation art. Of all the cultivation arts I will introduce today, it has the fastest cultivation speed, and its spiritual power is highly explosive. It is advantageous for learning Fire attribute techniques and alchemy. However, its nature is harsh. It can easily scorch your meridians, and cultivating it for long periods causes fire toxin to accumulate within the body. I do not recommend it to anyone hotheaded.”

Wang Jin lifted the third book.

“The Sovereign Earth Art. Earth attribute. Its cultivation speed is slow, but its spiritual power is substantial and stable. At the same realm, it can sustain defensive techniques longer than other cultivation arts. It is also useful for those who intend to tend spirit fields or learn formations.”

He continued with explanations of the fourth and fifth books, the 《Metal Edge Art》 and the 《Mystic Water Art》.

The Metal Edge Art produced sharp spiritual power and had great offensive strength, but it also eroded the cultivator’s own meridians, requiring a steady supply of medicinal materials to keep the body in good condition and making it expensive to cultivate.

The Mystic Water Art had a smooth flow of spiritual power and could change with great flexibility, making it compatible with all kinds of techniques, but prolonged use caused cold to accumulate within the body.

Of the cultivation arts introduced so far, Lee Hyun could choose from the three corresponding to the Wood, Fire, and Earth attributes.

The Verdant Wood Vitality-Nourishing Art was advantageous for cultivating spirit herbs, the Crimson Flame Art suited alchemy, and the Sovereign Earth Art excelled at managing spirit fields and defense.

None of them seemed like a particularly bad choice.

Then Wang Jin picked up the sixth and final cultivation art.

“Last is the Primordial One-Qi Art. It has no attribute requirement, so anyone can cultivate it regardless of their spiritual root. Because the process of drawing in spiritual qi corresponding to one’s own spiritual root and refining it into spiritual power is safe, it also carries the lowest risk of qi deviation.”

Wang Jin paused briefly.

“Its cultivation speed is the slowest.”

Disappointment appeared here and there throughout the lecture hall.

“However, the reason we teach this cultivation art to disciples is that it has many advantages. The spiritual power refined through this cultivation art is called Primordial True Qi, and as it is released, it can freely transform, allowing you to use techniques whose attributes do not match your own spiritual roots. Their power will be somewhat reduced, but it is an extremely useful property. Why do you think that is?”

Wang Jin looked over the disciples for a moment before continuing.

“Because we often need to use techniques of many different attributes. To give you a simple example, how many techniques would someone working as a spirit-plant cultivator in Qinghe Valley need to use?”

Wang Jin pointed at Wang Shao.

“You answer.”

Wang Shao’s eyes widened at being called on so suddenly.

“Techniques used by spirit-plant cultivators?”

“Yes.”

Wang Shao thought for a moment, folding down his fingers one by one.

“A technique for watering spirit herbs... and maybe one for making the soil more fertile?”

Wang Jin’s eyebrows rose slightly.

“Do you think that would be enough? Spirit plants are not weeds that grow on their own just because you plant them in a field and give them some water.”

He raised a finger and formed a small hand sign in the air.

A wisp of pale cloud appeared above his palm, then released several fine droplets of rain.

“First, there is the Spirit Rain Art. It is a Water attribute technique that uses spiritual power to create a small cloud and produce rain imbued with spiritual qi. It is broadly useful when cultivating most spirit herbs.”

As the cloud dispersed, a yellow glow appeared at Wang Jin’s fingertips.

A pile of soil in the corner of the lecture hall turned itself over and loosened. Only the tiny grass roots and fragments of stone mixed within it were pushed outside.

“The Earth attribute Soil-Turning Art. It is a representative technique used to till hardened ground, sift out stones and weed roots, and allow the soil of a spirit field to hold spiritual qi evenly.”

Wang Jin flicked his finger.

A slender silver needle cut through the air.

The needle pierced a flying insect clinging to one of the lecture hall’s pillars, then vanished without leaving so much as a mark on the pillar.

“The Metal attribute Yang Metal Art. It is a technique that kills only spirit insects without touching the leaves or stems of spirit herbs. Naturally, spirit insects are difficult to kill with Fire attribute techniques. Most of the time, using a Fire attribute technique will burn the spirit herbs as well. Therefore, this technique is a fundamental skill for spirit-plant cultivators. Of course, if your control is poor, you will riddle the spirit herbs with holes before you kill the spirit insects.”

Several youths unconsciously glanced toward the pillar.

“Then there is also the Wood attribute Germination Art. It infuses seeds with vitality to help them sprout.”

Wang Jin lowered his hand.

“Everything I just mentioned is nothing more than the basic techniques learned by spirit-plant cultivators. Yet even those already require four attributes: Water, Earth, Metal, and Wood.”

One boy raised his hand.

“Then couldn’t we simply assign a different spirit-plant cultivator to each attribute? We could have one person handle the rain and another till the soil.”

“That is also one method.”

Wang Jin readily acknowledged it.

“A great sect with cultivators to spare, one that can assign several specialized spirit-plant cultivators to every spirit field, could certainly do that.”

A trace of bitterness entered his voice.

“But aside from our one Golden Core Patriarch, every cultivator in Qinghe Valley is at Foundation Establishment or below. On top of that, because our spirit fields are of poor quality, we have to cultivate spirit herbs over a wider area to compensate. There is a great deal of work to be done, while the people and resources available to us are limited. If you had to call a cultivator who knew the Spirit Rain Art every time the spirit herbs needed watering, summon someone who knew the Soil-Turning Art whenever weeds needed clearing, and search for someone who knew the Yang Metal Art whenever spirit insects appeared, how troublesome do you think managing each spirit field would become?”

Wang Jin seemed to want the disciples to choose the Primordial One-Qi Art. However, after hearing that it had the slowest cultivation speed, the disciples’ reactions remained lukewarm.

Lee Hyun turned his gaze toward the place where the 《Primordial One-Qi Art》 lay.

‘But does it matter if my cultivation speed is slow?’

Chapter 5

When most of the children showed little interest in the Primordial One-Qi Art, Wang Jin continued his impassioned pitch.

“The Primordial One-Qi Art has many advantages. Its true qi flows smoothly, and its circulation method is simple. Once you become sufficiently familiar with the cultivation art, you can even cultivate without sitting in the lotus position. Whether you’re standing, walking, or even lying down, you can absorb spiritual qi.”

‘Lying down...? That sounds nice.’

“Then can we cultivate even while sleeping?”

Someone asked.

“Well... theoretically, I suppose there’s no reason you couldn’t. In any case, the important thing is that the Primordial One-Qi Art has no drawbacks aside from its cultivation speed. And in truth, even that isn’t much of a problem.”

Wang Jin raised the book and added,

“If you work as a spirit-plant cultivator, achieve good results, and become an inner disciple, you’ll be granted a superior cultivation art. When that happens, you won’t need to disperse your Primordial True Qi. Primordial True Qi is spiritual power that does not lean toward any particular attribute, so most of it can be converted into the spiritual power of your new cultivation art. In any case, the Verdant Wood Vitality-Nourishing Art, Crimson Flame Art, Sovereign Earth Art, Metal Edge Art, and Mystic Water Art are all merely Tier 1 cultivation arts. If you become an inner disciple, you’ll learn a better cultivation art anyway. So wouldn’t it also be a good choice to first learn the Primordial One-Qi Art and then distinguish yourself in the field of spirit plants?”

Wang Jin swept a hand over the six piles on the table.

“That concludes the explanation. Each of you may take one copy of whichever cultivation manual you want.”

Perhaps Steward Wang Jin’s sales pitch had worked, because more than half the children chose the Primordial One-Qi Art.

‘Learn the Primordial One-Qi Art, distinguish myself as a spirit-plant cultivator, and become an inner disciple? If becoming an inner disciple were really that easy, why would only a few ever manage it...? But I never wanted to become an inner disciple in the first place, so it doesn’t matter.’

‘The Primordial One-Qi Art is the best choice for me. If I want to cultivate my own spirit field and grow spirit plants by myself later, I need to be able to use techniques of multiple attributes.’

After thinking for a moment, Lee Hyun also chose the Primordial One-Qi Art.

Some of the more suspicious or thoughtful children chose one of the other five cultivation arts instead.

Each child received a book, sat down, and briefly looked through its contents. Then one child asked,

“Steward, what is this Primordial Body in the latter half of the Primordial One-Qi Art?”

‘Primordial Body?’

Lee Hyun also flipped to the latter part of the book and found a cultivation method described there.

“Don’t get your hopes up. It’s useless.”

“Why is that? From the looks of it, it tempers the entire body. Isn’t it a body-refining art? I heard that cultivators become stronger the more evenly they develop their essence, qi and spirit.”

“The Primordial Body is not an ordinary body-refining art. Most body-refining arts rely on external aids. You might soak yourself in a special bath prepared with a demon beast’s essence blood to temper your skin, or require spirit treasures or pills to temper your bones, muscles, and internal organs.”

The children listened quietly.

“Some cultivation arts temper the body inside special formations, while others require you to endure the heat in places where earth fire emerges.”

“Then what makes the Primordial Body different?”

“To begin with, the Primordial Body does not rely on any special external resources for its training.”

Another quiet stir rose at Wang Jin’s answer. To impoverished outer disciple candidates, a cultivation art that required no expensive resources sounded like the best possible option.

“It sounds good when you put it that way. But if there really were a way to become stronger for free, why would the world’s body refiners risk their lives to obtain resources?”

Wang Jin tapped the cover of the Primordial One-Qi Art with a finger.

“The method of creating a Primordial Body is simple. Instead of accumulating spiritual power around the dantian, you turn the entire body into a dantian.”

Wang Shao tilted his head.

“Wouldn’t making the entire body into a dantian be a good thing? It sounds like you could hold far more spiritual power.”

“Yes. If you only consider the advantages, that’s true. Since spiritual power would constantly flow throughout the entire body, the skin, muscles, bones, and internal organs would be continuously bathed in it. If you actually succeeded, your physical body would become stronger without any separate body-refining art. You could also contain vastly more spiritual power than other cultivators at the same realm. In truth, strengthening the physical body is merely a side effect. At its core, it is closer to a unique method of cultivating spiritual power.”

He looked over the children for a moment, then pointed to a tall boy in the front row.

“You. What do you think the dantian is?”

The boy looked flustered by the sudden question.

“An organ below the navel... that stores spiritual power?”

“Wrong.”

Wang Jin spoke decisively.

“Anyone who has killed a person and cut open their abdomen would know that there is no separate organ called a dantian inside the human body.”

Several children went pale.

“Meridians physically exist. But the dantian is merely a region designated by a cultivation art for storing spiritual power. Following the guidance of the cultivation art, you define a particular area below the navel and repeatedly gather refined spiritual power there, gradually forming it into a dantian.”

Wang Jin pointed at his own lower abdomen.

“The reason we use the center of the body is simple. It makes it convenient to send spiritual power to the limbs, the head, or any of the internal organs.”

“But accumulating spiritual power throughout the entire body isn’t impossible, is it?”

The boy asked cautiously.

“I never said it was impossible. I said it was useless.”

Wang Jin raised one finger.

“The hardest thing on the path of cultivation is not drawing in spiritual qi. It is gathering the spiritual qi you have drawn in at one place, compressing it, and transforming it into a higher-quality power. When a Qi Refining cultivator advances to Foundation Establishment, they must compress their diffuse, gaseous spiritual power and transform it into liquid true essence. Most cultivators spend their entire lives trying and still fail, even though they only need to condense the spiritual power contained within a space the size of a dantian.”

His finger swept toward all the candidates this time.

“And you want to make your entire body into a dantian? How great do you think the difference in volume is between a dantian and the entire body? It varies by cultivation art, but usually it would be around a hundred times. Even compared to cultivation arts that create especially large dantians, it would still be fifty times.”

The hall fell silent.

“Do you think the Seniors of past ages lacked wisdom and chose to cultivate within the narrow confines of a dantian for no reason? They found the most efficient method of achieving a qualitative transformation with limited spiritual qi and resources.”

Wang Jin opened the book to the section describing the Primordial Body.

“This method of using the entire body as a dantian was likely created a very long time ago. Perhaps it originated in antiquity, when heaven-and-earth spiritual qi was far denser than it is now, or perhaps it is a cultivation method usable only in a place like the immortal realm, where spiritual qi floods into the body merely from breathing.”

A sharp-eyed boy sitting toward the back raised his hand.

“Wouldn’t it be possible for a wealthy cultivation clan or great sect? If they poured in all kinds of pills and spirit stones, it seems like they could turn the entire body into a dantian.”

“Theoretically, perhaps. But what faction would ever do such a thing?”

He gave a dry laugh.

“Suppose you were the master of a sect. Would you raise a hundred Foundation Establishment cultivators, or a single Foundation Establishment cultivator whose entire body served as a dantian?”

The children fell completely silent.

“Foundation Establishment is not the end. What about Golden Core? Nascent Soul? Common sense tells you that the return is far too small for the resources invested. Once someone crosses a major realm, their combat power rises to an entirely different level. No matter how small the dantian of an early Foundation Establishment cultivator might be, do you really think a Qi Refining Stage 10 cultivator who made his entire body into a dantian could defeat him...?”

Wang Jin fell into thought for a moment.

“Hmm... now that I think about it, he might be able to. In any case, even if he could, it certainly wouldn’t be easy. And there’s an even bigger problem!”

Wang Jin spoke as though driving in the final nail.

“How many Foundation Establishment Pills would he have to swallow to break through to Foundation Establishment? Fifty? A hundred? Absurd. Ordinary late-stage Qi Refining cultivators risk their lives on missions just to obtain a single Foundation Establishment Pill.”

Wang Jin clicked his tongue.

“Even though a Qi Refining cultivator lives longer than a mortal, their lifespan is only around a hundred to a hundred and fifty years. In practice, once they pass eighty, their vitality declines, and the odds of dying while attempting Foundation Establishment rise sharply. Most Qi Refining cultivators fail to break through to Foundation Establishment because they cannot properly condense even the spiritual power accumulated in the small dantian beneath the navel within a hundred years. So how could anyone condense the spiritual power accumulated throughout the entire body?”

He tossed the book onto the table.

“There’s no harm in reading it. It may even help you study the principles of cultivation. But if you actually try to follow this cultivation method yourself, you will feel the hopelessness of filling an endless sea alone.”

Once Wang Jin’s long speech ended, the children lost interest in the Primordial Body.

Lee Hyun, however, became even more intrigued!

‘I could create a Primordial Body, couldn’t I? Time is the one thing I have to spare, and there’s no reason I need to break through to Foundation Establishment quickly anyway. I’m not trying to become strong as fast as possible.’

‘In the xianxia novels I read in my past life, no matter how high your realm was, there were always plenty of strong guys around who would pick a fight with you... In the cultivation world, the lower your apparent realm, the safer you are. It makes your opponent let down their guard! If that’s the case, maybe learning the Primordial Body and becoming the strongest within the same realm would be better...’

Lee Hyun thought the Primordial Body suited his disposition extremely well. Still, he had no intention of learning it immediately. At the early stage of Qi Refining, if his realm did not advance at roughly the same pace as everyone else’s, the sect might find it strange, and it could also make it difficult for him to carry out spirit-plant work.

‘I’ll learn the Primordial One-Qi Art to a reasonable level, learn about spirit plants, then run away from Qinghe Valley before anyone notices that I don’t age. After that, it won’t be too late to dig a tunnel, hide away, and create a Primordial Body.’

...

After the lesson ended and they returned to their quarters, Wang Shao saw the Primordial One-Qi Art in Lee Hyun’s hand and asked,

“Did you really choose that?”

“Yeah.”

“Brother, I hate to say this, but... there’s no way producing results as a spirit-plant cultivator will make you an inner disciple. The cultivation world is extremely treacherous and full of schemes. This has to be a trap Wang Jin is steering us into!”

“How dare you badmouth Steward Wang when you’re just a newcomer? Have you lost your mind?”

At Lee Hyun’s words, Wang Shao’s expression froze.

“Haha, I’m joking. You say the cultivation world is treacherous, but don’t you trust me, someone you’ve barely known for very long, a little too easily? You should always watch what you say.”

“You scared me! I certainly was careless. But I have a good eye for people. From the very beginning, I thought you were someone I could trust, Brother.”

“What did you choose?”

“I chose the Metal Edge Art. If you’re going to be a cultivator, shouldn’t you become a sword cultivator with the greatest combat power? And if you want to be a sword cultivator, naturally you should learn a Metal-attribute cultivation art. How long would it take to reach a high realm through spirit-plant work?”

“Didn’t they say the Metal Edge Art harms the meridians?”

“They said it would be fine as long as I keep taking medicinal ingredients.”

“That’ll cost a lot of spirit stones.”

“If I become a sword cultivator and earn merit in battle, won’t the sect provide all the pills and medicinal ingredients I need?”

“Have you ever killed anyone?”

“No...”

“Neither have I. Honestly, I’m not confident I can fight. Even killing an animal is hard enough, so how much harder would it be to fight another cultivator? I’m going to learn spirit-plant work.”

After chatting for a while, Wang Shao climbed onto his bed and opened the Metal Edge Art. After reading through the cultivation art’s mnemonic formula a few times, he immediately sat in the lotus position.

Lee Hyun also sat on his own bed and opened the Primordial One-Qi Art.

Compared to the Qinghe Qi-Drawing Art, the Primordial One-Qi Art contained far more material. It explained everything in detail, from the breathing method for absorbing heaven-and-earth spiritual qi, to the process of refining spiritual qi, to how Primordial True Qi should circulate through the meridians, and how to circulate Primordial True Qi when using techniques.

‘I need to reach Novice quickly so I can cultivate lying down! The lotus position is way too uncomfortable...’

...

A few days later.

Steward Wang Jin called in the newcomers who had reached Qi Refining Stage 1 one by one for interviews, and Lee Hyun was no exception.

“You’ll be assigned duties soon. Is there any particular work you want?”

“I’d like to learn how to grow spirit plants or spirit herbs.”

“You have a triple spiritual root of Wood, Fire, and Earth. That’s not a bad fit. Why?”

“It seems safer than fighting people.”

Wang Jin’s hand stopped as he wrote something in the register.

“You’re an honest fellow. But spirit-plant work is by no means easy. You have to guard against spirit insects and crop disease, and even a slight miscalculation in the amount of spirit rain can ruin the crop. Some spirit herbs with strong medicinal potency even emit poisonous qi. What cultivation art do you intend to learn?”

“The Primordial One-Qi Art.”

“Is that so? Good choice. You’ll learn the result of your assignment soon.”

On the hundredth day after entering the sect.

The newcomers gathered in the hall before sunrise.

Today was the day Steward Wang Jin would formally appoint the newcomers who had reached Qi Refining Stage 1 as outer disciples and assign them new duties and living quarters.

Chapter 6

Tension and anticipation mingled on the faces of the children gathered in the lecture hall.

Meanwhile, the two who had still failed to reach Qi Refining Stage 1 sat behind the folding screen in lotus position, their faces pale.

A short while later, Steward Wang Jin entered the lecture hall.

An outer disciple followed him in, carrying a wooden chest filled with small pouches.

Wang Jin slowly surveyed the new recruits.

“Today marks the hundredth day. Most of you have succeeded in Drawing Qi into the Body. Not a bad result.”

Wang Jin’s gaze shifted toward the folding screen.

“Zhu Ming.”

The young boy flinched and rose to his feet.

“Yes.”

“You will be sent down to the Menial Labor Compound. If you succeed in Drawing Qi into the Body within six months while working there, I will allow you to enter the Outer Gate.”

The boy’s face brightened.

“Thank you, Steward!”

“There is no need to thank me. The work at the Menial Labor Compound will be far harder than what you have been doing here.”

“I’ll work hard.”

Wang Jin turned his head.

“Gao Ze.”

This time, a young man rose from his seat.

“Yes.”

“Leave through the Mountain Gate.”

The color drained from the young man’s face.

“Steward, please give me just one more chance. I swear I’ll...”

“Enough! Zhu Ming cultivated diligently. He merely lacks talent, but that does not mean he has no potential. You, however, lacked both talent and effort. Leave the mountain.”

The young man bit his lip but could say no more.

The outer disciple who had entered with Wang Jin escorted the two of them out of the lecture hall.

Wang Jin opened the roster.

“From now on, those whose names I call will be formally accepted as outer disciples of Qinghe Valley.”

The atmosphere in the lecture hall changed. The children straightened their backs.

“Outer disciples receive one low-grade spirit stone and ten Hunger-Warding Pills each month, along with a modest amount of contribution points. You can earn additional contribution points by performing exceptionally well in your assigned duties or by completing separate missions. Contribution points can be used to borrow or purchase cultivation arts, techniques, pills, magic tools, and other items. This month’s supplies have already been placed inside the storage pouches you will receive today, and your contribution points have been recorded on your new identity tokens.”

Wang Jin called out the names one by one.

The disciples whose names were called stepped forward, returned their old wooden tokens, and received a new identity token and a storage pouch.

Soon, it was Lee Hyun’s turn.

“Lee Hyun.”

“Yes.”

“Your assigned duty is assistant caretaker for Spirit Field No. 73 on Medicinal Field Peak.”

Lee Hyun’s expression brightened.

“The caretaker of Spirit Field No. 73 is Lu Baishan. That fellow has handled spirit plant work in the Outer Gate for many years, so you should have plenty to learn from him.”

“Understood.”

Lee Hyun received his new identity token and a storage pouch that looked like a small cloth bag, then returned to his seat.

The new identity token was made of dark blue-black wood. It was about the same size as the old one, but the emblem of Qinghe Valley had been intricately carved into the front, while the back bore Lee Hyun’s name and the words Outer Gate.

He still had no idea how to use the storage pouch, however.

Before long, the last disciple received their items and returned to their seat.

After having the wooden chest removed, Wang Jin took an old storage pouch from his waist.

“Most of you have probably never seen a storage pouch before, so I’ll show you how to use one.”

He placed a finger against the mouth of the pouch.

“Channel spiritual power into the formation engraved around the opening, then send your consciousness inside along its flow. You do not need much spiritual power. A strand as thin as a thread is enough.”

Lee Hyun placed the storage pouch on his palm along with the other disciples.

From the outside, it looked like nothing more than a pouch made of gray cloth. A black cord was tied around its opening, and faint silver patterns were embroidered across the fabric.

He drew up a small amount of Primordial True Qi from his dantian and channeled it into the patterns.

At first, nothing happened.

When Lee Hyun closed his eyes and focused his consciousness on the pouch, the patterns began to glow faintly. At that moment, an empty space appeared in his mind.

It was dark in every direction, with indistinct boundaries. Inside lay a transparent stone and a wooden vial.

‘Oh... that’s fascinating.’
