Lee Hyun thought about taking out the stone. A cold sensation immediately touched his palm.

It was a transparent stone about two knuckles long. Inside it, something like a pale white mist slowly swirled as though alive.

Exclamations of wonder rose around him.

“Is this a spirit stone?”

A boy seated in the front row asked.

“That’s right. A low-grade spirit stone.”

Wang Jin took an identical stone out of his own storage pouch.

“Spirit stones are formed when heaven-and-earth spiritual qi condenses over a very long period of time. They can occur naturally in mineral veins, and they can also be artificially produced around spirit veins.”

One boy clutched his spirit stone in both hands and tried to draw out the spiritual qi within it. The mist inside the stone quivered slightly, and Wang Jin immediately rebuked him.

“Don’t absorb it recklessly.”

Startled, the boy loosened his grip.

“You can hold a spirit stone and draw out its spiritual qi directly. But at your current level, you cannot properly refine the spiritual qi contained within it. More than half of it would simply disperse into the air.”

Wang Jin rolled the spirit stone between his fingers.

“The most common use for spirit stones is powering formations. It’s the same when cultivating. If you obtain a portable Qi-Gathering Formation and place a spirit stone into its formation plate, it can draw the surrounding spiritual qi into a confined space. Cultivating inside it is several times more efficient than absorbing a spirit stone directly.”

Several children’s eyes lit up.

“Where can we get a portable Qi-Gathering Formation?”

“You can buy one at the Artifact Hall with contribution points or spirit stones. Even a crude one will cost at least fifty low-grade spirit stones.”

The children who had looked eager only moments before immediately deflated.

As though he had expected that reaction, Wang Jin continued.

“If your spiritual power is exhausted in battle and your life hangs by a thread, you may have no choice but to absorb from a spirit stone directly. But unless you are in such a situation, do not waste them. Spirit stones are the most widely used currency in the cultivation world, so keep them safe.”

Lee Hyun put the spirit stone back into his storage pouch.

The wooden vial inside contained ten bean-sized Hunger-Warding Pills. When he focused his consciousness on the identity token, the words 10 contribution points appeared faintly beneath his name.

“Do not try to put living animals or people inside a storage pouch. Even if you try to force them in, the formation will not activate.”

The children repeatedly put items into their storage pouches and took them back out.

Lee Hyun also put his identity token, spirit stone, and Hunger-Warding Pills in and took them back out several times. Once he grew accustomed to it, he could store and retrieve items with a mere thought without even opening the pouch by hand.

...

Once their duties and residences had been assigned, the new outer disciples dispersed from the lecture hall.

Most returned to their old quarters to pack their belongings. From now on, they would either live in quarters near their assigned duties or move into Outer Gate residences established on the various peaks.

Lee Hyun likewise returned to his room and packed the clothes, bedding, and books he had been issued.

Once he placed the bulky bedding and wooden dishes into his storage pouch, the belongings that had occupied one corner of the room vanished in an instant.

Wang Shao was crouched in front of his bed, completely absorbed in putting his belongings into his storage pouch and taking them back out again.

“Brother, look at this.”

He opened his hand, and a wooden dish appeared. He turned his hand over again, and the dish vanished.

“I feel like I’ve already seen that dozens of times.”

“Isn’t it still amazing? If I buy a bunch of storage pouches later, maybe I could even carry a whole house around with me.”

“Can you put one storage pouch inside another?”

“I tried it with another friend earlier, but it doesn’t work. The openings just close up as if they’re repelling each other.”

“Where were you assigned?”

“The Spirit Beast Garden.”

Wang Shao’s voice grew slightly quieter. Thinking he was unhappy with his assignment, Lee Hyun tried to console him.

“I heard not many people get the work they want right from the start. If you work hard at the Spirit Beast Garden, you might be able to learn swordsmanship later.”

Wang Shao shook his head.

“That’s not it. I asked around, and apparently aspiring sword cultivators are often sent to the Spirit Beast Garden when they first become disciples.”

“Why?”

“A disciple who’s only just reached Qi Refining Stage 1 isn’t much use, is he? Take someone like that on a Dharma Protector Hall mission and they’d only be a burden. So at first, they haul feed for the spirit beasts or clean their pens to build up their strength, while learning not to panic when dealing with spirit beasts.”

Unlike a moment earlier, Wang Shao now spoke with obvious excitement.

“I’ve been assigned to the area that looks after Azure-Horn Deer, a Tier 1 spirit beast. They’re docile, so it shouldn’t be dangerous.”

Wang Shao looked as though he had already stumbled upon some fortuitous encounter in swordsmanship at the Spirit Beast Garden.

“That’s good. Still, be careful not to get hurt.”

“I told you, they’re docile. I’m more worried about you, Brother. You might end up pulling weeds in a field all day.”

“It’s what I wanted, so I don’t mind.”

Wang Shao fastened his storage pouch securely at his waist.

The two of them had shared the same room for one hundred days. It was both a long time and a short one, depending on how one looked at it. Wang Shao certainly talked a lot, but thanks to him, Lee Hyun had been less bored as well.

“Let’s meet again in the Inner Gate someday.”

“I told you, I have no intention of entering the Inner Gate.”

“No one knows what the future holds. Brother might accomplish something great in the field of spirit plants and catch an Elder’s eye.”

“Then you get into the Inner Gate first and save me a place.”

“Of course.”

Wang Shao held out his fist. Lee Hyun bumped it with his own.

“Take care.”

“You too, Brother.”

...

Lee Hyun headed toward Medicinal Field Peak.

The entire mountain had been carved into the shape of a gigantic staircase.

Countless spirit fields stretched upward in terraces from the foot of the mountain to its middle reaches. Low stone walls and waterways divided the fields, and different spirit herbs grew in each one.

Some grasses had silver patterns flowing across their green leaves, while other plants had red roots protruding from the earth like human fingers.

Scarecrows woven from straw turned their heads on their own to drive away birds.

Small clouds drifted slowly through the air above the spirit fields. When a cultivator in gray robes formed a hand sign, a fine rain began to fall from one of the clouds.

In another spirit field, slender silver needles darted rapidly between the leaves, piercing tiny insects.

‘Looks like I came to the right place.’

The farther he climbed, the stronger an indescribable fragrance became amid the scents of earth and grass.

A sweet floral scent drifted from one spirit field, while another gave off a pungent odor sharp enough to sting his nose. Formation patterns had been carved into every stone wall, and whenever Lee Hyun drew close, his identity token trembled faintly.

Most of the senior cultivators paid no attention to him.

Lee Hyun checked the signposts along the paths as he made his way toward his assigned spirit field.

...

Spirit Field No. 73 lay near the edge of Medicinal Field Peak.

It was about as large as several of the fields in White Wood Village put together, where Lee Hyun had first settled after arriving in this world.

Green grass grew neatly within the low stone walls. At the center of the spirit field stood a small pond and a single-story building with earthen walls and a tiled roof.

It was not an ornate building, but it seemed more than adequate to serve as both a workshop and residence for the spirit field’s caretaker.

On one side of the front yard, bamboo mats had been spread out for drying spirit herbs. Beside them stood rows of earthenware jars filled with soil and medicinal ingredients. Along the edge of the pond, potted medicinal herbs Lee Hyun did not recognize had been lined up in a row.

An old man was bent over in the field, pulling weeds.

More than half of his hair had turned white, and deep wrinkles lined his sun-darkened face.

Lee Hyun approached and greeted him.

“Are you Senior Brother Lu?”

The old man raised his head.

His gaze moved from Lee Hyun’s face to the identity token hanging at his waist.

“You’re the new recruit?”

“Yes. My name is Lee Hyun. I’ve been assigned as assistant caretaker for Spirit Field No. 73.”

Lu Baishan straightened up.

“Follow me.”

He led Lee Hyun toward the building at the center of the spirit field. Up close, bundles of dried herbs could be seen hanging beneath the eaves, while dirt-stained boots and bamboo baskets of various sizes rested against the wall.

Lu Baishan opened the door.

“Come in.”

The interior was more spacious than it had appeared from outside. All manner of farming tools, including hoes, sickles, and watering cans, hung from one wall, while scrolls depicting various spirit herbs and listing their characteristics covered the opposite side.

A long table stood in the middle of the room. Several small pots containing young spirit herbs sat atop it alongside worn books and a teapot. A kitchen and two rooms lay farther inside, making it clear that the building served as living quarters as well as a workshop.

Lu Baishan lightly dusted off his hands. A faint glow passed over them, and the dirt vanished without a trace. He sat behind the table and took a sip of his cooling tea.

“Sit.”

Once Lee Hyun had taken a seat across from him, Lu Baishan asked,

“What cultivation art do you practice?”

“The Primordial One-Qi Art.”

Lu Baishan stared at Lee Hyun for a moment, then clicked his tongue.

“Tsk. Steward Wang recommended that art again, did he?”

“Is there a problem with that cultivation art?”

Chapter 7

“There is absolutely nothing wrong with the Primordial One-Qi Art itself. In fact, it is far more profound than the other basic cultivation arts given to new disciples. But... no, forget it. I still don’t know whether that applies to you...”

Lu Baishan pointed to the one of the two inner rooms whose door stood open.

“Use that room. Put your things away first, then come back out.”

Lee Hyun entered the room Lu Baishan had indicated.

Inside were a small bed and an old chest. It seemed to have been vacant for a while, as a faint layer of dust had settled over the floor and furniture, but there was no visible damage to the walls or ceiling. When he opened the window, the pond and verdant spirit field came into view at a glance.

Lee Hyun took his bedding and clothes from his storage pouch, set them on the bed, then stepped back outside.

Lu Baishan had already left the building, and Lee Hyun hurried after him.

“Today, you’ll be pulling weeds.”

“Won’t we be using techniques?”

“Do you know how to use any?”

“Not yet.”

“Then pull them by hand.”

“Yes.”

The green grass covering most of the spirit field had grown as high as his knees.

Its leaves were slender, with clear beads of dew gathered at their tips.

“What kind of spirit herb is this?”

“Green Dew Grass. It is used in Spirit-Restoring Powder, which quickly replenishes spent spiritual qi, and Meridian-Cooling Pills, which soothe heat in the meridians. It isn’t a precious spirit herb, but it has many uses, so there is always steady demand for it.”

“How do I tell the weeds apart?”

“Anything that isn’t Green Dew Grass is a weed. Don’t leave any roots behind.”

“Yes.”

The instructions were simple, but actually doing it was not.

The roots of Green Dew Grass were thin and white, and many weeds had similar roots. If he simply yanked on a weed, the stem would snap, so he had to carefully loosen the soil and pull out the roots as well.

It took quite a while to remove even a single weed. Before he knew it, Lu Baishan was already far ahead of him.

‘I thought cultivators would handle all their farm work with techniques... So they actually pull weeds by hand too.’

Still, he didn’t dislike it.

If he had done this sort of work in his previous life, he would have complained endlessly, but perhaps because he had reached Qi Refining Stage 1, neither his back nor his knees hurt at all.

With his body comfortable, the work did not feel mentally taxing either.

As he followed the roots of the weeds and loosened the soil around them, he occasionally came across unfamiliar insects or plant roots.

‘Ugh... What is that?’

When Lee Hyun found a bug with a green carapace and showed it to Lu Baishan, asking what he should do with it, Lu Baishan explained that it was a Green-Carapace Bug that sucked the sap from Green Dew Grass. With a gesture, he lifted it into the air and burned it away.

On the other hand, a creature that looked like an ordinary earthworm was an Earth Spirit Worm, which evenly distributed spiritual qi through the soil, so there was no need to kill it.

Even within the same soil, some things had to be eliminated while others had to be protected. It was only his first day, but Lee Hyun found the process of learning to distinguish them one by one rather interesting.

As the sun began to sink beyond the mountains, Lu Baishan was the first to straighten up.

“That’s enough for today.”

“There’s still some left over there.”

“After sunset, the dew on the Green Dew Grass returns to its roots. If you disturb the soil then, you’ll damage its medicinal potency.”

Lu Baishan gathered the weeds they had pulled into one pile atop the stone wall, then formed a hand sign with his fingers. The weeds were instantly engulfed in flames and burned away.

“Do you have anything for dinner?”

“I have Hunger-Warding Pills.”

“Save those for when you run out of food. There’s spirit rice in the storehouse behind the house. Scoop out a bowl, and we’ll cook it.”

Inside the storehouse stood rows of jars as tall as a person’s waist.

When Lu Baishan removed the lid from one of them, a faint fragrance spread through the air. Inside were grains of rice with a lustrous sheen.

“Is this spirit rice?”

“Yes. It’s a variety called Qinghe Rice. There’s no need to wash it.”

Lu Baishan put water and spirit rice into a pot, covered it with the lid, then lightly rested his palm against the side.

A faint red glow spread from his fingertips. Before long, a rich, savory aroma rose from the pot.

Lu Baishan divided the cooked Qinghe Rice between two bowls and took out a small portion of salted spirit vegetables from the cupboard. That was their entire dinner.

Lee Hyun picked up a mouthful of rice with his chopsticks and put it into his mouth.

The grains were soft, yet had a pleasant springiness the more he chewed. A subtle sweetness spread across his tongue, and after he swallowed, a warm current slowly unfurled within his stomach. The hunger he had built up from spending the entire day moving around the spirit field quickly subsided.

‘This is good.’

He had only eaten a meal, yet he could feel the Primordial True Qi in his dantian increase ever so slightly.

“Eating spirit rice regularly should help with cultivation by itself.”

“This Qinghe Rice is only a Tier 1 mid grade spirit grain even if you rate it generously, so it will probably only have an effect during early Qi Refining.”

“Thank you, Senior Brother Lu.”

“It isn’t coming from me. The sect provides it, so there’s no need to feel indebted.”

...

For the next several days, Lee Hyun pulled weeds and cleared irrigation channels in Spirit Field No. 73.

At night and before dawn, he cultivated the Primordial One-Qi Art, and when the sun rose, he went out to the spirit field.

He scooped fallen leaves from the irrigation channels and dug out mud that blocked the flow of water. He pulled weeds growing between the Green Dew Grass and searched for traces left by spirit insects during the night, reporting them to Lu Baishan.

Lu Baishan barely spoke while they worked.

But when Lee Hyun stopped repeating the same mistakes and competently handled tasks even without being told, his attitude gradually began to change.

On the tenth day, Lu Baishan stopped Lee Hyun as he was about to pull another weed.

“Don’t pull that one.”

“It doesn’t look like Green Dew Grass.”

“It’s an Earth Vein Flower. It isn’t a spirit herb, but its roots slowly draw spiritual qi up from deep underground. Leaving a few around the edges of the spirit field benefits the Green Dew Grass as well.”

Lu Baishan pointed to the soil around its roots.

“A spirit-plant cultivator who can only distinguish weeds from spirit herbs is only half-qualified. Don’t just look at the trees. Look at the whole forest. You need to see the larger picture and understand what harms the spirit field and what helps the things growing within it.”

“I’ll remember that.”

After that day, Lu Baishan would occasionally explain things about spirit fields and spirit herbs while they worked.

One day, while Lee Hyun was organizing supplies in the storehouse, he found an old book. When he looked through it, it contained nothing more than basic knowledge about the cultivation world, but two characters caught his eye.

“Senior Brother Lu, are these two characters also read as ‘yeongsik’?”

“Which yeongsik do you mean?”

Lu Baishan looked at the section Lee Hyun had opened, then used a dry branch to write two terms on the ground.

Spirit plant.

Spirit sense.

“They are both read as yeongsik, but their meanings are different. Spirit plant is a broad term for plants that grow while containing spiritual qi. Spirit grain, spirit fruit, spirit trees, and spirit herbs all fall into that category.” [TL Note: In Korean, both 靈植 and 靈識 are pronounced yeongsik.]

Lu Baishan pointed to the second term.

“Spirit sense, on the other hand, is an old term for a cultivator’s ability to perceive their surroundings beyond the physical senses.”

“Is it no longer used?”

“You’ll often see it in ancient texts, but these days, most people call it divine sense.”

With the tip of the branch, Lu Baishan drew a long line between the two terms he had written.

“It is said that in the ancient era, heaven-and-earth spiritual qi was abundant. Rather than deliberately planting spirit herbs in fields and cultivating them, it was more common to gather heaven-and-earth spirit treasures from the mountains and wilderness. Because of that, the term spirit sense usually referred to a cultivator’s perception. But as heaven-and-earth spiritual qi gradually declined and naturally occurring spirit treasures became scarce, later generations began cultivating spirit herbs, spirit grain, and the like professionally. As the field of spirit plants grew in importance, cultivators began using the term divine sense instead of the older spirit sense for convenience.”

“Can cultivators in Qi Refining use divine sense as well?”

“Didn’t you develop a new sense when you entered Qi Refining? That is simply what we call divine sense. Of course, compared to the divine sense of a Foundation Establishment cultivator, what a Qi Refining cultivator possesses is little more than child’s play...”

“I see.”

“Language has a life of its own, just like spirit herbs. Is it not natural that it changes with the passage of time?”

...

Lee Hyun realized that Lu Baishan’s knowledge and experience with spirit plants far surpassed that of the ordinary Senior Brothers on Medicinal Field Peak.

Lu Baishan supervised not only Spirit Field No. 73 but also several smaller spirit fields nearby. Outer disciples who were unable to deal with spirit insects or plant diseases would often come to Lu Baishan for advice, and after hearing his explanations, every one of them would politely thank him before leaving.

Lu Baishan sometimes took Lee Hyun around the nearby spirit fields to show him the spirit plants commonly cultivated in the Outer Gate.

He held up a yellowing ear of grain.

“This is the Qinghe Rice we ate. It needs to be harvested once more than half the ear has turned yellow. That way, its spiritual qi remains intact.”

This time, he pointed to a grass with red leaves.

“This is Blood-Clotting Grass. It can be applied directly to wounds or used to make Blood-Staunching Powder. Its medicinal effect is weak, but it grows well and demand is high, so it is commonly cultivated in Outer Gate spirit fields.”

The more Lu Baishan explained, the more Lee Hyun realized that spirit plants differed from what he had imagined in many ways.

None of the spirit plants he had seen so far were varieties that needed to be grown for long periods. Some even took less than twenty days from sowing to harvest.

“Senior Brother Lu, if we leave these spirit plants unharvested and grow them longer, their medicinal potency should become stronger, right?”

“Not necessarily. Most of the varieties we grow have short lifespans. If you leave them too long, their medicinal potency disperses, and many die after producing seeds.”

Lu Baishan plucked one of the red leaves from the Blood-Clotting Grass and rubbed it between his fingers.

“This Blood-Clotting Grass reaches its peak medicinal potency in three months. Once it passes six months, the stem hardens and produces less medicinal juice. Grow it for a year, and instead of becoming more potent, it becomes useless.”

“Then are there no spirit plants that become more valuable the longer they age?”

“There are plenty whose medicinal potency grows stronger over the years. But valuable varieties are mainly handled by the Inner Gate.”

“Is there no way for me to obtain seeds like that?”

“Valuable varieties would be difficult, but if you only want seeds for low tier spirit plants that require many years of growth before becoming useful, you can easily find them at cultivator markets frequented by rogue cultivators. They’re simply unpopular.”

“Unpopular?”

“Yes. Qi Refining rogue cultivators who belong to neither sect nor clan have short lifespans and little leisure to think about future generations. Even if they do manage to raise a spirit plant for many years, they often lack the strength to protect their spirit field and end up having it taken from them. Unless a variety can help them earn spirit stones in a short period of time, there isn’t much demand for it.”

‘It isn’t as simple as I thought. Still, that means cultivator markets have seeds worth growing for a long time. I should visit one someday...’

...

One day, Lu Baishan handed Lee Hyun four yellowed, faded books.

The covers read 《Introductory Guide on Spirit Plants》, 《Tier-1 Spirit Herb Compendium》, 《Spirit Soil and Water Veins》, and 《Qinghe Valley Spirit Field Regulations》.

“These contain the basic knowledge you’ll need for spirit plants. I’m lending them to you, so make sure you don’t lose or damage them.”

“Thank you.”

From that day onward, Lee Hyun read the books whenever he had spare time between bouts of cultivation after work.

...

After that, the seasons changed several times.

In spring, new shoots of Green Dew Grass blanketed the spirit field in green, while summer brought rampant spirit insects. In autumn, the yellow ears of Qinghe Rice bent low, and in winter, thin layers of ice formed over the irrigation channels of Medicinal Field Peak.

Lee Hyun repeated much the same work every day.

At first, he often confused even Green Dew Grass with weeds, but after a year, he could tell whether a plant lacked spiritual qi merely by looking at the color of its leaves.

He also began learning basic techniques from Lu Baishan.

The first thing he learned was the Spirit Rain Art. The first cloud he managed to produce was closer to a wisp of mist hovering above his palm than an actual cloud. It released three drops of rain, then stopped.

Only after practicing every day for several months could he finally summon enough rain to wet a single furrow.

Next, he learned the Soil-Turning Art.

Turning the soil over gently was easy enough, but removing only weeds and stones without disturbing the roots of the spirit herbs was difficult. Once, he lost control of the force and uprooted ten Green Dew Grass plants at once, earning a scolding from Lu Baishan.

The third and fourth techniques he learned were the Yang Metal Art and the Germination Art.

The Yang Metal Art was the most difficult technique he had learned so far. At first, the silver needle flew no farther than the length of a finger before dispersing. Even after he began to get the hang of it, he frequently pierced Green Dew Grass leaves instead of spirit insects.

Although the Yang Metal Art was classified as a basic technique, killing only spirit insects without damaging the spirit herbs required extremely precise control.

In the end, Lee Hyun continued practicing the Yang Metal Art, but caught and disposed of spirit insects by hand.

At least the Germination Art was easier to learn than the Yang Metal Art.

When he converted his Primordial True Qi to the wood attribute, gathered it at his fingertips, and infused it into a seed, he could sense a faint vitality stirring within the hard shell. However, if he infused too much vitality, the sprout would swell abnormally and quickly rot.

It was only near the end of his second year that Lee Hyun could finally be said to have reached the Novice stage in all four techniques.

“Senior Brother Lu, do I lack talent when it comes to learning techniques?”

“Hmm? No. Among all the juniors I’ve seen, your comprehension of techniques is among the best. You handle them with the seasoned skill of an eighty-year-old rather than a twenty-one-year-old.”

‘...’

“But I heard these four techniques are the basics of spirit-plant cultivation, yet they’re extremely difficult.”

“Hmph. They’re only called basic because that makes things convenient for the people assigning the work. Do you think there’s anyone in all of Qinghe Valley who has reached Major Attainment in the Yang Metal Art or Germination Art? Simply having more spiritual power does not make someone automatically better at using techniques. What matters is comprehending the principles behind them.”

...

Lee Hyun continued cultivating steadily as well.

Progress with the Primordial One-Qi Art was slow, but Lee Hyun did not grow impatient. Once he became accustomed to cultivating, he could even absorb spiritual qi while walking through the fields.

After cultivating every single day without fail, he finally broke through the barrier to Qi Refining Stage 2 one winter, two and a half years after entering the sect.

“Finally, Qi Refining Stage 2!”

Lee Hyun felt immensely satisfied by the sensation of power surging through his entire body.

The Primordial True Qi in his dantian was incomparably more abundant than when he had first begun, and his divine sense had also grown somewhat stronger. Even with his eyes closed, he could sense the outlines of objects within a little over ten zhang (about 30 m).

...

Life in Spirit Field No. 73 was not bad.

Lu Baishan was taciturn but dependable, and Lee Hyun had grown accustomed to the work. Whenever the harvest was good, he also received a small number of additional contribution points.

It seemed he could simply spend a few more years learning about spirit plants and techniques, then leave the sect before anyone discovered that he did not age.

One month later.

Lee Hyun had summoned a cloud over the spirit field with the Spirit Rain Art, while Lu Baishan stood opposite him, checking whether the irrigation channel Lee Hyun had dug was deep enough.

Just then, the cry of a crane sounded above the spirit field.

‘Hmm?’

A paper crane appeared in the sky, circled once above the spirit field, then stopped in front of Lu Baishan. Light flowed from Lu Baishan’s identity token, and the paper crane unfolded by itself, transforming into a letter.

As Lu Baishan read through it, his expression gradually hardened.

“Senior Brother Lu, what happened?”

Chapter 8

Lu Baishan did not answer Lee Hyun's question and simply remained silent.

He seemed displeased with the contents of the letter and went back over it from the beginning, as though checking whether he had misread something.

A moment later, the letter flew through the air and stopped before Lee Hyun.

"Read it yourself."

Lee Hyun took the letter, and the words written at the very top caught his eye.

「By order of the Outer Gate Affairs Hall on the main peak, outer disciple Lee Hyun is hereby appointed field caretaker of Withering Yin Field No. 8 on Medicinal Field Peak...」

Below that, it even stated that Lee Hyun cultivated the Primordial One-Qi Art and had reached Qi Refining Stage 2.

'Withering Yin Field?'

He had never heard the name before.

Being entrusted with a new spirit field was practically a promotion. Until now, Lee Hyun had merely been an assistant caretaker helping Lu Baishan. If he became the field caretaker of his own spirit field, there was a good chance the contribution points he received each month would increase as well.

But Lu Baishan's reaction was strange. He did not merely look like someone upset at losing a Junior Brother who helped lighten his workload.

"So the inevitable has finally happened."

"Is there something wrong with Withering Yin Field?"

Lu Baishan looked at Lee Hyun sympathetically.

"Do you remember me cursing Steward Wang when you first said you'd learned the Primordial One-Qi Art?"

"I... don't."

"Is that so? I suppose I only cursed him in my head."

Lee Hyun waited for Lu Baishan to continue.

"Withering Yin Field is a special spirit field where yin-aspected spirit herbs and highly poisonous medicinal herbs are grown. It's located in a gloomy valley where sunlight never reaches. As the spirit herbs there grow, they absorb the vitality around them and release foul toxic qi. Because of that, working there for too long eats away at your lifespan and easily damages your body."

Lee Hyun's eyes widened slightly.

'It eats away at your lifespan?'

"Don't tell me... only disciples who cultivate the Primordial One-Qi Art are assigned to Withering Yin Field?"

"For the most part. It's one of Qinghe Valley's less savory customs. Ordinary outer disciples without exceptional talent are rotated through Withering Yin Field. You had a triple spiritual root, didn't you? Your aptitude isn't bad, but you're older than your fellow disciples, so I suppose that's why they chose you."

"Why does cultivating the Primordial One-Qi Art matter?"

"To work in Withering Yin Field, you need to be able to use techniques of several different attributes. For example, you need a wind-aspected technique to breathe safely, and a fire-aspected technique to drive the yin qi out of your body."

Lu Baishan gave a bitter smile.

"The Primordial One-Qi Art is the only cultivation art that lets an outer disciple who has only recently joined the sect use techniques of multiple attributes. There are inner disciples who can handle several attributes without cultivating the Primordial One-Qi Art, thanks to unusual constitutions or exceptional magic tools, but those disciples are valuable talents the sect intends to nurture. They would never send them to Withering Yin Field to lose years of their lives."

"......."

"Don't be too discouraged. I worked in Withering Yin Field when I was young too."

Lee Hyun looked at Lu Baishan's graying hair.

"No disciple is assigned to Withering Yin Field for more than five years. Even if you follow every rule and minimize the damage to your essence, qi and spirit, five years there will still cost you roughly fifteen years of lifespan."

"Fifteen years...."

"In exchange, the spirit stones and contribution points paid each month are three times what an ordinary spirit-plant cultivator receives. You also get one Essence-Nourishing Pill each season, and you can learn the basic techniques you need without spending contribution points. You're essentially trading away your lifespan for resources."

'Selling my lifespan to buy resources... But I don't age anyway, do I?'

Lee Hyun had lived for nearly forty years since his transmigration, yet neither his appearance nor even his bone age had changed. That meant the ordinary passage of time had no effect on him.

But he had no way of knowing whether Withering Yin Field would truly have no effect on him.

'Is my constitution immune even to having my lifespan eroded by toxic qi...?'

He should be able to get some idea after working in Withering Yin Field for just a day. If something happened to his body, he could look for another solution then.

In fact, there would be a problem even if Withering Yin Field's toxic qi did not affect him.

If he worked there for five years without his appearance changing at all, that in itself would become a serious problem.

The other disciples were said to lose fifteen years of lifespan. If he alone did not age in the slightest, wouldn't that look strange to anyone?

If that happened, the sect would check Lee Hyun's bone age again and discover that he did not age. Then Lee Hyun would never be allowed to leave the sect.

But realistically, refusing the sect's order to take up his post at Withering Yin Field was impossible as well. At only Qi Refining Stage 2, he had no idea what price he would pay for defying the sect's command.

'For now, I'd better accept the appointment and see how things go. And I'll have to leave Qinghe Valley before the five years are up.'

It might even turn out to be a blessing in disguise. If he received three times the spirit stones and contribution points, he could obtain the cultivation arts and items he needed much faster.

Lee Hyun composed his expression and answered in a solemn voice.

"If that truly is the sect's will... I will gladly obey."

A trace of guilt and approval flickered through Lu Baishan's eyes.

"Good. Since the compensation is triple the usual amount, it isn't entirely hopeless. If you're lucky, those rewards might even shorten your path to Foundation Establishment."

"I'm really fine."

"That's only because you don't know what awaits you yet. Rest for a while."

Lu Baishan took the letter back from Lee Hyun's hand.

...

Lu Baishan returned from the direction of the main peak, opened his storage pouch, and took out a bundle of manuals.

"I told you that field caretakers of Withering Yin Field receive several benefits. This is one of them."

The covers of the manuals Lu Baishan had taken out were titled 《Cleansing Art》, 《Air-Clearing Art》, 《Breath-Sealing Art》, 《Fire-Kindling Art》, 《Qi Sphere Barrier》, 《Detoxification Art》, 《Poison-Discerning Art》, and 《Faint Light Art》.

They were all thin manuals, but there were eight of them in total.

"Normally, you'd have to spend contribution points to borrow these techniques from the Scripture Pavilion. They're issued for free because they're essential while working in Withering Yin Field."

"Do I have to learn all of them?"

"You won't last long there if you don't."

Lu Baishan opened the manual at the top of the pile.

"The Cleansing Art removes dust and medicinal powder from your body and clothes. They don't give it to you merely for convenience. If even a little poisonous powder from Withering Yin Field remains on your clothes, it can damage your skin overnight."

He picked up the second manual.

"The Air-Clearing Art pushes away foul air and creates breathable air around you for a while. The Breath-Sealing Art is a method of sustaining your body with spiritual power while you stop breathing."

"How long would I be able to hold my breath?"

"At your realm, about half a shichen (about one hour)."

The Fire-Kindling Art was a technique that produced a small flame at the fingertips. It was not powerful enough to use for attacking, but it was useful for dispelling damp yin qi or cooking spirit rice.

The Qi Sphere Barrier was a defensive technique that formed a thin barrier around the body, and disciples working in Withering Yin Field had to use it to keep out toxic qi.

The Detoxification Art was a qi-circulation method that gathered toxic qi that had entered the body into one place before expelling it, while the Poison-Discerning Art was a technique for roughly identifying the nature of poison mixed into water, soil, air, and the like.

"The Faint Light Art must be for use in the dark."

"That's right. Withering Yin Field receives almost no sunlight even at midday. At night, it's so dark you can't see your fingers in front of your face."

Lee Hyun placed the manuals inside his storage pouch.

"Did you learn all these techniques as well, Senior Brother Lu?"

"Of course. Quite a few of these techniques are commonly learned even by cultivators who have never worked in Withering Yin Field. The Cleansing Art in particular is popular with practically every cultivator."

"But there's no way I can learn all eight in a single day."

"For now, inserting a low-grade spirit stone into Withering Yin Field's access token will activate a formation that keeps out the toxic qi, so you shouldn't have any immediate problems. Practice one technique at a time each day inside the living quarters. The Breath-Sealing Art and Air-Clearing Art are simple and useful, so learn those first."

Lu Baishan led Lee Hyun to the hanging scrolls on the wall.

When he lifted one of the scrolls away, several old paintings were revealed behind it. He selected three of them.

"If it's Withering Yin Field No. 8... it's probably growing these three varieties."

The first painting depicted a grotesque flower with ivory-colored petals blooming from a pitch-black stem. A hazy powder floated around the stamens, while its roots were knobby like the joints of an animal's bones.

"This is the Bone-Rot Flower. Its pollen slowly dissolves bone. But once its toxicity is removed and it's refined, it becomes the main ingredient in Bone-Forging Powder. Body refiners use it to temper their bones or heal broken ones."

"A flower that damages bones is used to make medicine that heals them?"

"I don't know enough about alchemy to explain the exact principles myself. But the sect's alchemists often say there's only a fine line between poison and medicine. I suppose they remove the toxicity and leave only the medicinal potency behind."

The second painting showed an orchid with long, broad leaves spreading in every direction. The veins running through the leaves were a deep purple like blood vessels, and strands of purple mist flowed from the flower bud like threads.

"The Purple Poison Orchid is the most troublesome fellow of the three. Most of the mist you'll see in Withering Yin Field comes from these plants. Their leaves and stems constantly release purple toxic qi. When that toxic qi touches the body, it drains vital essence and gradually reduces one's lifespan. However, Purple Venom Extract refined from this toxic qi is indispensable as the main ingredient of Poison-Warding Pills, which increase resistance to poison."

"Can cultivators be poisoned too? I thought poison was something only used in the mundane world."

"Naturally, ordinary poisons from the mundane world can be forced out with spiritual power alone. But who says cultivators can't use poison themselves? They're rare, but there are certainly sects and cultivation systems that specialize in poison. The poisons used by cultivators are incomparably more dangerous than anything found in the mundane world."

The final painting showed a spirit herb whose dark blue-green leaves grew in a circular cluster. The leaves were thin and long, and pale blue droplets of dew clung to each tip. Among the roots exposed above the ground, faint shadows resembling human faces seemed to flicker.

"This is Yin Soul Grass. It's the main ingredient in Spirit-Calming Pills. A Spirit-Calming Pill is a valuable medicine used when a cultivator suffers from a heart demon during cultivation or begins showing signs of qi deviation. On top of that, it has a slight effect on tempering the primordial spirit and divine sense, so it's highly sought after."

"Can I really grow such extraordinary spirit herbs? Just hearing about them makes them sound difficult to cultivate."

"It's the opposite."

Lee Hyun blinked at Lu Baishan's answer.

"Most of the spirit plants in Withering Yin Field are easy to grow. As long as the yin qi is dense and the environment is damp, they'll thrive on their own. Their poison is so strong that most spirit insects avoid them, and they even drain the vitality from the weeds around them, so there's almost never any need to weed."

"Then what does the field caretaker actually do?"

"Check the formation, water them, and harvest them when the time comes. Occasionally, you'll move them around so the spirit plants don't steal each other's vitality. Compared to an ordinary spirit field, it's so easy even a child could do it."

Lu Baishan fell silent for a moment.

"The problem is that people grow old and sick while doing such easy work."

Lee Hyun looked at the Bone-Rot Flower in the painting.

"When do I have to leave?"

"Tomorrow at noon. Someone from the Outer Gate Affairs Hall will come to guide you."

Lu Baishan hesitated before adding,

"Don't get greedy in Withering Yin Field. Just because they give you three times the contribution points doesn't mean you need to do three times the work. If anything at all feels wrong with your body, stop and rest immediately."

"I'll remember that."

"And...."

After considering it for a moment, Lu Baishan sent Lee Hyun a voice transmission.

[The spirit plants grown in Withering Yin Field No. 8 have the characteristics you were looking for before. All three varieties become more valuable the longer they're allowed to mature. If there's still some surplus after you've met the harvest quota set by the sect, leave a portion unharvested and keep growing them. When you eventually leave, secretly set some aside. If you get a chance to visit a cultivator market some distance from the sect, you should be able to sell them for a fair number of spirit stones.]

'...!'

"Thank you, Senior Brother Lu!"

"Enough. Go pack your things."

...

Lee Hyun did not have much to pack.

Once he put his clothes, bedding, and a few small farming tools into his storage pouch, his preparations were quickly finished.

At noon the next day, a man dispatched from the Outer Gate Affairs Hall arrived at Spirit Field No. 73.

His name was Chen Jiuming, and he was an outer disciple at Qi Refining Stage 6.

"Are you Junior Brother Lee Hyun?"

"Yes."

"I'll guide you to Withering Yin Field. It's a long way, so let's leave at once."

Lee Hyun gave Lu Baishan one final farewell.

"Thank you for everything you've taught me."

"You're not going off to die. What's with the final farewell?"

Lu Baishan spoke gruffly.

Lee Hyun bowed deeply to Lu Baishan, then followed Chen Jiuming down the mountain.

After descending an unfamiliar mountain path for quite some time, the forest gradually grew denser.

At first, sunlight filtered through the branches, but the farther they descended into the valley, the more twisted the trees became and the more their leaves turned black. Not even the cries of birds or insects could be heard.

Before long, they reached a dark valley where almost no sunlight penetrated.

The entire valley was blanketed in thick, murky mist faintly tinged with purple.

When Lee Hyun breathed in, the tip of his nose stung and his chest seemed to tighten.

"This is Withering Yin Field."

Chen Jiuming, who had been guiding him, stopped outside the mist and went no farther.

"The field caretaker's living quarters are farther inside. You can get the formation's access token from your predecessor."

"I have to go in alone?"

"I'm not a field caretaker for Withering Yin Field, am I?"

Chen Jiuming looked as though he could not understand why Lee Hyun would ask something so obvious.

Just then, someone staggered out of an old hut deeper in the valley.

"Hah, hah... A replacement... Has my replacement come?"

Lee Hyun could hardly believe his eyes.

More than half the man's hair had gone white, and deep wrinkles were carved into his face. His skin was pallid, and his lips had a faint purple tint.

"I'm saved. Finally, I'm saved...!"

He seized Lee Hyun's hand. His hand was as cold as ice.

"Junior Brother, listen carefully. When you water those cursed Bone-Rot Flowers, never breathe in. If the Purple Poison Orchids turn black, don't go near them. Use the Air-Clearing Art first. If you spend more than two shíchen in the field in a single day, you'll suffer the agony of your bones rotting."

The man pulled a black iron token from inside his clothes and pressed it into Lee Hyun's hand.

"This is the formation's access token. At least the toxic qi doesn't enter the hut. When you're done working, you must return inside, cleanse yourself with the Cleansing Art, and use the Detoxification Art three times!"

"Senior Brother, how many years have you worked here?"

"Four years and eleven months."

Tears welled at the corners of the man's eyes.

"They said they'd give me extra contribution points if I lasted one more month, so I tried to hold out, but I just can't do it anymore. What good are contribution points if I don't live to use them!"

As soon as he finished speaking, he returned to the hut, grabbed his bundle of belongings, and came back out.

Chen Jiuming spoke.

"Junior Brother Wen, the handover...."

"I wrote everything down in the ledger on the table inside the hut!"

The man hurried up the mountain path without once looking back.

The sight of him channeling spiritual power into his legs and sprinting away showed just how desperate he was.

Lee Hyun watched his retreating figure and asked,

"Is he quite old?"

"You mean Junior Brother Wen Gang?"

Chen Jiuming tilted his head.

"He should be thirty-six this year."

"......."

"Well then, take care."

Chen Jiuming also hurried away as though fleeing.

Chapter 9

Left alone in the blink of an eye, Lee Hyun stood there in a daze.

After a moment, he came to his senses and looked at the iron token in his hand.

The front was engraved with the words "No. 8", while a fragment of a low-grade spirit stone was embedded in the back. A little spiritual qi still remained within the spirit stone.

When Lee Hyun held the access token and activated the formation with his divine sense, the token began to glow faintly.

Hummm–

An invisible force pushed the mist away from Lee Hyun's body in a circle.

The mist retreated about one zhang (about 3 m), revealing a narrow path leading to the cabin. Bone-Rot Flowers with ivory blossoms grew to the left of the path, while Purple Poison Orchids drooped their violet leaves on the right. In the shaded spirit field at the very back, dark blue-black Yin Soul Grass grew thickly.

Lee Hyun carefully stepped inside.

A faint barrier surrounded the cabin. When he brought the access token close, the barrier parted like rippling water.

Once inside, Lee Hyun immediately shut the door and checked the windows as well.

Unlike outside, the air inside the cabin was fairly clean. Formation flags had been planted throughout the walls and floor, and in one corner of the room sat a formation plate fitted with a low-grade spirit stone.

The low-grade spirit stone had lost nearly half its glow. It seemed to be what maintained the cabin's formation.

A ledger and a map of the Withering Yin Field lay on the table.

Lee Hyun opened the ledger first.

It listed the dates and amounts for watering, the harvest times, and even when the spirit stones powering the formations had to be replaced.

When he opened the drawer beneath the table, he found three wooden boxes. They were labeled "Yin-Gathering Formation", "Poison-Warding Formation", and "Emergency Use", respectively, and inside them were neatly arranged low-grade spirit stones meant for work in the Withering Yin Field.

At the beginning of every month, the Outer Gate Affairs Hall issued eight low-grade spirit stones. Five were used to maintain the formations around the spirit field and cabin, while the remaining three served as the monthly stipend for the disciple managing the Withering Yin Field.

Lee Hyun turned to the next page of the ledger. It contained instructions on managing the spirit field.

The Bone-Rot Flowers and Yin Soul Grass only needed the Spirit Rain Art once every two days. The Purple Poison Orchids had to be watered once every three days, and if their roots grew within three ja (about 90 cm) of one another, they had to be transplanted before they began stealing each other's life force.

The Yin-Gathering Formation at the center of the spirit field had to be activated every ten days. By inserting one low-grade spirit stone and running the formation for a full day, the yin qi scattered throughout the valley would gather in the spirit field.

Any spirit insects that appeared had to be caught personally, though the ledger stated that they were rarely seen in the Withering Yin Field.

The harvesting methods were recorded as well.

Every three months, the fully bloomed Bone-Rot Flowers were cut off along with their stems. If the flower was left intact on one plant out of every ten, white seedpods resembling fragments of bone would form where the petals had fallen. Once the seedpods split open, black seeds emerged from within, and those only needed to be buried one knuckle deep.

Every four months, the fully grown leaves of the Yin Soul Grass were harvested by cutting them at the base. The seeds that formed at the tips of old stalks were as light as dust, so they had to be scattered over damp soil on a windless day and gently pressed down with the palm.

Once every six months, the thickened roots of the Purple Poison Orchids were dug up. Finger-sized young bulbs could be separated from them and replanted three knuckles deep, where they would grow into new Purple Poison Orchids.

'It really is easy, at least.'

The problem was going outside the cabin.

From the ledger, Lee Hyun learned that the low-grade spirit stone inserted into the access token had to be paid for out of his own pocket.

If he failed to learn the basic techniques and relied on the access token while tending the spirit field, powering the token would cost one low-grade spirit stone every month. In other words, unless he learned the basic techniques quickly, his monthly stipend would be reduced by a third.

'First I need to find out whether the toxic qi in the Withering Yin Field actually reduces my lifespan. If it doesn't, there's no reason to waste a low-grade spirit stone.'

'If my lifespan doesn't decrease, I might not need the access token or even the basic techniques. But basic techniques are useful for plenty of things besides working in the Withering Yin Field, so I should learn them anyway...'

Checking the dates Senior Brother Wen Gang had written at the end of the ledger, Lee Hyun saw that all three spirit plants had last been watered today.

He only needed to go out two days later to use the Spirit Rain Art on the Bone-Rot Flowers and Yin Soul Grass, so until then, he decided to first learn the Air-Clearing Art, Breath-Sealing Art, and Qi Sphere Barrier.

...

After spending two full days inside the cabin practicing nothing but techniques, Lee Hyun became capable of using all three at a very rudimentary level.

Lee Hyun erected the Qi Sphere Barrier and activated the Breath-Sealing Art before heading out into the field.

Ssssh–

Murky energy laden with toxic qi crept up along the barrier.

Purple mist clung to the surface of the Qi Sphere Barrier as though gnawing away at it. Perhaps because his proficiency was still low, his spiritual power drained faster than expected.

Lee Hyun hurriedly used the Spirit Rain Art to water the Bone-Rot Flowers and Yin Soul Grass, then returned to the cabin.

There was nothing wrong with his body.

...

The third day.

Today, he had to use the Spirit Rain Art on the Purple Poison Orchids. This time, Lee Hyun dispelled the Qi Sphere Barrier from just one arm.

Chilly yin energy passed through his skin and seeped into his flesh. It felt as though an invisible hand inside his body were slowly tugging at something warm.

Lee Hyun had been slightly afraid that his agelessness might not protect him from such a strange force. Yet even after waiting, he felt no change in his body.

The chilly yin energy tried to draw out Lee Hyun's life force, but it dispersed uselessly, as though there were simply nothing there for it to pull on.

"Hmm... So I really am immune?"

Lee Hyun completely dispelled the Qi Sphere Barrier. Purple fumes entered through his nose and mouth and seeped deep into his lungs.

Ten breaths.

Twenty.

Thirty.

Lee Hyun's body showed no reaction at all.

He circulated his spiritual power and tried forcing the toxic qi out of his lungs. When Lee Hyun exhaled deeply, a whitish mist streamed from his mouth.

Having gained a little confidence, he walked farther into the field.

He crouched in front of a Bone-Rot Flower, brought his face close to its petals, and carefully inhaled.

"Sssniff–"

His lungs felt slightly ticklish.

"Yaaawn...."

Lee Hyun yawned so widely that his jaw nearly popped.

"......."

He felt none of the pain of his bones rotting. Instead, it felt pleasantly cool, like stepping into the shade on a sweltering summer day.

"So to me, this is basically just a cool, comfortable farm...."

After finishing his work and returning to the cabin, Lee Hyun carefully examined himself for any possible side effects.

He could find no sign that his life force or vital essence had diminished. His head merely felt a little heavy, and drowsiness washed over him, perhaps because he had inhaled too much of the mist.

Only then did Lee Hyun realize there had been a blind spot in his thinking.

'Damn, I let my guard down! Come to think of it, this stuff doesn't just eat away at lifespan, does it? Even if I don't age, that doesn't mean I'm immune to poison itself...'

...

Several days later, Lee Hyun confirmed that his body had suffered no damage.

He was relieved, but decided to remain more cautious from then on. In the cultivation world, a moment of carelessness could plunge him into grave danger.

One year later.

Lee Hyun had completely adapted to life in the Withering Yin Field.

At the prescribed intervals, he used the Spirit Rain Art and activated the formations. Whenever the spirit plants were ready for harvest, he cut them, placed them in wooden boxes, and replanted the seeds he had set aside.

The work took less than one shichen (two hours) a day.

Hardly any weeds grew, and whether because they could not withstand the toxic qi or simply disliked the three spirit plants, spirit insects rarely appeared.

Compared to when he had grown Green Dew Grass under Senior Brother Lu Baishan, the work was extremely easygoing.

He spent the rest of his time learning techniques and cultivating.

By now, a single gesture with the Cleansing Art could remove poisonous powder from his clothes and body. The flame created by his Fire-Kindling Art had grown to the size of a torch, and he could even use the Air-Clearing Art to replace the air inside the cabin.

He also deliberately practiced the Qi Sphere Barrier and Detoxification Art every day.

...

One day, an inspector from the Outer Gate Affairs Hall came to visit. There was no problem with his work. It was merely a routine inspection required by the rules.

"Junior Brother Lee, you still look remarkably healthy even after coming to the Withering Yin Field."

Chen Jiuming spoke while examining Lee Hyun's face.

"I've followed the rules the Senior Brothers taught me to the letter."

"Even so, most people start looking pale and losing some of their hair after about a year...."

"I suppose I've always had a strong constitution."

"How enviable."

Chen Jiuming brushed it off without much thought, but Lee Hyun could not laugh.

From that day onward, he began growing a beard and mixed a tiny amount of ash from the dried grass left in the hearth with water, dabbing it around his eyes and cheeks.

With his skin looking duller and shadows beneath his eyes, he appeared several years older than before.

However, it was not a fundamental solution.

A year had passed since he came to the Withering Yin Field, yet his bone age was still nineteen. If he still looked exactly the same after spending another four years here, even the dullest person would have no choice but to find it strange.

If Senior Brother Chen Jiuming grew suspicious and brought some means of checking his lifespan, Lee Hyun would be in serious trouble.

'There's no way I can hide this for five years. I need to leave the sect as soon as possible!'

Fortunately, he had gained plenty as well.

Every month, he received three low-grade spirit stones and thirty contribution points. When the harvest was good, he received additional contribution points on top of that.

Lee Hyun carefully saved every spirit stone he received as his share and used contribution points to cover his living necessities.

Little by little, he began preparing to leave Qinghe Valley.

...

Before he knew it, a year and a half had passed since he transferred to the Withering Yin Field, and late summer had arrived.

At the foot of a mountain several li (a few kilometers) from the valley where the Withering Yin Field lay, there was a small cave that had once been occupied by a bear long ago.

It lay far from any traveled path, and there was nothing of value nearby, so cultivators had no reason to visit.

Lee Hyun sat deep inside the cave, moving his brush across the page.

Across from him, Wang Shao had a book spread open before him and was frantically copying down its contents.

"Brother, you looked so honest. I never dreamed you'd be the one to suggest something like this first...!"

Wang Shao spoke in a low voice.

The boy who had once been sixteen was now a solidly built young man. A sword hung at his waist, and a shallow scar had appeared above his right eyebrow.

"You have to do whatever you can to survive in the cultivation world. How are you supposed to get ahead if you have the same advantages as everyone else?"

"That's true. But are we really going to be all right?"

Wang Shao glanced uneasily toward the cave entrance.

"Who pays much attention to outer disciples in early Qi Refining? As long as the two of us keep quiet, no one will ever know."

Books borrowed from the Scripture Pavilion were piled in front of them.

Qinghe Valley allowed disciples to take basic cultivation arts and technique manuals out of the pavilion so they could practice them at their residences whenever they had spare time.

Even cultivators did not use jade slips exclusively when recording or reading information.

From mid Qi Refining onward, cultivators often read jade slips with their divine sense, but disciples in early Qi Refining had divine senses too weak for that, so they frequently relied on ordinary books. Unlike jade slips, however, the contents of a book did not instantly enter one's mind after a single reading.

The Scripture Pavilion knew this as well, so cultivation art and technique manuals could be checked out for periods ranging from as little as fifteen days to as long as two months.

However, showing a borrowed book to another disciple or copying its contents and passing them on was naturally forbidden.

Even if these were not core inheritances, there was no chance the sect would allow disciples to privately transmit teachings without paying contribution points.

In other words, what Lee Hyun and Wang Shao were doing right now violated the sect rules!

After discussing it between themselves, they had divided up the techniques they needed, borrowed different manuals, and copied each other's books somewhere no one could see them.

Over the past six months, the two of them had copied several manuals using the same method.

Since Lee Hyun had been the one to make this risky proposal, he paid more of the contribution points than Wang Shao. Managing the Withering Yin Field had left him with far more contribution points to spare.

The manuals Lee Hyun had spent contribution points to borrow were The Three Protective Arts, Earth Escape Art, Spirit-Concealing & Aura-Concealing Art, The Six Arts of Perception, and Five-Element Fundamentals.

The Three Protective Arts contained the Spirit Light Shield, which formed a shield from spiritual power; the Earth Armor Art, which covered the entire body in earthen armor; and the Flowing Water Veil, which deflected attacks with a curtain of water.

The Earth Escape Art was a technique for moving through soil. Because his realm was still low, he could not pass through solid rock or ground covered by formations, and without sufficient proficiency there was also the danger of losing his sense of direction underground or suffocating.

The Spirit-Concealing & Aura-Concealing Art contained the Aura-Concealing Art, which concealed fluctuations in one's spiritual power, and the Spirit-Concealing Art, which made one's realm appear lower than it truly was. At first glance, the two produced similar effects, but the details of how they functioned were different.

The Six Arts of Perception was a manual compiling the Farsight Art, which allowed one to see far into the distance; the Keen Hearing Art, which amplified faint sounds; the Night Vision Art, which allowed one to see in darkness; the Scent-Tracking Art, which distinguished faint smells; the Aura-Reading Art, which observed the flow of qi; and the Ground-Sense Art, which detected nearby movement through vibrations in the earth.

Five-Element Fundamentals contained attack techniques commonly used throughout the cultivation world, such as the Fireball Art, Water Arrow Art, Metal Blade Art, Earth Spike Art, and Wood Binding Art.

Wang Shao, on the other hand, had borrowed Lightness Step Essentials, Azure Steel Sword Art, and Introductory Guide on Telekinesis and Sword Control.

Lightness Step Essentials contained the Lightness Art, which made the body lighter, and the Distance-Shrinking Step, which allowed rapid movement over short distances.

Azure Steel Sword Art was the basic sword art most commonly practiced by outer sword cultivators, while Introductory Guide on Telekinesis and Sword Control began with the Telekinesis Art, which used spiritual power to pull or push objects, and went on to cover the fundamentals of the Sword Control Art for controlling flying swords.

These techniques could all be learned from early Qi Refining onward. None could be called particularly exceptional, but their principles were simple and their fundamentals solid, making them useful foundations for learning better techniques later on.

In particular, the Earth Escape Art, Spirit-Concealing & Aura-Concealing Art, and Lightness Step Essentials were the techniques he most needed to learn first if he wanted to evade pursuit after leaving the sect.

...

After copying the final sentence, Lee Hyun set down his brush.

"Done."

He let the ink dry, then folded the copied pages one by one.

"This way, we've managed to learn all these techniques while spending only half the contribution points."

"As long as we don't get caught."

"If we do, let's say you were the one who suggested it first."

"Brother!"

Wang Shao looked utterly wronged.

"I'm joking."

Lee Hyun handed the book back to Wang Shao.

Wang Shao, having also finished copying, pushed his copies of Earth Escape Art and Spirit-Concealing & Aura-Concealing Art toward Lee Hyun.

"Remember this. Once you've memorized the copies, burn them until there's no trace left."

"Of course. Brother, are you really going to leave the sect?"

Chapter 10

“Yeah.”

Lee Hyun gazed outside the cave for a moment.

“The dangers of the Withering Yin Field are worse than people realize. I only understood that after working there myself. I can endure it for now, but if I stay there much longer, my immortal path will be cut off.”

Lee Hyun had made up a vague excuse for why he was leaving, but in a sense, he was also telling the truth.

If he remained in the Withering Yin Field too long, his secret would eventually be exposed. If that happened, it would not just be his immortal path that was cut short, but his life as well.

“What about asking the Outer Gate Affairs Hall for another assignment?”

“I heard they almost never reassign a disciple once they’ve been sent to the Withering Yin Field. Besides, I look perfectly fine, so they have no reason to transfer me.”

“Even so, disciples who desert the sect are treated as traitors.”

“A traitor? That’s overstating it. A single early Qi Refining disciple like me just isn’t important enough to warrant that. I haven’t stolen any treasures from the sect or harmed a fellow disciple. At most, they’ll send a few outer disciples to check my whereabouts. If I leave behind convincing signs of my death, they won’t have any reason to investigate further.”

“Do you really think so? I’m worried cultivators from the Law Enforcement Hall might come after you and kill you, Brother.”

“Think about it. Plenty of people will chase down someone who owes them money, but how many will go chasing after someone who made them money just to repay the favor? I’ve faithfully carried out every task the sect assigned me. The low-grade spirit stones and contribution points Qinghe Valley gives its outer disciples are only a portion of the value it gets from them in return. It might be different if I were an inner disciple, but....”

Wang Shao started to object, then closed his mouth. Lee Hyun’s words sounded convincing. Perhaps those extra few years really did make a difference. Lee Hyun understood the ways of the world far better than he did.

“Then where are you planning to go?”

“I haven’t decided yet. Somewhere far away from Qinghe Valley.”

Wang Shao thought for a moment.

“I think it would be best if you left the Great Yan Kingdom entirely. Wouldn’t it be safer to pass through the Anling Kingdom to the south and continue all the way to the Yunze Kingdom? I heard at the Spirit Beast Garden that Yunze Kingdom has very few spirit veins, so there are almost no major cultivation forces there. Instead, there are many rogue cultivators.”

“Yunze Kingdom....”

“I also heard there are several cultivator markets where rogue cultivators trade spirit plants, pills, talismans, magic tools, and the like. If you intend to keep cultivating after leaving the sect, wouldn’t somewhere like that be better?”

“Thanks. I’ll keep it in mind.”

Wang Shao looked at Lee Hyun for a moment, then took a small wooden box from inside his robes.

“Take this.”

Inside the wooden box were three black iron spikes, each about the length of a finger. Fine formation patterns had been engraved across their surfaces.

“What are these?”

“Spirit-Breaking Nails. I received them for completing a small task. They barely even qualify as magic tools, but if you infuse them with spiritual power and throw them, they pack far more force than a mortal’s crossbow. They should even be able to pierce the body-protecting spirit light of a Qi Refining Stage 2 cultivator.”

“Shouldn’t you keep them for yourself?”

“I intend to become a sword cultivator. I have no need for hidden weapons like these.”

Wang Shao said that, but his gaze lingered on the wooden box. They were clearly something he treasured.

“It’s fine. You keep them.”

“Are you sure?”

“I have far more means at my disposal than you think. How could I leave while owing my younger brother a debt?”

“If taking all three makes you uncomfortable, then at least take one.”

Wang Shao took a Spirit-Breaking Nail from the box and forcibly pressed it into Lee Hyun’s hand.

“It’s best if you never have occasion to use something like this, but if the day comes when you need it and don’t have it, you’ll regret it.”

“...You’re right. Then I’ll take just one.”

Wang Shao returned the wooden box containing the remaining two Spirit-Breaking Nails to his robes.

Lee Hyun took out a small bottle and handed it to Wang Shao.

“There are three Essence-Nourishing Pills in here from the allotment I received as a Withering Yin Field caretaker. Take one if you need to treat your meridians, or if your meridians are injured while cultivating the Metal Edge Art.”

“Are you really allowed to give these to me?”

“They were compensation for my work at the Withering Yin Field, so they belong to me. What I do with them is my choice. I still have several Essence-Nourishing Pills left, so don’t worry. Consider this payment for the Spirit-Breaking Nail.”

Wang Shao carefully placed the bottle into his storage pouch.

“Thank you. I wish you well, Brother.”

“You take care too.”

The two of them left the cave.

After walking a few steps, Wang Shao turned back.

“If you change your mind, please tell me anytime. I might be able to ask a Steward I know for help.”

“Got it.”

Lee Hyun carefully checked whether anyone was nearby, then concealed himself and watched Wang Shao disappear beyond the mountain path.

Wang Shao was the first fellow Lee Hyun could truly call a friend since entering Qinghe Valley. But he would probably never see him again.

That was why Lee Hyun had accepted only one of the Spirit-Breaking Nails Wang Shao offered and given him Essence-Nourishing Pills in return. He did not want to leave while owing him a debt.

...

After returning to the hut at Withering Yin Field No. 8, Lee Hyun lay down and cultivated the Primordial One-Qi Art while lost in thought.

Now that he had decided to leave Qinghe Valley, he began considering what he would need, one thing at a time.

The first was food.

People of the mundane world regarded cultivators as beings akin to immortals and assumed they had no need to rely on food.

But Qi Refining cultivators were not nearly that extraordinary. Even Foundation Establishment cultivators, let alone those in Qi Refining, could not completely abstain from food. A cultivator had to at least form a golden core before they could free themselves from dependence on food.

Of course, that did not mean Qi Refining and Foundation Establishment cultivators ate just anything. Relying on food from the mundane world caused turbid qi to accumulate, which interfered with cultivation, so they ate food containing spiritual qi whenever possible.

For the time being, Lee Hyun had around two hundred Hunger-Warding Pills. He had accumulated them by saving the pills issued by the sect while eating Qinghe Rice with Senior Brother Lu instead.

There were things in the mundane world that were also called Hunger-Warding Pills, but the ones issued by the sect were made by alchemically refining Qinghe Rice together with several spirit herbs, making them incomparably more precious than their mundane counterparts.

If Lee Hyun wanted to maximize his cultivation speed, refining ten Hunger-Warding Pills a day would not be impossible, but if he only wanted to stave off hunger, he needed to refine just one every two days.

Lee Hyun also had twenty jin (about 12 kg) of Qinghe Rice in his storage pouch. This was thanks to the generous Qinghe Rice allotment given to Withering Yin Field caretakers. One jin of Qinghe Rice, once cooked, was enough to stave off hunger for five days.

‘So if I’m only thinking about keeping myself fed... the Hunger-Warding Pills will last four hundred days, and if I include the Qinghe Rice, I have enough for five hundred days. I don’t need to worry about food anytime soon.’

‘Besides, unlike other cultivators, eating food from the mundane world shouldn’t matter much to me. Even if turbid qi accumulates and slows my cultivation, I’m not racing against my lifespan.’

The second was seeds.

After leaving the sect, he planned to dig a tunnel, hide away inside it, and grow various spirit plants to pass the time.

The problem was that he had no way to predict which spirit plants would thrive in the environment of an underground tunnel. For that reason, Lee Hyun needed to take seeds from as many varieties of spirit plants as possible.

Fortunately, after working with Senior Brother Lu for several years, he already had seeds from Green Dew Grass, Earth Vein Flower, and Blood-Clotting Grass in his storage pouch.

And while repeatedly harvesting and sowing crops at Withering Yin Field No. 8, he had quietly collected small amounts of leftover Bone-Rot Flower and Yin Soul Grass seeds after setting aside enough for the next sowing and for reserves. He had also secured enough young Purple Poison Orchid bulbs to start one small spirit field.

With Qinghe Rice seeds on top of that, he already possessed seeds from seven different kinds of spirit plants.

He planned to search for other seeds while traveling through cultivator markets outside Qinghe Valley. As far as Lee Hyun knew, none of the spirit plants cultivated by the outer disciples became more valuable simply by being grown for longer periods.

The third was combat capability.

This was his greatest problem. Lee Hyun still did not have a magic tool he could rely on as his primary weapon.

There had naturally been no reason to fight while he remained inside Qinghe Valley, but outside the sect, he would need a way to protect himself.

He had copied down and memorized several basic techniques, but the only ones he could use to any practical degree were the techniques he had employed while tending spirit plants. He had only barely reached Novice in a few techniques for self-defense and escape, while he still could not properly execute the rest.

A Qi Refining Stage 2 cultivator could take on tigers and bears barehanded, as well as ordinary bandits armed with melee weapons. But this was a xianxia world, and demon beasts capable of killing Qi Refining cultivators genuinely existed.

Even martial artists from the mundane world could kill the current Lee Hyun!

Lee Hyun had picked up quite a bit of knowledge about the world while working with spirit plants. Even among mortals without spiritual roots, there were realms along the martial path, and those who reached a certain level were known as martial artists.

Among martial artists were powerful experts who had reached Transcendent Peak, or even the Transformation Realm and Profound Realm beyond it. According to Senior Brother Lu, under favorable circumstances such as an ambush, these people were terrifyingly skilled enough to kill even Qi Refining cultivators, and such incidents had actually occurred from time to time.

Cultivators who were denied the chance to use their techniques or lacked combat experience were particularly vulnerable.

If Lee Hyun’s current strength had to be evaluated, he could not guarantee his survival if he encountered a hostile Transcendent Peak expert on the road.

Lee Hyun was still a greenhorn at Qi Refining Stage 2 who felt uncomfortable even killing animals. He was weaker than his younger brother Wang Shao, who had entered the sect at the same time and learned the Azure Steel Sword Art before him.

Of course, if he circulated his spiritual power and manifested body-protecting spirit light, a Transcendent Peak expert would not be able to kill him easily. But Lee Hyun had lived such a peaceful life that he had absolutely no combat proficiency.

Put simply, he was the sort of person who would reflexively squeeze his eyes shut if an ordinary person suddenly threw a punch at his face.

‘Do I need to learn how to fight too? First, I should get myself a magic tool before I leave. I suppose it’s finally time to spend my remaining contribution points and the low-grade spirit stones I’ve saved....’

...

A few days later, Lee Hyun headed to the Artifact Hall at the foot of the main peak.

The Artifact Hall was a building carved entirely out of a massive boulder. Palm-sized formation patterns were embedded in the doorposts, and the moment Lee Hyun stepped over the threshold, his identity token gave a faint tremble.

As he entered, the scents of metal and oil reached his nose.

Several rows of low shelves lined the walls. Items rested neatly on wooden stands, while the more expensive-looking pieces sat inside open wooden boxes, surrounded by faint halos of light.

A palm-sized throwing knife, a short sword with a dark blue sheen, a round shield engraved with wave patterns, a bronze mirror as large as a human face, a finger-sized jade plaque....

‘Oh....’

Lee Hyun slowed without realizing it.

Come to think of it, this was the first time he had entered a proper shop since falling into this world. The old feeling of staying up all night adding things to his shopping cart and then removing them again in his previous life suddenly returned after a very long time.

Behind the counter, a man who looked around forty was polishing a short spear with a cloth.

“What are you looking for?”

“Greetings, Senior Brother. I came to purchase a magic tool.”

The man set down the cloth and glanced at Lee Hyun’s identity token.

“An outer disciple at Qi Refining Stage 2... Where are you assigned?”

“The Withering Yin Field.”

“The Withering Yin Field... Ahem. Then I suppose you can afford a low-grade magic tool. You’ve had it rough.”

The man’s voice softened slightly.

“I’m Zhao Fan. I’ve worked at the Artifact Hall for fourteen years. Have you ever bought a magic tool before?”

“No.”

“I thought as much.”

“Forgive me, but could you explain a little about magic tools?”

“Hmm... The world of magic tools is far too broad for me to explain everything here. But as for the basics... magic tools are divided into low-grade, mid-grade, high-grade, and supreme-grade. Low-grade and mid-grade magic tools are generally used by Qi Refining cultivators, while high-grade and supreme-grade magic tools are used by Foundation Establishment Seniors.”

“Are there no magic tools above supreme-grade?”

“Above that, they’re no longer called magic tools, but magic treasures. Magic treasures are used by Great Seniors in the Golden Core realm. Those aren’t things the likes of us will ever have anything to do with. At your level, the only things you can handle or afford are low-grade magic tools.”

Zhao Fan gestured with his chin toward a short sword on the shelf.

“A higher grade isn’t always better. If an early Qi Refining cultivator uses a mid-grade magic tool, they’ll exhaust all their spiritual power after controlling it only a few times. And no matter how fast or powerful the magic tool is, if your divine sense can’t keep up, you’ll hit a tree or a rock instead of your enemy. What matters is finding something suited to you.”

Lee Hyun pointed to several small flying needles nearby.

“What about these?”

“Those are the Mother-Child Flying Needles. One mother needle and six child needles make a single set. You have to control all seven at once, so they consume a great deal of divine sense. They’re classified as a mid-grade magic tool, but in practice, even late Qi Refining cultivators have trouble handling them.”

The next item Lee Hyun examined was a palm-sized blue leaf.

“Is this a flight magic tool?”

“That’s right. The Azure Wind Leaf. But at Qi Refining Stage 2, you won’t be able to fly very high, and after riding it for half a shichen (about one hour), your spiritual power will be completely drained. The price is forty-eight low-grade spirit stones.”

Lee Hyun spent quite some time browsing the Artifact Hall, but he still could not decide what would suit him best.

‘Hmm... Come to think of it, thanks to Wang Shao, I’ve memorized both the Azure Steel Sword Art and the Introductory Guide on Telekinesis and Sword Control. In that case, buying a sword-shaped low-grade magic tool should be the safest choice.’

He had circled the shelves twice when something caught his attention.
