On the bottom shelf at the very back, where a thin layer of dust had settled, several strange objects had been tossed about carelessly.

A chipped sickle, a watering can with a long spout, and a broad longsword with a somewhat blunt appearance.

‘A longsword... is that really what it is?’

The weapon, a little over three and a half chi (about 1.15 m) long, looked unusual from the start.

The two edges of the blade ran almost perfectly straight and parallel, only curving gently inward near the end to form a blunt point. The blade and hilt were forged as one continuous piece of metal, and the grip was long enough to hold with both hands.

Most striking of all, the blade was a full half chi wide, far broader than an ordinary longsword.

“Why are you looking at that?”

Zhao Fan spoke with an incredulous expression.

“It hasn’t sold in nine years.”

“Is this also a magic tool?”

“It’s called the Earth Shovel Sword. Its restrictions are simple, so it’s classified as a low-grade magic tool, but the materials are good enough to be used in a mid-grade one. That makes it exceptionally sturdy.”

“It was made from such good materials, but no one bought it?”

“Because it’s a shovel.”

‘A shovel!?’

Zhao Fan sighed and lifted the Earth Shovel Sword.

“There was once a crazy Senior Brother who said he wanted to plow spirit fields with the Azure Steel Sword Art instead of the Soil-Turning Art. He had this magic tool specially commissioned from black iron mixed with earth-bone stone because he wanted a shovel capable of digging through solid rock. There’s even a restriction engraved inside it that activates the Soil-Softening Art. When you infuse it with spiritual power, any soil or stone touched by the blade softens.”

“I see. But if it was specially commissioned, why is it here?”

“While the Earth Shovel Sword was being made, the Senior Brother who ordered it advanced to Foundation Establishment and stopped working with spirit plants. I casually asked him about it afterward, but he said he had no use for it anymore and refused to buy it. And it’s not like I could argue with a Foundation Establishment cultivator....”

Chapter 11

“I see. But even if it is basically a shovel, if it was custom-made to plow fields with the Azure Steel Sword Art, shouldn’t it still be useful as a weapon? Did it fail to sell because it was too expensive?”

When Lee Hyun asked, Zhao Fan shook his head.

“That’s because... the Earth Shovel Sword falls into an awkward middle ground. They engraved a Soil-Softening Art restriction inside it, so they left out the restriction that assists with the Sword Control Art entirely.”

“Then you can’t use the Sword Control Art with it?”

“That’s right. Normally, even a low-grade magic tool shaped like a sword will have an auxiliary restriction engraved into it so that it can be controlled easily with spiritual power and divine sense. But pour spiritual power into this one, and all it does is activate the Soil-Softening Art. So if you want to use the Sword Control Art with this Earth Shovel Sword at a level viable in actual combat, you have to lift this heavy lump of iron into the air and control it using nothing but your own divine sense and spiritual power, without the help of an auxiliary restriction.”

Zhao Fan tapped the Earth Shovel Sword’s thick blade with his finger.

“In the end, it’s extremely difficult for a Qi Refining cultivator’s divine sense to lift this sword into the air and control it. You’d need spiritual power and divine sense at least as powerful as those of Foundation Establishment Seniors before you could properly control it through the air. But if you were already a Foundation Establishment cultivator, why would you bother buying such a broad-bladed, low-grade magic tool? You’d simply use a high-grade magic tool instead. In the end, it’s useless to everyone.”

“Can I just wield it by hand in a fight?”

“That you can do. It’s forged from black iron mixed with earth-bone stone, so if you infuse it with spiritual power, the edge shouldn’t chip even if it clashes with most mid-grade magic tools.”

After finishing his explanation, Zhao Fan looked Lee Hyun up and down.

“Don’t tell me you’re thinking of buying it.”

“Yes.”

“Didn’t you hear what I just said? A Qi Refining cultivator can’t use the Sword Control Art with this thing. Why not buy another low-grade magic tool instead?”

“You can’t dig soil with another sword, can you?”

“Why do you need to dig soil?”

“Because I’m a spirit-plant cultivator.”

Zhao Fan stared at Lee Hyun’s face for a while. His complexion was so pale it had turned dull and sallow, shadows hung beneath his eyes, and a beard had grown across a face that did not even look twenty yet.

‘Tsk... Looks like the toxic qi from the Withering Yin Field has already muddled his judgment at such a young age. Well, at least the materials and durability are decent.’

Perhaps out of pity, Zhao Fan’s expression softened.

“...The price is sixty low-grade spirit stones. It should normally cost a hundred, but... this fellow has been gathering dust in the corner of a shelf for nine years, so I’ll give you a special discount. This is the lowest price the Artifact Hall’s regulations allow.”

Lee Hyun counted the spirit stones inside his storage pouch.

‘Low-grade spirit stones... I saved thirty-one while working with Senior Brother Lu, and received fifty-four from the Withering Yin Field. That makes eighty-five altogether...’

“I’ll buy it.”

“Are you sure you won’t regret it?”

“Yes. It’s quite close to what I was looking for.”

“All right.”

“I’d like to use my contribution points toward the payment as well.”

Zhao Fan took Lee Hyun’s identity token and pressed it against the Artifact Hall’s spirit tablet. The characters engraved on the identity token blurred, and his contribution-point balance changed to zero.

Lee Hyun had already spent most of his contribution points at the Scripture Pavilion, so there had not been many left. He still had to pay fifty-five low-grade spirit stones.

After counting and putting away the spirit stones, Zhao Fan took a leather sheath and a strap from beneath the shelf and slid them over as well.

“Take these for free. No other sword would fit in this sheath anyway. You’ll have to carry it on your back or wear it at your waist, so take the strap too.”

“Thank you.”

“More importantly.”

Zhao Fan pointed at the Earth Shovel Sword with a finger.

“A magic tool isn’t something you can buy and use immediately. You need to bond with it first.”

“Bond with it?”

“That’s right. First, bite your finger and drip a drop of blood onto the blade. Then send your divine sense into it and imprint your mark on the restriction. After that, carefully envelop the core restriction at the center of the magic tool with your spiritual power. Once the magic tool accepts your spiritual power and the patterns respond, it has recognized you as its master. After that, spiritual power will flow smoothly in and out of the Earth Shovel Sword, and you’ll also be able to activate the Soil-Softening Art restriction engraved inside it. This magic tool’s restrictions are simple, so even if it’s your first time, you should be able to finish within two days. Have you ever read Introductory Guide on Telekinesis and Sword Control?”

“I have... not.”

Lee Hyun nearly answered that he had, but then remembered that Wang Shao had been the one who borrowed Introductory Guide on Telekinesis and Sword Control, while he himself had merely copied and memorized it, so he changed his answer.

The possibility was slim, but if Senior Brother Zhao somehow learned that Introductory Guide on Telekinesis and Sword Control was absent from Lee Hyun’s Scripture Pavilion reading records, it could cause trouble.

“You can read it at the Scripture Pavilion. Ordinary magic tools generally don’t require a dedicated ritual formula when you bond with them. What I just explained is the standard method, so Introductory Guide on Telekinesis and Sword Control at the Scripture Pavilion should explain it in detail as well.”

Zhao Fan lifted the Earth Shovel Sword once before handing it to Lee Hyun. Its hefty weight bore down through both of his arms.

The Earth Shovel Sword weighed a full ten jin (around 5 kg), more than three times as much as an ordinary long sword from the mundane world.

Fortunately, after reaching Qi Refining Stage 2, Lee Hyun possessed superhuman physical abilities and could lift it easily. Still, if he wanted to use it in combat, he would need dedicated practice and training.

...

After returning to his quarters at the Withering Yin Field, Lee Hyun immediately took the Earth Shovel Sword out of his storage pouch.

First, he reviewed the bonding method from Introductory Guide on Telekinesis and Sword Control that he had memorized.

Simply becoming a Qi Refining cultivator made one’s memory incomparably better than that of a mortal. This was because successfully Drawing Qi into the Body gave birth to the primordial spirit.

Cultivators were generally understood to consist of three aspects, essence, qi and spirit, corresponding to the physical body, spiritual power, and the primordial spirit.

When a mortal succeeded in Drawing Qi into the Body and broke through to the Qi Refining stage, the nerves throughout the entire body, including the brain and spinal cord, underwent a baptism of spiritual power, giving birth to the primordial spirit. This primordial spirit encompassed what people commonly referred to as the soul, the mind, and the divine soul.

Once a primordial spirit was born, one’s mental faculties as a whole became incomparably stronger than those of a mortal, and things seen once were not easily forgotten.

Lee Hyun laid the Earth Shovel Sword across his knees and began bonding with it, following Senior Brother Zhao’s advice and the contents of Introductory Guide on Telekinesis and Sword Control.

...

Two nights later.

Even while carrying out his duties in the spirit field, Lee Hyun finally succeeded in bonding with the Earth Shovel Sword!

Hummm–

The tiny formation patterns engraved on the blade emitted a faint yellow glow before fully connecting with Lee Hyun’s divine sense.

“Finally...!”

After completing the bonding process, Lee Hyun was itching to try it out. He left his hut at the Withering Yin Field and headed toward a nearby forest.

After making sure there was no one around, he swung the Earth Shovel Sword at a withered tree.

Slice!

The tree, which was as thick as a man’s thigh, was severed diagonally.

He had yet to properly learn the Azure Steel Sword Art and had merely infused the Earth Shovel Sword with spiritual power before swinging it with both hands, yet the cut was remarkably smooth.

“Oh...”

This time, he brought it down on a boulder.

Crack!

Perhaps because his form was still poor, the boulder only split halfway, but not a single mark appeared on the Earth Shovel Sword.

Lee Hyun activated the Soil-Softening Art restriction.

As yellow light spread along the sword, the surface of the solid boulder softened like wet clay.

Thunk!

The Earth Shovel Sword’s broad tip sank deep into the rock.

Lee Hyun twisted the hilt and applied force, causing a chunk of stone the size of a human head to fall to the ground.

‘Fascinating...!’

Two months later, an opportunity to leave the sect naturally presented itself to Lee Hyun.

The Yin Sand Soil used by the Withering Yin Field was almost depleted.

Yin Sand Soil was black earth dug from deep caves saturated with yin qi. When periodically scattered around the roots of Bone-Rot Flowers and Purple Poison Orchids, it stabilized their medicinal potency and prevented their toxic qi from dispersing.

There was nowhere inside Qinghe Valley where Yin Sand Soil could be gathered, so it had to be dug directly from an abandoned mine at Heiya Ridge, more than a hundred li (about forty kilometers) from the Mountain Gate.

By custom, the field caretaker of the Withering Yin Field personally went to gather Yin Sand Soil once every few years. Lee Hyun knew this from reading the ledgers and had long regarded it as an opportunity to escape the sect.

Strictly speaking, it was not completely impossible to leave the sect even without such an opportunity. However, using a routine mission as an excuse was the most natural way to avoid suspicion, and the later his escape was discovered, the less likely he was to be caught.

Lee Hyun went to the Outer Gate Affairs Hall and applied for the mission to gather Yin Sand Soil.

Permission to leave was inscribed onto his identity token, and he was instructed to return within seven days.

...

The day before his departure, Lee Hyun visited Spirit Field No. 73.

Lu Baishan was inspecting the leaves of the Green Dew Grass at the edge of the field.

“What is it?”

“I’m going to Heiya Ridge to gather Yin Sand Soil. I thought I’d stop by to pay my respects before I left.”

“You’re only going away for seven days. What’s with the farewell?”

Lu Baishan examined Lee Hyun’s face.

“You look surprisingly well for someone who’s been staying in the Withering Yin Field.”

“It’s thanks to the techniques and rules you taught me.”

“I didn’t teach you much. Don’t get greedy for Yin Sand Soil and venture too deep. Digging up soil from the outer areas will be enough.”

“Yes.”

Lee Hyun bowed at the waist.

“Senior Brother Lu, thank you very much for everything.”

Lu Baishan narrowed his eyes.

“You’re acting strange today.”

“Living in the Withering Yin Field has made me think that you never know when you might die.”

“Stop talking nonsense. Be careful and come back safe.”

“I’ll remember that.”

Lu Baishan was his Senior Brother, but to Lee Hyun, he felt something like a master.

Newly admitted outer disciples had no opportunity to formally take a master, so in practice, Senior Brother Lu had indeed filled half that role for him. His advanced age made Lee Hyun feel that way all the more.

Just as he had given Wang Shao an Essence-Nourishing Pill, Lee Hyun wanted to repay Senior Brother Lu as well. However, if Lu Baishan discovered that Lee Hyun had kept his Essence-Nourishing Pills untouched instead of taking them, he might begin to suspect the secret behind how Lee Hyun had endured the Withering Yin Field.

Giving him another gift was awkward as well. Lee Hyun was hardly flush with spirit stones, and there was no chance he possessed anything that would catch Senior Brother Lu’s eye.

‘Even if it’s far in the future, if I ever meet one of Senior Brother Lu’s descendants, I should repay him in some small way. Though I have no idea when I’ll ever be able to come near Qinghe Valley again....’

...

At dawn the next day.

Lee Hyun pulled out a cart that had been left abandoned in a corner of the Withering Yin Field.

He pointed the opening of his storage pouch toward the cart and poured spiritual power into it. Light streamed from the opening and enveloped the entire cart.

The cart’s image rippled like a reflection on water, then rapidly shrank and was sucked into the storage pouch.

Once the cart went inside, Lee Hyun sensed that it had taken up a considerable portion of the available space.

‘This storage pouch is a little cramped. Once I can afford it, I should buy myself a decent one.’

...

After passing through Qinghe Valley’s Mountain Gate, Lee Hyun glanced back without thinking. The peaks of Qinghe Valley rose amid the clouds and mist.

‘Goodbye! I hope everyone stays well.’

...

Even after leaving the Mountain Gate, Lee Hyun did not hurry.

He headed toward Heiya Ridge like an ordinary traveler. He greeted woodcutters and herb gatherers he met along the road and even spent a night at a small inn, registering under his own name.

That way, even if someone investigated his movements, they would have no reason to doubt that he had indeed been heading for Heiya Ridge.

...

On the second day after leaving the Mountain Gate, Lee Hyun arrived at the abandoned mine.

A cool, damp breeze flowed out from the mine.

Lee Hyun used the Faint Light Art to conjure a dim glow above his palm before entering.

The abandoned mine had been neglected for a long time. Rotten support beams leaned at angles throughout the tunnels, while stones fallen from the ceiling and black mud littered the ground.

After heading several hundred paces deeper inside, the walls and floor had turned completely black. When Lee Hyun scooped up a handful of soil, yin qi crept up through his palm.

Lee Hyun took the cart and Earth Shovel Sword out of his storage pouch.

When he dug into the ground with the Earth Shovel Sword while activating its Soil-Softening Art restriction, the damp, compacted Yin Sand Soil came loose with ease.

He filled the cart with Yin Sand Soil.

If he left no trace of having carried out the mission, it would be far too obvious that he had intended to flee from the very beginning.

After heaping the black soil high on the cart, Lee Hyun took a large wooden chest from his storage pouch.

He filled the wooden chest with Yin Sand Soil as well.

Unlike the cart, which he intended to leave behind as evidence of his mission, the Yin Sand Soil in the wooden chest was for growing spirit plants in his tunnel.

The Yin Sand Soil was not strictly necessary, but since the opportunity had presented itself, he decided to take some.

After firmly closing the lid and placing the wooden chest into his storage pouch, Lee Hyun walked around inside and outside the abandoned mine, surveying the terrain.

...

Rain began to fall around sunset.

At first it was only a light drizzle, but by nightfall it had grown so fierce that the mountain paths could no longer be seen.

‘Perfect timing.’

He pulled the cart into one of the branching tunnels deeper inside the abandoned mine.

At the end of a dead-end tunnel, he tipped the cart onto its side and dumped the Yin Sand Soil across the ground.

He brought the Earth Shovel Sword down on one of the cart’s wheels and smashed it apart, then broke the side of the cart as though it had struck the wall.

There were already some old claw marks nearby that appeared to have been left by a wild mountain beast. After examining their shape, Lee Hyun used the Earth Shovel Sword’s broad blade to make several similar marks in the surrounding rock.

They were not perfectly identical, but once rainwater from the downpour flooded into the mine, it would be difficult to examine them closely.

Next, Lee Hyun tore up a robe he had brought with him and hung the pieces on the rocks. Finally, he half-buried his Outer Gate identity token in the mud.

He had made it appear as though he had been attacked by a demon beast or wild animal inside the abandoned mine and dragged into a deep crevice.

There were several vertical shafts of unknown depth beneath the abandoned mine, so searching them would be difficult in the rain.

Lee Hyun did not take his spare sect robe out of his storage pouch. If his storage pouch was nowhere to be found yet both robes had been left behind, it would instead seem unnatural.

He took out a set of ordinary brown clothes and changed into them. He tied his hair firmly with a strip of cloth, then smeared yellow earth across his face and neck.

Afterward, he went deep into the abandoned mine and stopped before the wall he had already identified as the direction of his escape. He formed the hand seals for the Earth Escape Art with both hands.

As his Primordial True Qi shifted to the Earth attribute and enveloped his entire body, the solid wall of earth before him softened like water.

Lee Hyun stepped forward, and his body slowly sank into the wall.

Earth closed in on him from every direction. Even with his eyes open, he could see nothing, and he could not breathe through his nose or mouth.

He circulated the Breath-Sealing Art and spread out his divine sense.

He could faintly sense the density of the surrounding earth and stone. Lee Hyun chose a direction with fewer rocks and slowly advanced.

The Earth Escape Art consumed far more spiritual power than he had expected. His low proficiency was partly to blame, but it was not a technique that a Qi Refining Stage 2 cultivator could afford to use freely in the first place.

After traveling more than a hundred zhang (about three hundred meters), Lee Hyun felt the Primordial True Qi in his dantian rapidly dwindling. The earth qi enveloping his body began to waver, and the pressure from all sides started pressing directly against his skin.

‘If I keep going like this, won’t I end up trapped underground and actually be in danger...?’

The pressure around him steadily intensified, and even though he was circulating the Breath-Sealing Art, the instinctive urge to breathe threw his thoughts into disarray. The terror brought on by the darkness and the crushing earth exceeded anything he had expected.

He decided not to rely solely on the Earth Escape Art and instead make use of the Soil-Turning Art and the Earth Shovel Sword as well.

Using his divine sense, he searched for softer layers of earth and churned them loose with the Soil-Turning Art, then pushed the loosened soil aside with the Earth Shovel Sword to open a gap and advance.

Whenever a long stretch of soft earth lay ahead, he passed through it with the Earth Escape Art. When the rock grew dense, he gradually opened a path with the Soil-Softening Art. Alternating between the three methods greatly reduced his spiritual-power consumption.

As he got the hang of it, his confidence gradually returned. He recalled the surrounding terrain and the map he had studied beforehand, doing his best to maintain the correct direction.

...

Half a shichen (about one hour) later, his divine sense finally detected empty space above him.

Pfft!

Wet earth split apart as Lee Hyun’s body burst out into a patch of bushes on the mountainside.

“Haaah!”

Lee Hyun collapsed facedown in the mud, breathing hard.

Cold air and refreshing rain swept over his entire body. Simply being able to breathe filled Lee Hyun with an overwhelming sense of liberation!

“Whew...”

After looking around, he was relieved to find that he seemed to have crossed to the opposite side of the mountain ridge, just as planned.

Shhhhh–

The heavy rain continuously washed the dirt from his body and clothes. If he moved now, his footprints would quickly disappear.

After catching his breath for a moment, Lee Hyun used the Lightness Art to make his body lighter and began heading south toward Yunze Kingdom.

Chapter 12

Ten days had passed since Lee Hyun left for Heiya Ridge.

He had not returned to Qinghe Valley.

The Outer Gate Affairs Hall did not pay much attention for several days after Lee Hyun's seven-day mission period had expired, but when there was still no word from him on the tenth day after his departure, it dispatched three outer disciples at the mid stage of Qi Refining to Heiya Ridge.

At the abandoned mine, they found a broken cart, Yin Sand Soil scattered across the ground, a torn Qinghe Valley outer disciple robe, and Lee Hyun's identity token.

Marks resembling beast claws remained on the rocks around the cart and the walls of the mine tunnel, and several bottomless vertical shafts lay nearby.

When the search party failed to find Lee Hyun, the Law Enforcement Hall began an investigation.

An outer disciple going missing during a mission did not necessarily mean that he had suffered an accident. He could have staged his death to leave the sect, or he might have stolen sect property and fled.

But in Lee Hyun's case, there was nothing suspicious.

The harvests of Bone-Rot Flowers, Yin Soul Grass, and Purple Poison Orchids were stored in the Withering Yin Field warehouse in exactly the quantities recorded in the ledger. There were enough seeds left for the next sowing, and the low-grade spirit stones used to maintain the Yin-Gathering Formation and Poison-Warding Formation also remained in the prescribed amount.

The Essence-Nourishing Pills, spirit stones, Qinghe Rice, and other items Lee Hyun had received as compensation were no longer in the warehouse, but those had belonged to the field caretaker in the first place. Naturally, they would be in his storage pouch.

"Almost none of his contribution points remained."

"What did he spend them on?"

"Mostly at the Scripture Pavilion. He borrowed several basic technique manuals and returned them properly. He spent the rest at the Artifact Hall purchasing magic tools."

The Law Enforcement Hall steward nodded.

The sect liked it when disciples spent their contribution points at the Scripture Pavilion. Once books and jade slips had been prepared, they could be lent out again and again, so compared with handing out physical resources such as pills or spirit stones, it cost the sect almost nothing.

In fact, considering Qinghe Valley had gotten several years of labor out of Lee Hyun, it had suffered virtually no loss at all.

"And there's no record of him quarreling with any fellow disciples..."

"Correct. Before he was transferred to the Withering Yin Field, he worked at Spirit Field No. 73. Its caretaker, Lu Baishan, also gave him a good evaluation."

The Law Enforcement Hall steward no longer saw any need to investigate Lee Hyun's disappearance further.

"Record him as missing during a mission and presumed dead. If he does not return within three months, strike his name from the outer disciple roster. Separately, check the Heiya Ridge area for signs of demon beast activity and warn any disciples taking missions nearby to be cautious."

At that same time, Lee Hyun was already far to the south of Heiya Ridge.

He traveled mainly along mountain ridges and through forests, taking wide detours whenever he spotted an inhabited village.

The body of a Qi Refining Stage 2 cultivator was incomparably stronger than that of a mortal. He could cover in one or two shichen (about two to four hours) a distance that would take an ordinary person an entire day to walk, and he could climb steep mountain slopes as easily as if he were running across level ground.

...

Before he knew it, a month had passed since he left Qinghe Valley.

Lee Hyun roughly calculated how far he had traveled.

'Even by a conservative estimate... I've covered six thousand li (about 2,400 km)!'

Six thousand li was an enormous distance, roughly equivalent to making three round trips between Seoul and Busan in his previous life.

Lee Hyun stood atop a small mountain peak and looked north, but Qinghe Valley was already far beyond sight.

'They won't be able to find me this far away, right?'

Lee Hyun decided it was time to leave the mountains. Continuing to travel only through the wilderness was too dangerous.

Demon beasts could appear in sparsely inhabited mountains.

Unlike ordinary wild animals, demon beasts were creatures capable of absorbing and using spiritual qi.

Even the weakest among them, early Tier 1 demon beasts, were roughly equivalent in realm to early Qi Refining cultivators, but demon beasts possessed stronger bodies than humans and innate means of attack. Even at the same realm, Lee Hyun, who had little practical combat experience, was unlikely to win.

And in truth, other cultivators were even more dangerous than demon beasts.

Cultivators paid almost no attention to mortals of the mundane world, but they were extremely wary of other cultivators.

In remote regions beyond the influence of sects or cultivation clans, it was not uncommon for someone to kill a weaker cultivator and seize his possessions.

This was partly because there were plenty of cruel people among cultivators, but more importantly, cultivation resources such as spirit stones and pills were directly tied to extending one's lifespan.

When Lee Hyun had worked in the spirit field, Senior Brother Lu had occasionally explained the mindset of cultivators who enjoyed plundering others.

"They would rather live for a hundred and fifty years while the other person dies at twenty than have both of them live for a hundred years."

"Isn't that just the mindset of a lunatic?"

"Yes. The problem is that there are far too many lunatics. That's why you have to be careful. Cultivators all have storage pouches, so they carry their entire fortunes on their bodies. Every one of them is basically a walking treasure trove."

"Then how am I supposed to avoid them?"

"Once you're outside the sect, be especially careful in remote places where there are no witnesses. Cultivators care about face and reputation to some extent too, so if you're not confident in your strength, you're actually better off traveling through crowded places."

Remembering Senior Brother Lu's advice, Lee Hyun decided it was about time to start traveling along the highway.

It bothered him that he had not yet properly mastered the Spirit-Concealing & Aura-Concealing Art and therefore could not hide the fact that he was a cultivator, but he could hardly stop here and cultivate until the technique reached Major Attainment.

'I should avoid places that are too bustling and stick to smaller towns. Cultivators probably don't appear often in the mundane world, where spiritual qi is thin, and there should be even fewer of them in the countryside. I hope I don't run into any cultivators...'

Lee Hyun put the Earth Shovel Sword into his storage pouch. He tied the pouch to the inside of his belt and concealed it beneath his clothes.

...

Two shichen later.

Lee Hyun emerged onto the highway and, while traveling along it, spotted a merchant caravan passing nearby.

A long line of twelve wagons and pack mules stretched down the road, with guards carrying spears and bows protecting the front and rear.

Lee Hyun walked in the same direction, keeping a little distance from them.

Unlike the mountain trails, the highway was well maintained, and stone markers engraved with the distance and direction to the next village had been set along the roadside at intervals.

...

Two days later.

The merchant caravan arrived at a small walled town.

A wooden plaque hanging above the gate bore the two characters ‘Pingling’.

It was not a particularly large town. Tiled houses and mud-walled homes crowded together behind the low city walls, while wagons and travelers queued in front of the gate.

At the gate, the gate guards counted the cargo loaded onto the wagons and assessed duties accordingly. When the caravan leader handed one of the guards something, all twelve wagons were allowed through at once. Behind them, however, an old man with grain loaded on a donkey was held up for quite some time as he argued with the guards.

Since Lee Hyun had no visible luggage, he simply walked through the gate.

Lee Hyun first decided to find out exactly how far he had come.

'Could this be Yunze Kingdom?'

Just then, he spotted a peddler sitting by the roadside and sorting through his belongings.

Lee Hyun approached and asked politely.

"Uncle, may I ask if this is Yunze Kingdom?"

"Yunze Kingdom? Tsk, tsk. Young man, you've gone badly astray. This is Pingling County, Shuoning Circuit, Anling Kingdom. We're right at the far northwestern edge of Anling Kingdom."

"The northwestern edge?"

Lee Hyun wondered whether he had misheard.

Anling Kingdom shared a border with the southern part of the Great Yan Kingdom. Yet after traveling six thousand li south from Qinghe Valley in the southwestern part of the Great Yan Kingdom, he was still only at the far northwestern edge of Anling Kingdom?

"Do you happen to know how much farther it is to Yunze Kingdom?"

"You'd have to travel at least another fifteen thousand li south from here."

"F-fifteen thousand li?"

'Ah... Is it because this is a xianxia world?'

Only then did Lee Hyun remember the novels he had read in his previous life.

Xianxia worlds were usually far larger than Earth.

There were settings where a powerful demon beast occupied an entire mountain range, or a single sect exerted influence over tens of thousands of li. If that was the case, then the geographic scale of this world was probably far greater as well.

Lee Hyun was briefly taken aback, but he had plenty of time anyway.

'Well... I've already come six thousand li. I'll reach another fifteen thousand eventually.'

Lee Hyun decided to continue to Yunze Kingdom as planned.

At that moment, his stomach growled.

It had been two days since he refined a Hunger-Warding Pill, so it was about time he started feeling hungry.

Just then, Lee Hyun's sharpened sense of smell caught the scent of something frying in oil and meat roasting over a fire.

'Maybe I should buy some mundane food and save my Hunger-Warding Pills?'

The mundane copper coins he had saved while working as a woodcutter before entering Qinghe Valley were still sitting in a corner of his storage pouch, so Lee Hyun was not short on traveling money for the moment.

He headed toward the market. But the instant he reached its entrance, he stopped.

'Ugh... What is that smell?'

A collection of shabby stalls selling fish and meat occupied one side of the market entrance.

One merchant gave the knife he had just used to gut a fish a cursory rinse in murky water, then placed it straight back on the cutting board. Beside him, a customer pressed a slab of pork several times with his bare hands before simply putting it back down.

Blood runoff from the stalls mixed with the dusty earth into a muddy sludge, while insects buzzed around the meat.

Perhaps because his five senses had grown sharper after reaching Qi Refining, and because he had grown accustomed to Qinghe Valley's clean environment, even smells he would once have ignored now seemed exceptionally revolting.

"..."

Lee Hyun backed away several steps before finally leaving that part of the market.

There were shops and restaurants farther inside that looked somewhat cleaner, but his appetite was already gone.

He decided to try mundane food again later, once he found somewhere a little more upscale.

...

Lee Hyun resumed his journey south.

He mainly followed busy highways, and whenever he found a cargo boat that carried passengers for a small fare, he would sometimes travel along the rivers instead.

Grain barges formed long lines along the rivers, while private boats carrying salt and timber moved among them.

Traveling by water was not bad either. He could enjoy the scenery along the river, and while resting, he could circulate the Primordial One-Qi Art and refine his spiritual power.

...

As Lee Hyun passed through various towns in Anling Kingdom, he gradually found a few foods he could tolerate buying.

Eggs boiled in their shells, fruits that could be peeled before eating, and nuts he could shell himself were comparatively easier to stomach. As he gradually found more mundane foods he could eat, his consumption of Hunger-Warding Pills decreased.

Whenever he happened to find common medicinal herbs growing near the foothills, he gathered them and sold them to apothecaries, replenishing the silver he used in the mundane world.

...

Another three months passed.

Only after traveling roughly another fifteen thousand li from Pingling County Seat was Lee Hyun finally able to cross Anling Kingdom's southern border. Counting from Qinghe Valley, he had traveled more than twenty thousand li in total.

Yet despite that, the climate had changed astonishingly little.

Even the height of the sun at midday had shown no noticeable difference.

'This really is different from Earth.'

He had no way of knowing whether this world was simply an enormous planet far larger than Earth, or whether the structure of the universe itself was entirely different.

Lost in thought, Lee Hyun continued walking until he finally arrived in Yunze Kingdom.

...

Qingliu County Seat, located at the northwestern edge of Linjiang Circuit in Yunze Kingdom.

Lee Hyun looked around as he passed through the city gate.

A broad river flowed through the center of the city, and vessels large and small were moored in rows along its banks.

On one side of the wharf stood a long row of warehouses storing tax grain collected from Qingliu County and the surrounding districts. In front of them, clerks held brushes as they counted the sacks.

Ever since he entered Yunze Kingdom, rivers and lakes had become noticeably more common.

Having safely reached his destination, Lee Hyun felt much more at ease.

'Should I try to find a cultivator market?'

He still had around thirty low-grade spirit stones left.

Although he had brought some spirit plant seeds from Qinghe Valley, he wanted to obtain more varieties of spirit plants suitable for cultivating underground over many years.

The problem was that he had no idea where the cultivator markets were. As Lee Hyun walked through the streets while listening to the conversations around him, he overheard some merchants talking in a nearby teahouse.

"I hear there aren't any seats left on boats heading southeast these days."

"Isn't the capital examination being held in Yunjing? All the scholars selected from the various circuits are flocking to the royal capital, so of course there aren't."

'The capital examination....'

It seemed to be a system in which the court examined scholars and selected government officials.

Lee Hyun slowed his steps.

'Yunjing must be the capital of Yunze Kingdom. Wouldn't there also be a cultivator market nearby where rogue cultivators gather?'

Lee Hyun briefly considered looking for a boat to Yunjing, but then suddenly remembered his current situation.

'Right now, I'm only at Qi Refining Stage 2. I have no combat experience, almost no offensive techniques I can properly use, and my main magic tool is the Earth Shovel Sword, which is closer to a shovel than a sword...'

Back in Qinghe Valley, he had been surrounded by fellow disciples from the same sect, so nothing had happened. But the rogue cultivators gathered at a cultivator market would all be complete strangers.

'Dammit. Why was I already trying to mingle with cultivators? I nearly forgot my original goal of living peacefully...!'

'First, I'll make my own tunnel and focus on cultivation. It won't be too late to visit a cultivator market once I'm confident an ordinary Qi Refining cultivator won't be able to kill me easily.'

...

After leaving Qingliu County Seat, Lee Hyun headed south in search of sparsely populated hills and mountains.

'Now then... where should I build the historic Tunnel No. 1?'

His first thought was a mountain. But he could not simply dig a tunnel into just any mountain.

Famous mountains containing spirit veins, spirit herbs, or minerals attracted cultivators, while deep mountains might be home to demon beasts or frequented by herb gatherers. If he was particularly unlucky, he might even stumble across the cave abode of a secluded rogue cultivator.

But flat ground was not ideal either.

'If there's groundwater beneath flat land, the tunnel could flood, and it'll be harder to hide the excavated soil. Disguising the entrance and air shafts as natural features would also be more difficult than on a mountain.'

Lee Hyun had not been an expert in earth science in his previous life, and there was no guarantee that the geology of this world was the same as Earth's, so it was difficult for him to judge what conditions would be best.

'I guess I'll have to find somewhere with no people and thin spiritual qi, then try digging myself if the place looks suitable.'

Whenever Lee Hyun passed a gently sloping mountain or hill, he checked the surrounding waterways and signs of human activity. If a place seemed promising, he tested the ground with the Earth Shovel Sword.

After moving from place to place for several days, Lee Hyun finally discovered a low, gently sloping mountain roughly three hundred li southeast of Qingliu County Seat.

There was plenty of soil around the foot of the mountain, while gravel and rocks became gradually more common farther up the slope. A valley was not far away, but the mountainside stood well above the watercourse.

He still did not know whether it was the perfect location, but it looked better than anywhere else he had examined so far.

'Hmm... This place somehow seems about right.'

Chapter 13

One year later.

Three hundred li (about 120 km) southeast of Qingliu County Seat, Linjiang Circuit, Yunze Kingdom.

There stood a gently sloping mountain that did not even have a name.

It had no spirit vein, nor did it produce even common herbs or minerals. Fruit-bearing trees were scarce as well, so hardly any wild animals lived there.

Even woodcutters, herb gatherers, and hunters were rarely seen in this place. It was an utterly unremarkable mountain shunned even by villagers of the mundane world, let alone cultivators.

Rustle, rustle―

Something moved swiftly through the undergrowth halfway up the mountain.

At first, it looked as though a snake were slithering beneath the grass. But on closer inspection, it was a person dressed in brown, lying flat against the ground as he moved.

It was Lee Hyun.

Without moving his arms or legs, he was using the Soil-Turning Art together with the Earth Escape Art to slide his entire prone body across the surface of the ground.

Sliiide―

He cut through the undergrowth feet first with his head trailing behind, yet he moved faster than a snake, and the grass and branches barely stirred even after his body had passed.

Lee Hyun had named this peculiar movement technique the Reclining Escape Art. Strictly speaking, it should have been called the Reclining Earth Escape Art, but since he was the only one who used this escape art anyway, he had named it however he pleased.

There was a reason he was moving around in such a bizarre fashion.

If someone noticed Lee Hyun regularly coming and going, pointless rumors might spread that there was some secret hidden on this mountain.

But entering the ground from far away and traveling with the Earth Escape Art every single time consumed far too much spiritual power.

The Reclining Escape Art, on the other hand, merely skimmed along the surface instead of burying his entire body in the soil, so it consumed less than a tenth as much spiritual power as the Earth Escape Art.

If he followed the undergrowth from the foot of the mountain, he was also difficult to spot from a distance. Even if someone happened to be nearby, they would most likely assume that an animal was passing through the grass.

The strange figure gliding along on his back reached a broad, flat rock halfway up the mountain, then smoothly sank into the soil beneath it.

Slip―

Even if someone had been watching Lee Hyun until that very moment, the movement was so natural that they would have had difficulty telling exactly when he disappeared.

...

About ten li, roughly 4 km, beneath the surface.

Whoosh!

Lee Hyun dropped from the dark ceiling.

Thud.

After returning to Tunnel No. 1, Lee Hyun headed for the storeroom first.

A thick stone slab stood at the storeroom entrance like a door. When he pushed it aside, wooden shelves and jars of various sizes came into view.

Lee Hyun took six heavy bundles from his storage pouch and set them on the floor.

Thud, rustle―

When he opened the bundles, large walnuts, pine nuts, hazelnuts, peeled and dried chestnuts, roasted ginkgo nuts, pitted dried jujubes, and lotus seeds with their bitter hearts removed spilled out. He had bought all of them in Qingliu County Seat.

Lee Hyun divided the food by type among the jars. Before sealing each lid, he also placed inside a piece of charcoal wrapped in thin paper to absorb moisture.

Strictly speaking, storing everything inside the storage pouch would have been best, but Lee Hyun would eat it all before it spoiled anyway, so it hardly mattered.

Finally, he picked up a walnut and pressed it between his fingers.

Crack!

The hard shell split far too easily. Lee Hyun popped the kernel into his mouth and left the storeroom.

When he stopped in front of the narrow passage beside the storeroom, the soil beneath his feet rippled like water and swallowed his body.

A short while later, he emerged again in another passage several dozen zhang (roughly a hundred meters) away.

A crude wooden placard had been planted before him.

「Spirit Field No. 1-1」

It meant the first spirit field of Tunnel No. 1.

Several lines of smaller writing had been carved beneath it.

- Reclamation date.

- Sowing variety.

- Date of last Spirit Rain Art use.

- Spirit insect discovery record.

He had modeled it after the spirit field ledgers he had seen in Qinghe Valley.

Lee Hyun opened the stone door and went inside.

Spirit Field No. 1-1 was a long, narrow chamber measuring two zhang wide and sixteen zhang long. Its area was a little over half a mu (about 350 m²).

The ceiling was around one zhang high, and he had left the solid bedrock along both sides of the passage intact to serve as supports. Thick logs had been set closely together between them to further reduce the risk of collapse.

Lee Hyun had created this space using the Soil-Turning Art and the Earth Shovel Sword. The soil and stone he excavated had been used to reinforce the passages or fill empty spaces.

Long rows of Earth Vein Flowers lined the edges of the spirit field. They slowly drew the sparse spiritual qi from the surrounding geological strata into this place.

Inside them, Purple Poison Orchids with drooping violet leaves had been planted like a wall. Ivory-colored Bone-Rot Flowers and dark blue-black Yin Soul Grass grew in the central furrows.

The toxic qi emitted by the Bone-Rot Flowers and Purple Poison Orchids formed a faint purple mist within the spirit field.

The toxic qi was potent enough that even Qi Refining cultivators would have difficulty enduring it, so ordinary animals and insects could not even approach.

Even Lee Hyun, the owner of the spirit field, always entered while using the Qi Sphere Barrier and Breath-Sealing Art, then used the Cleansing Art and Detoxification Art after leaving.

Lee Hyun slowly walked along the passage, examining the condition of the leaves and stems. Then he spotted a tiny white speck near the roots of one Earth Vein Flower.

"Laid eggs here again."

When he brushed aside a little soil, several translucent eggs appeared, clinging together. Lee Hyun's finger flashed, and a slender silver needle pierced the eggs with perfect accuracy.

Several kinds of spirit insects he had never seen in Qinghe Valley lived underground in this area.

Some had long bodies like earthworms with pincers on their heads, while others were beetles almost impossible to distinguish from clumps of soil.

The spirit insects did not even dare touch the highly poisonous Yin Soul Grass, Bone-Rot Flowers, or Purple Poison Orchids. Instead, they tried to gnaw on the Earth Vein Flowers.

However, the toxic qi permeating the surroundings prevented them from damaging the Earth Vein Flowers as well, so at most they occasionally laid eggs near their roots.

Even if he left the eggs alone, the larvae would probably still be unable to harm the Earth Vein Flowers after hatching, but Lee Hyun removed every egg he found just in case.

"I suppose this counts as my first successful underground spirit field. It feels like I've worked out a proper system now..."

Lee Hyun looked around the spirit field with satisfaction.

In truth, this place was inferior to Qinghe Valley's Withering Yin Field in many respects. The three spirit plants grew at only one-third the rate they had in the Withering Yin Field. But aside from their growth speed, he had solved almost every other problem.

Perhaps because growth was slow, he did not need to use the Spirit Rain Art very often here either. Casting it over the entire spirit field once every ten days was sufficient.

At present, he had planted 120 Bone-Rot Flower plants, 300 clumps of Yin Soul Grass, and 80 Purple Poison Orchid bulbs.

If they continued growing without any major accidents, he would be able to harvest them roughly three hundred years later as spirit medicines with a hundred years of medicinal potency apiece.

...

There were two reasons Lee Hyun had built his hideout ten li underground.

The first was that the temperature had barely risen even at this depth.

According to something Lee Hyun had once heard in passing in his previous life, the deeper one went underground on Earth, the higher the temperature became. Deep geothermal power generation, for example, supposedly drilled holes between 3 km and more than 5 km underground to make use of geothermal heat ranging from 100 degrees to over 200 degrees Celsius.

Yet in this world, even ten li underground, around 4 km deep, the temperature barely changed.

Curious, Lee Hyun had once used the Earth Escape Art and Earth Shovel Sword to descend even farther. Around twenty-five li, roughly 10 km underground, however, he discovered that the temperature began rising sharply. In some places, reddish heat even seeped from cracks in the bedrock.

Lee Hyun guessed that something resembling an earth-fire vein or magma flowed below that depth, and afterward he saw no reason to descend any farther.

The second reason was that soil and bedrock interfered with outsiders' divine sense.

Divine sense propagated best through air, while its detection range decreased considerably in water or soil. Layers of bedrock or metal interfered with it even more severely.

When Lee Hyun tested it with his own divine sense, he found that its detection range dropped by nearly ninety percent in soil or water.

In other words, for someone to sense all the way down to ten li underground with divine sense, they would need divine sense powerful enough to scan more than a hundred li through open air.

If what Lee Hyun had overheard in Qinghe Valley was accurate, scanning a hundred li with divine sense was something only cultivators far beyond the Golden Core realm could accomplish. Perhaps even many Nascent Soul cultivators would be unable to discover a small cavern at this depth through divine sense alone.

Of course, even a low-realm cultivator might eventually discover Lee Hyun's hideout if they systematically searched the mountain using the Ground-Sense Art or a detection magic tool.

But that assumption was hardly realistic. There was no reason for a passing cultivator to meticulously search beneath a mountain that did not even possess a spirit vein.

The geographical scale of this world was enormous. Doing such a thing would literally amount to throwing time and spiritual power into the dirt.

Cultivators who frequently used the Earth Escape Art were rare as well.

In truth, judged purely by speed, the Earth Escape Art was not a particularly good technique. A Qi Refining cultivator could move faster by running across the surface, while anyone at Foundation Establishment or above could simply fly through the sky.

Thus, Lee Hyun concluded that unless someone already suspected this mountain and deliberately investigated it, the chances of Tunnel No. 1 being discovered by accident at a depth of ten li were very small.

There was one minor problem: food.

Qinghe Rice did not grow properly in the underground spirit field. Lee Hyun did not know whether it was because there was no sunlight or because the underground environment was unsuitable, but since cultivating it was impossible, he had to obtain food from the mundane world.

That was why Lee Hyun occasionally visited Qingliu County Seat or other nearby county seats and bought nuts like he had today.

The Blood-Clotting Grass and Green Dew Grass he had planted as an experiment had also failed to grow normally, but neither became more valuable with age, nor could they serve as food like Qinghe Rice, so Lee Hyun stopped paying them any further attention.

...

After finishing today's inspection of the spirit field, Lee Hyun followed the passage back to the cultivation chamber.

The cultivation chamber had been made by reshaping a natural rock cavern he had stumbled upon while constructing the hideout.

Gray granite formed a rounded ceiling, with the highest point reaching three zhang. The floor had been leveled with the Earth Shovel Sword, while a bed and shelves had been carved directly into the rock along one wall.

Neatly arranged on the shelves were wooden tablets inscribed with mnemonic formulas for techniques, jars containing spirit insects captured in the spirit field for research, and small wooden boxes filled with various kinds of soil.

A wooden table and a single chair stood in the center.

There were no windows here, and he was not currently using the Faint Light Art, leaving the chamber pitch-dark. Yet Lee Hyun felt more at ease whenever he entered this darkness.

One side of the cultivation chamber connected to the storeroom, while a curved passage on the opposite side led to the spirit field. Three wrist-thick air shafts had been bored near the ceiling.

The passage leading toward the spirit field had been dug lower than the living area. This was to keep the dense toxic qi from spilling into the cultivation chamber and make it settle on the floor of the spirit field instead.

Lee Hyun crossed the cultivation chamber and headed toward the new passage he had been excavating.

It was where he intended to build Spirit Field No. 1-2.

"Maybe I'll dig just a little farther today."

Lee Hyun took out the Earth Shovel Sword.

Humm―

As he infused it with spiritual power, the patterns engraved on its broad blade glowed yellow.

When he thrust the Earth Shovel Sword into the ground and pushed forward, the solid earth and gravel softened like wet clay. He used the Soil-Turning Art to send the loosened soil behind him.

He had advanced about three zhang when it happened.

Pshk.

The sensation at the tip of the Earth Shovel Sword suddenly changed.

"Hm?"

Ahead stretched a long layer of fine sand mixed with rounded gravel. The soil was strangely damp.

Lee Hyun pinched up a little sand between his fingers.

"Is there water?"

A term he had heard in his previous life surfaced faintly in his mind.

'Wasn't there something called an aquifer...? A layer where water flows underground?'

He knew almost nothing about geology. He had merely heard that layers of sand and gravel underground could hold or channel water, and that digging a well into one would bring the water out.

Lee Hyun cautiously prodded ahead with the Earth Shovel Sword.

Pshhh!

A thin stream of water sprayed from the hole pierced by the sword tip.

Fwoooosh―

The next instant, the opening widened to the size of a fist, and an enormous torrent of water burst through.

"Kgh!"

The cold jet struck Lee Hyun squarely in the face and chest.

Water rapidly began filling the floor of the passage.

'Damn!'

Lee Hyun activated the Soil-Turning Art and pushed the surrounding clay-rich soil into the opening. But the rushing water immediately washed it away.

Lee Hyun dragged over the broad stone slab he had left standing nearby.

Boom!

Using the Earth Shovel Sword's Soil-Softening Art, he softened the bedrock around the opening, then pushed the edge of the slab nearly one chi (about 30 cm) into it.

When he released the Soil-Softening Art, the bedrock hardened again and clamped tightly around the slab. Lee Hyun then packed several layers of clay and gravel over it and compressed them firmly with the Soil-Turning Art.

Water continued seeping through the gaps around the slab for a while, but after he filled even the tiniest cracks with clay, the flow finally stopped.

"Haa...."

Lee Hyun stood ankle-deep in water and swept back his soaked hair.

The stone slab before him trembled faintly. There seemed to be groundwater trapped under considerable pressure on the other side.

"Is this an aquifer...? If I mess with it carelessly, I could ruin all my farming..."

Lee Hyun pulled out the wooden placard he had originally set up.

「Planned Site for Spirit Field No. 1-2」

He carved new words onto the reverse side.

「Aquifer No. 1. Do Not Open Carelessly.」

After thinking for a moment, Lee Hyun carved two more lines beneath it.

「Potential Future Use for Water Storage.」

「Potential for Cultivation of Aquatic Spirit Plants.」

...

After changing his clothes, Lee Hyun returned and sat at the table.

"Spirit Field No. 1-2 needs to be far away from the aquifer... I'll have to dig it in a completely different direction. Anyway, Tunnel No. 1 finally has the bare essentials. It's time to make a cultivation plan."

He took out a blank wooden tablet and began writing down, one by one, the cultivation arts and techniques he needed to learn.

「Primordial Body, Aura-Concealing Art, Spirit-Concealing Art, Distance-Shrinking Step, Azure Steel Sword Art, Spirit Light Shield, Fireball Art, Sword Control Art, Farsight Art, Keen Hearing Art, Night Vision Art, Scent-Tracking Art, Aura-Reading Art, Ground-Sense Art, ...」

Lee Hyun's expression stiffened as he stared at the writing that filled the entire wooden tablet.

"There's too much to learn. But all of it seems useful..."

Properly mastering a technique required countless repetitions, but practicing was difficult for a Qi Refining Stage 2 cultivator because his spiritual power ran dry so quickly.

"I should cultivate the Primordial Body first. If I have more spiritual power, learning techniques should become easier too."

...

Lee Hyun sat in the lotus position atop the bedrock and, following the cultivation method of the Primordial Body, drew a thread-thin strand of Primordial True Qi from his dantian.

The energy flowed through his meridians, passing through his chest and shoulder before entering his right arm.

Rather than keeping the Primordial True Qi within the meridians of his palm, he slowly allowed it to seep into the surrounding flesh and bone.

Ssshh―

The Primordial True Qi dispersed in an instant.

When he examined it carefully with divine sense, he found it spread in an extremely thin layer throughout his entire palm. It had simply become so faint that he could no longer sense it as distinctly as before.

Lee Hyun drew out another strand of Primordial True Qi.

The second was the same. So was the third.

For one full shichen (two hours), he continuously transferred Primordial True Qi from his dantian, yet he could barely sense any change in his palm.

He recalled what Steward Wang Jin had told him.

- It will feel hopeless, like trying to fill a boundless sea all by yourself.

Lee Hyun looked down at his palm.

"It certainly is daunting. Still, if I keep pouring water into the sea, someday..."

From that day onward, he began cultivating the Primordial Body whenever he had spare time.

One hundred years later.

The wooden placard of Spirit Field No. 1-1 had darkened after enduring the passage of countless years.

The Bone-Rot Flowers, Yin Soul Grass, and Purple Poison Orchids had continued producing seeds and bulbs, while the original parent plants had accumulated some thirty years of medicinal potency. Considering the growth rate here, everything was progressing according to plan.

Countless rains and snows had fallen upon the mountain above.

The county magistrate of Qingliu County Seat had changed several times, and the owner of the shop where Lee Hyun had first bought nuts had died long ago.

Every decade or so, Lee Hyun changed the market he frequented. At times, he attached a false beard or smeared dirt over his face to alter his appearance.

Yet his face and body had not aged in the slightest compared to a hundred years ago.

...

At the center of the cultivation chamber in Tunnel No. 1.

Lee Hyun lay there comfortably.

Inside his body, there was no longer any distinct boundary marking the dantian beneath his navel.

Primordial True Qi had seeped throughout his entire body, into his skin and muscles, blood vessels and bones, and even his internal organs.

At first, spreading a single strand of true qi through just one arm had taken an entire day.

After ten years, he could connect his limbs and torso into a single flow.

After thirty years, Primordial True Qi began to reside within his bones.

By the sixtieth year, the Primordial One-Qi Art circulated naturally even while he breathed or walked.

Lee Hyun had initially cultivated while sitting in the lotus position, but as he became increasingly proficient with the Primordial One-Qi Art, he began circulating the cultivation art constantly even while tending the spirit fields, excavating passages, or cracking open nuts.

At some point, he even became capable of refining spiritual qi at maximum efficiency while lying down comfortably.

And today, after a hundred years.

Hummm―

Primordial True Qi spread throughout his entire body from the crown of his head to the soles of his feet. The instant it evenly filled the tips of his fingers and toes, even the most minute flesh and tissue beneath his skin...

Thrum!

A faint light spread from Lee Hyun's body, then vanished.

His bones, muscles, and internal organs vibrated simultaneously as the Primordial True Qi scattered throughout his body connected into a single whole!

Lee Hyun opened his eyes.

"Finally, Primordial Body, 2nd Stage...!"

Primordial Body, 2nd Stage meant that his entire body, from head to toe, had been developed to the same level as the dantian of an ordinary Qi Refining Stage 2 cultivator.

In other words, Lee Hyun's entire body had now become one enormous dantian!

Lee Hyun slowly raised his right hand.

Flash!

A slender silver needle appeared at his fingertip.

Pshk!

The silver needle pierced straight through the center of a wooden board on the opposite side of the cultivation chamber.

Lee Hyun immediately cast the Yang Metal Art a second time, then fired a third and fourth silver needle in rapid succession.

Pshk! Pshk! Pshk!

Even after using the Yang Metal Art dozens more times, the Primordial True Qi filling his entire body barely diminished.

Yet Lee Hyun's expression turned strange.

"Huh?"

He had discovered a new secret of the Primordial One-Qi Art and the Primordial Body.

Chapter 14

Lee Hyun wondered if he had been mistaken, so he tried several other techniques as well, but there was no mistake.

The moment he formed the hand seal for Qi Sphere Barrier, a translucent barrier appeared around him almost simultaneously.

"So that's it! This wasn't actually a flaw in the Primordial One-Qi Art...."

When he had first heard the explanation of the Primordial One-Qi Art in Qinghe Valley, Steward Wang Jin had said the following.

- The spiritual power refined through this cultivation art is called Primordial True Qi. It can be freely converted as it is released, allowing you to use techniques that do not match your own spiritual root attributes. Their power will be somewhat reduced, though....

Steward Wang Jin had vaguely described the drawback as reduced power, but the greatest problem with the Primordial One-Qi Art was actually its slow technique activation.

In fact, whenever Lee Hyun used Primordial True Qi to cast a technique, he had always found the activation speed somewhat lacking.

Until now, Lee Hyun had assumed this drawback was simply the price he had to pay for gaining the ability to use techniques of multiple attributes.

Since Primordial True Qi had to be converted into the attribute required by a technique, he had thought it only natural that activation would be delayed.

But that was not the case. It seemed the Primordial One-Qi Art had been created from the very beginning on the assumption that its practitioner would form a Primordial Body. Once Lee Hyun formed one, that weakness all but disappeared.

After running several experiments, Lee Hyun figured out why his technique activation speed had improved.

It was because spiritual power now filled his body all the way to the surface of his skin!

Previously, he had to send Primordial True Qi from his dantian through his meridians to his hands, then manifest the technique from his fingertips.

Now, however, the Primordial True Qi already filling his fingertips reacted the instant he formed a hand seal, making the activation delay almost imperceptible.

For techniques cast through his hands, the Primordial True Qi spread throughout his palms and fingers responded. For techniques that enveloped his entire body, the spiritual power flowing beneath his skin moved all at once. The very process of transporting spiritual power from his dantian out to distant parts of his body had disappeared.

Lee Hyun felt that if the Primordial One-Qi Art had previously been worth fifty points in terms of technique activation speed, it was now worth around ninety.

Of course, there might be cultivation arts with even faster activation speeds than the Primordial One-Qi Art, perhaps ones worth ninety-five points. But even compared to those, the difference was only five points. Compared to when it had been worth fifty, the flaw in the Primordial One-Qi Art had essentially disappeared.

It would have been even better if he could close the remaining ten-point gap and turn it into a perfect hundred-point cultivation art, but that did not seem realistic.

After all, the Primordial One-Qi Art still required an intermediate step in which its spiritual power was converted into the appropriate attribute. No matter how much the cultivation art improved, it would probably be impossible to completely eliminate even the minute delay caused by that process.

But that was fine. He did not mind being ten points short. In the cultivation world, the ability to use techniques of multiple attributes was far more valuable in most situations.

'So the true core of the Primordial One-Qi Art was the Primordial Body! Most cultivators probably don't even know that the Primordial Body can compensate for the cultivation art's flaws like this. Just look at me. It took me more than a hundred years merely to create a Primordial Body at the level of Qi Refining Stage 2. There's no way anyone but me would ever have tried something like this.'

...

Since he had reached Primordial Body, 2nd Stage, Lee Hyun decided to write down his accomplishments where he could see them and savor the lingering satisfaction of his breakthrough a little longer.

He took out a wooden board and began carving a "handmade status screen" into it with his fingertip.

'Judging from how long I've cultivated and what I can feel inside my body, I think my total spiritual power is about fifty times what it used to be. If I assume my total spiritual power was 1 when I was around the middle of Qi Refining Stage 1... then I guess this is roughly where I stand now?'

【Age: 61 → 161】

【Realm: Qi Refining Stage 2 → Qi Refining Stage 2 Throughout the Entire Body】

【Spiritual Power: 1.7 → 83】

【Constitution: Primordial Body, 2nd Stage】

【Spiritual Roots: Wood, Fire, Earth】

【Cultivation Art: Primordial One-Qi Art】

The age Lee Hyun recorded was calculated by adding the years he had spent in this world to the body's age of nineteen at the time of his transmigration.

If his body truly did not age, his age was not particularly meaningful, but since Lee Hyun still did not know the true nature of his body, he decided to record it for reference.

The most important entry on his handmade status screen right now was spiritual power. Lee Hyun tried to calculate that number according to as consistent a standard as possible.

A spiritual power value of 83 despite being only at Qi Refining Stage 2 was utterly absurd. By Lee Hyun's estimate, it might rival that of an ordinary late Qi Refining cultivator.

'Even though my total spiritual power is fifty times what it was at Qi Refining Stage 2, cultivation becomes harder with every Stage even within Qi Refining, so there's no way I've reached Foundation Establishment level. I'm probably somewhere around Qi Refining Stage 7 or 8....'

If there were a Qi Refining Stage 2 cultivator and a Qi Refining Stage 8 cultivator, the latter did not simply possess four times as much spiritual power as the former.

In a typical xianxia world, the large divisions such as Qi Refining, Foundation Establishment, Golden Core, and Nascent Soul were called major realms.

Minor realms also existed within each major realm. Stages 1 through 3 were generally classified as early, Stages 4 through 6 as mid, and Stages 7 through 9 as late. Those who reached Stage 10 were said to have attained Great Perfection.

Great Perfection was not actually a separate realm in its own right. It simply meant the completion of Stage 9. Calling such a person a Stage 10 cultivator was merely a special mark of respect for someone who had finished preparing to break through to the next major realm.

Strictly speaking, there was no separate Stage 10, so each major realm could be divided into three minor realms: early, mid, and late.

There was a reason cultivators went out of their way to distinguish between minor realms.

Cultivators generally encountered considerable difficulty when advancing from early to mid and from mid to late. As a result, many Qi Refining cultivators became stuck at Stages 3 and 6.

In other words, a Qi Refining Stage 8 cultivator had broken through two more minor-realm bottlenecks than a Qi Refining Stage 2 cultivator. There had to be some difference not only in the quantity of spiritual power, but in its quality as well.

This was only Lee Hyun's conjecture based on what he had picked up during his time in Qinghe Valley, but Qinghe Valley had quite a few mid and late Qi Refining cultivators, so he was probably not wrong.

'Even within the same major realm, both the amount of growth and the difficulty increase with each Stage. So as I am now, I'd probably still have a hard time defeating a late Qi Refining cultivator. As for a mid Qi Refining cultivator, maybe I could win once I get more accustomed to techniques and combat....'

Lee Hyun continued carving his handmade status screen into the wooden board.

'The techniques I've learned should look something like this right now.'

【Techniques (Novice): Faint Light Art, Lightness Art, Ground-Sense Art, Germination Art, Poison-Discerning Art】

【Techniques (Minor Attainment): Night Vision Art, Spirit Rain Art, Soil-Turning Art, Yang Metal Art, Earth Escape Art, Cleansing Art, Air-Clearing Art, Breath-Sealing Art, Qi Sphere Barrier, Detoxification Art】

【Techniques (Major Attainment): None】

【Techniques (Perfection): None】

【Applied Technique: Reclining Escape Art】

Lee Hyun had arbitrarily estimated the proficiency divisions from Novice to Perfection, so they might not be entirely accurate. The wooden board was only meant to serve as a reference for his current cultivation progress, so a little error did not matter.

"I'll stop advancing my realm for a while and start by learning some basic combat techniques. Ah, before that, I should sow the new spirit fields first."

Over the past hundred years, Lee Hyun had gradually prepared additional sites for Spirit Field No. 1-2, Spirit Field No. 1-3, Spirit Field No. 1-4, and Spirit Field No. 1-5. However, he had not sown them yet, because increasing the number of places he needed to maintain with the Spirit Rain Art would have interfered with his cultivation.

But now that he had reached Primordial Body, 2nd Stage and possessed plenty of spiritual power, he could make the rounds of several spirit fields at once and use the Spirit Rain Art as much as he pleased. This meant he could synchronize all their maintenance schedules to the same day, so even managing five spirit fields would not be a burden.

...

The newly created spirit fields were almost identical to Spirit Field No. 1-1 in both structure and area.

Lee Hyun went from Spirit Field No. 1-2 through Spirit Field No. 1-5 in order, planting Bone-Rot Flower, Yin Soul Grass, Purple Poison Orchid, and Earth Vein Flower before using the Spirit Rain Art.

Patter-patter―

Rainwater infused with spiritual qi fell evenly over the freshly prepared furrows.

After finishing the sowing, Lee Hyun carved the date, plant variety, and time he first cast the Spirit Rain Art onto the wooden boards at the entrance to each spirit field.

Perhaps because he had reached Primordial Body, 2nd Stage, even after making the rounds of all four spirit fields, plenty of Primordial True Qi remained throughout his body.

Finally, he visited Spirit Field No. 1-1.

The moment he opened the stone door, purple toxic mist far denser than before seeped out through the gap.

Hiss―

As the toxic mist clung to the surface of Qi Sphere Barrier, a faint sound arose. Wave-like ripples spread across the transparent barrier one after another.

Even with greater proficiency in Qi Sphere Barrier and far more spiritual power than before, the toxic qi still felt threatening.

"...The poison has gotten pretty strong, hasn't it?"

The mother plants that had grown for a hundred years possessed roughly thirty-three years' worth of medicinal potency, even considering the harsh growing environment.

The roots of the Bone-Rot Flower had grown thick and knotted like the bones of a beast, while the buds of the Purple Poison Orchid slowly tightened like living creatures as they spewed purple toxic mist.

After trimming away a few wilted leaves, he used the Spirit Rain Art. Since he had watered the four new spirit fields and Spirit Field No. 1-1 on the same day, from now on he only needed to make one complete round every ten days.

After leaving the spirit field, Lee Hyun used the Cleansing Art to remove the poisonous powder clinging to his body and clothes, then followed it with the Detoxification Art.

...

A few days later.

While digging a new passage, Lee Hyun discovered a small natural cavern surrounded by hard, crystalline bedrock. Even when he brought the Earth Shovel Sword down against the wall with all his strength, it left only a shallow scratch.

'Perfect.'

Lee Hyun created a passage connecting the cultivation chamber to the rocky cavern, then wrote "training cavern" on the wooden plaque at the entrance. Inside the training cavern, he shaped the leftover excavated stone into practice targets.

'I can practice the more restrained basic techniques in the cultivation chamber and use more destructive ones like the Fireball Art here. It's more than a hundred jang (over 300 m) from my living quarters, and the passage bends several times, so the impacts shouldn't reach the cultivation chamber.'

From that day onward, explosions and flashes of light never ceased inside Lee Hyun's training cavern.

Ten years later.

Lee Hyun succeeded in reaching Novice proficiency in six new techniques!

【Techniques (Novice): Aura-Concealing Art, Distance-Shrinking Step, Azure Steel Sword Art, Spirit Light Shield, Fireball Art, Aura-Reading Art, ...】

Lee Hyun was moved by his own diligence.

'I don't have any lifespan restrictions, so I could throw away ten years without a care, yet I still managed to learn a whole six techniques. I really am unbelievably diligent! This must be the Korean in me. Whenever I'm doing nothing, I feel like I'm committing some kind of sin...'

After returning from the training cavern to his living quarters, he lay down on his bed and reopened the book he had been reading until recently.

Lately, popular books known as tales of everyday life had become fashionable in Yunze Kingdom. Many dealt with the daily lives and conflicts of people from the mundane world, such as merchants, courtesans, and lower-class commoners, but there were also plenty of utterly ridiculous works among them.

The book Lee Hyun was reading was titled 《Yunze Kingdom's Royal Family Has No Princes, Only Five Peerlessly Beautiful Princesses, and All Five Are Obsessed with Me, a Woodcutter》.

Lee Hyun, who had spent some time living as a woodcutter after first arriving in this world, had been drawn in by the title and found himself buying the book almost without thinking.

The story was quite absurd.

A poor woodcutter happened to rescue one of the princesses in the mountains and entered the royal palace, only to become entangled one after another with the remaining four princesses, who secretly slipped in and out of the palace while concealing their identities. The princesses schemed against one another over the woodcutter, while the King of Yunze Kingdom, rather than stopping his daughters, was actually considering passing the throne to the woodcutter.

By the time Lee Hyun reached the third volume, he could no longer even remember why the woodcutter had gone into the mountains to cut wood in the first place.

Then, when he discovered that the color illustration of the peerlessly beautiful princess that should have appeared at the most important point in the story had been completely torn out, Lee Hyun became quite angry.

His Night Vision Art had already reached a considerable level, allowing him to see even the details of illustrations clearly in the dark without the Faint Light Art. Yet the illustration he had been looking forward to most was missing, taking much of the satisfaction out of having learned the Night Vision Art in the first place.

"How dare a mere mortal from the mundane world sell damaged goods to me, an underground Immortal! I'll teach him a lesson by demanding a refund. Hmm... Now that the royal family came up, I wonder if there's a cultivator market where rogue cultivators gather somewhere near Yunjing?"

He sat up and perched on the edge of the bed.

"With my current strength, entering a cultivator market shouldn't be too dangerous. It's not like I have any enemies out there...."

Over the past ten years, Lee Hyun had confirmed that even after making the rounds of all five spirit fields, he still had plenty of spiritual power left. He could probably create several more without any trouble.

"I should see if I can find spirit plant varieties at the cultivator market that become more valuable the longer they're grown."

...

Three days later.

Rustle―

Lee Hyun's head suddenly popped out of the ground in a deserted forest.

Lee Hyun no longer surfaced directly from Tunnel No. 1 as he had in the past. He first traveled ten li horizontally underground, then made his way upward for roughly another ten li until he reached the surface.

'Now that I have so much spiritual power, the Earth Escape Art is actually pretty convenient to use.'

He wore a new dark blue long robe he had purchased in Qingliu County Seat. An ordinary cloth pouch hung from his waist, hiding the storage pouch inside it, while the Earth Shovel Sword had been tucked deep inside the storage pouch.

His spirit plant seeds and most of his wealth were stored separately in a hidden storeroom inside Tunnel No. 1. The only things he had brought in his storage pouch this time were low-grade spirit stones, some silver, a small pouch of nuts, and the Earth Shovel Sword.

Lee Hyun properly activated the Aura-Concealing Art.

A thin film of energy from the Aura-Concealing Art spread over his skin, partially masking the fluctuations of Primordial True Qi that constantly leaked from his entire body.

He examined himself with the Aura-Reading Art and nodded in satisfaction.

'It's only at the Novice level, but the Aura-Concealing Art still hides my aura surprisingly well.'

Tunnel No. 1 lay three hundred li (about 120 km) southeast of Qingliu County Seat in Linjiang Circuit, Yunze Kingdom, but from the perspective of Yunze Kingdom as a whole, it was still near the far northwestern edge.

The capital, Yunjing, was roughly eight thousand li to the southeast.

A mortal of the mundane world would have needed several months, switching between carts and boats along the way, but it would not take Lee Hyun nearly that long.

On deserted mountain roads, he used the Lightness Art and Distance-Shrinking Step. Near villages or highways, he walked like an ordinary traveler.

Each time Lee Hyun used the Distance-Shrinking Step, spiritual power burst beneath his feet and propelled his body forward.

Using the Distance-Shrinking Step while his body had been lightened by the Lightness Art sent him hurtling ten jang forward with a single step.

'Whoa!'
