Racing through the forest with his body lightened made even his mood feel remarkably buoyant. By his estimation, his speed while traveling this way was roughly equivalent to eighty kilometers per hour in his previous life.

Even while enjoying the journey, he periodically used the Aura-Reading Art and never neglected to stay alert.

Qi Refining cultivators had a pitifully short detection range with their divine sense, so they placed great importance on visual information when keeping watch over their surroundings.

The auras of mortals seen through the Aura-Reading Art were dimmer than candlelight. Young, healthy men had somewhat stronger reddish blood qi, while murky gray energy hung faintly around the bodies of sickly old people.

Among wild animals, the larger the creature, the more vivid its blood qi tended to be.

Cultivators, however, were entirely different.

Any being that contained spiritual power within its body would stand out from afar like a lantern. Of course, that was assuming it was not concealing its realm.

...

The next day.

He had traveled roughly two thousand li.

Lee Hyun had left the highway and was making his way along a narrow mountain path.

Ahead of him, low mountain peaks overlapped one after another, while a thin mist lay between the valleys. He was far from any mortal village.

Lee Hyun activated the Aura-Reading Art out of habit, and a faint light shimmered in his eyes.

'Huh?'

He could see the glow of spiritual power on the mountainside to his right.

There was more than one.

Four streams of aura, each different in size, were moving along the mountain path. Three people were coming outward, while the remaining person was heading farther in with a load on his back.

The spiritual power of all four appeared fainter than Lee Hyun's through the Aura-Reading Art, but they were undoubtedly Qi Refining cultivators!

Lee Hyun stopped walking.

'Could this be a cultivator market?'

Chapter 15

Lee Hyun approached cautiously.

Ancient pines and green bamboo grew together along the mountainside. Between them, a faint trail barely wide enough for one person wound onward.

At the end of the path, white cloud-mist hung like a wall.

To ordinary eyes, it looked like nothing more than a narrow valley shrouded in fog. But when Lee Hyun examined it with the Aura-Reading Art, he saw countless threads of spiritual power woven together in orderly patterns within the mist.

The fog remained unmoved even by the wind, and some sort of formation seemed to have been laid out inside it.

Lee Hyun kept his distance and observed the interior for a while.

Beyond the formation, he could faintly make out tiled roofs and wooden pavilions. A small stream flowed along the valley, with shops and stalls stretching along both sides.

At one stall, wooden boxes filled with medicinal herbs were stacked in piles, while another had talismans and worn magic tools spread across a cloth. Cultivators leisurely came and went, drinking tea or haggling over prices.

The cultivator who had entered carrying a load on his back had already disappeared among the stalls.

The place was hardly extravagant, but it had the quiet charm of a mountain marketplace from the mundane world with a few mysterious cultivation shops mixed in.

The peaceful atmosphere put Lee Hyun somewhat at ease, and he cautiously approached the entrance.

Near the entrance to the formation stood a small stone stele, and three early Qi Refining cultivators who had come out from inside were gathered in front of it.

A middle-aged man in a worn blue robe, a young woman with a basket of herbs strapped to her back, and a fat man carrying a bundle of pelts were speaking quietly among themselves, apparently acquainted.

Had Lee Hyun not noticed the storage pouches at their waists, he might have mistaken them for ordinary mortals.

Lee Hyun hesitated for a moment.

For more than a hundred years, the only people he had properly spoken with were merchants selling nuts and workers at inns.

Cultivators could be dangerous.

But if he wanted to make use of a cultivator market, he would eventually have to ask someone about the entrance and its rules.

As far as the cultivation world went, the cultivators before him at least looked like the less dangerous sort.

'I can't keep avoiding everyone forever.'

Lee Hyun checked once more that the Aura-Concealing Art was functioning properly, then walked onto the trail.

Rustle–

At the sound of his footsteps, all three cultivators turned their heads at once.

The middle-aged man's hand moved toward the storage pouch at his waist. The young woman took a step back, while the fat man instinctively pulled his bundle against his chest.

Clear tension appeared on their faces.

In particular, the moment the middle-aged man narrowed his eyes as though trying to inspect Lee Hyun's aura, all the color drained from his face.

'So they really are cultivators.'

Lee Hyun had heard that rogue cultivators were highly wary. It was only natural for them to tense up after encountering a strange cultivator on a deserted mountain.

Lee Hyun put on the friendliest expression he could manage and cupped his hands together.

"Greetings."

All three flinched at once. Paying no mind to their reaction, Lee Hyun asked politely,

"I'm a wandering rogue cultivator. Is this a cultivator market?"

Silence followed for a moment.

The oldest of the three, the middle-aged man, hurriedly bowed.

"Y-yes! That's right, Senior. This is Songyun Market. It's a small cultivator market mainly used by rogue cultivators in northwestern Yunze Kingdom."

"Songyun Market...."

It seemed he had found the right place after all.

Lee Hyun smiled and asked again.

"Senior? I'm also a Qi Refining cultivator. I lack experience and was hoping to seek some guidance. Is there any special procedure required to enter the cultivator market, fellow Daoist?"

"F-fellow Daoist?!"

The middle-aged man's face turned deathly pale. The other two hurriedly bowed as well.

"Senior, how could you possibly address early Qi Refining rogue cultivators like us as fellow Daoists? Such an address is far beyond what we deserve."

"If we have offended you in some way, please tell us. We beg you, please do not test us like this!"

The three of them looked utterly flustered, as though Lee Hyun had laid some kind of trap for them.

'Huh?'

Lee Hyun was bewildered.

"Wait. Why are you calling me Senior? Am I not also an early Qi Refining cultivator?"

Even deeper fear appeared on their faces.

Apparently thinking Lee Hyun intended to test them to the bitter end, the middle-aged man broke out in a cold sweat. Yet he seemed even more afraid that refusing to answer would bring greater disaster, so he cautiously spoke.

"Senior, although we are merely insignificant early Qi Refining rogue cultivators... we have at least learned the Aura-Reading Art."

"What does that have to do with anything?"

"How could a cultivator whose entire body is glowing like Senior's possibly be a Qi Refining cultivator?"

This time, the young woman carrying the herb basket hurriedly chimed in.

"That's right. Senior's entire body is glowing evenly. Surely your realm is so high that even the residual spiritual power overflowing through your body shines as brightly as our dantians?"

The fat man nodded desperately.

"Exactly! We have never even heard of a cultivator whose entire body is uniformly filled with spiritual power. How profound must Senior's abilities be to display such an absurd phenomenon? For us to dare call Senior a fellow Daoist would be an unforgivable act of disrespect!"

'Ah....'

Only then did Lee Hyun realize the problem.

The Aura-Concealing Art he had obtained from Qinghe Valley worked by enveloping the entire surface of the body in a veil, reducing the fluctuations of spiritual power leaking out from within.

It reduced the intensity of the light visible through the Aura-Reading Art, but it did not change where that light appeared.

'So that's what it was!'

Lee Hyun forced out a hearty laugh.

"I-I see! Haha. I wasn't trying to put you fellows in an awkward position."

The three did not dare respond.

"I won't enter the cultivator market. Don't worry about me and go about your business."

Lee Hyun used the Lightness Art and Distance-Shrinking Step to descend the mountain path.

...

Only after Lee Hyun had completely vanished from sight did all three let out sighs of relief at once.

"Th-thank goodness. At first, I thought that Senior was...."

The middle-aged man hurriedly raised a finger to his lips.

[Shh! Use voice transmission. The range of a great cultivator's divine sense is beyond anything we can imagine.]

The young woman startled and immediately shut her mouth.

[My apologies.]

The fat man cautiously asked,

[Still, he doesn't seem as frightening as I expected. He didn't get angry even after we saw through his realm.]

The middle-aged man looked at him with displeasure.

[What foolishness are you spouting? Have you still not realized how deep that Senior's schemes run?]

[What do you mean?]

[Did you not see how, even after being exposed, he perfectly imitated the crude Lightness Art and Distance-Shrinking Step of an early Qi Refining cultivator? Look at that terrifying patience, hiding his true identity to the very end. If I had not used the Aura-Reading Art, even I would have believed he was truly an early Qi Refining cultivator.]

The young woman's face went pale again.

[Could he be... a bandit cultivator who wanders around pretending to be weak, then kills anyone who provokes him and steals their possessions?]

[There is a good chance. He intends to rob others without even tarnishing his own reputation.]

[How could that be... Now people even want a righteous justification for committing robbery....]

The middle-aged man nodded gravely.

[There are so many schemes in the cultivation world these days that it has become impossible to tell who is a bandit cultivator. I've heard that some great cultivators wander around concealing their realms like that, then if someone behaves even slightly rudely toward them, they reveal their hidden realm, rebuke the person, and seize their possessions.]

The middle-aged man looked fearfully in the direction Lee Hyun had disappeared.

[Fortunately, that Senior was poor at concealing his realm, so we weren't deceived.]

...

Lee Hyun, who had somehow been mistaken for a bandit cultivator, did not return directly to Tunnel No. 1 even after leaving the mountain path.

He traveled another hundred-odd li (about 40 km) using the Distance-Shrinking Step, changing direction three separate times. At times, he followed the flowing water of a mountain stream, and at others, he used the Earth Escape Art to pass through the foot of a mountain.

Considering the possibility that someone might be tracking him, he first traveled far in the opposite direction from Tunnel No. 1, then circled back in a wide loop.

...

A few days later.

Inside the cultivation chamber of Tunnel No. 1, Lee Hyun continuously maintained the Aura-Concealing Art while examining his own body with the Aura-Reading Art.

"This won't do."

The three cultivators had been right.

When he used the Aura-Concealing Art, his apparent realm did decrease, but the dimmed light spread evenly across his entire body from head to toe.

Compared to an ordinary cultivator, the sight was bizarre beyond belief. There was no way he could pass for a normal Qi Refining cultivator.

"If I enter a cultivator market like this, everyone will think I'm strange. Being mistaken for a high-realm cultivator isn't necessarily bad, but...."

If others mistook him for a powerful cultivator, they would be less likely to provoke him first. But that would also make him more likely to attract the attention of truly powerful cultivators.

If even a single Foundation Establishment cultivator or higher came to investigate what realm this mysterious cultivator had reached, Lee Hyun would have no way to deal with it.

"Wait, what about the Spirit-Concealing Art instead of the Aura-Concealing Art? I think it said the principles were different...."

Lee Hyun postponed his visit to the cultivator market and took down a wooden tablet from the shelf on which he had recorded the mnemonic formula of the Spirit-Concealing Art.

...

One year later.

Lee Hyun had reached Novice proficiency in a new technique!

【Technique (Novice): Spirit-Concealing Art, ...】

After using the Spirit-Concealing Art, Lee Hyun examined himself with the Aura-Reading Art.

'Still not enough... Hm?'

His entire body still glowed, but Lee Hyun noticed a difference between the Spirit-Concealing Art and the Aura-Concealing Art. The surface of his body looked mottled.

His palms and forearms had grown noticeably darker, while his thighs were somewhat brighter. His hands and arms were precisely the areas he had spent the most time practicing on over the past year.

'Could it be...?'

After studying it for a while, Lee Hyun discovered a new possibility in the difference between the Spirit-Concealing Art and the Aura-Concealing Art.

If the Aura-Concealing Art was an active disguise technique that masked spiritual power fluctuations generated within the body, then the Spirit-Concealing Art was more like a passive disguise technique that controlled the body so those fluctuations were never generated in the first place.

In other words, if the Aura-Concealing Art was like covering a lamp with cloth, the Spirit-Concealing Art was like lowering the lamp's wicks one by one.

The Spirit-Concealing Art had two advantages over the Aura-Concealing Art: it consumed even less spiritual power, and it could selectively conceal specific parts of the body.

Its disadvantage, however, was that it took a long time to cultivate. Because of this, most cultivators preferred to learn the much quicker Aura-Concealing Art, and almost no one bothered spending precious time mastering the Spirit-Concealing Art.

'I see! Once I reach Major Attainment in the Spirit-Concealing Art, I can conceal every part of my body except for an area the size of a dantian.'

Fifty years passed.

Lee Hyun had reached Major Attainment in the Spirit-Concealing Art!

And that was not all. He had newly reached Novice proficiency in the Farsight Art, Keen Hearing Art, and Scent-Tracking Art recorded in The Six Arts of Perception, while raising the seven techniques that had previously remained at Novice proficiency to Minor Attainment.

【Spiritual Power: 83 → 101】

【Technique (Novice): Farsight Art, Keen Hearing Art, Scent-Tracking Art, ...】

【Technique (Minor Attainment): Aura-Concealing Art, Lightness Art, Distance-Shrinking Step, Azure Steel Sword Art, Spirit Light Shield, Fireball Art, Aura-Reading Art, ...】

【Technique (Major Attainment): Spirit-Concealing Art】

Since he had spent those fifty years focusing on the Spirit-Concealing Art, he had not invested much time in cultivating his spiritual power.

Even so, he had made noticeable progress in eleven techniques, so his actual combat strength had risen considerably.

With the Spirit-Concealing Art active, Lee Hyun looked down at his body through the Aura-Reading Art. Not a trace of spiritual power light leaked from anywhere on his body. Through the Aura-Reading Art alone, he looked less like a cultivator and more like a vigorous young mortal with abundant qi and blood.

When Lee Hyun focused his consciousness, light bloomed from a fist-sized area below his navel. The light gathered into a round mass like the dantian of an ordinary early Qi Refining cultivator.

A smile appeared on Lee Hyun's face.

"It worked! Now I can look like a mortal if I want, or disguise myself as an ordinary early Qi Refining cultivator."

At a thought, he could freely adjust the brightness of the light from the level of someone who had only just entered Qi Refining Stage 1 all the way up to Qi Refining Stage 2.

...

Even while cultivating the Spirit-Concealing Art, Lee Hyun made his rounds of the five spirit fields once every ten days.

Spirit Field No. 1-1 currently contained 119 Bone-Rot Flowers, 298 Yin Soul Grass plants, 79 Purple Poison Orchids, and 58 Earth Vein Flower plants with more than fifty-three years of medicinal potency.

Because Earth Vein Flowers grew multiple stems from a single root system, Lee Hyun counted each connected cluster of roots as one plant.

The other four spirit fields contained 478 Bone-Rot Flowers, 1,195 Yin Soul Grass plants, 319 Purple Poison Orchids, and 238 Earth Vein Flower plants with just over twenty years of medicinal potency.

Not every specimen he planted had survived. On rare occasions, roots rotted, or changes in the flow of groundwater caused one side of a spirit field to become excessively damp and create problems.

Even so, the overall survival rate remained extremely high.

The medicinal potency of the spirit plants kept increasing, but Lee Hyun still had no sense whatsoever of how valuable they were.

"Just how much would a fifty-three-year-old Bone-Rot Flower be worth? Hehe...."

Watching the spirit herbs in all five spirit fields grow more precious with every passing year filled him with satisfaction.

"I've reached Major Attainment in the Spirit-Concealing Art, and I can hide my realm now. It's finally time to get some fresh air outside. I should find some different spirit plant seeds to grow as well."

Lee Hyun decided to search for another cultivator market rather than return to Songyun Market. The three Qi Refining cultivators he had encountered outside Songyun Market fifty years ago might be shocked if they saw his face again.

"I'll go to Yunjing, my original destination. A cultivator market near the capital should have more goods than Songyun Market, and there should be some force maintaining order there too. Of course, I could still run into those three from fifty years ago at another cultivator market in Yunze Kingdom... I suppose I should at least put on a simple disguise."

Lee Hyun prepared to head out. This time, he carefully altered his appearance before departing.

He rubbed dirt onto his face to roughen his skin, changed the shape of his eyebrows and beard from fifty years ago, and styled his hair somewhat differently. He also dusted it lightly with gray powder to make it look faintly streaked with white.

"I should look for a technique or skill that can alter my appearance too. If I keep wandering around with the same face for decades on end, it'll cause trouble eventually...."

Finally, Lee Hyun activated the Spirit-Concealing Art to conceal the spiritual power fluctuations throughout his body, leaving only a glow at the level of Qi Refining Stage 2 beneath his navel.

After checking himself several times with the Aura-Reading Art, Lee Hyun nodded.

"Now I really do look ordinary."

Five days later.

Yunjing, the capital of Yunze Kingdom.

Lee Hyun stood atop a hill and looked down below.

A vast city stretched out before him.

Three layers of city walls of differing heights stretched across the land. The outermost wall extended endlessly to either side, both ends disappearing into the haze along the horizon. Even from atop the hill, Lee Hyun could not take in the entirety of Yunjing at a glance.

Countless villages, estates, and markets sprawled outside the walls. The outskirts alone looked as large as dozens of ordinary county seats combined.

The massive Yunshui River, flowing in from the northwest, split into several branches before reaching the capital. Dozens of waterways passed beneath the city walls and continued into the city, while hundreds of bridges large and small spanned the river and canals.

Grain barges piled high with grain, ornate multi-decked ships, and flat ferries crowded the waterways.

Most of the roofs in the outer city were gray or black, but within the inner city where the royal palace stood, red walls and golden tiles gleamed brilliantly beneath the sunlight.

At the very center of the city towered a nine-story pavilion several times taller than the surrounding buildings. A massive banner bearing the image of clouds fluttered from its roof.

"It's huge...."

The sheer scale of Yunjing's outskirts alone made his chest swell with awe.

'Even the great capitals of China throughout history might have been smaller than this... And this is only the capital of a single kingdom, not even an empire. I shouldn't underestimate a nation of mortals.'

Perhaps because the world itself was so vast, its technological level might have been low, but the sheer scale of the city was astonishing.

The highway leading toward the city gates was packed with carts and people. Officials and scholars arriving from the provinces, merchant caravans transporting goods, and farmers leading cattle and horses moved in long lines, kicking up clouds of dust.

Scholars and nobles in silk robes, along with bustling merchants, flowed endlessly along the main roads, while music poured ceaselessly from teahouses and winehouses.

It did not seem as though finding cultivators would be difficult.

Lee Hyun used the Aura-Reading Art from atop the hill, but the light of qi and blood radiating from countless living beings blended together like a vast fog. There were also lights that he suspected belonged to cultivators, but at such a great distance they blurred into one another, making it nearly impossible to tell who each one belonged to.

'I don't know whether it's because my proficiency is lacking... but it's difficult to distinguish distant auras with the Aura-Reading Art.'

This time, he used the Farsight Art to look around and take in the sights. As the name suggested, the Farsight Art was a technique for seeing far into the distance.

'Hm? That's!'

Inside the outer city, Lee Hyun spotted someone in luxurious clothing with a storage pouch hanging from their waist. After that, he lost track of time and spent roughly one shichen (two hours) sightseeing around the capital, during which he spotted two more people wearing storage pouches.

'Just as I thought, there are quite a few cultivators here.'

...

Outside the western gate sprawled a vast market formed by traveling merchants and farmers who had been unable to enter the city.

Between stalls selling grain and vegetables stood shops piled high with medicinal herbs, hides, and timber. Fish from the Yunshui River continually leapt from wooden tubs filled to the brim.

Dressed like an ordinary scholar in a simple pale jade-colored robe, Lee Hyun strolled leisurely through the market. He had bought it nearby as a memento of his arrival in Yunjing.

'Hm?'

At the edge of the market, Lee Hyun spotted an early Qi Refining cultivator!

He was a thin man who looked to be around fifty years old. Deep wrinkles lined his sun-darkened face, and he wore faded gray clothes.

Mud-covered roots and dark green aquatic plants were spread across a bamboo mat in front of him. At first glance, he looked like nothing more than an ordinary herb gatherer selling plants he had dug up by the river.

But through the Aura-Reading Art, Lee Hyun could clearly see a faint light flowing from below the man's navel. The light was gathered into a round mass within his dantian, almost identical to the appearance Lee Hyun was imitating.

The man's realm appeared to be around Qi Refining Stage 3.

After briefly checking his surroundings, Lee Hyun approached the man's stall.

"What medicinal herbs are these?"

"Water Root Grass and Green Fern Leaf. They both grow in water. Water Root Grass is used to reduce fever, while Green Fern Leaf can be crushed and applied to wounds to prevent festering."

"Are they spirit herbs that cultivators use as well?"

The man's eyes instantly sharpened.

Instead of answering, he narrowed his eyes as though examining the area below Lee Hyun's navel. After a moment, some of the wariness faded from his expression.

"Water Root Grass that contains spiritual qi can be classified as a spirit herb, but everything here is a mundane herb. It seems, fellow Daoist, that you didn't come here to buy herbs."

'He finally called me fellow Daoist!'

Lee Hyun was moved. The fifty years he had spent cultivating the Spirit-Concealing Art had not been wasted!

"I am... Li Dongyi. I'm a rogue cultivator who cultivated elsewhere and has only just arrived in Yunjing. I was looking for a nearby cultivator market, but I don't know anyone here, so I took the liberty of approaching you."

Thinking of Tunnel No. 1, Lee Hyun gave the alias Li Dongyi.

"I'm Zhang Ping. I'm a rogue cultivator who lives around the Yunshui River. You said you were looking for a cultivator market? The most dependable choice would be... Cuiyun Market to the south. It's more than five hundred li from here, though, so getting there on foot can be a bit of a bother."

"Is it always open?"

"It is. It's not particularly large, but since it's near the capital, there is a decent variety of goods. It's managed by the Cuiyun Society, a small rogue-cultivator organization."

"What kind of organization is the Cuiyun Society?"

"Nothing special. Some rogue cultivators at mid Qi Refining or above who have lived in Yunze Kingdom for a long time formed it to protect the cultivator market and help one another."

"Is there an entrance fee to enter Cuiyun Market?"

"Buying goods and coming and going are free. However, if you sell anything in the cultivator market, you must pay one-tenth of the sale price to the Cuiyun Society. It isn't a small sum, but if a dispute arises inside the cultivator market, the Cuiyun Society will step in to settle it."

When Lee Hyun nodded, Zhang Ping asked,

"Leaving the cultivator market aside... since you've come all the way to the capital of Yunze Kingdom, are you also planning to join the Fengtian Bureau?"

"What is the Fengtian Bureau?"

Chapter 16

Zhang Ping was momentarily at a loss for words at Lee Hyun's question.

"It seems you truly have come from a very distant place, fellow Daoist."

"I only arrived in Yunze Kingdom recently."

"Then it is no wonder you did not know."

Zhang Ping explained as he neatly gathered the Water Root Grass on the mat to one side.

"The Fengtian Bureau is an institution established by the Yunze royal family to recruit rogue cultivators as Retainers."

"They recruit rogue cultivators as Retainers?"

"That's right. Yunze Kingdom has almost no worthwhile spirit veins, as you know. There isn't a single proper cultivation sect, and most clans that produced Foundation Establishment cultivators left for other places in search of better spirit veins. I heard that even counting the Fengtian Bureau's high-ranking Retainers, there are only a handful of Foundation Establishment cultivators currently staying in Yunze Kingdom."

Zhang Ping glanced toward the capital.

"But poor spirit veins don't mean that nothing involving cultivators ever happens. Demon beasts sometimes descend from the mountains, and spirit insects sometimes breed in the rivers. Bandit cultivators may target members of the royal family or wealthy merchant companies, and rogue cultivators from other countries sometimes cross the border."

"Do the Fengtian Bureau's Retainers deal with such matters?"

"For the most part."

According to Zhang Ping, the rogue cultivators affiliated with the Fengtian Bureau were broadly divided into Retainers and guest retainers.

Retainers stayed at Fengtian Bureau offices in Yunjing or the provinces and received a monthly stipend. The royal family guaranteed them a residence and official status, and sometimes provided them with spirit stones and pills or granted them the right to gather spirit herbs on mountains owned by the royal family.

In return, they had to carry out assigned duties, such as guarding the royal family, subjugating demon beasts that appeared near Yunjing, or escorting valuable goods.

Guest retainers, on the other hand, were rogue cultivators whose names were entered on the Fengtian Bureau's rolls but who otherwise lived freely.

They received no monthly stipend, but upon completing missions, they could be rewarded with spirit stones, spirit herbs, pills, talismans, cultivation arts, techniques, and the like. Nor did they need to swear loyalty to the royal family or remain in Yunjing.

Naturally, the reward for completing a single mission was modest compared with the benefits enjoyed by Retainers. The quality of the rewards offered by the Fengtian Bureau also fell short of what a proper cultivation sect could provide.

"So guest retainers are basically mercenaries."

"More or less."

"Then... if you're going to join the Fengtian Bureau anyway, wouldn't it be better to become a Retainer? It doesn't seem like there would be many dangerous jobs in the mundane world."

Zhang Ping laughed.

"Not necessarily. If you're taking the royal stipend, you may be called upon for dangerous work."

"You mean subjugating demon beasts?"

"That too, but there is another, more important reason the Fengtian Bureau is recruiting Retainers and guest retainers on such a large scale."

Zhang Ping lowered his voice slightly.

"Qianyang Kingdom."

"Qianyang Kingdom?"

"It shares a border with the south of Yunze Kingdom. Its territory is at least four times the size of Yunze Kingdom's, and its population and military strength are greater beyond comparison."

According to Zhang Ping, Qianyang Kingdom also had poor spirit veins, preventing cultivation forces from establishing themselves there.

However, the martial path had developed to an exceptional degree in Qianyang Kingdom.

Martial sects and clans with traditions stretching back hundreds or even thousands of years could be found throughout the country, and even the royal court taught its soldiers internal energy methods and combined-attack formations.

Not only did it have far more Transformation Realm experts than Yunze Kingdom, it also had many more who had reached the Profound Realm. There were even rumors that someone within the military directly under the royal family had surpassed the limits of the Profound Realm.

"That certainly sounds dangerous. I've heard that a Profound Realm expert can contend with a Qi Refining cultivator."

"More than merely contend with one. If a Qi Refining cultivator with little combat experience is ambushed by a Profound Realm expert, he could die on the spot. Qianyang Kingdom has also spent many years developing group combat methods specifically designed to fight Qi Refining cultivators, such as the Interlocking Sword Formation. They truly are not to be underestimated."

Zhang Ping gave a bitter smile.

"Qianyang Kingdom was always a land where the martial path flourished. But until several hundred years ago, they also welcomed cultivators as Retainers, much like Yunze Kingdom does. Then a few cultivators behaved so outrageously that the royal family's dignity suffered a severe blow. After that, the court began reducing its reliance on cultivators and started training martial artists on a massive scale. By now, the results have been remarkable, and they have been using martial artists to push the border northward little by little."

Qianyang Kingdom had raised large armies and invaded Yunze Kingdom several times. However, Qianyang's forces had been bogged down by Yunze Kingdom's river- and marsh-filled terrain, while even its martial experts were kept in check by the Fengtian Bureau's Retainers, resulting in heavy losses each time.

Afterward, rather than wage full-scale war, Qianyang Kingdom adopted a strategy of gradually seizing border fortresses, mines, and strategic points along the waterways. Even recently, clashes large and small had continued throughout the borderlands.

"I see. But if Qianyang Kingdom is four times larger than Yunze Kingdom and has a much greater military, why is it called a kingdom rather than an empire?"

Zhang Ping burst out laughing.

"Haha! How dare a dynasty of the mundane world claim to be an empire?"

"Would someone actually stop them if they declared their ruler an emperor?"

"All of this lies within Kun Kingdom."

"Kun Kingdom?"

"More than ten mundane kingdoms, including Yunze Kingdom, Anling Kingdom to the north, and Qianyang Kingdom to the south, all lie within Kun Kingdom, a Tier 4 cultivation nation."

It was a concept Lee Hyun had never heard of before.

"A cultivation nation? Don't tell me... the borders of countries founded by mortals and the cultivation nations spoken of by cultivators are different?"

"That's right. Mortals generally divide countries using mountains, rivers, cities, and highways as borders. When a kingdom prospers, it expands its territory, and when it declines, neighboring countries seize its lands. But cultivation nations are divided according to spirit veins and the spheres of influence of sects, and a single cultivation nation encompasses a far greater area than a mundane country."

"Then what forces govern Kun Kingdom?"

"The Biluo Sect and the Danxiao Sect."

Zhang Ping pointed east.

"About thirty thousand li (about 12,000 km) east of Yunjing lies an enormous mountain range called the Biluo Range. A Tier 4 spirit vein runs through it, and the Biluo Sect, where a Nascent Soul great cultivator resides, is located there."

"Where is the Danxiao Sect?"

"If you travel another ten thousand li east from the Biluo Range, you'll reach the Danxiao Range. A Tier 4 spirit vein runs through that place as well, and the Danxiao Sect occupies it. From Yunjing, that puts it roughly forty thousand li to the east."

"Does the Danxiao Sect also have a Nascent Soul cultivator?"

"Yes. As far as I know, the Biluo Sect and Danxiao Sect are the only sects in Kun Kingdom with Nascent Soul cultivators."

Zhang Ping lowered his voice for a moment.

"There are also several sects and cultivation clans below them led by Golden Core cultivators, but I hear that most major matters concerning Kun Kingdom as a whole are decided according to the wishes of those two great sects."

"What sort of major matters?"

"For example, deciding the taboos cultivators must observe. If demonic cultivators massacre mortals on a large scale or conduct blood sacrifices, they may send enforcement cultivators after them. And if forces from another cultivation nation invade Kun Kingdom, I hear the two great sects step forward to deal with them."

Lee Hyun organized the relationships in his mind.

"I see. If a mundane country proclaimed itself an empire, the great cultivation sects really would laugh at it."

Zhang Ping stroked his beard.

"So even if Qianyang Kingdom swallowed every other kingdom within Kun Kingdom, it would still be difficult for its ruler to proclaim himself emperor without at least the tacit approval of the Biluo Sect and Danxiao Sect. No matter how vast a mortal army might be, it could never stand against a Nascent Soul cultivator."

"Then in the eyes of the two great sects, the war between Yunze Kingdom and Qianyang Kingdom must be nothing more than a quarrel between mortals within the same enclosure called Kun Kingdom."

Zhang Ping nodded.

"Exactly. It isn't something worth the involvement of the two great sects. In fact, cultivators at Foundation Establishment and above do not recklessly interfere in mundane wars. If they killed mortals by the thousands or tens of thousands, enforcement cultivators from the Biluo Sect or Danxiao Sect might come looking for them."

"Are Qi Refining cultivators allowed to?"

"Not unconditionally. Naturally, even a Qi Refining cultivator would offend the two sects if he slaughtered mortals indiscriminately. If someone killed countless mortals to conduct a blood sacrifice, or practiced demonic cultivation arts using human essence blood and souls, he would be hunted to the ends of the earth. But as long as they do nothing of the sort, I hear the great sects do not concern themselves with every Qi Refining cultivator."

"So that's why mundane countries can hire Qi Refining cultivators."

"That's right. Serving as a Retainer of a mundane country, fighting martial experts, and even participating in wars are generally not considered problems. In the eyes of the great cultivation sects, perhaps Qi Refining rogue cultivators and the martial experts of the mundane world are all equally mundane beings."

'Mundane beings....'

Lee Hyun felt a little strange.

To him, a late Qi Refining cultivator was an immensely powerful expert. Yet to the Nascent Soul cultivators of the Biluo Sect and Danxiao Sect, the entire Qi Refining realm apparently seemed to belong in much the same category as martial artists of the mundane world.

"Is Great Yan Kingdom also part of Kun Kingdom?"

"Great Yan Kingdom? You mean that backwater north of Anling Kingdom?"

"Yes."

"I don't believe it belongs to Kun Kingdom... I heard it falls under another cultivation nation to the north. But I don't know much about affairs over there either."

"I see."

'Hmm... Is that why I never heard anything about the Biluo Sect or Danxiao Sect when I was in Qinghe Valley....'

At that moment, an old man wearing a conical hat stopped in front of Zhang Ping's stall.

"How much for the Water Root Grass?"

"Three coins per bundle."

The old man carefully examined the condition of the roots before picking up two bundles. Six coins dropped into Zhang Ping's palm.

"Next time, shake off a little more of the dirt before bringing it."

"Hmph. The dirt keeps the roots from drying out."

After the customer left, Zhang Ping tucked the coins into the worn pouch at his waist. Lee Hyun suddenly grew curious.

"Fellow Daoist Zhang, you're a cultivator, yet you sell medicinal herbs from the mundane world."

Zhang Ping smiled bitterly.

"I've been stuck at Qi Refining Stage 3 for more than fifty years."

"Fifty years?"

"I'm eighty-four this year, so there's almost no chance I'll ever make another breakthrough. I've grown tired of spending all day shut away in my cave abode cultivating."

Zhang Ping looked at the people in the street.

Peddlers carrying packs shouted loudly to attract customers, while children ran around spinning wooden tops at one side of the market.

"So these days I gather medicinal herbs by the river and bring them to the market to sell. It's less about making money than coming out to see people. A day feels far too long when I sit alone in my cave abode, but time passes quickly when I come here."

"I see."

Lee Hyun felt a sense of affinity toward Zhang Ping.

It was regrettable that the man had nearly given up on cultivation, but judging from how thoroughly he had explained everything to a rogue cultivator he had only just met, he seemed to be a genuinely kind person.

"Thank you for explaining everything so kindly."

"If you're grateful, buy a bundle of Water Root Grass."

Lee Hyun thought of the low-grade spirit stones inside his storage pouch.

He would not have minded giving Zhang Ping one as thanks for the explanation. Considering that spirit plants already several decades old continued to grow in Tunnel No. 1, a single low-grade spirit stone might not seem like much money to him in the future.

But Lee Hyun quickly changed his mind.

'If a Qi Refining Stage 2 rogue cultivator hands over a low-grade spirit stone after hearing a simple explanation, instead of feeling grateful, he might start wondering how many spirit stones I have.'

Zhang Ping might look good-natured, but there was no telling who nearby might be listening.

Lee Hyun bought several bundles of Water Root Grass with mundane coins.

The Water Root Grass was nothing more than a mundane herb, but if he planted it near the aquifer in Tunnel No. 1 and left it there for many years, there was no telling what changes it might undergo.

"Do you happen to know when the Fengtian Bureau recruits Retainers?"

"The Fengtian Bureau welcomes cultivators at any time, so there is no need to worry about timing."

"I see."

"And if you're looking for Cuiyun Market, follow the highway outside the South Gate for about five hundred li, then find Cuiyun Mountain. Infuse spiritual power into the green stele at the foot of the mountain, and the entrance will appear."

"Thank you."

Lee Hyun bid Zhang Ping farewell and stepped away from the stall.

'He's a kind man. If I meet him again, I should bring him some of the Qinghe Rice I have left.'

...

Lee Hyun headed to a quiet spot on the outskirts of Yunjing.

After confirming that no one was nearby, he was about to head to Cuiyun Market when he suddenly remembered the spirit field in Tunnel No. 1.

'Ah, right... I need to use the Spirit Rain Art every ten days. Should I go straight back?'

Lee Hyun calculated the date when he had last cast the Spirit Rain Art. There were still about five days before he needed to use it again.

'No, Cuiyun Market is practically right nearby anyway. Since I've come all this way, I might as well stop by the cultivator market before going back.'

Tunnel No. 1 was more than eight thousand li northwest of his current location. Cuiyun Market, on the other hand, was only about five hundred li south of Yunjing, and if Lee Hyun ran at full speed, he could reach it in under two shichen (about four hours).

...

Cuiyun Mountain was not as tall as the surrounding mountains, but long banks of blue clouds lingered beneath its peak.

When Lee Hyun channeled spiritual power into the green stele at the foot of the mountain, a narrow path appeared where there had seemed to be a sheer cliff.

At the end of the path lay a small valley that appeared to be roughly the same size as Songyun Market.

Wooden shops stood in rows along both sides of the valley, while several tents and stalls occupied the open area in the center. A little over ten rogue cultivators browsed goods or haggled over prices.

The cultivator guarding the entrance looked Lee Hyun over once before speaking.

"Private fighting is forbidden inside the cultivator market. If you sell anything, you must pay one-tenth of its price to the Cuiyun Society."

"I'm only here to buy."

"Go in."

Lee Hyun entered the cultivator market. The first thing that caught his eye was a shop selling magic tools, but he forced himself to look away.

'I came here today to buy spirit plant seeds.'

Lee Hyun slowly browsed the area where spirit plant seeds were sold and first purchased seeds of a spirit herb called the Yin Water Lotus.

The Yin Water Lotus grew in cold, lightless water, and the lotus seeds produced by mature plants were said to be popular among alchemists. Its drawback was that it took at least fifty years before the first flowers bloomed. Because of that, it was difficult to find Qi Refining cultivators willing to grow them.

As he continued looking around, Lee Hyun finally stopped in front of one stall. Dried roots, seeds, and small pots were packed closely together across it. The owner was an elderly Qi Refining cultivator who had lost nearly all his hair.

"Do you have any spirit plants that can be grown somewhere without sunlight?"

The old man rummaged through his goods for a moment before taking out a small wooden box.

"These are Stone Honey Peach seeds."

"Peaches?"

"They look similar. But unlike ordinary peach trees, they dislike sunlight. They grow by absorbing water qi and earth qi that have seeped into the ground, so they can even be cultivated inside caves."

Lee Hyun's eyes lit up.

"When do they bear fruit?"

"I'm afraid that even under the best circumstances, it takes thirty years."

"Then I suppose they're not very popular."

"Well, that's true. Qi Refining cultivators like us don't have enough lifespan to spare thirty years carefully raising something like this. Even after thirty years, they'll only produce one or two fruits a year for the next few decades. I'm told that the older the tree becomes, the more fruit it bears and the better the flavor gets. The flesh of a hundred-year-old Stone Honey Peach is said to be sweeter than honey while still cold and crisp."

"Have you tried one yourself?"

"Where would someone like me ever get the chance to eat a hundred-year-old Stone Honey Peach? I read about it in an ancient text."

"What medicinal effects does it have?"

The old man shrugged.

"It absorbs spiritual qi, so it certainly qualifies as a spirit fruit, but the part of my ancient text describing its effects was damaged, so I don't know."

Lee Hyun gazed at the Stone Honey Peach seeds and imagined what they would look like a hundred years from now. He pictured himself sitting beneath the tree, plucking and eating one honey-sweet peach after another.

"I'll buy them."

...

Lee Hyun spent two low-grade spirit stones on several Yin Water Lotus and Stone Honey Peach seeds.

After leaving Cuiyun Market, an idea suddenly occurred to him.

'If I collect the rainwater from the Spirit Rain Art in a reservoir beforehand and find some way to release it into the spirit field at regular intervals while I'm away....'

Before heading to Tunnel No. 1, Lee Hyun returned to Yunjing first.

...

Once he reached Yunjing, Lee Hyun asked around until he found a district in the outer city where craftsmen lived. Workshops that made waterwheels, watermills, farming tools, and similar equipment were clustered there.

Displayed in front of the largest workshop were water clocks of various sizes and intricate wooden gears.

When Lee Hyun entered, an old craftsman missing two fingers stopped sanding a wooden board and looked up.

"What brings you here?"

"There's something I'd like to have made."

"Tell me."

Lee Hyun considered it for a moment before asking.

"Could you make a device that stores water in a large container beforehand, then releases a fixed amount into a field once every ten days?"

The old craftsman frowned.

"Once every ten days?"

"Yes."

"Without anyone touching it?"

"That's right."

"How large is the field?"

"It's two zhang (about 6 m) wide and sixteen zhang long, roughly half a mu (about 330 m²)."

"Where will you get the water?"

"I can collect it in a large reservoir beforehand. I only need the water inside to be released into the field in a fixed amount at intervals of around ten days."

The old craftsman rubbed his beard in thought.

"If the water is already prepared, there would be no need for a complicated mechanism."

He picked up a brush and drew a large reservoir on a wooden board, with a water container beneath it. A horizontal axle ran through the middle of the container.

"You make the water drip slowly from the reservoir into this container. After about ten days, once a certain amount has collected, the front becomes heavy and tips over on its own."

The old craftsman added a drawing of the tilted container and a channel running beneath it.

"Then all the collected water pours into the field at once. Once the container empties, the stone counterweight at the back returns it to its original position."

Lee Hyun looked down at the drawing.

"Simple."

"The simpler a device like this is, the more reliable it will be. Does it need to operate exactly once every ten days?"

"A little variation is fine."

"Then this method is best."

The old craftsman asked how many furrows there were in the field and how much water needed to be released each time. Lee Hyun explained the layout of one of the spirit fields he managed.

"I'll make a small test device first. Come back in a month."

"How much will it cost?"

"Do I need to make the reservoir and channels as well?"

"I can make those myself."

"Then fifteen liang of silver for the test device, bronze tubing, and axle."

Lee Hyun paid part of the silver as a deposit. It was quite expensive for something from the mundane world, but obtaining silver was not difficult for Lee Hyun.

"I'll come back in a month."

After leaving Yunjing, Lee Hyun ran back toward Tunnel No. 1 at full speed.

...

Three days later.

He reached Tunnel No. 1 safely.

"Phew... I really ran my heart out."

There were still nearly two days remaining before it was time to use the Spirit Rain Art.

After confirming that he had plenty of time and feeling relieved, Lee Hyun suddenly realized something felt strange.

'I've never actually tested the Spirit Rain Art's interval in detail.'

Lee Hyun had spent more than a hundred and fifty years in Tunnel No. 1, yet he did not actually know how many days the spirit plants could last without the Spirit Rain Art.

The reason he had never wondered about it before was that he had never intended to go on any long journeys.

While living in Tunnel No. 1, using the Spirit Rain Art once every ten days had been no burden at all for Lee Hyun.

During the rest of his time, he cultivated the Primordial One-Qi Art or practiced techniques and read novels and miscellaneous books bought from the mundane world. If there was nothing else to do, he lay down and slept.

A cultivator's body did not develop an aching back or waist from lying down too long, nor did the skin develop sores from prolonged pressure. Whether Lee Hyun slept for one day or three while circulating the Primordial One-Qi Art, rather than harming his body, it actually made him healthier.

He would occasionally open his eyes, eat a few nuts, and pick up the next volume of whatever book he had been reading, and ten years would pass in the blink of an eye. Lee Hyun truly knew how to pass the time.

Because he was not being chased by the limits of his lifespan, he never bothered worrying about things that were not necessary. As a result, he had never even thought of improving the way he managed the spirit fields.

But once he wanted to be away for extended periods, the situation changed.

'I'd like to join the Fengtian Bureau and interact with other cultivators.'

The fact that the Fengtian Bureau had endured for so many years and consistently provided rewards to rogue cultivators meant that it must possess its own accumulated traditions and foundation of research.

Of course, joining the Fengtian Bureau was not entirely without risk.

The Yunze royal family would not want to be pushed around unilaterally by cultivators recruited from outside. That meant there were surely late Qi Refining cultivators or Foundation Establishment cultivators within the Fengtian Bureau who had maintained ties with the royal family for many years, and they would keep the other Retainers and guest retainers in check.

But Lee Hyun had no intention whatsoever of antagonizing the royal family, so there was no reason for them to dislike him.

If he simply registered as a guest retainer and completed a few missions, he might gain opportunities to exchange basic knowledge on alchemy, artifact refining, talisman crafting, formations, spirit plants, insect control, and other fields.

'And martial experts probably come and go from the Fengtian Bureau too.'

The Retainers alone would not be enough to subjugate demon beasts or fight martial experts from Qianyang Kingdom. There were surely military officers and martial artists who cooperated with the Fengtian Bureau. Yunze Kingdom must also have at least a few experts who had reached the Profound Realm.

'Could I learn how to fight for real from them?'

The Azure Steel Sword Art he had practiced had already reached Minor Attainment, but the only opponent Lee Hyun had ever swung his weapon at was the empty air inside the training cavern.

As Lee Hyun saw it, his greatest weakness at present was his lack of combat experience. But accumulating that experience safely was not easy.

He could enter a cultivation sect and learn combat there, but it was difficult to predict what kinds of situations might arise.

There could be trouble if his abnormally vast amount of spiritual power was discovered, and he might suffer a serious injury during sparring. Most importantly, there was no guarantee he would even meet a master or Senior Brother willing to teach him how to fight.

By contrast, if he joined the Fengtian Bureau as a guest retainer, he could choose which missions to accept, and there seemed to be little danger in gaining combat experience by sparring with martial artists.

"Hmm. Sparring might actually be pretty fun. Better to move around a little than spend every day holed up sleeping...."

For a moment, Lee Hyun imagined himself engaging in an impressive sword duel with a Profound Realm expert.

He pictured a spectacular exchange of attacks and defenses across the training cavern, thrusting out his Earth Shovel Sword and deflecting his opponent's deadly counterattack.

'Heh....'

The total spiritual power of 101 shown on his handmade status screen was quietly filling Lee Hyun with confidence.

In reality, the Qi Sphere Barrier and Spirit Light Shield he cast by pouring enormous amounts of spiritual power into them were far sturdier than the techniques of an ordinary Qi Refining Stage 2 cultivator could ever hope to be.

On top of that, his body-protecting spirit light was also extraordinary.

Body-protecting spirit light was a barrier naturally formed by a body containing spiritual power. If the Qi Sphere Barrier was an applied technique created in imitation of it, then body-protecting spirit light was closer to the cultivator's spiritual power itself. It clung tightly to the body and could not be resized, but its defensive strength increased along with the cultivator's realm and spiritual power.

With defensive power like this, Lee Hyun felt he would not be easily defeated even if he sparred with a Profound Realm expert.

After grinning to himself while lost in fantasy for a moment, Lee Hyun suddenly shook his head and came back to his senses.

'Wait, though... There's no reason I need to go to the Fengtian Bureau right now, is there? I may have more than fifty times the spiritual power of a Qi Refining Stage 2 cultivator, but in the end, the quality of that spiritual power is still only at Stage 2. It would be much safer to start venturing outside after my realm rises further, wouldn't it?'

According to Zhang Ping, a Qi Refining cultivator with little combat experience could die on the spot if ambushed by a Profound Realm expert.

Even if he became a guest retainer rather than one of the Fengtian Bureau's Retainers, could there possibly be nothing but safe work in the world?

Lee Hyun realized that his intention to join the Fengtian Bureau immediately had been somewhat hasty. It was not because there was something he absolutely needed to do there. Rather, after spending more than a hundred and fifty years holed up inside a tunnel, he had simply started wanting to see more of the outside world.

'I let my guard down again! My lifespan is infinite, so there's no need to rush, is there? I can go to the Fengtian Bureau later. For now, let's start with what I can do inside the tunnel.'

Chapter 17

Lee Hyun first inspected the seeds he had bought at Cuiyun Market.

The Yin Water Lotus seeds were about the size of a fingernail, black and hard. He pressed lightly on the outer shell with a finger, but it did not give in the slightest. When he dropped one onto the stone floor, it rang with a clear clink.

'A sprout is supposed to break through a shell like this?'

The stall owner had explained that Yin Water Lotus seeds should not simply be thrown straight into water. One side of the hard shell had to be ground thin against a stone, then soaked in cold water for several days to improve the germination rate.

Avoiding the part containing the embryo, Lee Hyun carefully ground the rounded end of each seed against a whetstone. Once the pale inner shell showed beneath the black outer layer, he stopped.

He left the ground seeds soaking in cold water for several days.

He had already decided where to plant the Yin Water Lotus.

It was near the aquifer he had discovered long ago while creating Spirit Field No. 1-2.

However, Lee Hyun had no intention of reopening the stone slab that sealed the aquifer. The groundwater beyond it was under considerable pressure. If he opened it carelessly, he might flood most of Tunnel No. 1.

Instead, he dug a separate cavern about thirty zhang (about 90 m) away from the slab. He left a thick layer of bedrock intact between the cavern and the aquifer so that even if cracks formed, they would not create a direct channel for the water.

He left several support pillars between the ceiling and floor to prevent collapse, then coated the floor with several layers of fine clay to keep water from seeping out. At one end, he created an overflow channel so that if the water rose too high, it would drain into a sealed cavern on the opposite side of the spirit fields.

Although he had not drawn water directly from the aquifer, perhaps because it was so close, the air inside the cavern was colder and damper than elsewhere.

"This should be suitable enough for growing Yin Water Lotus."

Lee Hyun cast the Spirit Rain Art several times to fill the newly made reservoir with water. Even at its deepest point, the water did not rise above his waist, while a broad shallow section about knee-deep remained in the center.

He spread fine mud gathered from around the aquifer across the reservoir floor. Lee Hyun buried the ground Yin Water Lotus seeds at regular intervals in the shallow section, lightly covered them with mud so they would not float up, then carefully sent a faint stream of energy from the Germination Art into them.

The dormant vitality within the seeds stirred faintly.

In the damp soil outside the reservoir, he planted the Water Root Grass he had bought in Yunjing.

Water Root Grass was merely a mundane herb, but it had the characteristic of sending its roots deep into waterside mud. It seemed likely to help hold the newly made reservoir terrain firmly in place and stabilize it.

Finally, Lee Hyun carved words into the wooden board at the reservoir entrance.

「Spirit Field No. 1-6」

After staring at the words for a moment, Lee Hyun nodded.

...

He chose a slightly elevated area above the reservoir for the Stone Honey Peach seeds.

Stone Honey Peach grew by absorbing water qi and earth qi, but its roots might rot if submerged in water. For that reason, rather than planting them in the damp soil directly beside the aquifer, he decided on a place where moisture could slowly seep through while still allowing proper drainage.

Lee Hyun dug deeply into the floor of a bedrock cavern, then laid down layers of large gravel, small gravel, and sand in that order. Over that, he spread a mixture of spirit-field soil and mud from around the aquifer, shaping the ground into a gentle slope so excess water would drain into a pit on the opposite side.

There were seven Stone Honey Peach seeds in total.

Lee Hyun soaked the seeds in spirit rainwater for a day, then planted them three zhang apart so their roots would not become entangled.

He placed a separate wooden board at the entrance to the spirit field.

「Spirit Field No. 1-7」

...

Next, Lee Hyun created a small test spirit field and divided the interior into several sections, planting small amounts of Bone-Rot Flower, Yin Soul Grass, Purple Poison Orchid, and Earth Vein Flower in each.

Once the spirit plants had grown to a certain point, he planned to vary the Spirit Rain Art watering intervals between sections, while leaving one section entirely unwatered until signs of wilting appeared. Lee Hyun recorded the conditions and dates on the wooden boards in each section.

He placed another wooden board at the spirit field entrance.

「Test Spirit Field」

...

A month later, Lee Hyun returned to Yunjing and collected the small model the old artisan had made.

The model consisted of a forearm-length tank, a thin bronze pipe, and a water bucket that tipped around an axle.

Lee Hyun brought it back to Tunnel No. 1 and tested it countless times. At first, once the bucket tipped, it would not return to its original position. When he increased the weight of the stone counterweight, the bucket refused to move even after filling with water.

He shaved down the counterweight little by little and adjusted the axle position, but when the axle was too close to the center, the bucket would not tip, while if it was too far forward, the water spilled out after only a small amount had collected.

'This is surprisingly finicky....'

Lee Hyun shaved the bottom of the bucket so that it tapered slightly narrower toward the front. That way, as more water collected, the center of gravity would shift forward more quickly.

Even after that, he made several more trips to Yunjing to obtain spare parts and bronze pipes of different thicknesses.

He used the Soil-Softening Art of the Earth Shovel Sword to soften the bedrock before excavating the tanks and channels. In sections without bedrock, he tightly packed pottery clay and fired it hard. He also built the bucket and stone counterweight himself, enlarging the old artisan's model to match the scale of an actual spirit field.

He made the tank low and wide so that the water level would not change drastically as the amount of water decreased. Even so, the flow rate through the bronze pipes still differed between when the tank was full and when it was nearly empty.

But Lee Hyun did not need a water clock capable of measuring ten days with perfect precision. He only needed it to supply water periodically before the spirit plants reached the limit of what they could endure.

...

One year later.

Spirit Field No. 1-1 in Tunnel No. 1.

A newly expanded cavern lay about one zhang diagonally above the entrance to the spirit field. Inside sat a wide, shallow tank. Lee Hyun had covered it with hemp cloth purchased in the mundane world to keep dust from getting inside.

Two bronze pipes, each thinner than a finger, ran side by side from beneath the tank. Clear droplets of water slowly fell from their ends into a small wooden bucket balanced on an axle.

Drip.

One drop fell.

Drip.

Another followed.

The water inside the tank was spirit rainwater Lee Hyun had prepared in advance with the Spirit Rain Art.

Rather than flowing directly into the spirit field, the water accumulated little by little inside the bucket on the axle.

For the past ten days, the bucket had not tipped.

But with the drop that had just fallen, the water's center of gravity crossed the axle.

Clack.

The bucket tipped forward.

Splashhh―

The spirit rainwater that had accumulated inside poured all at once into the distribution basin below.

From the distribution basin, the water split into several streams and flowed down gently sloping channels into the furrows of the spirit field.

The parched soil rapidly grew damp, and the water spread evenly around the roots of the Bone-Rot Flowers and Yin Soul Grass.

Once the bucket had emptied and become lighter, the small stone counterweight hanging from the rear descended.

Click.

The empty bucket returned to its original position.

Drip.

A fresh droplet fell from one of the bronze pipes.

Water for the next irrigation cycle began accumulating once again.

Lee Hyun watched as the water spread evenly across the entire spirit field.

"Hmm... Why did it work properly right from the start? That actually makes me nervous...."

Strictly speaking, it was not the first attempt. He had already gone through several rounds of trial and error.

He had installed the bronze pipes in pairs, so that even if one became blocked, the irrigation interval would merely double rather than stop completely.

Water produced through the Spirit Rain Art contained no impurities to begin with, and perhaps because of the spiritual qi within it, it hardly evaporated at all compared with ordinary water, so long-term operation presented few difficulties.

He had also finished compiling the results from the test spirit field.

Once more than thirty days passed without irrigation, some of the spirit plants began losing vitality from their leaves, and the medicinal potency they had painstakingly accumulated started dissipating little by little.

In conclusion, an automatic irrigation interval of roughly ten to fifteen days was sufficient, and even in the worst case, it only needed to remain under thirty days.

Each spirit field's tank held enough spirit rainwater for the bucket to tip thirty times. If the field was watered once every ten to fifteen days, one tank could maintain the spirit field for about a year.

However, this method allowed the spiritual qi within the water to gradually dissipate, so growth was somewhat slower than when Lee Hyun personally used the Spirit Rain Art each time.

In other words, this device was not meant to grow spirit plants in optimal condition. Its purpose was to keep them from dying or losing too much medicinal potency while Lee Hyun was away.

"Now I won't have to tend the spirit fields every ten days. Of course, it still needs more testing. I'll run it long-term and gradually expand it to the other spirit fields."

...

Most of the Water Root Grass planted around Spirit Field No. 1-6 took root without issue.

However, there were no signs that any of the mundane herbs had transformed into spirit herbs.

Lee Hyun was not disappointed. He recorded the result on a wooden board. If mundane herbs could turn into spirit herbs so easily, spirit herbs would have no reason to be rare in the world.

Of the twenty Yin Water Lotus seeds, eleven sprouted. At first, a coin-sized leaf appeared at the end of each slender stem, and as time passed, green circular leaves unfurled one by one across the surface of the water.

An extremely faint trace of cold water qi lingered beneath the leaves. It was hardly enough to justify calling them spirit herbs yet, but at least the reservoir's environment seemed well suited to Yin Water Lotus.

The Stone Honey Peach seeds showed no change for a long time.

Lee Hyun suspected they might already have rotted, but whenever he examined them with the Aura-Reading Art, he could still detect the faintest trace of vitality within.

After half a year, sprouts finally pushed through the soil from three of the seven seeds.

The sprouts had brown stems, and their leaves were thicker than those of ordinary peach trees. He could also see faint yellow-brown energy flowing along the veins.

"At least three survived...."

Lee Hyun installed the same irrigation devices in Spirit Fields No. 1-2 through No. 1-5.

After filling the last tank with water using the Spirit Rain Art, he sank to the floor with a slightly exhausted expression.

"Phew... Filling several tanks all at once isn't easy."

The Primordial True Qi that had filled his entire body was now nearly depleted.

Lee Hyun simply lay down on the floor.

With his eyes closed, he circulated the Primordial One-Qi Art, and the sparse spiritual qi around him slowly seeped into his entire body.

"Automatic watering... and recovering spiritual power while lying down...."

A smile appeared at the corners of Lee Hyun's mouth.

"Life keeps getting more comfortable."

...

Two years later.

The automatic irrigation devices installed across five spirit fields had undergone repeated improvements and were now dependable.

One bronze pipe had once become clogged with fine stone dust, but thanks to the backup pipe, the spirit plants suffered no harm. Afterward, Lee Hyun added a filter screen to every tank.

The Stone Honey Peach saplings had also grown to the height of Lee Hyun's knees.

The Yin Water Lotus leaves had grown as large as an adult's palm and covered nearly half the reservoir's surface in green. There was still no sign of flowering, but it was a variety that required decades before producing its first bloom in the first place.

Lee Hyun gradually grew accustomed to a life where he filled the spirit-field tanks, occasionally checked the devices for malfunctions, and spent the rest of his time cultivating whenever there was nothing else to do.

Three hundred and thirty years later.

A low vibration stirred the cultivation chamber of Tunnel No. 1.

The Primordial True Qi flowing throughout Lee Hyun's body surged once like a vast wave.

The energy filling his bones and muscles, meridians, and internal organs had grown far denser and heavier than it had been in the past.

Lee Hyun, who had been lying down, slowly opened his eyes.

"Hmm...."

He had already reached Primordial Body, 3rd Stage two hundred and thirty years earlier.

He was no longer merely at the level of someone who had just entered Qi Refining Stage 3, but had reached late Qi Refining Stage 3, close to the threshold of Qi Refining Stage 4. In other words, his Primordial Body was likewise nearing the 4th Stage.

For the first time in a long while, Lee Hyun took out a wooden board and carved himself a new handmade status screen, savoring the changes. Writing everything down where he could see it from time to time made even accomplishments he had already achieved feel fresh again!

【Age: 555】

【Realm: Qi Refining Stage 3 (late)】

【Spiritual Power: 206】

【Spiritual Root: Wood, Fire, Earth】

【Cultivation Art: Primordial One-Qi Art】

【Constitution: Primordial Body, 3rd Stage (late)】

For a Qi Refining Stage 3 cultivator, a spiritual power value of 206 was downright absurd.

Even accounting for the quality of his spiritual power, Lee Hyun estimated that he had already far surpassed the level of a cultivator at Qi Refining Great Perfection. In fact, he had.

This was all because the volume of his entire body was vastly greater than that of a dantian.

After cultivating for so many years, the proficiency of his techniques had also changed greatly. Most of the techniques he had used consistently over the past three hundred and thirty years had reached Major Attainment!

【Techniques (Minor Attainment): Sword Control Art, Earth Spike Art, Wood Binding Art, Poison-Discerning Art】

【Techniques (Major Attainment): Azure Steel Sword Art, Fireball Art, Lightness Art, Distance-Shrinking Step, Aura-Concealing Art, Spirit Rain Art, Soil-Turning Art, Yang Metal Art, Germination Art, Earth Escape Art, Qi Sphere Barrier, Spirit Light Shield, Aura-Reading Art, Farsight Art, Night Vision Art, Ground-Sense Art, Keen Hearing Art, Scent-Tracking Art, Cleansing Art, Air-Clearing Art, Breath-Sealing Art, Detoxification Art, Faint Light Art, Fire-Kindling Art】

【Techniques (Perfection): Spirit-Concealing Art】

【Applied Technique: Reclining Escape Art】

He had made noticeable progress in no fewer than twenty-nine techniques. Among them were the Sword Control Art, Earth Spike Art, and Wood Binding Art, which he had newly learned over the long years simply to relieve his boredom.

Most of the techniques that had reached Major Attainment were ones he had found at least some use for over the past three hundred and thirty years. They had become so deeply ingrained in him that his Primordial True Qi now responded almost the instant his intent formed.

Lee Hyun had not brought so many techniques to Major Attainment because he was a genius, but because Tier 1 basic techniques had simple structures. Even an ordinary talent who lived for more than five hundred years would inevitably comprehend nearly all techniques of this level.

Lee Hyun stopped carving into the wooden board and turned his awareness inward, examining his essence, qi and spirit.

"That's strange... It feels like my realm isn't rising anymore...."

Over the past ten years, Lee Hyun's maximum spiritual power had barely increased.

Whenever his entire body was already filled with Primordial True Qi and he tried to draw in even more spiritual qi, the surrounding spiritual qi slid across the surface of his skin and dispersed. No matter how he circulated his cultivation art, he could not force any more of it inside.

It felt like trying to pour more water into an already full waterskin.

'Could this be the bottleneck between Qi Refining Stage 3 and Stage 4...?'

Lee Hyun recalled Zhang Ping, whom he had met long ago in Yunjing.

- I've been stuck at Qi Refining Stage 3 for more than fifty years.

Back then, Lee Hyun had thought there must be something wrong with Zhang Ping, but now he realized that was not the case. He had heard about it before, but there truly did seem to be a bottleneck when advancing from early to mid Qi Refining.

"This doesn't seem like something I can solve just by cultivating harder... There must be something I don't know."

It seemed the time had finally come for him to truly venture outside.

Chapter 18

Lee Hyun had not spent all of the past 330 years wide awake.

Roughly every fifteen days, he made the rounds of the spirit fields. The rest of the time, he cultivated the Primordial One-Qi Art while lying down in a half-asleep state.

By his own sense of time, it felt as though less than a few decades had passed. Of course, even that was an extremely long time, and Lee Hyun had already grown tired of life in the tunnel.

Now that even his realm had stopped advancing, there was no reason to remain in Tunnel No. 1.

'Maybe I should visit Yunjing for the first time in ages and look into how to break through to mid Qi Refining while I'm there?'

...

Before leaving, Lee Hyun decided to briefly inspect the spirit fields first.

His prone body began sliding across the floor.

Shhk-shhk-shhk-shhk―

His entire body crossed the cultivation chamber and slipped out into the passage.

When he reached a bend, Lee Hyun turned sideways without getting up, slid up the wall, across the ceiling, and down onto the floor on the opposite side.

By now, Lee Hyun was even capable of the bizarre feat of using the Distance-Shrinking Step while performing the Reclining Escape Art.

As though tunneling through solid bedrock underground while lying flat were not enough, he now hovered just above the passage floor and glided along like a ghost.

...

Spirit Field No. 1-1.

Dense poisonous pollen floated like a hazy mist around the overlapping layers of ivory petals. Still lying flat, Lee Hyun approached and examined the inside of the Bone-Rot Flower.

'Around 160 years.'

"Still, this isn't bad."

Using the Yang Metal Art, Lee Hyun carved their current condition into a wooden board.

"116 Bone-Rot Flowers, 294 Yin Soul Grass plants, 77 Purple Poison Orchids, 55 Earth Vein Flowers... The numbers have decreased slightly, but they're in good condition. Average medicine age, 164 years."

Lee Hyun then inspected Spirit Field No. 1-2 through Spirit Field No. 1-5 in order.

"The remaining spirit plants in the other four spirit fields... 466 Bone-Rot Flowers, 1,182 Yin Soul Grass plants, 310 Purple Poison Orchids, 224 Earth Vein Flowers. Average medicine age, 131 years...."

...

Spirit Field No. 1-6.

The surface of the reservoir was completely covered in green lotus leaves.

Several flowers bloomed among the leaves, while honeycomb-like seedpods riddled with holes had formed where other flowers had shed their petals.

Lee Hyun lifted the nearest seedpod.

A hard seed sat inside each hole.

He had tried taking the seeds out and eating them before.

Young seeds were cool and faintly sweet, and after eating them, his mind felt a little clearer while the heat inside his body subsided.

They tasted quite good as well, so Lee Hyun often cracked open lotus seedpods as snacks. Thanks to that, he had even fewer reasons to venture into the mundane world.

"I have no idea how quickly professional spirit-plant cultivators can raise these in a spirit field. Let's call the medicine age 110 years."

...

Spirit Field No. 1-7, the last place he visited, contained three Stone Honey Peach trees growing like a small forest.

Because the cavern ceiling was low, the trees could not grow straight upward and instead spread broadly to the sides. Thick trunks and branches twisted along the rock walls, while faint yellow-brown qi flowed through the veins of their thick leaves.

Fist-sized fruits hung sparsely among the branches.

When they had first begun bearing fruit, all three trees combined produced only three or four peaches a year. As the trees aged, however, their yield steadily increased. Now they bore more than twenty fruits every year.

Lee Hyun plucked a fully ripened fruit and peeled away the skin.

When he bit into the translucent, honey-colored flesh, the firm, chilled pulp crunched between his teeth. Rich sweetness and refreshing water qi spread through his mouth together.

"Ahh..."

There was no dramatic change in his body immediately after eating it. He recorded the Stone Honey Peach's medicine age as 110 years for the time being.

...

After recording the condition of all seven spirit fields, Lee Hyun returned to the cultivation chamber and sank into thought.

There were now more than 2,700 Bone-Rot Flowers, Yin Soul Grass plants, Purple Poison Orchids, and Earth Vein Flowers over a hundred years old in total, and he could also steadily harvest Yin Water Lotus seedpods and Stone Honey Peach spirit fruits.

'The problem is who I can sell these to, and for how much....'

Putting one or two century-old spirit herbs up for sale might have been fine. He could claim that he had happened across them in a secret spirit field deep in the mountains or in the cave abode of some ancient cultivator. But if he repeatedly sold the same species or put dozens up for sale at once, anyone would become suspicious of their origin.

"Well, there's no need to rush. It's not like I'm desperate for spirit stones right now... and they'll only get more expensive if I wait, won't they?"

...

Lee Hyun went to the storeroom and retrieved the storage pouch he had used since his days at Qinghe Valley.

He had eaten the few Essence-Nourishing Pills inside long ago simply out of boredom, leaving behind only a little of the food he had eaten in those days.

When he opened the stopper of a small bottle, four Hunger-Warding Pills rolled out. After eating them occasionally over the centuries, only these last few remained.

When he examined them with the Aura-Reading Art, more than half of the spiritual qi within had already dissipated.

Lee Hyun put one Hunger-Warding Pill into his mouth.

They had never tasted good in the past, but now that most of their spiritual qi was gone, it tasted like nothing more than chewing powdered medicinal ingredients without water.

Still, once it reached his stomach, a faint warmth spread through him.

Lee Hyun also took a small cloth pouch from the storage pouch.

There was roughly one jin (about 600 g) of Qinghe Rice left.

The once white and translucent grains had not spoiled, but much of the spiritual qi they once contained had dissipated.

Lee Hyun put the Qinghe Rice back into the pouch.

...

For several days before leaving, Lee Hyun put Tunnel No. 1 in order.

He filled the tanks in each spirit field with spirit rainwater and inspected each bronze pipe and the axles of the water barrels. He replaced worn components with new ones and thoroughly cleared away the dirt and stone dust that had accumulated in the waterways.

...

Four days later.

Lee Hyun was already walking along the western highway leading toward Yunjing.

He had occasionally visited the nearby county seat to buy nuts, hardware, paper, and books, but it had been a long time since he had come all the way to Yunjing.

Even from a distance, Yunjing looked considerably different from what Lee Hyun remembered.

The first thing that caught his eye was the city wall.

A new outer wall had been built far to the west of the old western gate, and both its height and thickness far surpassed those of the old wall. Towers fitted with enormous crossbows stood along the top at regular intervals.

Strangely enough, Yunze Kingdom was still standing.

A long line of carts and pedestrians stretched out before the city gate. The soldiers inspecting cargo wore armor unlike what Lee Hyun remembered, and a huge bronze mirror that had not existed in the past had been installed above the gate.

Each time someone passed through, a hazy light appeared on the mirror's surface before fading away.

'What's that? Could it be... a magic tool? I wouldn't expect a nation of the mundane world to possess any particularly impressive magic tools....'
