Lee Hyun circulated the Spirit-Concealing Art and Aura-Concealing Art at the same time as he followed the line through the gate. The bronze mirror faced him, but no alarm sounded and no soldiers approached.

'Hm. I guess it really wasn't anything special.'

...

Inside the new outer wall, warehouses, inns, and workshops stood packed closely together.

It seemed the city had expanded into areas that once held rice paddies and ordinary homes. The main roads were wider than before, and large stone bridges had replaced the wooden bridges spanning the waterways.

Lee Hyun asked a passerby for directions and headed toward the site of the old western gate.

Only after walking for quite some time did the old city wall finally come into view. Sections of it had been demolished and were now being used like market walls, while the tower above the former western gate had been converted into a teahouse.

A place that had once stood outside the city was now the entrance to a market known as the Old West Gate.

There were still many stalls selling medicinal herbs and miscellaneous goods around the Old West Gate.

Lee Hyun slowly looked around, then abruptly stopped. Several bundles of Water Root Grass lay atop a shabby mat.

Behind them sat a thin man who looked to be a little over fifty.

He bore an astonishing resemblance to Zhang Ping, whom Lee Hyun had met more than three hundred years ago.

When Lee Hyun found himself staring without realizing it, the man looked up.

"Is something the matter?"

"May I ask your name...?"

"I am Zhang Youshan."

"I see."

Lee Hyun lowered his head with an awkward expression.

"You looked so much like someone I knew that I mistook you for him."

"There are plenty of people in the world who resemble one another, are there not?"

'What are the odds of this...?'

After hesitating for a moment, Lee Hyun picked up a bundle of Water Root Grass from the mat.

"How much?"

"Four copper coins."

"That's more expensive than it used to be."

"How many things in this world are cheaper now than they used to be?"

"Fair point."

Lee Hyun handed over the coins and placed the Water Root Grass in his storage pouch.

When he still did not leave despite having made his purchase, Zhang Youshan looked him up and down.

"Is this your first time in Yunjing?"

"It's been a long time."

"You must be a fellow Daoist who has been cultivating in seclusion in the mountains."

"That's right."

"Judging by your realm, you seem to be at Qi Refining Stage 3. Did you come here hoping to join the Fengtian Bureau?"

"Does the Fengtian Bureau still exist?"

Zhang Youshan stared at him as though he had just heard something bizarre.

"What do you mean, does it still exist? If the Fengtian Bureau vanished, who would hold back the demon beasts and the martial artists of Qianyang Kingdom?"

Hearing that not only Yunze Kingdom but also the Fengtian Bureau still existed, Lee Hyun felt relieved.

"I came to Yunjing to find out how to advance from Qi Refining Stage 3 to Stage 4."

"How long have you been stuck?"

"About ten years."

Zhang Youshan gave a bitter smile.

"You're still a youngster."

"And how long has it been for you, fellow Daoist?"

"Forty-five years. I reached Qi Refining Stage 3 at thirty-four, and I'm seventy-nine this year. Exactly forty-five years. No need to do the arithmetic."

Lee Hyun felt strangely unsettled. The man was a mirror image of Zhang Ping, whom he had met long ago, not only in appearance but in circumstances as well.

"Is advancing from Qi Refining Stage 3 to Stage 4 really that difficult?"

"It is, if you have neither a good spirit vein nor pills."

"Is a spirit vein absolutely necessary?"

Zhang Youshan studied Lee Hyun's face for a moment, then gestured toward a low wooden crate beside him.

"You truly must have cultivated alone in the mountains. I have no customers anyway, so sit for a while."

Once Lee Hyun sat on the crate, Zhang Youshan began explaining as he brushed dirt from the roots of the Water Root Grass.

"Up to Qi Refining Stage 3, even if heaven-and-earth spiritual qi is thin, you can somehow advance as long as you put in enough time. But...."

Zhang Youshan curled one hand inward, then mimed pressing into it from outside with the other.

"To advance from early Qi Refining to mid Qi Refining, you must raise the quality of your spiritual power by another level while the pressure of external spiritual qi exceeds a certain threshold. People often compare the spiritual power of a Qi Refining cultivator to gas and that of a Foundation Establishment cultivator to liquid... but that is only an analogy. In reality, the quality of spiritual power varies even among cultivators within Qi Refining."

"So the pressure of the external spiritual qi is important. Then the reason a spirit vein matters is...."

"Exactly. Usually, one attempts the breakthrough somewhere with a Tier 1 high-grade spirit vein. In a place like that, the surrounding spiritual qi naturally presses into the body. But pills are actually the best option. The pressure produced when the concentrated spiritual qi inside a pill is released all at once within the body is so much stronger that it is difficult to compare with what a spirit vein can provide. When breaking through to Qi Refining Stage 4, cultivators generally take a Barrier-Breaking Pill."

"Does having a Barrier-Breaking Pill make the breakthrough easy?"

Zhang Youshan let out a dry laugh.

"If that were true, would I be sitting here selling Water Root Grass? The chance of success varies depending on one's spiritual root, cultivation art, age, and the condition of one's dantian. Plenty of people still fail even after taking a pill at a good spirit vein. Even so, it is far better than attempting a breakthrough with no preparation whatsoever."

Lee Hyun thought for a moment before asking,

"Where can I obtain a Barrier-Breaking Pill?"

"You would either have to obtain the pill recipe and try making one yourself, or buy one at a cultivator market."

"Isn't alchemy the exclusive preserve of great sects and cultivation clans?"

"Just how old is the information you're working with?"

Zhang Youshan picked up a stalk of Water Root Grass.

"Since the ancient era, spiritual qi has declined, and as the cultivation of spirit plants became more widespread, the number of alchemists naturally increased as well. Every cultivation force that operates spirit fields now has alchemists of its own. Even the Fengtian Bureau over there has pill recipes and alchemists...."

"The Fengtian Bureau does? If I joined, could I learn the Barrier-Breaking Pill recipe and the basics of alchemy as well?"

"Learning them isn't difficult in itself. These days, there's even a saying that two out of every three rogue cultivators try their hand at alchemy, and one of those two gives up after doing nothing but wasting spirit stones."

"Were you also once affiliated with the Fengtian Bureau, fellow Daoist?"

"I was."

"Then couldn't you simply make your own Barrier-Breaking Pills?"

"I thought the same thing when I was young."

Zhang Youshan smiled bitterly and lightly rubbed his side.

"I worked as an External Retainer for the Fengtian Bureau for seventeen years. I hunted demon beasts, escorted medicinal ingredients, and even tracked down martial artists from Qianyang Kingdom."

"An External Retainer? Wasn't that called a guest retainer?"

This time, Zhang Youshan looked genuinely puzzled.

"How do you know that?"

"I read it in an old book."

"That is an outdated term. The guest retainer system was abolished more than sixty years ago."

"Why was it abolished?"

"During a major war with Qianyang Kingdom, the Fengtian Bureau urgently summoned its guest retainers, but most of them disappeared. They took advantage of the Bureau's registry and benefits in ordinary times, then fled the moment things became dangerous. Guest retainers were originally free to choose their own missions, so there was hardly any basis for punishing them."

After that incident, the Yunze royal court reportedly changed the system so that every Qi Refining rogue cultivator receiving support from the Fengtian Bureau was placed on the rolls as a Retainer.

The current Retainers were divided into Standing Retainers, External Retainers, Military Retainers, and Craft Retainers.

Standing Retainers remained at government offices and received a stipend, but in return, they could not easily refuse orders. External Retainers lived freely most of the time and chose whichever missions they wanted, but they were required to meet a minimum mission quota within a set period.

Military Retainers fought the martial artists of Qianyang Kingdom along the southern frontier, while Craft Retainers contributed to the Fengtian Bureau through skills such as alchemy, talisman crafting, formations, and medicine.

"So you accumulated merit points as an External Retainer and used them to learn alchemy?"

"Indeed. But actually practicing alchemy was another matter entirely."

Zhang Youshan raised his right hand. The tips of two fingers were blackened and twisted as though badly burned.

"I learned alchemy from the Craft Retainers, but in the end, I realized I had no talent for it. So instead of buying a pill furnace and pill recipe with my remaining merit points, I bought a Barrier-Breaking Pill. I took it, and I failed."

"......."

"After that, I had neither the spirit stones to gather another set of medicinal ingredients nor the will to keep taking dangerous missions. After a Qianyang Kingdom martial artist slashed my side, I even returned my retainer badge."

"If you were an External Retainer, couldn't you choose safer missions?"

"Safe missions award too few merit points to make buying pills easy. I do not have much lifespan left now, either, so I have no intention of risking my life for a breakthrough."

Lee Hyun sank into thought as he listened to Zhang Youshan.

The man before him lacked medicinal ingredients, spirit stones, and time, but Lee Hyun was different.

Still, there was a good chance that obtaining only a few Barrier-Breaking Pills would not be enough to overcome his bottleneck.

An ordinary Qi Refining Stage 3 cultivator's spiritual power was concentrated in the dantian, but Lee Hyun's Primordial True Qi filled his entire body.

'If everyone else attempts the breakthrough with one Barrier-Breaking Pill, how many would I need?'

Buying dozens of times as many pills as everyone else would be the same as advertising how many spirit stones he possessed. If rumors like that spread through the cultivation world, it would be extremely dangerous.

Even if he bought enough pills to overcome the bottleneck to Stage 4, there would still be the bottleneck to Stage 7, and above all, the bottleneck to Foundation Establishment.

Was he supposed to buy dozens of Foundation Establishment Pills, then once he reached Foundation Establishment Stage 3, buy Tier 2 pills in bulk again just to advance to Stage 4?

'Hm... it looks like I really do need to start learning alchemy... Even if it takes a long time, I can grow the spirit plants myself....'

After organizing his thoughts, Lee Hyun changed the subject.

"Is the war with Qianyang Kingdom still going on?"

Zhang Youshan's expression darkened slightly.

"The fighting between Yunze Kingdom and Qianyang Kingdom is nothing new, but Qianyang Kingdom has been especially formidable over the past thirty years. Yunze Kingdom managed to hold Qianyang Kingdom back for centuries thanks to its rivers and wetlands, along with the strength of the Fengtian Bureau's Retainers. Recently, though, that balance has been gradually breaking down."

"Has the border been pushed back far?"

"Qingluo Pass fell twenty years ago, Baishui City was captured seven years ago, and last year even Hei'an Mine fell into Qianyang Kingdom's hands. The country is not on the verge of collapse just yet, but unlike before, it has been unable to easily reclaim the territory it loses. That is why the Fengtian Bureau is desperate to recruit Qi Refining rogue cultivators as Retainers."

"I see. Thank you for explaining."

Lee Hyun started to rise, then looked at Zhang Youshan's face once more.

'No matter how I look at him, he looks exactly like Zhang Ping....'

"By any chance, fellow Daoist Zhang, did you have an ancestor named Zhang Ping?"

Zhang Youshan's eyes widened.

"How do you know?"

"..."

"My eighth-generation ancestor was a man named Zhang Ping. They say he never made it past Qi Refining Stage 3 either."

For a moment, Lee Hyun was at a loss for words.

"Why do you ask?"

"I once saw Zhang Ping's name in a record left by one of my ancestors."

"Your ancestor?"

"A very long time ago, one of my family's ancestors received some help from a rogue cultivator named Zhang Ping west of Yunjing. The record said he kindly explained the circumstances of the surrounding cultivation world. My ancestor was grateful and wrote that if they ever met again, he wanted to give Zhang Ping some Qinghe Rice as a gift."

"What is Qinghe Rice?"

"Spirit rice. Please accept it as my way of fulfilling my ancestor's wish."

Lee Hyun took a small cloth pouch from his storage pouch and held it out to Zhang Youshan.

"Some of the spiritual qi has dissipated, though...."

Zhang Youshan accepted the pouch, opened it, and smelled the contents. He could not hide the smile that spread across his lips.

"Thank you, truly! To think something like this could happen in my lifetime. You rarely see Qi Refining rogue cultivators growing spirit rice...."

Zhang Youshan placed a few grains of Qinghe Rice on his palm and stared at them in fascination.

"I didn't grow it myself. By the way, where is the Fengtian Bureau?"

"Head about a hundred li (about 40 km) east from here. Just look for the tall walls with blue roof tiles. It should not be difficult to find."

"Thank you."

Lee Hyun bid Zhang Youshan farewell and headed for the Fengtian Bureau.

...

The farther east he went from the Old West Gate, the more rapidly the streets changed.

Market stalls and restaurants grew fewer, replaced by orderly government offices and mansions surrounded by high walls.

Yunjing was divided into the outer city, middle city, and inner city. The new outer wall now enclosed a vast area that had contained villages and manors outside the city centuries ago, while the wall that had once formed Yunjing's outermost boundary now remained as an old wall dividing the interior of the outer city. The inner city centered on the royal palace stood much farther within.

Armored soldiers stood in formation before the gate leading into the inner city.

On either side of the gate crouched stone beasts several times taller than a person, while an enormous drum and bronze bell looked down over the capital from the tower above.

The soldiers checked the travel tokens of everyone entering through the gate one by one. When Lee Hyun's turn came, a spear-bearing soldier looked him up and down.

"Show your travel token."

"I am a cultivator heading to the Fengtian Bureau."

The soldier's expression changed slightly. He looked toward a lower-ranking military officer standing beside him. After briefly examining Lee Hyun's clothes and waist, the military officer said,

"Please reveal a little of your spiritual power."

When Lee Hyun produced a faint glimmer of spiritual power at his fingertip, the military officer took a small bronze token from his waist and held it near the light. A blue pattern appeared on the surface of the bronze token, and he nodded.

"Your status as a cultivator has been confirmed. However, since you do not have a retainer badge, please do not leave the main avenue."

"Understood."

Once he passed through the gate, the previous clamor faded away as though it had never existed.

The streets were far wider than those of the outer city, yet there were fewer pedestrians. The main avenue, paved with blue stone slabs, was broad enough for six carts to travel side by side, while deep drainage channels ran along both sides to carry away rainwater.

There were no stalls selling goods along the avenue and no clerks calling out to customers. Instead, walls more than two jang (about 6 m) high and imposing gates appeared one after another.

Some gates had signboards hanging beneath their eaves, with golden lettering written against black backgrounds, while other mansions had spear-bearing private guards and silk-clad gatekeepers standing outside.

Even the number of bronze studs embedded in a gate, the shapes of the beasts decorating the eaves, and the colors of ornamental cords hanging from carriages appeared to be dictated by the owner's official rank.

When a red carriage drawn by six white horses passed, officials along the roadside hurriedly bowed. Behind it followed a long procession of attendants wearing jade plaques at their waists and guards clad in scale armor.

On another street, officials in blue robes stepped down from sedan chairs and entered a government office behind red walls. Their black official hats and the wave patterns embroidered in silver thread across their chests caught Lee Hyun's attention. The number of waves composing each pattern appeared to indicate the official's rank.

'So this is the real inner city.'

It was nothing more than a place inhabited by mortals of the mundane world.

And yet Lee Hyun found himself unconsciously intimidated.

The authority and laws of a dynasty that had endured for centuries seemed infused into every stone road, wall, gate, and banner.

Of course, if Lee Hyun truly wanted to, knocking down the dozens of soldiers before him and vaulting over the walls would have been effortless.

But within this inner city were thousands of warriors, officials, and experts of the martial world, and behind them stood the Fengtian Bureau and the immense nation that was Yunze Kingdom.

This was not a place where someone could act recklessly merely because his individual strength was somewhat greater than others'.

Lee Hyun continued east while asking for directions to the Fengtian Bureau.

Before long, he reached a broad street lined with red walls. This was the district where the residences of the royal family and royal kin were concentrated.

Royal residences had gates noticeably larger than those of ordinary high officials. Glazed tiles covered their eaves, while rows of beast-shaped roof figurines sat along the sloping ridges at the four corners of the roofs.

At that moment, a sharp voice rang out from ahead.

"Make way― The procession of the Huiling royal house is passing through!"

At the cry ordering everyone to clear the road, the people walking along the street immediately moved to both sides.

Merchants and servants knelt at the roadside, while those in official robes brought their sleeves together and bowed at the waist.

Lee Hyun followed everyone else's movements and stepped aside to the right.

In the distance, a large carriage drawn by four black horses approached. Its body was lacquered a deep reddish-black and engraved with silver patterns of clouds and waves, while small jade bells hung from all four corners of the roof.

Sixteen spear-bearing cavalrymen escorted the carriage from the front and rear.

An official of the Huiling royal house who had been scanning the surroundings suddenly raised a hand.

"Stop!"

The horses pawed at the ground, and the carriage procession gradually came to a halt.

The middle-aged official leading the procession dismounted and approached Lee Hyun.

Chapter 19

The official looked back and forth between Lee Hyun's face and his waist, then cupped his hands in greeting.

"May I ask you something?"

"Go ahead."

"Do you happen to have a Fengtian Bureau retainer badge?"

"I do not."

"Then please wait a moment."

He immediately turned and headed back to the carriage.

Lee Hyun watched the official's retreating back and frowned slightly.

'What is it?'

Just then.

Chime–

One of the four cultivator bells hanging from the corners of the carriage roof began to sway on its own despite the lack of wind.

Each time its clear chime rang out, the tip of the bell tilted a little farther toward Lee Hyun.

Chime. Chime.

'Is that a magic tool?'

When Lee Hyun used the Aura-Reading Art, he saw faint threads of spiritual power intertwined across the surface of the cultivator bell.

A moment later, the curtain opened.

The first person to step down from the carriage was an elderly cultivator in blue robes.

He looked to be around sixty, but the spiritual power emanating from him was on an entirely different level from Zhang Youshan, the Qi Refining Stage 3 cultivator Lee Hyun had seen outside the Old West Gate.

'Late Qi Refining!?'

A gleam flashed through the elderly cultivator's eyes as he looked at Lee Hyun. His gaze lingered near Lee Hyun's dantian for a moment before sweeping over his entire body.

His expression did not change in the slightest.

'He couldn't see through the Spirit-Concealing Art? That's a relief.'

A young man stepped down from the carriage after him.

He did not appear to be over thirty.

His black hair was bound beneath a golden coronet, and clouds and waves had been embroidered in silver thread across his dark purple long robe. A jade belt and longsword hung at his waist, and he wore spotless black leather shoes.

The moment the man appeared, the surrounding officials and soldiers bowed even deeper.

The middle-aged official shouted loudly.

"His Highness the Crown Prince!"

'The Crown Prince?'

The Huiling Liu clan was the royal clan that had ruled Yunze Kingdom for hundreds of years. People also called them the Huiling royal house.

That meant the man before him was the current King's legitimate son and had already been designated as the next ruler.

Lee Hyun had not expected someone like that to personally step out of the carriage because of him.

The Crown Prince walked up to Lee Hyun.

Lee Hyun did not know what etiquette he was supposed to observe before the Crown Prince, so he cupped his hands as cultivators did when greeting one another.

"My name is Li Dongyi."

Even though Lee Hyun greeted him first, the Crown Prince gave no reply. Instead, he lifted the front hem of his robe.

Thud.

The Crown Prince dropped to his knees in the middle of the street.

"......?"

Lee Hyun's eyes widened.

The people nearby also drew sharp breaths in surprise.

The Crown Prince cupped his hands and bowed his head deeply.

"I, Liu Zhenghui, Crown Prince of Yunze Kingdom, implore the Immortal. Please become a Retainer of the Fengtian Bureau and protect Yunze Kingdom."

"......."

'What in the world is going on?'

'I heard Qi Refining rogue cultivators were highly valued here, but valued enough for a member of the royal family to kneel in the street before a rogue cultivator he's never even met?'

Lee Hyun instinctively glanced around. He wondered whether there was some trap or scheme he had failed to notice, but he saw nothing suspicious.

The Crown Prince continued speaking with his head still bowed.

"The Immortal need not take up a sword and go south. Merely drawing a single talisman would be enough. Simply adding your name to the Fengtian Bureau's rolls would give tremendous strength to the people of Yunze Kingdom."

"Um...."

"If what we can offer is insufficient, please tell me. Spirit stones, spirit herbs, a residence... As long as it lies within Yunze Kingdom's means, we will do everything we can to provide it."

The elderly cultivator in blue robes finally sighed.

"Your Highness."

"Retainer Zheng, do not stop me."

"I cannot simply stand by."

The elderly cultivator stepped beside the Crown Prince and took hold of his arm.

"Showing respect to an Immortal and putting a fellow Daoist you have just met in an awkward position in the middle of the street are two different matters."

"But...."

"If Your Highness keeps this up, even someone who was interested will run away."

The elderly cultivator helped the Crown Prince to his feet.

The Crown Prince rose without resistance, yet showed not the slightest hint of embarrassment.

"Retainer Zheng is always talking about appearances."

"This is not about appearances. It is about proper etiquette. Every time Your Highness sets out to recruit a Retainer, you begin by dropping to your knees. You have even earned a nickname among Yunjing's rogue cultivators by now."

"What nickname?"

"You are better off not hearing it."

The Crown Prince's expression stiffened slightly.

The elderly cultivator cupped his hands toward Lee Hyun.

"My apologies. I am Zheng Yuanbo, a Standing Retainer of the Fengtian Bureau."

"I am Li Dongyi."

"Judging by the look of things, fellow Daoist, this must be your first time in Yunjing. Please do not take His Highness's behavior too seriously. Ever since Baishui City fell, he has done this whenever he meets a cultivator who has yet to join the Fengtian Bureau."

"Retainer Zheng!"

"Am I wrong?"

Zheng Yuanbo ignored the Crown Prince's protest.

"Was it the cultivator bell on the carriage that recognized me as a cultivator?"

"Correct."

Zheng Yuanbo pointed toward the carriage roof.

"It is a low-grade magic tool that rings whenever a Qi Refining cultivator is nearby. However, the moment it resonates with a Fengtian Bureau retainer badge, it falls silent."

"I see."

Zheng Yuanbo glanced sideways at the Crown Prince.

"That does not mean a member of the royal family should personally kneel the instant it detects someone."

"If kneeling can gain us someone the kingdom needs, what does it matter?"

The Crown Prince replied without a trace of shame. Zheng Yuanbo sighed again.

Lee Hyun spoke.

"Actually, I was already on my way to the Fengtian Bureau."

"...Truly?"

"I wanted to learn how to advance from Qi Refining Stage 3 to Stage 4, and also look into alchemy. I was considering registering as a Retainer of the Fengtian Bureau as well."

The Crown Prince turned toward Zheng Yuanbo.

"You heard him?"

"I did."

"He says he would have come to the Fengtian Bureau even if I had not knelt."

"Which is precisely why I told Your Highness not to make a spectacle of yourself."

"......."

The Crown Prince cleared his throat, then dusted off the knees of his robe.

Zheng Yuanbo spoke.

"However, registering as a Retainer requires two Standing Retainers qualified to conduct the assessment to be present together. Unfortunately, everyone who can conduct one right now is away on assignment. Of the two who will return first, one has gone to inspect a formation in another city, while the other went east to deal with a demon beast... You will likely have to wait three or four days."

"I can wait that long."

"We will arrange a place for you to stay in the meantime."

The Crown Prince immediately added,

"We will send someone to inform you as soon as the two return."

"Thank you."

"We are on our way to the Grand Drill Ground of the Martial Training Academy. If the Immortal does not mind, would you care to accompany us?"

"What are you going there for?"

"There is a review today for the reinforcements departing for Lushui Pass. Before that, a sparring match is also scheduled to assess the general's martial arts."

"In that case, I will come with you."

The Crown Prince gestured toward the carriage.

"There is room inside."

Lee Hyun considered it for a moment. The Crown Prince himself did not bother him, but riding in a cramped carriage with Zheng Yuanbo, a late Qi Refining cultivator, was another matter.

Lee Hyun was inexperienced in combat. He possessed plenty of spiritual power, but he was not confident he could respond properly if he were ambushed at close range.

He also worried that remaining together inside such a confined carriage might allow Zheng Yuanbo to notice the spiritual power throughout his body that the Spirit-Concealing Art was concealing.

After all, his assessment of his proficiency in the Spirit-Concealing Art was merely something he had carved into a wooden board himself. He had no way of knowing whether it could truly fool a late Qi Refining cultivator observing him from extremely close range.

"I will walk."

"That will not do. If the Immortal walks while I ride in the carriage, people will say the Huiling royal house mistreats its guests."

At that moment, Zheng Yuanbo said calmly,

"Then Your Highness can walk as well."

"Whose side are you on, Retainer Zheng?"

"The Fengtian Bureau's."

"Now that I think about it, that works too. We are almost there anyway."

In the end, neither the Crown Prince nor Zheng Yuanbo returned to the carriage. They walked side by side with Lee Hyun along the main avenue of the inner city, while the carriage and mounted guards followed slowly behind them.

As they walked, the Crown Prince continuously explained the Fengtian Bureau.

According to him, the Fengtian Bureau currently had fewer than two hundred Qi Refining cultivators.

Of those, only around fifty Military Retainers were actually deployed in combat, nowhere near enough to defend the entire southern frontier.

Fifty Qi Refining cultivators might sound like a formidable force, but Qinghe Valley alone, in the southwestern region of the Great Yan Kingdom where Lee Hyun had once lived, had around a thousand Qi Refining cultivators.

If so many cultivators had existed in such a small territory, then having only around fifty Qi Refining cultivators immediately available for war across the vast Yunze Kingdom truly was an extremely small number.

The southern border where Yunze Kingdom met Qianyang Kingdom stretched more than twenty thousand li (about 8,000 km) from east to west.

In the end, Qianyang Kingdom was not the only nation forced to rely on masters of the martial path. Aside from key strongholds, Yunze Kingdom likewise had to entrust many areas to martial masters rather than Qi Refining Retainers.

"Are there not far too few Military Retainers? If so, you will have no choice but to ask the External Retainers to join the war as well."

"We can ask them, but we cannot force the External Retainers onto the battlefield."

The Crown Prince continued.

"If the royal house is the first to break the promises made when we invited them to become Retainers, what Immortal would trust Yunze Kingdom enough to join the Fengtian Bureau in the future?"

Lee Hyun looked mildly surprised.

"Even if the kingdom were truly in grave danger?"

"We might gain one or two more people in the short term."

The Crown Prince shook his head.

"But from that moment onward, Yunze Kingdom would cease to be a kingdom that honors Immortals and become one that commands them. When our circumstances grow even worse than they are now, no one will help us."

...

They continued along the avenue.

Before long, rhythmic shouts and the clash of weapons could be heard from beyond a high wall.

"That is the Martial Training Academy's Grand Drill Ground."

...

The Grand Drill Ground of the Martial Training Academy was larger than Lee Hyun had imagined.

The yellow-earth field enclosed by high walls was so vast that the wall on the opposite side could not even be seen.

A separate training ground for archery and mounted drills had also been built along one side.

Martial artists wielded weapons everywhere, while tens of thousands of soldiers armed with spears and shields moved in multiple square formations.

"Thrust!"

"Ha–!"

Thousands of spears shot forward in unison.

The combined sound of them tearing through the air resembled the roar of some enormous beast.

"Recover!"

Thud!

As the soldiers stamped their feet simultaneously, the ground trembled faintly.

Lee Hyun climbed a tall reviewing pavilion on one side of the Grand Drill Ground with the Crown Prince's party.

From there, they could overlook the entire Grand Drill Ground.

The most conspicuous sight of all was the enormous sparring platform in the center.

Its floor was paved with thick stone slabs fired with black sand mixed into them. Sword marks that looked carved by blades and deep depressions scarred the surface everywhere.

More than a thousand masters of the martial path stood around the sparring platform.

Those in the front row all possessed extraordinarily vigorous blood and vitality.

More than ten of them radiated presences powerful enough to pique even Lee Hyun's interest.

'Are those masters of the Transformation Realm?'

Yet those very experts now stood silently, staring only at the center of the sparring platform.

Two men faced each other there.

One was a huge elderly man whose hair had gone half white. He had rolled up the sleeves of his gray martial robes and held an unadorned longsword in one hand.

The Crown Prince pointed toward him.

"That is Great Hero Guo Tianxiong, Academy Head of the Martial Training Academy. He is a master of the Profound Realm who oversees the martial training and live-combat sparring of martial artists belonging to the military."

Opposite Guo Tianxiong stood a middle-aged martial artist in armor.

"That is General Jiang Wuzhen of the Southern Army. He too has reached the Profound Realm. Today, he is scheduled to depart at the head of thirty thousand reinforcements to bolster the defenders of Lushui Pass."

Lushui Pass was a fortress where the waterways and embankment roads of southern Yunze Kingdom converged. Any large Qianyang army entering southern Yunze Kingdom had to pass through it.

Today's sparring match was meant to assess Jiang Wuzhen's martial arts before his departure and conduct one final check of how he should respond to the enemy commanders he would encounter at Lushui Pass.

The two men stood over a hundred jang (over 300 m) apart.

"They are starting that far away from each other?"

"If they stood close together, the match might be decided before the drum announcing the start even sounded."

No sooner had he finished speaking than a massive drum boomed.

Boom–

The drumbeat still hung in the air when both men vanished simultaneously.

Boom!

A thunderclap erupted at the center of the sparring platform.

A violent gust spread in every direction, whipping even the banners atop the pavilion.

The first thing Lee Hyun saw was a brilliant white sword aura soaring through the air.

The crescent-shaped sword aura, several jang long, cut diagonally across the sparring platform. A line as thin as a strand of hair appeared across the black stone slabs, and only a moment later did the slabs split apart along it.

Boom!

The instant Guo Tianxiong's and Jiang Wuzhen's swords collided, the air itself seemed to cave inward, and a translucent circular ripple spread outward from the point of impact.

The black stone slabs covering the sparring platform exploded in every direction.

Slice!

Jiang Wuzhen's sword aura cleaved Guo Tianxiong's body in half. But what it cut was only an afterimage.

Guo Tianxiong had already appeared behind Jiang Wuzhen and swung his sword. Three streams of sword aura descended toward Jiang Wuzhen's neck, waist, and knees.

Jiang Wuzhen spun around and swung his own sword. The sword aura extending from his longsword collided head-on with all three incoming streams.

Flash!

A burst of white light erupted.

Before the sound of the first collision could even be heard, the second and third impacts followed in rapid succession.

To ordinary soldiers, all that could be seen were flashes of light.

Lee Hyun, however, could see both men's movements.

Whenever a sword was blocked, an elbow came flying in. If the upper body slipped away, a knee targeted the abdomen. The instant one man retreated half a step, the other had already begun his next attack.

Boom!

At some point, Jiang Wuzhen was sent sliding back dozens of jang. A long crack appeared across his armor.

Before his backward momentum had even stopped, Jiang Wuzhen stamped his foot.

Boom!

The stone slabs burst apart, and a black figure shot forward like an arrow.

Slice!

A sword aura grazed Guo Tianxiong's cheek and cut through a stone pillar behind him.

Before the severed pillar could even hit the ground, a low hum rose from Guo Tianxiong's longsword. Dust and powdered stone were blasted outward all at once as brilliant white sword aura surged upward like a whirlwind.

Rumble–

A flash of light swallowed the sparring platform.

When the light faded, both men had already stopped moving.

The tip of Guo Tianxiong's sword rested against Jiang Wuzhen's throat.

A finger joint's length of sword aura also extended from Jiang Wuzhen's longsword, stopping one cun (about 3 cm) from Guo Tianxiong's chest.

The two remained that way for a moment.

Guo Tianxiong was the first to withdraw his sword.

"Half a move too slow."

Jiang Wuzhen lowered his longsword as well.

A thin line of blood remained across his neck where the sword tip had cut him.

"Had this been a real battle, Academy Head, you would not have escaped unscathed either."

"If all of Qianyang Kingdom's experts were only at my level, that would be true."

Guo Tianxiong wiped the blood from his cheek with his sleeve.

"But the Army-Breaking Sword, Wu Tianyue, who is advancing on Lushui Pass, is faster than I am."

Jiang Wuzhen's expression grew grave.

"While General Jiang keeps Wu Tianyue occupied, the rest of you must work with the Military Retainers and cut off the experts under his command."

...

Lee Hyun looked down at the sparring platform.

'So that's what a master of the Profound Realm is capable of.'

It was difficult to compare them directly with cultivators, but there was no doubting their ability to kill an enemy.

More impressive than their power was the speed of their judgment.

Neither man waited for the other's technique to be completed. The moment a sword began to move, the other was already evading. The instant an attack was blocked, the next method followed.

Lee Hyun, on the other hand, had learned dozens of techniques, yet when he imagined Guo Tianxiong charging toward him right now, he could not immediately decide what he should use first.

Should he force him back with the Qi Sphere Barrier? Pierce his skull with the Yang Metal Art? Blast him head-on with the Fireball Art and create some distance? Escape underground with the Earth Escape Art? Meet his sword with the Azure Steel Sword Art?

By the time he finished considering each option in turn, Guo Tianxiong's sword might already be at his throat.

'Achieving Major Attainment in techniques and being good at fighting are two different things.'

The techniques Lee Hyun had learned thus far were like finely honed weapons, but no matter how many weapons he possessed, they were useless if he did not know which one to draw at the right moment.

At that moment, a great drumbeat sounded.

Boom–

The soldiers scattered throughout the grounds began to move.

A short while later, thirty thousand soldiers stood in formation at the center of the Grand Drill Ground.

The Crown Prince silently descended from the pavilion.

When he stepped onto the platform in the center of the Grand Drill Ground, the murmuring among the soldiers died down.

The Crown Prince did not immediately raise his voice.

First, he looked toward the shattered sparring platform. Then his gaze slowly traveled from the front of the formation all the way to the rear.

"At dawn three days ago, civilians fleeing Qianyang Kingdom's invasion entered through the southern gate. They had escaped from three villages outside Lushui Pass."

Messengers stationed throughout the ranks repeated the Crown Prince's words in loud voices. His speech was relayed from messenger to messenger until it reached the very back of the formation.

"There were twenty-seven carts. Most of those riding in them were old people and children. Only eleven able-bodied men could still walk on their own. They said the rest had either remained behind and died or fought at the chokepoints to buy their families time to escape."

"If Lushui Pass falls, next time we will not even be able to count the carts. The household registers of the three southern counties will empty. The grain meant for the autumn harvest will burn. The grain barges carrying military provisions will stop running. Before winter comes, a procession of refugees will reach the very gates of Yunjing."

"Seven years ago, when Baishui City fell, my elder brother was among those defending it. When the court debated withdrawal, I was the one who insisted that the city be defended to the end. I believed we could not abandon the people within the walls and withdraw only the soldiers."

"My brother died, while I, who pushed that decision through, am still alive. So today, I will not tell you to give your lives, nor will I tell you to consider death an honor. Death is simply death. It leaves a debt to those who survive and ends the line of a family."

Liu Zhenghui looked over the soldiers in the front ranks before shifting his gaze to the army banner farthest away.

"But if we surrender Lushui Pass, someone else will have to pay that debt in your place. Elderly parents will die on the road, and young children will have to beg for food in unfamiliar towns."

"What you are going to defend are the people who will call your names from inside when you return home and knock on the door."

Not even the scrape of armor could be heard across the Grand Drill Ground.

Only then did the Crown Prince draw the sword at his waist.

Shing–

The sword tip pointed south.

"There is no second city behind Lushui Pass for us to retreat to. Behind it are only the people. Your parents, your wives and children, your ancestors' graves, and the fields whose crops have yet to be harvested."

Liu Zhenghui paused.

"Do not die. If you want to return alive, do not surrender Lushui Pass."

"Go and hold it."

The messengers repeated the final command, and the words fell over the heads of thirty thousand soldiers.

Thud–

The weapons of thirty thousand soldiers struck the ground as one.

"We obey!"

A single roar shook the Grand Drill Ground.

No further chant followed.

Jiang Wuzhen turned, and the standard-bearers raised the army banners. The thirty thousand soldiers split into several columns and began moving toward the southern gate.

For a long while, the clash of metal and the footsteps of thirty thousand soldiers continued to echo across the Grand Drill Ground.

Lee Hyun silently watched the sight.

To him, dynasties of the mundane world were fleeting things with short lifespans.

But to those soldiers, Yunze Kingdom seemed to be their entire world, the villages and homes where they had been born, where their parents and children lived.

Lee Hyun felt he could understand, at least a little, why the Crown Prince had cast aside all concern for appearances and knelt before a cultivator he had never met.

...

After the troop review ended, the Crown Prince returned to the pavilion.

His voice had become slightly hoarse.

"My apologies for keeping you waiting."

"It is fine."

"Were you bored?"

"Quite the opposite. I learned a great deal."

Lee Hyun looked toward the sparring platform split apart by sword marks.

"Can cultivators also learn martial arts or combat at the Martial Training Academy?"

The Crown Prince's eyes brightened.

"Of course. Some of the Retainers regularly spar with experts from the Martial Training Academy to develop practical combat experience."

Zheng Yuanbo added,

"Being powerful with techniques does not mean one is good at fighting. Rogue cultivators who train alone in the mountains, in particular, are often poor at fighting other people."

Lee Hyun nodded with an unconcerned expression. It felt as though Zheng Yuanbo were describing him exactly.

"Then if I register as a Retainer, I could learn as well."

"An excellent idea. Once you become a Retainer, fellow Daoist, if you wish, I will personally ask Academy Head Guo."

"Would that be all right even though I know nothing about combat?"

"It is precisely fellow Daoists like you who need to learn."

Zheng Yuanbo pointed toward the shattered sparring platform.

"A Qi Refining Stage 3 cultivator who knows nothing of combat can be killed even by a Transcendent Peak master. But a properly trained cultivator can fight a master of the Transformation Realm, and if talented enough, would not simply be killed without resistance even by a master of the Profound Realm."

"The difference is truly that great?"

"In real combat, cases even more extreme than my example are common. A realm only shows a portion of the power one possesses. The difference between someone who accurately understands both the enemy and himself and someone who does not is far greater than fellow Daoist imagines."

Zheng Yuanbo stroked his beard.

"Cultivators possess many more methods at their disposal, so once they learn how to fight properly in real combat, they can grow stronger far faster than martial artists. Most, however, consider learning from martial artists beneath them."

"If it helps me survive, I am willing to learn from anyone. I want to learn not only how to fight martial artists, but martial arts themselves if possible."

"Ha ha. Ordinarily, there would be no need to go so far as learning martial arts yourself, but that attitude is truly admirable."

The Crown Prince's expression brightened as he listened to Lee Hyun and Zheng Yuanbo speak. It seemed increasingly likely that Lee Hyun would join the Fengtian Bureau.

"First, let us arrange somewhere for you to stay for the next few days."

Chapter 20

After leaving the Martial Training Academy, the Crown Prince led Lee Hyun to a canal a short distance from the Fengtian Bureau.

Large and small villas lined the canal that ran through the inner city. They were guest villas where envoys from other kingdoms and rogue cultivators invited from outside stayed.

The residence the Crown Prince had arranged for Lee Hyun was one of them, Qingliang Villa.

A high white wall surrounded the villa. Above the main gate hung a signboard bearing the words Qingliang Villa in gold against a blue background, while two warriors in blue martial uniforms stood guard beneath it.

When they reached the main gate, the Crown Prince said,

“Retainer Zheng and I have matters to attend to back at the Fengtian Bureau. If you need anything, please speak to the villa’s steward.”

“Is it really all right for me to stay here? I haven’t even become a Retainer yet.”

Lee Hyun looked at the villa beyond the gate. Even in modern Korea in his past life, he had never stayed anywhere this luxurious.

‘This place looks incredibly expensive...’

The Crown Prince smiled.

“Yunze Kingdom is neither shameless nor poor enough to force someone to become a Retainer merely because we offered them hospitality. Please don’t worry.”

Zheng Yuanbo, standing beside him, cleared his throat.

“At least, not yet.”

“Retainer Zheng, you have a remarkable talent for making things sound strange whenever you add a comment.”

After exchanging a few more words, the two departed.

Inside the main gate, the villa’s staff stood in a line waiting for Lee Hyun.

At the very front stood a thin man in his fifties. A ring of keys and a small ledger hung from his waist.

“I am Cui Da, steward of Qingliang Villa. I pay my respects to the Immortal.”

He bowed deeply at the waist.

After him, a clerk, four maidservants, a cook and assistant cook, two guards, a coachman, and several servants greeted Lee Hyun in turn. Altogether, there were well over ten people.

The four maidservants in particular were all elegant and beautiful. Two of them were even more striking than the beauties in the illustrations of the tales of everyday life Lee Hyun had read before.

‘Did they hire them based on looks alone?’

The four maidservants simultaneously took a step back and opened a path.

Even the height to which they raised their hands matched perfectly, not just their movements.

‘Looks like they’ve been thoroughly trained in etiquette too.’

Cui Da guided Lee Hyun farther inside.

Beyond the main gate lay a spacious garden.

A pond sat in the middle of the garden, crossed by a jade-colored bridge. Gold-and-red carp swam lazily through the water.

Low flowering trees and Insect-Warding Grass had been planted in rows on either side of the stone path.

At the very back stood a large two-story hall.

Its roof, covered in blue glazed tiles, glittered in the sunlight.

And yet water was constantly flowing over the roof.

“What is that?”

When Lee Hyun stopped and asked, Cui Da explained as though he had been waiting for the question.

“The waterwheel behind the villa draws water up from the canal.”

When they went around the back of the building, they saw a huge waterwheel rising higher than the hall’s roof ridge, turning slowly.

Wooden buckets were attached at regular intervals around the outer rim of the wheel, each tilted at an angle.

The buckets scooped up canal water at the bottom and carried it upward. When a bucket reached the top, it overturned and poured its contents into a trough beside it. The water then flowed along the trough into an elevated tank behind the hall.

The water collected in the tank flowed through several bamboo pipes to the roof ridge.

Countless narrow grooves had been carved into the surface of the blue-green glazed tiles.

The water divided along those grooves and spread across the entire roof, then fell from the eaves in thin streams like a curtain.

Some of the water evaporated from the roof beneath the sunlight.

Whenever the wind blew, the cooled air flowed beneath the eaves.

“Is it a device for cooling the roof?”

“As expected of an Immortal. Your wisdom is extraordinary to recognize it at a glance. It was designed to keep the interior cool even at the height of summer. The water that flows over the roof collects in channels beneath the eaves before draining into the garden pond.”

“I see. Fascinating.”

“The entire device was made by craftsmen of the mundane world.”

Lee Hyun stared at the waterwheel and roof for quite some time.

‘I have to admit it. This is way more impressive than Tunnel No. 1’s water supply system...’

When he entered the hall, a genuinely cool breeze greeted him.

The doors and windows were wide open, yet not a single insect was in sight.

“That’s impressive. There aren’t any insects?”

As Lee Hyun looked around, Cui Da pointed to a thin silk mesh fixed over the window frame.

“This mesh keeps out flying insects. We also use Insect-Warding Grass and Insect-Warding Incense throughout the villa. We have even stocked the pond with fish that feed on mosquito larvae.”

“You’ve thought of everything.”

“An Immortal will be staying here. There must be nothing lacking.”

The first-floor reception room contained tables and chairs made from reddish wood.

Landscape paintings and calligraphy hung on the walls, while a brazier in the corner gave off an extremely faint grassy fragrance.

Farther inside were a bedroom, a study, and a separate bathing room.

The bedroom contained a bed wide enough for three people to lie side by side with room to spare. A soft mattress and thin silk quilt had been neatly laid across it.

Tea chilled with ice and sliced fruit had been prepared on the table.

After explaining the villa’s facilities and meal times, Cui Da withdrew.

The maidservants also brewed fresh tea, set down a plate of fruit, and left the room.

Once alone, Lee Hyun first used the Aura-Reading Art to examine the walls, ceiling, and floor in turn, but he found no suspicious traces of spiritual power.

He circulated the Keen Hearing Art and listened even to the faintest sounds nearby.

He could hear the maidservants speaking softly in the distance and the sound of a knife striking a cutting board in the kitchen, but there was nothing suspicious.

Finally, he used the Ground-Sense Art.

An intricate network of drainage channels and water pipes ran beneath the villa, but there did not seem to be anyone hiding below or any secret passages.

‘There really aren’t any traps...’

He carefully sat on the edge of the bed.

The soft mattress yielded beneath his weight.

A moment later, he lay back completely.

He could faintly hear water flowing across the roof, and a cool breeze drifted through the open window.

He picked up a piece of fruit a maidservant had peeled and put it into his mouth.

It was sweet and cool.

‘So this is what a life of wealth and luxury is like....’

Even as he simply lay there, a cool breeze continued to blow.

‘I think I understand a little why people like power so much.’

Lee Hyun marveled at it for a moment before sitting up again.

‘Maybe I should look around some more.’

...

Hundreds of books filled the shelves in the study.

Perhaps because this was a place where guests of the royal family and the Fengtian Bureau stayed, many of the books concerned the history, geography, and etiquette of Yunze Kingdom.

Lee Hyun first took out Lives of the Fengtian Retainers.

It was a collection detailing the deeds of Retainers who had left their names in history since the Fengtian Bureau was founded.

There was a cultivator who had saved a village by killing a demon beast, and a Craft Retainer who had spent three years studying aquatic plants to eradicate spirit insects breeding in a river. Another Retainer had fought a master at the Profound Realm from Qianyang Kingdom, only for both of them to fall into a river and disappear.

Lee Hyun next opened Record of Yunze Waterways.

It was a book describing the rivers and canals of Yunze Kingdom, along with its ferries, sluice gates, and waterwheels.

The book was surprisingly interesting.

It contained discussions of floods, rivers, wetlands, and embankments, as well as an account of enormous sluice gates beneath Yunjing that diverted the flow of water depending on the rainy and dry seasons.

There were also illustrated diagrams of devices similar to the waterwheel that cooled Qingliang Villa’s roof.

As Lee Hyun flipped through the pages, he found an illustration of a small waterwheel lifting water and supplying it to several tiers of fields.

‘Come to think of it, could I combine the tunnel’s water tanks into one...?’

Lee Hyun had also built elevated tanks and stored spirit rainwater in them, but each spirit field had its own separate tank.

The tunnel’s spirit fields did not use flowing water, so he could not use a waterwheel, but he wondered whether it would be better to connect several spirit fields to one large tank and manage them together.

‘If I ever end up making Tunnel No. 2... it might be worth laying out the water supply system properly from the start.’

Lee Hyun studied the illustration for a long while before taking out the next book.

Eleven Days in Baishui City.

It was a record written by a clerk of what had happened inside Baishui City during the final eleven days before its fall. Lee Hyun browsed it briefly, his expression growing grim at the heavy subject matter, then returned it to the shelf.

Lee Hyun looked for something lighter.

A collection of popular novels fashionable among common folk occupied the lower shelves. Their spines were more worn than those of the other books, and their corners had been polished smooth by many hands.

My Youngest Daughter Turns Out to Be the Greatest Master Under Heaven

I Emerged from Ten Years of Secluded Cultivation to Find My Junior Sister Had Become the Sect Leader

I Took In What I Thought Was a Demon Beast, but It Was a Prince of Qianyang Kingdom

...

By the time he finished browsing through the books, evening had already arrived.

Just then, a maidservant spoke cautiously from outside the door.

“Immortal, your evening meal is ready.”

“Come in.”

Two maidservants entered carrying a low dining table.

Upon it were clear fish soup, roast duck, glutinous rice wrapped in lotus leaves, pickled vegetables, and fruit.

It was food of the mundane world, but both the ingredients and preparation were excellent.

For the first time in a long while, Lee Hyun ate a properly prepared meal while reading.

At first he found the maidservants’ attendance somewhat uncomfortable, but by the third day he had grown accustomed to it.

He refused to let them go so far as to remove his shoes, but he no longer objected to ordinary services such as bringing him tea and food.

Cleanly laundered clothes were prepared every morning, and bathwater at the perfect temperature was made ready without him even asking.

‘This is dangerous...!’

Lee Hyun thought as he sipped plum tea.

‘How am I supposed to go back to living in a dank tunnel after getting used to this kind of luxury?’

...

On the morning of the fourth day.

Zheng Yuanbo came to Qingliang Villa.

“The Retainers conducting your examination have arrived.”

“Have they?”

Lee Hyun quietly closed I Became a Prisoner of Qianyang Kingdom, and Now I’m Popular, which he had been reading.

He slipped it beneath another book so the title would not be visible.

“I’ll be there shortly.”

“Take your time.”

Zheng Yuanbo’s gaze swept over the pile of books.

Lives of the Fengtian Retainers lay on top.

“Looks like you’ve been studying hard.”

“There seemed to be a great deal I should know before entering the Fengtian Bureau.”

“Excellent.”

...

Within the jade-colored walls of the Fengtian Bureau stood a cluster of massive tiled buildings resembling government offices.

Above the main gate hung a signboard bearing the words Fengtian Bureau in gold against a black background.

Stone statues stood on either side of the gate, one holding a sword and the other a fan. One seemed to depict a martial artist, the other a cultivator.

Beyond the main gate, a broad road split into several branches.

Directly ahead stood the Retainers Hall, which handled the Fengtian Bureau’s administration, while the Military Service Hall was to the right.

To the left were buildings used by Craft Retainers, including the Alchemy Hall, Talisman Court, Formation Court, and Infirmary.

The entire Fengtian Bureau felt like a small city unto itself.

Many of the people traveling along its roads were officials and clerks from the mundane world.

Cultivators with storage pouches or retainer badges hanging from their waists could also be seen from time to time.

Most appeared older than Lee Hyun, and there were hardly any young people.

‘Come to think of it, a young Qi Refining cultivator with a promising future would probably join a cultivation sect rather than serve the royal family of the mundane world.’

Zheng Yuanbo guided Lee Hyun into a spacious room inside the Retainers Hall.

Three tables stood side by side inside. A gray-haired female cultivator sat at the center table, while a middle-aged cultivator sat at the table beside her reviewing documents.

Both appeared to be at mid or late Qi Refining.

Zheng Yuanbo sat down at the remaining table.

The female cultivator at the center table spoke.

“I am Standing Retainer Lu Xiaoyan.”

The middle-aged cultivator beside her also cupped his hands.

“Standing Retainer Ma Zhenhao.”

“I am Li Dongyi.”

Lu Xiaoyan unfolded the documents on the table.

“Calling it an examination makes it sound more impressive than it is. We merely verify that there are no problems with your identity, realm, or cultivation art, then explain the rules of the Fengtian Bureau.”

“Understood.”

“Where are you from?”

“I cultivated in the mountains of the north.”

“Can you disclose the exact region?”

“I’m afraid I cannot.”

“Rogue cultivators who keep their master and the origins of their cultivation art secret are hardly uncommon. The Fengtian Bureau will not pry. Is there anyone within Yunze Kingdom who bears you a grudge, or any faction pursuing you?”

“No.”

“Have you ever practiced a demonic cultivation art, or used a mortal’s essence blood or soul in your cultivation?”

“No.”

Lu Xiaoyan nodded to the clerk beside her. The clerk recorded Lee Hyun’s answers in the retainer register.

“Your age?”

“Twenty-nine.”

After careful consideration, Lee Hyun had decided to claim he was twenty-nine.

If he said he was in his early twenties, it would be difficult to explain why someone his age had chosen a mundane dynasty over a cultivation sect. On the other hand, if he claimed to be too old, it would shorten the amount of time he could continue living without arousing suspicion even if his appearance never aged.

‘No one should find it strange if my appearance doesn’t change for around twenty years. I have to get the pill recipe for the Barrier-Breaking Pill and learn alchemy before then.’

Lu Xiaoyan did not seem particularly suspicious.

“Next, we will verify your realm and attributes.”

Lu Xiaoyan took a black stone from beneath the table. It was round and about the size of an adult’s head, with three overlapping circles engraved into its surface.

“This is a realm-measuring stone. It roughly determines one’s realm by examining the quality of their spiritual power. Send a little spiritual power into it.”

Lee Hyun placed a hand on the stone.

He drew only an extremely thin strand of the Primordial True Qi throughout his body into his palm.

Hummm―

The innermost circle of the realm-measuring stone shone brightly.

“The peak of early Qi Refining...”

Lu Xiaoyan said.

“You’ve reached the end of Stage 3, but the qualitative change has not occurred yet.”

“That’s correct.”

“Your control over your spiritual power is extraordinarily stable. Enough to make me wonder whether you possess an exceptional inheritance...”

Ma Zhenhao said as he examined the realm-measuring stone.

“It seems my spiritual power is pure because I have cultivated the same cultivation art steadily without ever switching to another.”

Next came a round tray inset with five differently colored pieces of jade.

When Lee Hyun sent spiritual power into it, the blue jade representing Wood, the red jade representing Fire, and the yellow jade representing Earth lit up in sequence.

“A triple spiritual root?”

Lu Xiaoyan recorded the result.

“At twenty-nine... you are still fairly young, and your spiritual root is not bad. Is there a reason you came to the Fengtian Bureau of Yunze Kingdom rather than joining a cultivation sect?”

“In a cultivation sect, I would have to live as a low-ranking disciple, while in a kingdom of the mundane world, I can enjoy a high status and be treated with respect.”

Lu Xiaoyan fell silent for a moment, then nodded.

“...Well, you are not wrong. Most Qi Refining cultivators spend their entire lives in sects laboring like slaves before dying there. Though if I were in your position, I think I would have aimed for Foundation Establishment.”

Finally, Ma Zhenhao took a small bronze lamp from beneath the table.

The lamp’s body was densely carved with the faces of beasts with gaping mouths, and a single silver wick stood in its center.

Although it contained no oil, when Ma Zhenhao rubbed the wick with his finger, a white flame the size of a fingernail sprang to life.

“This is a demon-detecting lamp, a magic tool used to determine whether someone has practiced a sinister cultivation art. You need only send a little spiritual power into it.”

Lee Hyun placed a hand on the body of the lamp and sent a strand of Primordial True Qi into it. The white flame did not change. If anything, its light became even clearer than before.

“No problem.”

Ma Zhenhao closed the demon-detecting lamp’s lid.

“Lastly, show us one technique you use frequently. It is rare, but there are some who cannot properly use even a single technique.”

Lee Hyun formed a simple hand seal with his fingers.

Hummm―

A translucent Spirit Light Shield appeared before his palm.

It was about the size of a small tray.

Lu Xiaoyan flicked a small iron ball from the table with her finger.

Clang!

The iron ball struck the Spirit Light Shield and fell to the floor.

Not even a ripple appeared across the Spirit Light Shield.

“Good.”

Lu Xiaoyan said so, but Ma Zhenhao examined the Spirit Light Shield a little more closely.

“Could this really be... a Spirit Light Shield?”

“That’s right. Is there a problem?”

“No, it’s... not a problem... It’s just incredibly stable. You look like someone who has cast the Spirit Light Shield every day for decades.”

“I didn’t know many techniques. I suppose I naturally became proficient by repeatedly practicing the few I had learned.”

“Excellent.”

Zheng Yuanbo spoke.

“It’s better to master even one technique properly than to constantly covet new ones. And if that technique happens to be the Spirit Light Shield, you may have a talent well suited to becoming a Military Retainer.”

...

The examination ended without any particular problems.

Lu Xiaoyan opened the retainer register.

“At present, the Fengtian Bureau’s Retainers are divided into four categories: Standing Retainers, External Retainers, Military Retainers, and Craft Retainers. Do you know the differences?”

“Yes.”

“Which do you want?”

“Can I change categories later?”

“As often as you like.”

“Then I’ll start as an External Retainer.”

In truth, Lee Hyun would have liked to become a Craft Retainer and practice alchemy, but he knew nothing about alchemy.

If an alchemist volunteered to become a Craft Retainer, Yunze Kingdom would practically bow in gratitude, but someone who merely wanted to learn alchemy was just another nobody.

If Lee Hyun wanted to learn alchemy, he would instead have to accumulate merit points and ask a Craft Retainer to teach him.

There was also the option of choosing spirit plants as his Craft Retainer specialty, then mingling with the other Retainers and subtly learning alchemy from them. But spirit plants were not a field that produced results quickly, so it was unsuitable for earning the merit points he needed to learn alchemy and obtain the pill recipe within twenty years.

Moreover, there was another problem with becoming a Craft Retainer through spirit-plant work. Every one of Lee Hyun’s spirit-plant cultivation techniques had been learned at Qinghe Valley.

If it were discovered that Qinghe Valley’s spirit-plant cultivation techniques were being used by a mortal dynasty, both Lee Hyun and Yunze Kingdom could find themselves in tremendous danger.

Even excluding Qinghe Valley’s Golden Core Patriarch, there were dozens of Foundation Establishment cultivators serving as Elders. If even one of them came and began slaughtering people, the royal family of Yunze Kingdom would be laid waste.

Of course, Lee Hyun had no way of knowing whether Qinghe Valley still retained the same strength it once had. But unless its power had declined drastically in the meantime, Yunze Kingdom was in no position to contend with it.

‘Even if nothing happens while I’m here, disaster could strike Yunze Kingdom after I leave. I can’t take on spirit-plant work...’

...

Lu Xiaoyan explained the merit-point system and the rules Retainers were required to follow.

Most of it was common sense, such as prohibitions against killing mortals without cause or seizing their property.

“If you have no particular objections, I will register you as an External Retainer.”

“I have no objections.”

After recording the final details, the clerk stamped the Fengtian Bureau’s seal onto the retainer register.

The moment the red seal paste soaked into the paper, the tiny formation patterns engraved along the edges of the retainer register lit up one after another.

The clerk placed a blue jade badge atop the retainer register and engraved Lee Hyun’s name into it with a silver needle.

Lu Xiaoyan handed him the jade badge.

A crane soaring above the clouds was carved on the front, while the back bore the words ‘External Retainer Li Dongyi.’

“Your retainer badge, fellow Daoist.”

It felt strange to have suddenly become a Retainer of a kingdom in the mundane world.

“Your registration is complete. You may continue using Qingliang Villa as your residence. Do you have any other questions?”

Lee Hyun was about to put the jade badge into his storage pouch when he stopped.

“How many merit points would I need to learn alchemy and obtain the pill recipe for the Barrier-Breaking Pill?”

“See for yourself.”

Lu Xiaoyan gestured to the clerk.

The clerk retrieved the Fengtian Merit Register from a bookshelf on one side of the room.

The Fengtian Merit Register was a ledger classifying missions, rewards, and the requirements for using various facilities. Dozens of colored index tabs lined the edges of its pages.

Lee Hyun immediately opened the section on pills and alchemy.

「One Barrier-Breaking Pill: 100 merit points. 10 low-grade spirit stones charged separately.」

「Introductory Alchemy Lecture: 20 merit points.」

「Advanced Alchemy Lecture: 50 merit points. Completion of the Introductory Alchemy Lecture required.」

「Rental of pill furnace and earth fire facilities: 10 merit points per month. Medicinal ingredients and auxiliary materials must be prepared separately.」

「Pill recipe for the Barrier-Breaking Pill: 500 merit points. External transmission and sale prohibited.」

‘Hmm... Even if I only learn introductory and advanced alchemy, obtain the pill recipe for the Barrier-Breaking Pill, and rent a pill furnace for a single month... that comes to 580 merit points? But to actually practice alchemy, I’ll need medicinal ingredients too, and I’ll have to rent the facilities for longer.’

In practice, Lee Hyun would need well over 600 merit points.

‘How much work would it take to earn 600 points?’

Lee Hyun flipped farther through the Fengtian Merit Register.

This time, he found missions available to External Retainers.

But most missions rewarded only between one and five merit points.

‘Why are they so stingy...?’

“Can I apply for this mission now?”

“Four people have already applied. Priority goes to those who have served as External Retainers for a long time and those who have not received a mission recently.”

“What about removing the spirit insects from the Qingshui River?”

“The same applies.”

“Then this investigation mission....”

“It has already been assigned.”

“There are fewer missions than I expected.”

“It cannot be helped. There are many External Retainers, but very few missions worth awarding merit points in the first place. Aside from fighting Qianyang Kingdom...”

‘There’s no way I can learn alchemy and obtain the pill recipe within twenty years as an External Retainer...’

Lee Hyun examined the Fengtian Merit Register again. Other types of Retainers, particularly Military Retainers, had far more missions available and received the most merit points as rewards.

‘Maybe I’d be better off becoming a Military Retainer. First, I need to find out whether I’m actually strong enough to handle Military Retainer missions.’

Lee Hyun closed the Fengtian Merit Register and asked,

“Do I also need merit points to receive sparring instruction from masters of the martial path at the Martial Training Academy?”

“No.”

Zheng Yuanbo answered with a smile.

“The martial artists of the Martial Training Academy love sparring with cultivators, so do not worry. I will contact Academy Head Guo for you.”

...

The next day.

Lee Hyun visited the Grand Drill Ground of the Martial Training Academy.

Unlike before, when it had been filled with soldiers preparing for deployment, the Grand Drill Ground was quiet. In the distance, soldiers were practicing shield techniques, while pairs of martial artists crossed weapons on several smaller training platforms.

Lee Hyun was guided to a separate training ground enclosed by walls.

Wooden swords, wooden spears, and blunted iron weapons were neatly arranged along one side.

Two people were waiting in the center of the training ground.

One was Academy Head Guo Tianxiong, a master of the Profound Realm. The other was a middle-aged martial artist who appeared to be in his mid-forties. He wore a dark navy martial uniform, and an old scar ran from his temple down to his jaw.

Guo Tianxiong introduced him.

“This is Instructor Xu Zhenming of the Martial Training Academy. Not only is he a master of the Transformation Realm, he is also better at teaching people than I am.”

“Greetings, Immortal. I am Xu Zhenming.”

“Nice to meet you. I am Li Dongyi.”

A short while later, Lee Hyun and Xu Zhenming each held a wooden sword with its edges rounded smooth.

“First, we need to see where you currently stand. Since this is your first time, don’t overthink it. Just fight however you like. There’s no need to be too afraid, either. I’ll be right beside you, so neither of you will suffer any serious injuries.”

“Understood.”

Lee Hyun and Xu Zhenming faced each other from about ten zhang (about 30 m) apart.

Guo Tianxiong turned to Xu Zhenming.

“Zhenming, this Immortal is a young, newly appointed Retainer. Show him a little of what real combat is like. Just don’t press him too hard from the very beginning.”

“Yes.”

Xu Zhenming answered, but his voice cracked slightly. His right hand trembled around the wooden sword.

Xu Zhenming tightened his fingers to suppress the trembling. But the moment he focused on Lee Hyun standing before him, the sword began to shake again.

Cold sweat ran down his back. The hairs on the back of his neck stood on end, and without realizing it, his breathing grew shallow.

‘What is going on?’

Chapter 21

Xu Zhenming stood gripping his wooden sword, unable to bring himself to take the first step.

There was nothing particularly unusual about Lee Hyun's stance before him.

Even so, the instincts that had kept Xu Zhenming alive for so many years continued to warn him of the same thing.

'I must not fight that young Immortal.'

For the first time in a long while, Xu Zhenming recalled a memory from his childhood.

He had been only ten years old when he encountered an enormous bear that had come down from the mountain in search of food before winter.

The bear had merely looked down at the young Xu Zhenming from the slope above. Yet at the time, Xu Zhenming had barely been able to breathe.

The sense that his life and death rested entirely in the beast before him. The helplessness of knowing that nothing he did could change the outcome.

Decades had passed since then, and now that he had reached the Transformation Realm, Xu Zhenming had never imagined he would once again feel like a child standing before a savage beast.

...

Meanwhile, Lee Hyun was carefully observing Xu Zhenming.

'So this is a master of the Transformation Realm.'

The tip of Xu Zhenming's sword trembled almost imperceptibly without pause. At a glance, it looked as though his hand was shaking, but a master of the Transformation Realm was a martial artist who had reached a level rarely seen even across an entire kingdom. There was no way such a man was simply trembling.

Naturally, every tiny movement had to contain profound skill honed through real combat.

Lee Hyun was a cultivator who trained the Primordial Body, and his entire body had been tempered by spiritual power. His dynamic vision was exceptional as well.

Looking more closely, he saw that the wooden sword never remained in the same position. The tip seemed to point upward before dropping down, and the instant it angled left, it was already poised to transition into a straight thrust. The angles of Xu Zhenming's wrist, elbow, and shoulder were also shifting by amounts too small for an ordinary eye to notice.

It was completely different from the fixed opening stances he had seen in the Azure Steel Sword Art. Was Xu Zhenming creating constant variations from the very moment he raised his sword, allowing a single stance to flow into dozens of different attacks?

'So this is the martial path... A form unconstrained by predetermined moves. Since they can't directly harness spiritual qi, they must have refined their handling of weapons to the absolute limit.'

Lee Hyun's expression grew even more serious.

Just then, Xu Zhenming hurriedly shouted.

"W-wait!"

Guo Tianxiong, who had been watching from beside the training ground, frowned.

"What is it?"

"Please wait a moment."

Without taking his eyes off Lee Hyun, Xu Zhenming retreated two steps. Then his lips moved slightly as he sent a voice transmission that only Guo Tianxiong could hear.

[Something is strange.]

[What is strange?]

[It's difficult to explain. Standing in front of him, my body refuses to move.]

[Do you sense killing intent?]

[No. I just... feel that I must not oppose him.]

Guo Tianxiong was slightly surprised.

He knew Xu Zhenming's temperament well. Xu Zhenming was a bold fellow who had once held a chokepoint while surrounded by two Transformation Realm masters from Qianyang Kingdom until his companions could escape.

And yet that same man could not even begin a sparring match with wooden swords?

Guo Tianxiong walked onto the training ground.

[I'll try first.]

When he extended a hand, Xu Zhenming passed him the wooden sword. Guo Tianxiong lightly swung it several times to gauge its weight, then stood opposite Lee Hyun.

"Instructor Xu seems to be feeling unwell today. Allow me to face you first."

"Please go easy on me."

"Of course."

Guo Tianxiong replied as though it were nothing, but the moment he faced Lee Hyun directly, his gaze changed.

The instant he leveled his sword, his chest tightened. It felt as though an enormous, invisible mountain were suspended above his head.

Before he realized it, Guo Tianxiong was gripping the wooden sword tightly. As he suppressed the tremor threatening to shake the sword tip, the veins stood out sharply on the back of his hand, and tiny beads of sweat had already formed across his forehead.

...

Lee Hyun found himself impressed once again.

'Academy Head Guo's opening stance is even more profound.'

Guo Tianxiong's wooden sword was also trembling ever so slightly. But while Xu Zhenming's sword had revealed clear variations, Guo Tianxiong's instead seemed as though all variation had vanished.

Yet on closer examination, the pressure of his fingers on the hilt and the angles of his wrist, elbow, and shoulder were changing from one instant to the next.

The sword stood still, yet it was constantly moving. There was no predicting which direction his attack would come from.

Compared to the limitless possibilities created by Guo Tianxiong's restraint, the changes at Xu Zhenming's fingertips looked like child's play!

'Is this the realm of stillness within motion!'

The moment Lee Hyun tensely gripped his wooden sword with both hands, Guo Tianxiong lowered his sword first.

"?"

"There are a few things I would like to confirm first. I want to know what offensive means Retainer Li can use in actual combat."

"For offensive techniques, I've learned one that launches a ball of fire, one that fires needles of spiritual power, and a type of sword art. I also know a technique that uses a barrier of qi to push away everything around me..."

"Do you have techniques for defense and movement as well?"

"One creates a shield, one lightens my body, one lets me run quickly, and one lets me enter the ground."

"How proficient are you with the techniques you just mentioned?"

"I've used all of them for a long time, so I'm quite familiar with them."

"For a long time..."

Guo Tianxiong pointed to several wooden boards, leather shields, iron plates, and stone pillars set up along one side of the training ground.

"Before we begin sparring, I would like to see how dangerous Retainer Li's techniques are. After all, if we do not know their exact power, someone may be injured."

"Understood."

'Hmm... If I want to look like an ordinary Qi Refining Stage 3 cultivator... how much spiritual power should I use for a basic technique...?'

After calculating for a moment, Lee Hyun drew a small amount of spiritual power to his fingertip.

"This is a technique called the Yang Metal Art. It's used to kill spirit insects."

A thin strand of silvery-white energy condensed at the tip of his finger.

Flash.

A slender silver needle tore through the air.

The Yang Metal Art pierced through the wooden board in front, passed straight through the leather shield behind it, then left a small hole in the center of an iron plate as thick as a finger.
