Even after piercing the iron plate, the remaining silver needle drove nearly half a chi (about 15 cm) into the stone pillar behind it before finally disappearing.

Guo Tianxiong approached the iron plate and examined the hole.

'Hell... this is what he uses to kill bugs?'

Lee Hyun had deliberately used only a little spiritual power, but his mastery of the technique was so high that its power was still astonishing.

"Then... would you show us the next technique as well?"

Next came the Fireball Art.

A fireball the size of a fist appeared above Lee Hyun's palm. A chillingly immense power emanated from it.

Unlike ordinary flames, the fire on its surface did not spread outward, but curled inward toward the center of the sphere. The closer it came to the center, the brighter it grew, until it turned a dazzling white.

When he extended his hand, the fireball shot rapidly toward a stone pillar.

Flash!

A blinding burst of light erupted.

BOOM!

Scorching heat and a violent shockwave blasted outward in every direction.

The impact shook the ground, traveled up through Guo Tianxiong and Xu Zhenming's feet, and rattled their organs. Dust billowed into the air along with an acrid smell.

The stone pillar had been shattered by the blast pressure. The surface of the remaining stump was cracked like a spiderweb, while several areas glowed red-hot and had even begun to melt slightly.

"......?"

Finally, Lee Hyun decided to demonstrate the Azure Steel Sword Art.

With a flash of light, the broad, thick Earth Shovel Sword sprang out of his storage pouch. Its tip struck the stone floor with a heavy sound.

Thud.

Guo Tianxiong and Xu Zhenming looked back and forth between the Earth Shovel Sword and Lee Hyun's face for a moment, then nodded.

'Weapons used by Immortals really do have unusual shapes.'

Lee Hyun gripped the Earth Shovel Sword with both hands and activated the Azure Steel Sword Art. Blue light spread across the broad blade.

The light extended far beyond the sword, forming a translucent blade three chi long.

Once the blue energy covered the blunt shape of the Earth Shovel Sword, it finally resembled a properly proportioned greatsword.

Lee Hyun swung the sword diagonally.

Slice!

The upper section of the standing stone pillar remained in place for a moment before slowly sliding sideways and falling to the ground.

Guo Tianxiong inspected the cut surface and fell silent.

"......"

Lee Hyun lowered the Earth Shovel Sword.

"My apologies. Did I destroy too much?"

"It's fine. Things break here all the time anyway."

Lee Hyun returned the Earth Shovel Sword to his storage pouch.

Guo Tianxiong maintained a calm expression, but his thoughts were considerably more complicated.

The newly appointed Retainer named Li Dongyi possessed techniques far too powerful to judge him solely by his realm of Qi Refining Stage 3.

Guo Tianxiong had heard that cultivation realm and mastery of techniques were separate matters, but it still left him somewhat deflated to see such a young man wield means that even he, one of the foremost martial artists in all of Yunze Kingdom, could not casually confront head-on.

'Even a martial genius as exceptional as me would struggle to take the techniques of a Qi Refining Stage 3 cultivator head-on...?'

The Retainers of the Fengtian Bureau rarely sparred with Guo Tianxiong and the others, and even when they occasionally did, neither the power nor activation speed of their techniques matched those of the new Retainer before him.

Furthermore, unlike Yunze Kingdom, Qianyang Kingdom did not deploy Qi Refining cultivators, so Guo Tianxiong had almost never had cause to fight one.

Because of that, he had never considered a mere Qi Refining Stage 3 cultivator particularly threatening, making the shock of seeing Lee Hyun's techniques all the greater.

Guo Tianxiong pushed aside his thoughts and spoke.

"As expected, an Immortal's methods are on a completely different scale when it comes to raw power. But such a comparison only means something if we assume the opponent will politely wait while you cast your technique."

"I agree. When I watched the sparring match between Academy Head Guo and General Jiang recently, both of you moved extremely quickly."

"The martial artists of Qianyang Kingdom will not kindly wait for Retainer Li to activate a technique."

At that moment, Xu Zhenming cautiously asked,

"Before that, may I ask you something?"

"Go ahead."

"Have you perhaps learned a technique or cultivation art that frightens people?"

"Hm? I've never learned anything like that..."

Xu Zhenming turned toward Guo Tianxiong with an awkward expression. Guo Tianxiong explained in his place.

"When we stood opposite Retainer Li with swords in hand, we felt an inexplicable pressure."

"Pressure?"

Lee Hyun thought for a moment, then activated the Aura-Concealing Art without releasing the Spirit-Concealing Art. A thin veil that concealed the fluctuations of his spiritual power spread over his skin and wrapped around his entire body.

At that moment, Xu Zhenming and Guo Tianxiong blinked.

"H-how did you do that? The pressure from before is gone."

"It truly is."

'Does the Aura-Concealing Art hide not only fluctuations in spiritual power, but also all the little traces of energy leaking from my body? I should keep the Spirit-Concealing Art and Aura-Concealing Art active together from now on.'

To dispel their suspicions, Lee Hyun offered a plausible excuse.

"It's probably because of my constitution. My family has been unusually strong for generations, and even before I entered the immortal path, my body was sturdy enough to face wild beasts in the mountains. The cultivation art I practice also has some body-tempering properties. Perhaps the two of you sensed the energy that has become ingrained in my body."

Guo Tianxiong stroked his beard as though the explanation made sense.

"So you are an Immortal who also practices body cultivation. No wonder your presence felt unusually powerful."

Xu Zhenming also relaxed and picked up a wooden sword from the rack at one side of the training ground.

"Then allow me to properly explain how martial artists fight cultivators. What do you think is the greatest difference between martial artists like us and cultivators?"

"Isn't it whether one possesses spiritual roots?"

"Correct. Because we have no spiritual roots, we cannot directly absorb heaven-and-earth spiritual qi. We nourish the body's vital essence through food and medicinal ingredients, then refine it over many years into internal energy."

Xu Zhenming opened his palm. As he circulated his internal energy, a faint current moved along the veins on the back of his hand and wrist.

"Once we reach the Transformation Realm or the Profound Realm, we possess power that can hardly be called mortal. Even so, if we compare only our total reserves of power, we cannot match cultivators. That is why masters of the martial path do not compete with cultivators through raw strength."

Xu Zhenming brought over a thick wooden shield and stood it upright, then moved the tip of his sword close to it.

White light gathered at the tip of the wooden sword. At first, the sword aura was as thick as a finger, but with each breath Xu Zhenming took, it gradually narrowed. From the thickness of a little finger to that of a chopstick, then further still until it had been compressed into a fine line no thicker than a large needle.

Xu Zhenming lightly thrust his sword forward.

Thunk!

The thin sword aura pierced through the thick wood and left a small hole in the iron plate positioned behind it.

"Martial artists of Qianyang Kingdom generally call this One Point Pierces the Surface. It means piercing a surface by concentrating force on a single point."

Guo Tianxiong added,

"No matter how sturdy a Qi Refining cultivator's defensive technique may be, any method designed to protect a broad area at once is bound to be vulnerable to an attack concentrated on a single point."

"I see."

'It's not a difficult concept for someone from the modern world like me. The amount of force is fixed, so you reduce the surface area to increase the pressure.'

Next, Guo Tianxiong stabbed the same spot on the wooden shield three times with the tip of his sword. From the outside, the strikes left only shallow marks, but when his fourth thrust drove into exactly the same point, the shield burst apart from within.

Crack!

"If a single strike cannot break through, we can also attack the same point repeatedly. Qianyang Kingdom's Interlocking Sword Formation has several martial artists thrust at the same spot in sequence as though they were a single person."

Xu Zhenming continued explaining.

"It would not be an exaggeration to say that whatever method martial experts of the mundane world use to break through an Immortal's defenses, it ultimately comes down to some form of thrust. Using the principle of One Point Pierces the Surface is the most practical way to kill an Immortal."

This time, Xu Zhenming took out three short wooden throwing knives.

"The next thing you should be wary of is... because Immortals generally have so many different methods available, their attention can easily become divided the moment they hesitate over which one to use. That is when martial experts like us cut their fingers to disrupt their hand seals, attack their eyes so they lose sight of their target, or interfere with their breathing to throw off their mnemonic formula."

He threw the first knife. As it arced high over Lee Hyun's head, Lee Hyun's gaze naturally followed it upward.

At that instant, Xu Zhenming threw the second knife. When it flew toward Lee Hyun's wrist, Lee Hyun drew his hand slightly back. By then, the third knife was already flying toward the top of his foot.

"The third one might be the real attack, or all three could be feints."

"And the moment I evade all the feints, you could rush me directly."

"On top of that, we may hide hidden weapons inside our sleeves and launch them, or scatter stone dust or powdered medicinal ingredients to interfere with sight and smell."

Guo Tianxiong spoke again.

"Then let us consider things from Retainer Li's perspective. If the Fireball Art were the only technique you knew, you would use the Fireball Art the moment you saw an enemy. But Retainer Li knows many techniques, so when attacked, you will first have to decide whether to block, push the enemy away, evade, hide, or counterattack."

"That's true."

"Having many methods is an advantage in itself, but using them seamlessly in actual combat requires that much more situational training. In battle, even if a choice is somewhat imperfect, making it quickly is better than delaying while searching for the perfect answer."

Lee Hyun fell silent for a moment, then nodded.

"I understand that in theory, but how should I train?"

"At first, I will limit the methods you are allowed to use."

Guo Tianxiong raised two fingers.

"Defensive techniques and movement techniques. For now, use only those two categories. Any method that pushes the opponent away must also be used solely for defense."

"No offensive techniques?"

"You may use them if you wish to kill Instructor Xu."

"I won't use them."

Xu Zhenming returned to his position opposite Lee Hyun.

"The rules are simple. Block my attacks or push me away. If that proves difficult, create distance."

"May I enter the ground?"

"That... will be forbidden for now."

"Understood."

The two once again stood facing each other with ten jang (about 30 m) between them.

"Let us begin."

The instant he finished speaking, Xu Zhenming advanced straight toward him and thrust his sword.

Without hesitating, Lee Hyun immediately summoned a translucent Spirit Light Shield in front of his chest.

'Blocked...'

Boom!

Just before Xu Zhenming's sword struck the Spirit Light Shield, he unleashed a stomping step, and the floor of the training ground burst apart.

The shock made Lee Hyun lose his balance and lifted him slightly off the ground. In that instant, Xu Zhenming brought his wooden sword crashing down against the Spirit Light Shield. With the impact of the stomping step combined with the sword strike, Lee Hyun was thrown backward!

Xu Zhenming did not miss the opening and surged forward. Just as Lee Hyun's back was about to hit the ground, the wooden sword descended toward his chest.

Shhhk–

Still lying flat, Lee Hyun's body slid backward.

"...?"

Chapter 22

Xu Zhenming watched Lee Hyun slide farther away while lying comfortably on the ground.

He wasn't even moving his arms or legs, yet his body sped across the ground as though gliding over slick ice.

Xu Zhenming's competitive streak flared.

He immediately used his footwork and chased after Lee Hyun. With every step, his body shot forward two or three jang (about 6–9 m).

But just as he was about to close the distance, spiritual power burst from beneath Lee Hyun's back and heels.

Bang!

His prone body bounced along like a water strider kicking off the surface of a pond. Each bounce made him even faster.

Xu Zhenming's eyes widened.

‘He's accelerating?’

Gritting his teeth, he changed direction. Whenever Lee Hyun slid to the right, Xu Zhenming raced ahead to block his path. Whenever Lee Hyun moved left, he extended his sword to cut off his retreat.

But every time the ground rippled beneath him, Lee Hyun's body darted sideways. At times, he retreated feet-first only to instantly reverse direction and shoot away head-first. He moved with complete freedom.

After they had crossed the middle of the training ground several times, Xu Zhenming finally stopped.

When Xu Zhenming gave up the chase, Lee Hyun, who had retreated to the edge of the training ground, smoothly rotated his body.

Ssssh―

The feet that had been pointing toward Xu Zhenming turned sideways, and Lee Hyun looked over at him by turning only his head while remaining flat on the ground.

He seemed to be saying, ‘You can't catch me even when I'm lying down?’

"......."

Without realizing it, Xu Zhenming tightened his grip on his wooden sword.

‘I really want to hit him once.’

Guo Tianxiong also watched in silence for a moment before asking,

"Retainer Li."

"Yes."

"Was what you just used another kind of technique?"

"It's a technique I created."

"Why did you ever think of moving around while lying down?"

"Why should I have to get up?"

"......."

"I can also conceal myself in the undergrowth and move stealthily."

At first, Guo Tianxiong had thought it was merely bizarre, but after hearing the explanation, he had to admit there was some logic to it.

Losing one's balance and falling during actual combat was dangerous. But if someone could move that quickly while lying down, it was a different matter. That posture was no longer a weakness.

"It seems I've been trapped by my own preconceptions all this time. Still, no martial artist could imitate such absurd movement using internal energy."

Guo Tianxiong looked for a moment at Lee Hyun, who was still lying comfortably on the training ground, then continued.

"For now, lying down is forbidden as well. It's too unusual for Instructor Xu to teach you properly otherwise. In any case, Retainer Li still needs to learn how to fight while standing on two feet."

Lee Hyun's spar with Xu Zhenming resumed.

...

After about half a shichen (about one hour), Xu Zhenming's wooden sword could scarcely touch Lee Hyun.

Lee Hyun occasionally responded clumsily, but every time Xu Zhenming pointed out a problem, he quickly corrected it.

When the spar ended, Xu Zhenming lowered his sword and steadied his ragged breathing.

"You adapt remarkably quickly."

"It's because Instructor Xu points out what I'm doing wrong."

"Normally, even after someone has a mistake pointed out, they repeat it several more times..."

Guo Tianxiong spoke.

"After you rest for a moment, I'd like to see your swordsmanship."

"May I use a sword art practiced by cultivators?"

"Use only the swordsmanship, without spiritual power. Instructor Xu won't use internal energy either."

"Understood."

Xu Zhenming brought over two new wooden swords.

Lee Hyun completely suppressed his spiritual power and assumed the opening stance of the Azure Steel Sword Art.

Xu Zhenming also raised his wooden sword.

"The sword art I've learned is called the Seventy-Two Whirlpool Swords."

Xu Zhenming's wooden sword began tracing circles.

...

One ke (about fifteen minutes) later.

Clack! Clack-clack-clack!

Their wooden swords collided in rapid succession.

Xu Zhenming was growing unsettled.

Lee Hyun's swordsmanship contained almost no deception or feints, yet its precision and speed made it difficult to deal with. Above all, Lee Hyun was incredibly strong.

Lee Hyun was restraining his strength as much as possible, but,

Bang!

At one point, Xu Zhenming's arm was knocked upward.

"Ah."

Lee Hyun hurriedly pulled back his wooden sword.

"I'm sorry. Did I use too much strength?"

"...No."

Xu Zhenming took a step back, hiding his tingling wrist.

Guo Tianxiong spoke.

"This time, let me have a look."

He took the wooden sword from Xu Zhenming.

"My sword art is called the Sea-Calming Sword Art. It contains the opponent's variations and suppresses even their next move."

Guo Tianxiong did not circulate his internal energy. He merely held the wooden sword upright before his chest, yet Lee Hyun had no idea what he should do.

If he struck high, it felt as though his attack would be blocked. If he aimed low, it seemed the tip of Guo Tianxiong's sword would reach his throat first.

Even if he tried to circle around, it felt as though Guo Tianxiong would turn to face him one step ahead.

‘So this... is someone who has reached the pinnacle of the martial path.’

...

One ke (about fifteen minutes) later.

Guo Tianxiong withdrew his sword in surprise.

"You've clearly practiced the sword for a very long time."

"Does it look that way?"

"You make almost no unnecessary movements. However, your sword is far too honest."

"Too honest?"

"Between one move and the next, you make no attempt to draw out your opponent's reaction. It looks as though you've barely ever crossed swords with another person..."

"That's right."

"If I had to point out one flaw, it would be this: never forget that your opponent is also a living enemy who can read your intentions and alter their sword path according to the situation."

"A living enemy...."

"No matter how great a sword art may be, if you merely move according to predetermined patterns, it becomes a dead martial art. Spar regularly with Instructor Xu from now on and learn to read your opponent's reactions. You'll improve greatly."

"Sounds good."

"The sword art Retainer Li practices seems to have been created with a cultivator's body and spiritual power in mind. It lacks the intricate deception and variations found in the sword arts of martial artists, but if performed with spiritual power, its sheer force could overwhelm most variations."

"When I learned the sword art, I thought of it as another kind of technique as well."

"In truth, the swordsmanship itself isn't low-level either. Even if I were to create a sword art specifically for cultivators, I'm not confident I could make anything better than what Retainer Li uses."

...

After finishing their sparring, the three moved to a pavilion beside the training ground.

Lee Hyun took a sip of tea, then suddenly asked,

"May I ask the two of you one more thing?"

"Go ahead."

"Are there martial arts that can change one's appearance?"

Guo Tianxiong raised an eyebrow slightly.

"You wish to change your appearance?"

"There are times when I'd rather have a different face. It would help me avoid getting dragged into pointless trouble."

"Then what you're looking for is a disguise art."

Beside him, Xu Zhenming pointed at his own face.

"There are indeed martial arts that actually shift the bones and joints. But they're difficult to learn, and using them incorrectly can damage the meridians or bones."

"I don't need to go that far."

"The most commonly used disguise techniques combine makeup with control of the facial muscles."

Xu Zhenming tucked his chin in slightly.

His breathing changed, and the muscles of his face and neck shifted subtly.

The scar running from his temple to his jaw remained unchanged.

Even so, once his eyelids drooped slightly and the corners of his mouth sagged, the rugged-looking man seemed to transform in an instant into a gloomy, exhausted middle-aged man.

His shoulders hunched inward as well, and his voice became slightly hoarse.

"Like this."

"Huh? You barely did anything, but you look like a completely different person."

"People are surprisingly poor at distinguishing faces. Even without making any major changes, a few tricks combined with props such as a beard can fool even people close to you to some extent."

"Can I learn that technique?"

"There is a Seven-Aspect Disguise Method taught to military scouts and spies. It isn't some great secret art, so there should be no problem showing it to a Retainer. What I just demonstrated was only the basics. If you reach Major Attainment in the Seven-Aspect Disguise Method, you should be able to fool most people."

Lee Hyun's eyes brightened.

"Could I also study martial arts secret manuals or internal energy methods?"

This time, Guo Tianxiong answered.

"An individual's secret martial arts are as precious as their life. Showing you part of the sword path from my Sea-Calming Sword Art or Instructor Xu's Seventy-Two Whirlpool Swords is entirely different from transmitting the underlying inner method as well."

"Ah, of course I don't mean that I covet either of your martial arts. I'm fine with martial arts that anyone is permitted to study."

"A Retainer may also consult the standardized martial arts used by the military and the Martial Training Academy. There is an internal energy method called the Cloud Water Origin-Returning Art. It is the internal energy method most widely practiced by military officers and elite soldiers of the Yunze Kingdom."

Xu Zhenming added,

"There is also a standardized martial art called the Eighteen Formation-Breaking Forms. It lays out basic footwork and methods of exerting force so that soldiers wielding swords, spears, and sabers can all use it."

"I'd like to see that as well."

"We'll gather some of the martial arts books that the Fengtian Bureau's Military Retainers generally hold in high regard and send them to Qingliang Villa. We'll include books on disguise as well."

"Thank you."

Guo Tianxiong set down his teacup.

"But they probably won't help you much. The internal energy used by martial artists is completely different from the spiritual power of cultivators... And the greatest problem is time."

"Time?"

"Although mortals in the mundane world have short lifespans, the depth of the martial path is by no means shallow. It is the culmination of the insights and research of countless geniuses across generations. In some respects, there are martial arts even more difficult than the techniques of Immortals. After all, martial artists must produce astonishing results with limited power."

"I see."

"And that's where the problem arises. Cultivators may live long lives, but the lifespans of Qi Refining Retainers aren't all that long. In fact, they're not much different from mine now that I've reached the Profound Realm. From their perspective, then, do they truly have the leisure to learn martial arts of the mundane world? Spending that time learning techniques and advancing their realm is far more practical."

"True. Cultivators are the ones who are actually short on time. Besides, aren't the grandmasters of the martial path people of tremendous talent who simply lack spiritual roots?"

"Exactly! How many people can possibly possess talent in both the immortal path and the martial path? Martial arts take time to learn, yet they aren't as well suited to a cultivator's spiritual power as techniques are. Naturally, cultivators eventually lose interest."

Xu Zhenming also spoke.

"I recommend you don't spend too much time on them. It would be best to use them only as light reference material, focusing on the forms of the moves, footwork, breathing, and the principles of transmitting force. Just learn enough to deal with martial artists from the Qianyang Kingdom."

"Understood."

...

That evening.

A wooden chest arrived at Qingliang Villa.

Inside were military martial arts books, including 《Cloud Water Origin-Returning Art》, 《Eighteen Formation-Breaking Forms》, 《Twelve Autumn Water Swords》, 《River-Suppressing Sword Art》, 《Twelve Linked-Shadow Forms》, and 《Long Dike Spear Art》.

There were also several books on footwork, including 《Duckweed Water-Crossing Step》, 《Coiled-Root Step》, and 《Inch-Shadow Step》.

The remaining books included 《Seven-Aspect Disguise Method》, which dealt with disguise, 《Eight Methods of Disguise》, which explained how to use disguise tools and dyes, and a draft of 《Bone-Changing Sinew-Shrinking Art》, which involved shifting the bones and joints.

Lee Hyun opened the Seven-Aspect Disguise Method first.

The first page listed the seven elements that made up a person's overall impression.

「Eyes, mouth, voice, gait, posture, breathing, habits.」

"This will take a lot of practice."

After briefly skimming the Seven-Aspect Disguise Method, Lee Hyun opened the Cloud Water Origin-Returning Art and read it for about one ke (about fifteen minutes).

"The method is completely different..."

...

From then on, Lee Hyun visited the Martial Training Academy every few days and read martial arts books whenever he returned to Qingliang Villa.

Lee Hyun thought becoming a Retainer of the Fengtian Bureau hadn't been a bad decision.

He could use the Martial Training Academy's facilities for free and even receive instruction from masters of the martial path. Qingliang Villa provided him with food and lodging as well.

In the process, he also discovered that he was fairly strong.

In front of Guo Tianxiong and Xu Zhenming, he restrained his spiritual power as much as possible. Even when demonstrating the Yang Metal Art, Fireball Art, and Azure Steel Sword Art, he tried to limit himself to what he imagined was the level of an ordinary Qi Refining Stage 3 cultivator.

Even so, the two men judged Lee Hyun's offensive techniques too dangerous and forbade him from using them in sparring.

‘It seems I've been underestimating myself too much. At the very least, there's no need to avoid missions out of fear of ordinary martial artists from the Qianyang Kingdom.’

As Lee Hyun continued attending the Martial Training Academy, he developed a sense of how strong masters of the Transformation Realm and Profound Realm actually were.

He thought that if he fought seriously, merely unleashing the Qi Sphere Barrier forcefully in every direction would send a martial artist on Xu Zhenming's level flying and break bones throughout his body.

Even if he were surrounded by several masters of the Profound Realm, as long as he had enough time to properly deploy the Spirit Light Shield and Qi Sphere Barrier, he didn't think he would be defeated instantly.

Simply escaping underground with the Earth Escape Art would likely make it difficult for his opponents to find him, and with the Yang Metal Art at Major Attainment, he believed he could inflict fatal wounds even on masters who protected themselves with Protective Aura.

Thinking about it, that was only natural.

Lee Hyun could continuously unleash by himself the techniques that dozens of Qi Refining cultivators would otherwise have to pour out one after another. By the standards of the Yunze Kingdom and Qianyang Kingdom, that alone made him something close to a monster.

‘Once I've trained a little more at the Martial Training Academy, I should be able to take Military Retainer missions.’

...

Before he knew it, a little over twenty days had passed since he arrived in Yunjing.

Lee Hyun left Qingliang Villa to inspect Tunnel No. 1.

After telling Cui Da that he would be away for a few days, he left Yunjing and alternated between the Earth Escape Art and Distance-Shrinking Step.

Since he had built an automatic irrigation device, in theory his spirit plants should remain fine even if he stayed away for nearly a year. But he had never left the tunnel unattended for so long before, and the thought made him uneasy enough to return and check on it.

...

A rugged mountain valley roughly halfway between Yunjing and Tunnel No. 1.

Ssshhhk―

Lee Hyun's body slid swiftly across the mountainside.

Skimming over the ground as though flying with the Reclining Escape Art, he kicked hard against the trunk of a tree blocking his path.

Bang!

His prone body shot into the air.

Lee Hyun rotated half a turn in midair and planted his feet against a boulder on the opposite side.

Thud.

His body shot across the valley.

Lee Hyun was becoming increasingly familiar with the terrain along the route between Yunjing and Tunnel No. 1.

He had learned where to cross the mountain ranges to find gentler slopes, which rivers to follow to avoid villages and highways, and how much spiritual power to use in sparsely populated stretches for maximum efficiency.

Thanks to the 206 spiritual power shown on his handmade status screen, he could keep moving all day without rest.

Lee Hyun's current average travel speed was close to eighty kilometers per hour by the standards of his previous life. That meant he could cover nearly five thousand li (about 2,000 km) in a day.

The distance from Yunjing, capital of the Yunze Kingdom, to Tunnel No. 1 was about eight thousand li, but a one-way trip now took less than two days.

...

Two days later.

Lee Hyun dropped from the ceiling of the cultivation chamber in Tunnel No. 1.

Thump.

The automatic irrigation devices were the first things he checked, and all of them were operating normally.

"Good."

Starting with Spirit Field No. 1-1, Lee Hyun recorded their conditions one by one and found no problems.

Finally, he entered Spirit Field No. 1-7, where the Stone Honey Peaches grew.

A sweet, refreshing fragrance filled the cavern.

More than ten honey-sweet fruits hung from the branches of the three mature Stone Honey Peach trees.

Most were fully ripe.

Lee Hyun reached for the nearest fruit, then stopped.

There was a tiny hole near its stem, with something resembling brown powder clinging around it.

"Hm?"

Lee Hyun brought the fruit close to his face and examined it.

He could sense faint spiritual qi from inside the hole.

When he used the Aura-Reading Art, a thin thread of light writhed inside the fruit.

Lee Hyun's expression stiffened.

"Don't tell me...."

He carefully sliced open the fruit with the Yang Metal Art.

A thin, winding tunnel ran through the flesh.

A white larva about one finger joint in length wriggled among the browned flesh.

Its head was black and hard, and short hairs sprouted from each segment of its abdomen.

"Ugh!"

Silver light flashed from Lee Hyun's fingertip.

Shnk!

The Yang Metal Art pierced straight through the larva.

It writhed a few times inside the fruit before going limp.

"You ate my spirit fruit...."

This was the first time Lee Hyun had found such an insect in a Stone Honey Peach.

He inspected the remaining fruits one by one.

Two had similar holes, and a white egg smaller than a sesame seed clung to the surface of another.

When he checked the undersides of the leaves, he found a little gray powder.

‘If there's a larva, there must be an adult that laid the eggs.’

Lee Hyun meticulously scanned the surroundings with the Aura-Reading Art and spotted a tiny light where the tree trunk met the cavern wall.

A gray moth the size of a fingernail clung there with its wings folded.

It looked like an ordinary moth, but an extremely faint trace of spiritual qi flowed through its body.

Lee Hyun disposed of the moth with the Yang Metal Art.

"How did it get in here?"

Tunnel No. 1 lay ten li underground.

However, many kinds of spirit insects had always lived in the soil and bedrock around the spirit fields.

After the reservoir and waterways were created, small insects that had never appeared before began showing up as well.

They might have entered through the air shafts or waterways, or perhaps larvae or pupae had already been hiding in the soil around the roots of the Stone Honey Peach trees.

There had probably been no problems until now because Lee Hyun had always picked the fruits as soon as they ripened and either eaten them or stored them in his storage pouch.

"From now on, whenever I'm away, I'll make thin paper bags and cover the fruits with them. I shouldn't tie them too tightly around the stems, and I'll leave a small opening at the bottom...."

It wasn't as though he had hundreds of fruit trees to manage, so covering each fruit individually with paper shouldn't be difficult.

...

The incident with the Stone Honey Peaches prompted Lee Hyun to inspect the other spirit fields more carefully than usual.

Near the roots of the Earth Vein Flowers, he found the translucent eggs he had occasionally seen there for a long time.

Under the leaves of the Yin Water Lotuses, a small six-legged spirit insect was clinging to one of the pads.

In the test spirit field, a black beetle crawled about, surviving despite the faint toxic qi.

"Ugh..."

Lee Hyun tossed the spirit insects into jars whenever he found them.

He had collected spirit insects before, but because he disliked bugs, he had never studied them properly.

He also scraped up the eggs he found around the Earth Vein Flowers along with the surrounding soil and put them into jars.

Before long, the storeroom was lined with jars sorted according to criteria even Lee Hyun could no longer make sense of.

"What if these bastards chew their way out...?"

Lee Hyun moved the ordinary jars to the training cavern, which was formed from crystalline bedrock.

He softened some granite near the training cavern with the Soil-Softening Art, broke it loose, and shaped it into a thick, crude breeding case.

After transferring the contents of all the jars into the breeding case, he covered it with a granite lid and used the Yang Metal Art to bore several tiny holes so that it wasn't completely sealed.

It wasn't a good environment for spirit insects, but Lee Hyun didn't care if the creatures died. He still wasn't interested enough in them to raise spirit insects with any real care.

...

The next day, Lee Hyun obtained thin mulberry paper and fine hemp cord in Qingliu County Seat, then bought several pieces of tightly woven silk mesh from a fabric shop. He also acquired small rings and clips made from thin strips of bamboo.

After returning to Tunnel No. 1, he harvested all the ripe Stone Honey Peaches and covered each unripe fruit with a paper bag.

He secured the top of each bag with a bamboo ring without tightening it completely and left enough of a gap at the bottom for air to pass through.

He installed silk mesh over the entrances and air shafts of Spirit Field No. 1-6 and Spirit Field No. 1-7.

...

Two days later.

Lee Hyun returned to Yunjing and headed for the Fengtian Bureau's Alchemy Hall.

He intended to find out how valuable the spirit plants he grew were and, if the Fengtian Bureau would buy them, exchange them for spirit stones.

For that purpose, he had brought several kinds of young spirit plants from the test spirit field, along with wilted ones whose medicinal potency had become unstable.

...

Around the Alchemy Hall were a broad courtyard for drying medicinal ingredients and several storerooms.

Apothecary apprentices carried baskets back and forth, while the sound of medicinal ingredients being pounded rang constantly from within the hall.

Lee Hyun asked the Alchemy Hall clerk whether anyone there recognized several of the spirit plants, including the Bone-Rot Flower and Yin Soul Grass.

The clerk tilted his head as he wrote down the names of the spirit plants.

"I don't recognize a single one of these medicinal ingredients."

"Could you ask one of the alchemist Retainers?"

"Please wait a moment."

The clerk went inside.

A long while later, an elderly man appeared wearing a long robe permeated with the scent of medicinal ingredients.

His hair and beard were white as snow, but his back was straight, and the hands protruding from his sleeves were rough, as though they had been burned many times.

The clerk introduced him respectfully.

"This is my lord Wen Shenghe, chief alchemist of the Alchemy Hall."

Wen Shenghe cupped his hands toward Lee Hyun.

"Some call me the Medicine King. It's a sobriquet I hardly deserve."

"I'm External Retainer Li Dongyi."

"Let's go inside and talk."

...

Lee Hyun showed Wen Shenghe the samples he had brought and told him their names.

A short while later.

"To be frank, it would be difficult for the Fengtian Bureau to appraise or purchase these spirit plants."

"Are they all useless?"

"That's not it."

Wen Shenghe shook his head.

"To put a price on a spirit herb, one needs to know many things: how much of it is used in which pill recipes, what can substitute for it, and how difficult its detoxification and storage are."

"I see."

"The Fengtian Bureau doesn't possess a single pill recipe that uses these spirit plants. More precisely, the Bureau doesn't have many pill recipes at all."

"It's impressive that you can practice alchemy under such conditions."

"My finest creation is the Barrier-Breaking Pill. I'm ashamed to say I have little else worth boasting about."

...

Lee Hyun left the Alchemy Hall.

‘So I can't sell my spirit plants through the Fengtian Bureau. Their medicinal potency has accumulated for so long that they should be quite valuable... If I find a large cultivator market or an auction where cultivators gather, I should consider putting a small amount up for sale.’

Three months later.

Lee Hyun occasionally traveled back and forth to Tunnel No. 1, but spent most of his time researching martial arts or sparring at the Martial Training Academy.

Guo Tianxiong and Xu Zhenming judged that he had learned enough of the basics to handle himself in actual combat.

There was still much for him to learn and research about martial arts, but he decided it was time to start earning merit points. Only then could he learn alchemy and obtain the pill recipe for the Barrier-Breaking Pill.

...

Fengtian Bureau, Military Service Hall.

A map of southern Yunze Kingdom hung on one wall.

Red flags densely covered the areas bordering the Qianyang Kingdom. Around Lushui Pass in particular, there were so many that the surface of the map could barely be seen.

"You intend to serve as a Military Retainer?"

"Yes."

Chapter 23

“You’ve only been registered for four months, yet you’re already planning to head south. Were there really that few External Retainer missions?”

“There were none.”

“...Truth be told, that is indeed the case.”

Across the desk sat a Standing Retainer responsible for administrative affairs at the Military Service Hall.

“If you convert to Military Retainer status, you must serve for at least six months at a post designated by the Military Service Hall. In return, you accrue one day of leave every seven days, and you may save those days up and use them together every few months. You can also earn a great many merit points by killing or capturing martial artists from the Qianyang Kingdom.”

...

Two days later, a new retainer badge hung from Lee Hyun’s waist.

The blue jade badge engraved with a crane soaring above the clouds had been returned to the Fengtian Bureau. In its place, he had received a black jade badge threaded with a red cord. The front was engraved with a crane holding a spear upright, while the back bore the words, ‘Military Retainer Li Dongyi’.

Six months later.

Southern Yunze Kingdom, Hui’an Fort.

Lushui Pass lay five thousand li (about 2,000 km) south of Yunjing, and Hui’an Fort had been built another thousand-odd li to its west.

It was far smaller than Lushui Pass, but it stood where the western waterways and the embankment roads leading into Yunze Kingdom’s interior diverged.

People often said that Lushui Pass was the most important stronghold, but in truth, there was no such thing as an unimportant stronghold.

If even one small post like this were breached, Qianyang Kingdom’s martial artists could circle around through the rivers and reed marshes and infiltrate the rear of Lushui Pass. If that happened, not only Lushui Pass but even the grain barges carrying military provisions would be threatened.

Fortunately, no large army had advanced on Hui’an Fort during the past six months.

There had only been a handful of incidents in which Qianyang scouts crossed the reed marshes or took advantage of the darkness to raid watchposts along the embankments.

...

A vast reed marsh stretched out beneath the high watchtower.

Whenever it rained, the waterways changed shape, and on days when the fog was thick, it was difficult to see even a few dozen jang (roughly 60 to 90 m) ahead.

During his stay at Hui’an Fort, Lee Hyun spent most of his time in Azure Crane Pavilion, a small residence within the fortress.

Azure Crane Pavilion was not as luxurious as Qingliang Villa, but it was far better furnished than an ordinary officer’s quarters.

The detached residence, enclosed by an inner wall of Hui’an Fort, contained not only a bedroom and study but also a small bathing room.

Two young maidservants named Xiaoyun and Meixiang had also been assigned to him. Thanks to them, Lee Hyun no longer had to prepare his own meals or deal with minor chores, leaving him plenty of time to study martial arts and techniques.

...

Military Retainers accumulated one day of leave every seven days. Lee Hyun saved his leave, then left his post for roughly seven days every couple of months to visit Tunnel No. 1.

Each time, he inspected the spirit field and automatic irrigation device, repaired the paper bags and silk nets around the Stone Honey Peach fruits, then refilled the water tank with the Spirit Rain Art.

Hui’an Fort was an astonishing eleven thousand li from Tunnel No. 1 one way, but with Lee Hyun’s abilities, making the trip during his leave presented no particular difficulty.

Whenever he returned to Hui’an Fort, he watched the soldiers train or read martial arts manuals.

He had acquired quite a few martial arts manuals during his service as well.

Whenever Qianyang scouts were captured, searching their bodies was standard procedure. Ordinary soldiers rarely carried anything useful, but experts at the Peak realm or above occasionally possessed thin booklets containing mnemonic formulas for martial arts or personal insights from their training.

Since Lee Hyun was a Military Retainer treated as Hui’an Fort’s strongest combatant, there was no problem with him examining such books first or making copies for himself.

The person who assisted him most closely was Hui’an Fort’s vice commander, Zhuo Wucheng.

Zhuo Wucheng was an expert in the Transformation Realm, a little over fifty years old.

He had served in the Southern Army since his teens and knew the waterways, reed marshes, and embankment roads around Hui’an Fort like the back of his hand.

He was always courteous toward Lee Hyun.

“Retainer, my lord, the water level at the western sluice has risen today. If you intend to go out at night, I recommend using the northern embankment road.”

“Understood.”

“If there is anything you need, please let me know.”

Vice Commander Zhuo clasped his hands in salute before withdrawing.

His courtesy contained a mixture of respect and fear.

That was because on the day Lee Hyun first arrived at Hui’an Fort, he had conjured a fireball over his palm and demonstrated how the Yang Metal Art could pierce an iron plate.

Still, Zhuo Wucheng harbored one question in his heart.

‘Can he really use those techniques properly in actual combat?’

He had fought alongside other Military Retainers of the Fengtian Bureau before.

The cultivators’ techniques were strange and powerful.

But Qianyang Kingdom’s martial artists were not going to politely wait dozens of jang away for them.

They threw hidden weapons, scattered poisonous powder, and targeted the fingers forming hand seals and the eyes first.

By the time a startled cultivator was still deciding which technique to use, an expert in the Transformation Realm was already upon him.

Retainer Li Dongyi’s techniques were undoubtedly stronger than those of his predecessor. However, Zhuo Wucheng had no idea whether someone so young possessed sufficient real combat experience as well. More than a few Military Retainers had been injured or killed in battle.

‘If I ambushed this Retainer from within ten jang (about 30 m), I might have a chance myself.’

Zhuo Wucheng was confident in his martial learning. What expert who had reached the Transformation Realm would not believe in his own martial path?

But Retainer Li Dongyi was not a bad person.

He was modest, did not order the soldiers around without reason, and never complained about his food or accommodations.

That was why Zhuo Wucheng hoped Retainer Li Dongyi would not die a pointless death on the battlefield.

...

One dawn.

A denser fog than usual had settled around Hui’an Fort.

Even from the high watchtower, the reed marshes below the embankment could not be seen.

Damp wind swept across the fortress walls.

Lee Hyun lay on the bed in his quarters, reading a martial arts manual.

His finger stopped as he turned a page.

Creeeak―

A faint metallic scraping sound came from very far away.

It was so quiet that an ordinary person would never have heard it, and even if they had, they would probably have mistaken it for the sound of a door hinge. But to Lee Hyun, who had activated the Keen Hearing Art, it sounded like a taut steel string catching on a latch.

Creak. Creeeak―

‘A crossbow?’

Lee Hyun closed the martial arts manual.

At that moment, a shout erupted from a distant watchpost outside his residence.

“Attack!”

Boom!

The lattice windows of the pavilion burst apart all at once.

Dozens of black crossbow bolts poured into the room.

Their tips were coated in a dark bluish-black liquid.

Hummm―

A translucent Spirit Light Shield appeared.

Clang-clang-clang!

Several of the crossbow bolts in the barrage carried an unusual force.

‘Aura?’

Crossbow bolts infused with aura slammed repeatedly into the center of the Spirit Light Shield.

A second and third bolt struck precisely where the first had landed.

The moment the fourth bolt hit, a small crack appeared on the Spirit Light Shield’s surface.

‘They’re using aura-infused crossbows from a distance to apply the principle of One Point Pierces the Surface? Their accuracy is impressive...’

Lee Hyun stopped holding back his spiritual power as he usually did and swept his hand out in earnest.

The first Spirit Light Shield instantly blazed with dazzling light, becoming more than ten times sturdier, and the crack vanished without a trace.

At the same time, Spirit Light Shields of similar strength appeared all around him.

Boom! Boom! Boom!

The crossbow bolts continued hammering the same points.

Soon, dark figures surged through the shattered windows.

The first to leap into the room was a middle-aged martial artist wielding twin swords.

Behind him came an expert with a spear and two more men wielding swords.

Powerful pressure poured from all four men.

‘Four experts in the Transformation Realm? So they must have been the ones firing those aura-infused bolts.’

The moment they saw Lee Hyun, they scattered in all directions.

“Kill the Immortal!”

The twin-sword wielder kicked off the floor.

Booom!

Sword aura smashed into the left edge of a Spirit Light Shield.

At the same instant, a spearpoint drove into another Spirit Light Shield from the opposite side.

Clang!

Yet neither Spirit Light Shield broke.

The instant bewilderment appeared in the two attackers’ eyes, light erupted from Lee Hyun’s body.

A dazzling curtain spread outward from him at tremendous speed.

Booom!

The two martial artists wielding the twin swords and spear were hurled outside, smashing through the pavilion wall.

Just then.

Thud-thud-thud-thud!

The instant another volley of arrows from outside struck the Spirit Light Shields, black powder burst outward, and poisonous qi rapidly filled the room.

“Poison!”

Vice Commander Zhuo’s voice rang out from afar.

Lee Hyun activated the Breath-Sealing Art and Qi Sphere Barrier, then stepped outside through the collapsed wall.

Several corpses already lay scattered across Hui’an Fort’s inner courtyard, shrouded in fog.

Shouts and the clash of weapons could be heard from the distant barracks.

It seemed the four men before him were not the only intruders.

Then a low voice came from within the fog.

“What are you fools doing, unable to handle a single Qi Refining cultivator?”

Step.

The dense fog parted to either side.

An old man wearing a crimson robe walked out from between it.

In his right hand was a long, narrow sword. The blade had a reddish sheen, and blood trickled down its surface.

The pressure emanating from him was on an entirely different level from the Transformation Realm experts who had come before.

Vice Commander Zhuo’s face turned pale.

“Red Cloud Sword Zhao Bingyue...!”

Zhao Bingyue.

He was an expert in the Profound Realm belonging to the Qianyang Western Army.

More than ten years ago, he was said to have cut down three Transformation Realm experts from Yunze Kingdom at once, and during the battle for Baishui City, he had supposedly slaughtered a thousand soldiers by himself. He was an infamous powerhouse.

Zhao Bingyue looked at Lee Hyun.

“You’re as young as I heard.”

“You know me?”

“I heard rumors that the Fengtian Bureau had gained a young Military Retainer.”

‘Looks like information is leaking out.’

Zhao Bingyue’s gaze swept over Lee Hyun.

“Cultivators are too unpredictable. It’s safer to kill them first.”

He raised his sword.

At that moment, the four scattered Transformation Realm experts moved simultaneously.

Two spread out to either side, one retreated and raised a crossbow, while the remaining man pulled three black pouches from inside his robes.

Zhao Bingyue stepped forward from the front.

Thump!

With a single step, he covered more than twenty jang (about 60 m).

Red sword aura flashed toward Lee Hyun’s throat, while the Transformation Realm experts on either side simultaneously stabbed at him with a sword and spear cloaked in aura.

From behind came an aura-infused crossbow bolt, while the black pouches burst in midair and spewed red and blue poisonous smoke.

Every attack converged on Lee Hyun at exactly the same instant, with flawless timing.

Vice Commander Zhuo, watching from afar, froze with his sword drawn. If he had been caught in such a situation, he would have died instantly.

Just then.

Hummm! Hum! Hum!

Twelve Spirit Light Shields blossomed around Lee Hyun all at once.

The translucent shields overlapped to form a sphere with no openings at all, covering not only his front, back, left, and right, but even above his head and beneath his feet.

Booom-boom-boom!

Sword aura, spear aura, and crossbow bolts all slammed into the Spirit Light Shields, yet not a single one broke through.

Zhao Bingyue was horrified.

‘What!?’

He had seen many Qi Refining cultivators before. Yet even among cultivators at late Qi Refining, he had never seen anyone deploy such a powerful defensive technique in every direction without leaving a single opening.

Just then.

Booom!

Several Spirit Light Shields shot outward as though exploding.

The enormous translucent discs spun as they swept in every direction. The Transformation Realm experts stabbing with sword and spear from either side were struck in the chest before they could recover their stance, and flew backward vomiting blood as bones cracked inside them.

The man holding the crossbow twisted aside to dodge, but when a Spirit Light Shield grazed his thigh, his leg buckled and he rolled across the ground.

Another Spirit Light Shield flew straight toward Zhao Bingyue.

“Hmph!”

Zhao Bingyue gripped his sword in both hands and slashed diagonally downward with red sword aura.

Claaang!

Zhao Bingyue tried to split the Spirit Light Shield head-on, but his sword aura could not force the shield back at all. Instead, the Spirit Light Shield drove against his sword and forced his arms and shoulders backward.

‘Dammit!’

Zhao Bingyue immediately angled his sword sideways to redirect the shield’s force.

The Spirit Light Shield’s trajectory finally shifted, and he threw himself aside with so little room to spare that his hair brushed its surface.

Booom!

The missed Spirit Light Shield struck the base of the watchtower behind him head-on. A wooden pillar more than two armspans around shattered to pieces, causing one side of the watchtower to tilt.

Zhao Bingyue rolled across the ground several times before rising onto one knee. Blood streamed from both hands gripping his sword.

“You bastard...!”

He tried to find Lee Hyun again, only to discover that Lee Hyun had already vanished from before his eyes.

‘Above!?’

Zhao Bingyue raised his head and saw an unreal sight.

Against the dark blue light of dawn, the young cultivator’s finger traced a gentle semicircle. Dozens of streaks of silver light spread from his fingertips like an opening fan.

The silver needles targeted the wrists, ankles, shoulders, knees, and other joints and vital points of the Transformation Realm experts scattered nearby.

Pfft! P-p-pfft!

Blood sprayed from their limbs.

One man gritted his teeth, activated his Protective Aura, and twisted his body. Yet the Protective Aura failed to stop the silver needles and shattered. As he twisted, a needle originally aimed at his shoulder instead pierced straight through the space between his eyebrows.

“Urk....”

The martial artist fell backward with disbelief on his face.

The remaining three did not die, but their limbs had been pierced through, and they rolled on the ground unable to rise again.

“How dare you!”

Zhao Bingyue surged into the air toward Lee Hyun. Even denser sword aura than before had gathered at the tip of his sword.

The sword aura surged upward from below with the force of a crimson waterfall flowing in reverse, swallowing Lee Hyun’s body.

Lee Hyun extended one hand and layered three Spirit Light Shields diagonally over one another.

Skreeeeech―

Sparks flew from the surface of the first Spirit Light Shield. The sword aura failed to pierce the shield, but Zhao Bingyue fixed his sword tip on a single point and poured all his internal energy into it.

When even the second shield bent deeply, Lee Hyun compressed the power of the Qi Sphere Barrier into a single point behind the Spirit Light Shields.

The instant Zhao Bingyue drove his sword farther forward.

Booooom!

The compressed Qi Sphere Barrier exploded. Riding the recoil, Lee Hyun’s body shot more than ten jang (about 30 m) higher into the air, while Zhao Bingyue plunged toward the ground as though struck by an enormous iron mace.

Crack!

Both of Zhao Bingyue’s legs sank into the ground up to his knees. Unable to withstand the impact, his body folded forward and dark red blood burst from his mouth.

“Guhak!”

Zhao Bingyue gritted his teeth and forcibly dragged his legs out of the ground. His shoes and trouser cuffs tore, and blood ran down both legs, but he ignored it and raised his sword once more.

Zhao Bingyue’s sword aura began gathering at the tip of his blade.

Hummmmm―

The aura compressed without pause until it formed a fist-sized sphere, its surface spinning madly.

Vice Commander Zhuo drew in a sharp breath.

“A sword ring...!”

Zhao Bingyue thrust his sword forward.

Whoooosh!

The crimson sword ring tore through the air toward Lee Hyun. The rotating sword aura even sucked the surrounding fog and air into the red sphere.

Lee Hyun hurled a dazzling fireball, then layered a Qi Sphere Barrier and Spirit Light Shield in front of himself.

Fwoosh!

Lee Hyun’s fireball collided head-on with the sword ring.

The crimson sword ring spun madly as it bored into the center of the fireball, its sword aura shredding the flames apart.

Yet the fire split into dozens of streams that curved like snakes and wrapped around the surface of the sword ring. The faster the sword ring rotated, the faster the flames were drawn inward.

Zhao Bingyue’s face stiffened.

The moment the flames penetrated all the way to the sword ring’s core, Lee Hyun clenched his five fingers.

Flash!

The darkness of dawn was bleached pure white.

Booooooom!

The fireball erupted from within.

The compressed sword ring could not withstand the explosion and shattered into hundreds of pieces. Fragments of crimson sword aura and flame rained down in every direction.

Crack-crack-crack-crack!

Countless sword marks were carved into the ground and walls.

Disbelief filled Zhao Bingyue’s eyes.

“My sword ring... broken that easily....”

Flames and dust kicked up by the explosion obscured his vision.

At that moment, Zhao Bingyue felt something he had long since forgotten. It was the fear of death.

Swish!

Lee Hyun suddenly appeared and brushed past Zhao Bingyue’s side.

Zhao Bingyue reflexively turned his sword, but Lee Hyun was already behind him.

Lee Hyun’s palm slammed into Zhao Bingyue’s right shoulder.

Thud! Crunch!

The shoulder bone broke, twisting his arm.

Zhao Bingyue gritted his teeth and switched his sword to his left hand, but Lee Hyun chopped down on his left elbow with the edge of his hand.

Crack!

“Aaaargh!”

Zhao Bingyue’s left elbow shattered, and his sword dropped to the ground.

Even with both arms ruined, Zhao Bingyue lifted a leg and kicked at Lee Hyun’s side. The aura condensed around his toes was as sharp as a spearhead.

A Spirit Light Shield appeared at Lee Hyun’s flank.

Thump!

The instant Zhao Bingyue’s foot struck the shield, Lee Hyun pressed the Spirit Light Shield downward.

Crunch!

Zhao Bingyue’s knee buckled.

His body tilted to one side.

Lee Hyun kicked his remaining leg.

Crack!

“Urgh!”

Zhao Bingyue collapsed to the ground.

Then the energy flowing through Zhao Bingyue’s entire body suddenly reversed.

Through the Aura-Reading Art, Lee Hyun saw the energy scattered throughout Zhao Bingyue’s meridians rush backward toward his heart and dantian.

‘Is he trying to kill himself?’

Just as Zhao Bingyue’s chest and abdomen began to swell, Lee Hyun’s hand flashed.

Pfft! Pfft!

Two silver needles from the Yang Metal Art pierced the Chest Center Acupoint at the center of his chest and the Sea of Qi Acupoint beneath his navel with perfect accuracy.

As Primordial True Qi cut through the reversed flow of internal energy, the energy lost its direction and dispersed.

“Stay still.”

“What... did you do....”

Lee Hyun’s fingers rapidly pressed Zhao Bingyue’s neck, shoulders, chest, and sides.

It was an acupoint-striking method he had learned over the past several months by comparing martial arts manuals from Yunze Kingdom and Qianyang Kingdom.

Lee Hyun pushed strands of Primordial True Qi as fine as thread into his body and gathered them around the acupoints like tiny knots.

Strength instantly drained from Zhao Bingyue’s body.

‘A cultivator... using acupoint striking?’

...

Once Lee Hyun subdued Zhao Bingyue and the Transformation Realm experts, the Qianyang Kingdom martial artists who had infiltrated deeper into the fortress also lost their route of escape. Vice Commander Zhuo and Hui’an Fort’s martial artists counterattacked, and most of the surviving intruders were captured.

By the time the fog lifted, prisoners lay in rows across the inner courtyard.

Xiaoyun and Meixiang had hidden in the rear wing of Azure Crane Pavilion and were rescued unharmed. Despite their pale faces, the two brought cloth and water to help tend the wounded soldiers.

Lee Hyun looked briefly at the corpse of a Transformation Realm expert lying before the ruined pavilion, then turned away. It was the first time he had killed someone with his own hands.

Had he hesitated, the maidservants of Azure Crane Pavilion, Vice Commander Zhuo, and many more soldiers would have died. Even as he repeated that to himself, the sight of corpses scattered everywhere made his stomach churn.

After finishing the prisoners’ restraints, Vice Commander Zhuo approached Lee Hyun carrying a bloodstained bundle of oiled cloth in both hands.

“Retainer, my lord.”

“What is that?”

“These are the possessions we found on the Transformation Realm experts. Since they were all subdued by you, my lord, it is only right that the spoils be offered to you first.”

The bundle contained martial arts secret manuals, records of personal insights, notes on mixing poisonous powders, and instructions for infusing crossbow bolts with aura. To an ordinary martial artist, every one of them was something worth risking one’s life to obtain.

Lee Hyun quickly flipped through the pages and grasped their contents, but nothing caught his interest. He tied the bundle closed again and handed it back to Vice Commander Zhuo.

“Vice Commander Zhuo, keep them or handle them as you see fit.”

“Pardon?”

“You can distribute them to whoever needs them.”

“Are you truly allowing me to handle them?”

“Yes. I’ll examine this man’s belongings.”

Lee Hyun began searching Zhao Bingyue’s robes.

Martial artists did not use storage pouches, but they often carried useful possessions on their person.

In particular, quite a few kept family martial arts, secret martial arts, and the personal insights they had accumulated throughout their lives with them rather than entrusting such things to others.

Several thin, oil-treated leather pouches had been sewn into the lining of Zhao Bingyue’s crimson robe.

The first things Lee Hyun found were thin booklets such as the Red Cloud Sword Scripture, Essentials of Sword Ring Condensation and Refinement, and Red Cloud Step. They covered swordsmanship, the training method for the sword ring, and footwork.

There were also books on a coordinated attack art for breaking cultivators’ defensive techniques, texts on the body’s acupoints, and records detailing the failures and realizations Zhao Bingyue had experienced during his training.

Among them, the one that caught Lee Hyun’s eye was the Record of Opponents, which documented the martial arts and weaknesses of powerful opponents Zhao Bingyue had fought over more than forty years.

The Record of Opponents also described his experiences fighting three cultivators at early Qi Refining. It went into considerable detail, covering methods for interrupting hand seals, records of tests conducted on the weaknesses of defensive techniques, and tricks for reading a cultivator’s habits when activating techniques.

‘This could be quite useful.’

The enemies Lee Hyun truly feared were not martial artists of the mundane world but other cultivators, so the Record of Opponents had real value to him.

Meanwhile, Vice Commander Zhuo stared down at Zhao Bingyue lying on the ground.

To most martial artists in Yunze Kingdom, the name Red Cloud Sword Zhao Bingyue was synonymous with despair.

Yet this expert in the Profound Realm now lay immobilized with all four limbs broken and even his internal energy sealed.

Vice Commander Zhuo looked back at Retainer Li Dongyi.

There was only a little dust on his sleeves. He did not have a single wound, and even his breathing remained steady. Despite fighting Zhao Bingyue and four Transformation Realm experts, he showed no sign whatsoever of exhausting his spiritual power.

Vice Commander Zhuo remembered what he had once thought.

That if he ambushed the Retainer from within ten jang (about 30 m), he might have a chance.

It had been an utterly ridiculous delusion.

‘So this man was the real monster...’

Vice Commander Zhuo bowed deeply.

“If not for you, Retainer, my lord, Hui’an Fort would have fallen today.”

“We held because you and the soldiers stopped the remaining intruders as well, Vice Commander Zhuo.”

“No. The credit for today belongs entirely to you, Retainer, my lord. If there is ever anything you wish to command in the future, please give the order.”

“For now, calm yourself and see to the aftermath.”

...

Fifteen days later.

News of what had happened at Hui’an Fort traveled through Lushui Pass and the Fengtian Bureau before reaching the royal palace in Yunjing.

Military documents Zhao Bingyue had been carrying, along with testimony from the prisoners, revealed several Qianyang Kingdom infiltration routes, allowing Yunze Kingdom to intercept in advance the movements of a detached force that had been targeting the rear of Lushui Pass.

The Fengtian Bureau awarded forty merit points for capturing Zhao Bingyue alive, eighteen for capturing or killing the Transformation Realm experts, and fifteen for defending Hui’an Fort and obtaining intelligence.

Together with the merit points Lee Hyun had accumulated over the previous six months, his total exceeded eighty.

‘This should be enough to attend every alchemy lecture. I could use a change of pace anyway, so I might as well learn alchemy for a while.’

Having completed the minimum six-month term of service, Lee Hyun informed the Military Service Hall that he intended to return to External Retainer status.

A new Military Retainer was assigned to Hui’an Fort.

On the day Lee Hyun departed, Vice Commander Zhuo accompanied him all the way to Hui’an Fort’s main gate.

Soldiers on duty stood in rows atop the walls and on either side of the gate. None of them spoke, but unmistakable respect filled their gazes.

“If you ever take another military assignment, Retainer, my lord, please come to Hui’an Fort if you can.”

“If the opportunity arises, I will.”

“Every soldier at Hui’an Fort will await your return, Retainer, my lord.”

“Don’t be too tense. They lost an expert in the Profound Realm themselves, so it is unlikely they will send another powerhouse here anytime soon.”

...

After returning to Yunjing, Lee Hyun visited the Fengtian Bureau’s Alchemy Hall.

The buildings of the Alchemy Hall above ground were used to sort and dry medicinal ingredients or as residences for the alchemists and apothecary apprentices. The actual alchemy chambers that used earth fire had been built separately deep underground.

When Lee Hyun presented his retainer badge, the Alchemy Hall clerk checked the register.

“Are you applying for both the introductory and advanced alchemy lectures?”

“That’s right.”

“You must complete the introductory lectures first. My lord Wen Shenghe will be your instructor.”

The clerk handed him a black bronze token engraved with a flame-shaped pattern.

「Earth Fire Cavern, Level C, No. 7」

Under the clerk’s guidance, Lee Hyun headed toward the black stone hall at the deepest part of the Alchemy Hall.

Inside the stone hall was an enormous vertical shaft whose bottom could not be seen. An iron lift platform hung above it from four thick chains.

Red silk lanterns lined the walls of the shaft at regular intervals, while hot air continually surged upward from the depths below.

“Do I take this down?”

“Yes. The Earth Fire Cavern is five li underground.”

“Does earth fire normally occur at such a shallow depth?”

“No. The upper layers composed of ordinary soil and bedrock are called the common soil stratum, while the deeper layers where earth veins and spirit veins begin to flow in earnest are known as the earth-vein stratum. The boundary generally forms around twenty-five li underground, but occasionally branches of an earth vein rise into the common soil stratum. This is one such place, which allows us to use earth fire starting at a depth of five li.”

“I see.”

When Lee Hyun stepped onto the lift platform, the attendant pulled a lever on the wall.

The sound of massive gears engaging came from overhead, and as the chains slowly unwound, the platform began descending into the shaft.

Creeeeak―

Chapter 24

The farther the lift platform descended, the faster the light above receded into the distance.

The deeper they went, the hotter the wind rising from below became, while water channels of unknown purpose and thick bronze pipes ran through the rock walls.

After quite some time.

Clunk!

The lift platform shuddered lightly and came to a stop.

A vast underground space, larger than Lee Hyun had expected, spread out before him.

Dozens of massive stone pillars supported the cavern ceiling, while rows of air shafts had been bored into the ceiling.

‘No wonder the facilities are so impressive when they carried out construction on the scale of an entire kingdom...’

As he walked along the stone path, the resonant hum of pill furnaces and the scent of medicinal ingredients never ceased behind the stone doors on either side.

...

Earth Fire Cavern, Level C, No. 7.

The moment he opened the thick stone door, a wave of scorching heat struck his face.

A familiar old man's voice rang out.

"You've come?"

Wen Shenghe, whom he had met at the Alchemy Hall before, was sitting inside the stone chamber.

Around him lay medicine cases of various sizes, mortars, steelyard scales, jade knives, tongs, jade bottles, and other implements. At the center of the stone chamber stood a pill furnace as tall as a man's waist.

"It is good to see you again, my lord."

Lee Hyun cupped his hands, and Wen Shenghe gave a slight nod in return.

"I heard you rendered great service at Hui'an Fort."

"I was fortunate."

"If the man who captured a Profound Realm expert alive says he was merely fortunate, the martial artists who died at that expert's hands would feel terribly wronged in their graves."

Wen Shenghe tapped the pill furnace with his palm.

Thunk–

"You said you wanted to learn alchemy?"

"Yes."

"Why?"

"Because I want to make the pills I take myself. For now, I want to refine Barrier-Breaking Pills."

"I thought as much."

Wen Shenghe did not press him further.

"Most people who want to learn alchemy think along similar lines. They imagine making pills themselves will be cheaper than buying them, and that if they can make their own pills, they will no longer have to go asking others for favors."

"Is that mistaken?"

"Half right, half wrong. It is true if you can successfully make the pills. But if you burn through ten bundles of medicinal ingredients to produce a single pill, buying a finished pill would be cheaper."

"So you mean the pill-refining success rate needs to be high? But before even discussing success rates, obtaining a pill recipe itself is far too difficult. I heard alchemy became widespread after the cultivation of spirit plants became commonplace, so why are pill recipes still so expensive? The thought of collecting five hundred merit points just to obtain the Barrier-Breaking Pill recipe is daunting."

"Haha, that is a somewhat different matter."

Wen Shenghe picked up a dried medicinal herb from the table and slowly rubbed it between his fingertips.

"Have you never wondered how the Fengtian Bureau sustains itself? The Barrier-Breaking Pill is actually quite important compared to most other pills. It is used to break through a minor realm, so to exaggerate somewhat, it is similar to the Foundation Establishment Pill a Qi Refining cultivator uses when breaking through to Foundation Establishment."

"Are you saying that if the Fengtian Bureau did not monopolize the Barrier-Breaking Pill recipe, no one would work for it?"

"Exactly. There is a reason so many members of the Fengtian Bureau are at Qi Refining Stage 3. In the first place, the Yunze Kingdom only obtained the Barrier-Breaking Pill recipe because someone from the previous royal bloodline who possessed immortal affinity received aid from a certain cultivation faction. Normally, it is not the sort of thing that would be handed out to a mere mundane dynasty simply because it distinguished itself in war. Pill recipes are created from knowledge accumulated over thousands, even tens of thousands of years. Even a Tier 1 pill recipe is not something an individual can simply discover through research or deduction unless extraordinary fortune favors them. Think about it. Suppose you were a Foundation Establishment cultivator leading a cultivation faction. Would you sell the Foundation Establishment Pill recipe to members who had contributed to your organization?"

"I don't think I would."

"But there are times when you might make a pill recipe public. Under what circumstances do you think that would happen?"

"Hmm... I'm not sure."

"Haha. Let me give you an analogy. Suppose you made the laws of a kingdom and sentenced a murderer to ten years in prison, but a thief to twenty. What would happen?"

"That doesn't seem reasonable. Wouldn't a thief who was caught decide he would be better off killing the witness instead?"

"Exactly. If such a law were enacted, order in the kingdom would collapse. Now then, think about it. What do you suppose it means that obtaining the Barrier-Breaking Pill recipe costs five hundred merit points?"

"That..."

"Let me put it another way. If the Barrier-Breaking Pill recipe could not be exchanged for merit points, or if the number of merit points required were excessively high, what do you think a cultivator who wanted the recipe would do to the Yunze Kingdom?"

"They would simply seize it by force. Ah! Then the five hundred merit points are..."

"Exactly. A cultivator capable of accumulating five hundred merit points might not be able to take on the royal family as a whole, but there is a good chance they would possess enough strength to pose a considerable threat to the Yunze Kingdom."

"I see..."

"What the Fengtian Bureau expects from its Retainers in the first place is for them to collect one hundred merit points, obtain a Barrier-Breaking Pill, and break through to mid Qi Refining. The pill recipe is less a reward for the Retainers and more a route deliberately left open so they have no need to seize it by force."

Wen Shenghe set the dried medicinal herb back down on the table.

"Then even if I earn five hundred merit points, are you saying the royal family might refuse to hand it over if I am not strong enough for them to fear?"

"Haha! That's too much of a leap. They would most likely hand it over to a cultivator who had accumulated that much merit. Of course, if someone were gravely injured while earning those merit points and became weak enough that anyone with the inclination could easily eliminate them, the situation might be slightly different...."

Lee Hyun cleared his throat quietly.

"Goodness. I'm trying to obtain the Barrier-Breaking Pill recipe, so I'd better make sure no one underestimates me."

"I'm joking. Don't worry too much. What I described was an extreme case, and there is little chance the current royal family would do such a thing to a hero of the Yunze Kingdom. If they resorted to killing to silence those who accumulated merit points, who would continue working for the Fengtian Bureau?"

"I see. A thought just occurred to me. Does the Yunze Kingdom perhaps have a pill recipe for breaking through from Qi Refining Stage 6 to Stage 7 as well?"

"Hm? We don't have anything like that."

"Then how did the late Qi Refining Retainers make their breakthroughs?"

"Most of them were already in the late Qi Refining realm when they joined the Fengtian Bureau. They probably just wanted to spend their later years in luxury."

Lee Hyun thought that perhaps Wen Shenghe or the Yunze royal family might be concealing a pill recipe for breaking through the second minor realm.

‘Even if such a pill recipe exists, there must be a reason they're hiding it. There's no need to keep probing and make them wary of me. For now, all I need is the Barrier-Breaking Pill recipe.’

After thinking for a moment, Lee Hyun realized that his last question had been careless.

‘I shouldn't have asked that. If Wen Shenghe is close to the Yunze royal family, I may have already made him wary of me.’

Lee Hyun quickly spoke.

"That certainly makes sense! After being treated so well at Qingliang Villa myself, I found myself getting thoroughly spoiled. The thought of returning to a dreary cave abode and cultivating alone again is already depressing."

"Haha! I know the feeling. You said you were staying at Qingliang Villa? Is there perhaps a maidservant there who has caught your eye? If you wish, you could even take a concubine. If there are any young women you like, I could introduce you to as many as you want..."

"Ahem, I'm still at an important stage of cultivation. If possible, I'd like to preserve my primordial yang."

In general, once a cultivator's primordial yang or primordial yin was broken, reaching Foundation Establishment or forming a golden core became somewhat more difficult.

"Hah, to think you would even give up that pleasure. Perhaps because you're still young, your aspirations toward the immortal path are quite strong. Well, that's enough idle chatter. Let me teach you the fundamentals of alchemy."

As though he had prepared them in advance, Wen Shenghe pushed three books toward him titled 《Herb Identification Record》, 《Essentials of Fire Control》, and 《Introductory Guide on Alchemy》.

"You will be studying these for some time during the basic lectures. Start by opening 《Introductory Guide on Alchemy》. Alchemy can broadly be divided into four stages. Ingredient Selection, where you choose the medicinal ingredients; Refining, where you extract the necessary medicinal potency; Harmonizing, where different medicinal potencies are blended together; and lastly Pill Condensation, where everything is solidified into a single pill. We will begin with Ingredient Selection."

From that day onward, Lee Hyun began learning alchemy from Wen Shenghe.

...

A few days later.

"You know the Fireball Art? Show me."

A fist-sized fireball appeared above Lee Hyun's palm.

"An excellent flame for burning someone to death."

"...Thank you."

"That was not a compliment. If you used it for alchemy, the medicinal ingredients would be reduced to ash the instant they entered the furnace."

Wen Shenghe produced a tiny flame above his own palm.

It was smaller than a candle flame.

He placed a thin leaf over it.

The leaf did not burn.

Instead, tiny droplets of moisture on its surface slowly rose, turning into blue mist that gathered above Wen Shenghe's palm.

"In alchemy, precision matters more than power."

Wen Shenghe moved his finger slightly.

The flame changed from red to yellow.

"Every medicinal ingredient requires a different temperature, and even with the same ingredient, there are times when the heat must be raised and times when it must be lowered. Even inside the pill furnace, different areas may need different levels of heat."

Wen Shenghe pointed to the formation beneath the pill furnace.

"The burners below are connected to the earth-fire formation. By channeling true qi into it, you can adjust the intensity of each burner separately."

"Each one separately?"

"Exactly. Heating the entire pill furnace evenly is not enough. Depending on the state of the medicinal ingredients, you may need to raise the heat on one side and lower it on another. First, open three burners."

Lee Hyun sat before the pill furnace and channeled Primordial True Qi into the earth-fire formation.

Whoosh–

Flames simultaneously rose from three burners.

"Too strong."

Lee Hyun reduced his spiritual power, and the flames shrank by half.

"Still too strong. Lower it a little more."

The flames dwindled until they were as small as candle flames.

Wen Shenghe nodded.

"That's about right. Now make the three flames different sizes."

Lee Hyun focused his mind.
