He raised the eastern flame slightly, lowered the western one, and thinned the central flame to a narrow tongue. The three flames burned at different heights.

"......?"

Wen Shenghe's eyes widened.

"Not bad for your first attempt."

"I've used a great many techniques."

For Lee Hyun, whose entire body was permeated with Primordial True Qi, splitting his true qi and directing it to several places at once was already familiar.

"That is no reason to become complacent. This time, gradually raise the heat of the eastern burner while keeping the other two exactly as they are."

The eastern flame slowly grew.

The western and central flames did not so much as flicker.

Wen Shenghe's gaze changed slightly.

"Could you divide the fire among nine points?"

"I'll try."

Wen Shenghe manipulated the formation beneath the pill furnace, revealing six additional burner patterns.

Lee Hyun split his Primordial True Qi into threads and connected each one to a different burner pattern.

Whoosh.

Nine flames rose to different heights.

Wen Shenghe circled the pill furnace, examining the nine flames one by one. A peculiar expression appeared on his face.

"Your control over spiritual power is already at the level of a Tier 1 alchemist."

"Then does that mean I have talent for alchemy?"

"A little."

Wen Shenghe answered coolly.

"Controlling fire well and making pills well are two different things. Just because someone can wield a knife with precision does not make them a fine chef."

He set three kinds of medicinal herbs down before Lee Hyun.

"Today, you will make a Heat-Clearing Pill. It uses medicinal ingredients from the mundane world, so there is less burden if you fail. It is a pill that suppresses mild fire toxin, but it has little effect on cultivators."

Wen Shenghe began by teaching him how to prepare the medicinal ingredients.

Lee Hyun separated the leaves and stems of the Clear Qi Grass, peeled the outer skin from the Meridian-Warming Root, and removed the seeds from the Crimson Yang Fruit, setting them aside.

Once all the preparations were complete, Lee Hyun placed the medicinal ingredients into the pill furnace one by one.

Blue medicinal liquid seeped from the leaves of the Clear Qi Grass, while the Meridian-Warming Root slowly melted and released a crimson aura.

Lee Hyun adjusted the strength of the flames according to Wen Shenghe's instructions.

"Lower the eastern burner."

Whoosh.

"Raise the central burner slightly."

Flames wrapped around the bottom of the pill furnace.

"Put in the Crimson Yang Fruit seeds now."

Lee Hyun dropped in the seeds.

Sizzle–

Red smoke rose from inside the pill furnace.

"Lower the heat!"

Lee Hyun immediately reduced the intensity of the burners.

But he was a little too late.

Pop!

A small explosion erupted inside the pill furnace, and black smoke leaked through the gap beneath the lid.

Wen Shenghe sighed.

"Burned."

Lee Hyun opened the pill furnace's lid.

Blackened medicinal residue clung to the inside, and a foul odor spread through the chamber.

"This isn't easy...."

"Even seeds from the same Crimson Yang Fruit can vary slightly in nature. The seeds you just used contained more oil than usual. You should have noticed that by sight beforehand, and after putting them into the furnace, you should have paid attention to the sound and smell so you could lower the heat sooner."

"The sound and smell...."

"Simply following the sequence and temperatures written in a pill recipe will not produce a finished pill. Medicinal ingredients are living things, not drawings in a book. Even those grown in the same field differ in nature, and the amount of moisture they contain changes depending on how long they have been stored."

Wen Shenghe pointed to the blackened residue.

"It's far more complicated than I expected. I thought there would be something like a fixed formula."

"A fixed formula... There is, of course, a general framework. But following only that will make it difficult to become a good alchemist. You've captured a Profound Realm expert alive, so surely you understand. If you swing your sword along a predetermined sword path, will your opponent simply stand there and let you hit them?"

"No. The other person is a living opponent too, so you have to adapt to the situation every time."

"Medicinal ingredients are the same. A pill recipe only shows you the path. It does not tell you the exact condition of the ingredients in front of you. In the end, you must look with your own eyes, smell them, and judge for yourself. Miss the smallest difference and you will burn an entire batch, just as you did now."

Lee Hyun stared into the pill furnace for a long while.

"May I try again?"

"We have plenty of medicinal ingredients."

...

A few days later.

"Now! Form the Pill-Condensing Seal."

Lee Hyun's fingers moved.

Hummm–

The pill furnace trembled faintly.

A moment later.

Tap. Rattle.

Six round objects dropped onto the bottom of the pill furnace.

Lee Hyun opened the lid.

Six pills, each about the size of a fingertip, lay inside.

Two had cracked surfaces, and one was scorched black.

A faint medicinal fragrance wafted from the remaining three.

"Did I succeed?"

Wen Shenghe picked up one of the pills, pressed it with his finger, then brought it beneath his nose and smelled it.

"Poor quality even by low-grade standards. Thirty percent of the medicinal potency dispersed, and there is still a trace of fire qi left."

"So it's a failure."

"If you call producing three finished pills after only a few days a failure, nine out of ten alchemists in this world ought to give up alchemy."

Wen Shenghe returned the pills to Lee Hyun.

"Your control over spiritual power is sufficient. Your way of using your senses is unusual, but it works. What you lack now is experience with medicinal ingredients."

"How long do I need to study?"

Wen Shenghe pointed to a bowl piled with blackened medicinal residue.

"Once you've gone through about a thousand more failures like those, you'll begin to get a rough feel for it."

Lee Hyun looked at the amount of residue.

"With that much experience, could I say I'm no longer a beginner?"

"A thousand attempts only means you're someone who has done it a thousand times. Compared with someone who has handled the same medicinal ingredient two thousand times, you would still be a beginner. And if you encountered a spirit herb you'd never seen before, you would become a beginner all over again."

Wen Shenghe looked at the pills resting atop the pill furnace.

"Alchemy is ultimately about countless substances and heat, and the combinations and transformations between them. Faced with all those possibilities, who could readily call themselves a master? Perhaps if one could study them for an eternity..."

"That's good advice."

Half a year later.

"That concludes the advanced lectures on alchemy as well. I have nothing more to teach you. If you truly manage to collect five hundred merit points and obtain the Barrier-Breaking Pill recipe someday, come back then. I will teach you until you are at least capable of refining a low-grade Barrier-Breaking Pill."

Chapter 25

"I'll come visit again."

Lee Hyun bade Wen Shenghe farewell and left the Earth Fire Cavern. The six months he had spent training in alchemy had been more enjoyable than he expected.

Now all that remained was the pill recipe for the Barrier-Breaking Pill.

'Five hundred merit points....'

Lee Hyun took out his retainer badge again.

That more or less settled what he would be doing for the time being.

One year later.

Tunnel No. 1.

Lee Hyun had returned to his old life as a Military Retainer, and whenever he came back on leave, he would visit Tunnel No. 1 like this.

As usual, he checked the spirit fields before finally harvesting ripe seedpods from the Yin Water Lotuses and ripe Stone Honey Peaches.

Crunch–

The moment he bit into a ripe Stone Honey Peach, a sweet, refreshing sensation swept through his entire body.

"Ah..."

Whenever he happened across spirit insect eggs, larvae, dead spirit insects, or the like, he tossed them into the breeding case he had built in the training cavern as casually as throwing away trash.

Today, Lee Hyun had come to the breeding case to dispose of a few small spirit insects and some eggs he had found in Spirit Field No. 1-6. He lifted the heavy lid.

Scrrrape–

"...Hm?"

Lee Hyun's hand stopped.

Something inside the breeding case was looking up at him.

"What are you?"

Lee Hyun cast the Faint Light Art.

Fwoom.

A fist-sized orb of light floated above the breeding case, brightly illuminating the interior.

Five small, round insects were huddled together atop a piece of stone. Their plump bodies had short legs, and small translucent wings were attached to their backs, undersized compared to their bodies.

Their fur stood out the most. Soft hairs patterned in alternating pale gold and black covered their entire bodies in a fluffy coat. The pitch-black eyes on either side of their round heads were unusually large and glossy.

'What the... bumblebees? Do bumblebees exist in this world too? Even if they do, there's no way they could survive in a place like this....'

They looked like bumblebees made even rounder.

As soon as the lid opened, they all placed their short forelegs against the wall of the case and raised their antennae in unison, like baby birds waiting for their mother to bring them food.

Spiritual qi was clearly flowing through their bodies. It was simply so faint that whenever Lee Hyun had used the Aura-Reading Art from outside the breeding case, their presence had apparently been buried beneath the qi of the soil and the other spirit insects.

'Did I ever put anything like these in here?'

No matter how hard he thought, he couldn't remember doing so.

'Were their eggs mixed in with something else?'

Lee Hyun dropped a dead spirit insect into the breeding case.

Plop.

At once, all five pairs of antennae turned toward the dead spirit insect.

A transparent liquid shot from the mouth of the nearest fellow like a bullet.

Pfft!

The moment the liquid struck the dead spirit insect, it stretched into sticky threads.

Pshh! Pshh!

The others joined in. Within just a few breaths, the dead spirit insect was completely wrapped in translucent mucus, and the fluffy insects climbed on top of it and began gnawing at its shell with their tiny mouths.

Crunch. Crunch.

"So you guys eat bugs?"

Come to think of it, most of what he had thrown into that case so far had been spirit insects and their eggs. If so, that explained how these creatures had survived in such a harsh environment. They had endured by feeding on the other insects.

After considering it for a moment, Lee Hyun picked up the smallest of the five between his fingers. Startled, the fellow buzzed its wings, but it neither bit him nor spat mucus. Instead, it moved its short legs and crawled onto the back of Lee Hyun's hand.

"You're not afraid at all, are you?"

Looking at it closely, it was surprisingly cute. Its round body made its rear sway slightly from side to side whenever it walked, and perhaps because its wings were too small for its body, whenever it tried to fly, it only managed to float one or two cheok (about 30–60 cm) into the air before settling back down.

'I have no idea what kind of spirit insect this is. I'll call them fuzzbees for now. More importantly, do these fellows only eat spirit insects and not spirit plants?'

Lee Hyun took the fuzzbee to Spirit Field No. 1-7 and set it on the branch of a Stone Honey Peach tree. A sweet, refreshing fragrance drifted from the ripe spirit fruits.

The fuzzbee moved its antennae for a moment.

Twitch.

Then it walked straight past.

This time, Lee Hyun cut open a Stone Honey Peach and held the flesh in front of it. The fellow touched the fruit once with its antennae, then turned away.

It was the same at the reservoir where the Yin Water Lotuses grew. Even when Lee Hyun split open a seedpod and placed the tender young seeds directly in front of it, the fuzzbee showed no interest.

Instead, after wandering among the lotus leaves for quite some time, its antennae suddenly perked up.

Pshh!

Mucus shot toward the underside of a lotus leaf. A rice-grain-sized spirit insect hiding beneath it was caught in the sticky liquid, and the fuzzbee quickly rushed over and gnawed it apart.

"Huh."

This time, Lee Hyun headed to Spirit Field No. 1-1.

When he opened the stone door, dense medicinal fragrances and toxic qi drifted out. Toxic dust released by the aged Bone-Rot Flowers and Purple Poison Orchids hung in the air like a faint mist.

Lee Hyun set the fuzzbee down on the soil near the entrance.

'Can it really withstand this toxic qi too?'

The fellow briefly drew in on itself. A little poisonous dust from the Bone-Rot Flowers settled on its golden fur.

Lee Hyun examined it with the Aura-Reading Art.

'There's no change in its qi.'

The time it takes to eat a meal went by.

The fellow was perfectly fine. If anything, it seemed bored as it wandered deeper into the spirit field, passing beneath the Purple Poison Orchids' long leaves and circling around the roots of the Yin Soul Grass. It rubbed itself against the soil around the Earth Vein Flowers for a while, but never took a bite from the leaves or stems of any spirit plant.

'Could it be....'

Still crouching, Lee Hyun followed behind it.

Before long, the fuzzbee stopped. Its antennae pointed toward the ground.

Pshh!

Mucus shot into the soil. The fellow rapidly scratched away the dirt with its forelegs.

Beneath it were three translucent spirit insect eggs.

Crunch. Crunch.

One egg vanished in an instant.

Lee Hyun's eyes gleamed.

'This fellow... couldn't I use something like this as a guard for the spirit fields?'

Of course, drawing a conclusion from a single test would be dangerous. Perhaps it simply wasn't hungry enough yet to eat spirit plants, or perhaps its diet would change once it reached a certain stage of growth.

Lee Hyun moved just that one fuzzbee into Spirit Field No. 1-5.

"Try living here for now."

The fuzzbee waved its antennae as though it understood.

Lee Hyun closed the stone door.

...

For the next several years, Lee Hyun continued observing the creatures whenever he visited Tunnel No. 1.

The results exceeded his expectations. They were especially fond of living spirit insects and eggs, and even when he deliberately starved them, they never touched the spirit plants. They also remained perfectly active amid the toxic qi of the Bone-Rot Flowers and Purple Poison Orchids.

Another interesting point was that the fuzzbees took to Lee Hyun quite well.

Whenever he opened the lid of the breeding case, they would swarm toward the edge even if he had no food, and when he held out his hand, several would naturally crawl onto his fingers or sleeves. Perhaps because Lee Hyun had been throwing food into the breeding case for so long, they had come to associate his scent or spiritual power with food.

Of course, not every individual was docile. Occasionally, one would bite his finger or spit mucus before trying to flee.

Lee Hyun killed those individuals and kept only the docile ones that hunted nothing but insects.

As the years passed, an interesting change emerged. Their population rose and fell over time, but at some point, most of the newly emerged young became more docile than the individuals he had first discovered.

More and more of them even climbed onto his hand first whenever he held it out.

'Could it be because I've kept only the ones that listen to me?'

He recalled the silver fox domestication experiment he had heard about in his previous life. The story went that after selecting only the least aggressive individuals to breed, a clear tendency toward friendliness with humans emerged within just a few generations.

He hadn't intended it, but it seemed he was doing something similar.

Still, he had no idea what their breeding cycle was like, how they developed, or how long they lived. His life as a Military Retainer made it impossible to observe them continuously, and Lee Hyun had no knowledge of spirit insects to begin with.

Even so, one thing was certain. The creatures were extremely useful in the spirit fields.

Before he knew it, Lee Hyun had released them into every spirit field from Spirit Field No. 1-1 through Spirit Field No. 1-7. Before, he had needed to inspect every leaf and root to check for damage from spirit insects, but once the fuzzbees became established, the number of pests dropped noticeably.

Whenever Lee Hyun entered a spirit field, a few fluffy balls would occasionally buzz over and land on his shoulders or head.

Plop.

"...Don't poop on me."

And so, the years Lee Hyun spent traveling back and forth to Tunnel No. 1 while serving as a Military Retainer reached fifteen.

During that time, Lee Hyun traveled not only to Hui'an Fort but to many other fortresses throughout the south. Profound Realm powerhouses like Zhao Bingyue appeared on several occasions, and skirmishes large and small never ceased along the border between Qianyang Kingdom and Yunze Kingdom.

He captured scouts, dealt with infiltrating masters, supported outposts in danger, and stopped martial artists who targeted military provisions.

Once Lee Hyun realized that his strength was a little too overwhelming, he actually began restraining his involvement so that he would not influence the course of the war between the two kingdoms too heavily. He feared that having too great an impact on a war in the mundane world might attract the attention of Kun Kingdom's cultivation world.

Even so, over the years, his merit points eventually surpassed six hundred. That was enough to buy the pill recipe for the Barrier-Breaking Pill, his original goal, and still have more than a hundred points remaining.

Merit points weren't the only thing he had accumulated.

During his travels throughout the south, countless martial arts manuals passed through Lee Hyun's hands. Some were secret manuals taken from fallen martial artists, while others were personal insights offered by captured masters in exchange for their lives. There were also martial artists indebted to Lee Hyun who showed him portions of their own martial learning.

At first, he studied any martial arts that caught his eye, but as his discernment grew with time, he naturally learned to separate the gems from the dross. Now, unless something was the supreme art of a Profound Realm master, he wouldn't even give it a second glance.

...

In a mountain valley a little over a hundred li (a little over 40 km) north of Hui'an Fort.

There was a broad clearing that had been abandoned long ago.

Thud!

The instant Lee Hyun's right foot struck the ground, his body shot forward half a jang (about 1.5 m).

But no second step followed.

His toes scraped diagonally across the ground, and his forward momentum vanished as if it had never existed. The next instant, he slid roughly one cheok (about 30 cm) to the left. He advanced another half step, lowered his body, twisted at the waist, and drove diagonally to the right.

Short, rapid movements flowed one after another without pause.

At most, he covered only one or two jang (about 6 m)with each movement. Most carried him less than a single step. Yet within the span of one breath, Lee Hyun's position changed several times.

《Square-Inch Step》.

Of all the footwork Lee Hyun had encountered, this was the supreme art he judged to be the finest when it came purely to close combat.

Its creator was Liu Baichuan, a Profound Realm martial artist who had made a name for himself in Qianyang Kingdom sixty years ago. Liu Baichuan had participated in invasions of Yunze Kingdom since his youth and spent decades fighting aboard swaying ships and narrow decks. It was said that he placed little value on lightness skills that only displayed their true worth across broad, flat ground.

The essence of Square-Inch Step lay in momentary bursts of acceleration and abrupt stops, minute shifts of one or two cheok (about 30–60 cm), continuous changes in direction, and quickly recovering from a compromised stance.

Thud!

Lee Hyun shot forward,

Whoosh!

and in the next instant, he had already slid sideways and was straightening his upper body. Had an opponent been standing before him, he would have dodged the attack while simultaneously slipping within range of his sword.

"Not bad."

Square-Inch Step suited Lee Hyun's Primordial Body particularly well.

Martial artists had to draw internal energy from their dantian and send it through fixed meridians into their legs, but Lee Hyun could draw on the Primordial True Qi already spread throughout his body directly from whatever area he wished.

On top of that, his physical abilities were beyond comparison with those of a mortal.

His understanding of Square-Inch Step still fell short of its creator, Liu Baichuan, but judging by the outward movements alone, he had already surpassed Liu Baichuan by a wide margin.

Shff–

Lee Hyun abruptly stopped after sweeping across the clearing.

Clang!

An ordinary iron sword of the sort used by Yunze Kingdom soldiers slid free from his waist.

Alongside Square-Inch Step, the art Lee Hyun had devoted the most effort to mastering was 《One Ultimate, Six Swords》.

This swordsmanship was also something he had selected after comparing the supreme arts of countless Profound Realm masters.

The creator of One Ultimate, Six Swords was Chen Baishan, a Profound Realm swordsman known as the Iron Sword Elder in Qianyang Kingdom thirty years ago.

Among the Profound Realm masters of his generation, Chen Baishan did not possess especially deep internal energy. Instead, he spent his entire life delving into the principle of One Point Pierces the Surface, concentrating the same amount of internal energy into a single point to draw out greater power.

The result was One Ultimate, Six Swords. An anecdote from his later years even claimed that he once shattered the defensive technique of a late Qi Refining cultivator with a single sword strike and gravely wounded him.

"Hoo."

Light flowed along the blade of the iron sword in Lee Hyun's hand.

At a glance, it resembled the sword aura used by martial artists, but its essence was entirely different. What Lee Hyun had wrapped around the sword was spiritual power.

By drawing on several supreme arts, Lee Hyun had succeeded in creating something with spiritual power that resembled sword aura, and for convenience, he called it Spirit Aura.

Following the principles of One Ultimate, Six Swords, he compressed that Spirit Aura to the extreme along the blade.

Flash!

The sword cut through the air.

A finger-thick strand of Spirit Aura shot from the blade and pierced a perfectly smooth hole through the center of a cliff face a little over ten jang (about 30 m) away. The end of the hole could not be seen.

"Hm."

Lee Hyun lowered his sword.

'Martial arts really do suit me well. Is it because of the Primordial Body...? Now that my entire body has been tempered, I'm in a position similar to a body refiner.'

A body refiner was a cultivator who tempered the flesh through a body-refining art. Body refiners naturally excelled in close combat, and in that regard, they had quite a lot in common with the martial artists of the mundane world.

'I'll take my time studying the rest of the martial arts.'

The supreme arts possessed by Profound Realm masters were truly profound, so there was no way he could master all of them in a short period.

Lee Hyun had only been able to reach this level because, as a cultivator, his concentration, memory, and physical abilities far surpassed those of mortals.

...

Lee Hyun slowly looked around at the surrounding scenery.

He had obtained nearly everything he had wanted from Yunze Kingdom. He had learned alchemy, studied numerous martial arts while accumulating real combat experience, and gathered more than enough merit points to obtain the pill recipe for the Barrier-Breaking Pill.

"It's time to leave."

Chapter 26

A few days later.

Hundreds of soldiers stood in formation before the main gate of Hui'an Fort.

“What is all this?”

Lee Hyun looked slightly taken aback as he was about to leave through the gate.

Zhuo Wucheng stood at the very front.

He was already in his late sixties, and a fair amount of white had crept into his once-black hair.

“You intend to step down as a Military Retainer after this final term of service, don’t you?”

“How did you know?”

“I’ve known you for more than a day or two. How could I not?”

“I see.”

Lee Hyun nodded.

“You’ve worked hard all these years. I intend to leave now.”

At Lee Hyun’s words, Zhuo Wucheng turned around.

“Everyone, bid my lord the Retainer farewell!”

Clang!

Hundreds of soldiers raised their weapons at once, and the spearheads and sword blades flashed in the sunlight.

The soldiers bowed deeply toward Lee Hyun in unison.

“There was no need to go this far....”

“If not for my lord, most of the people here would have died long ago.”

Several veteran soldiers nodded at Zhuo Wucheng’s words.

An old soldier standing in the rear called out loudly.

“No matter where the Immortal goes, the soldiers of Hui'an Fort will never forget your kindness!”

“Kindness, my foot.... I was paid for my work too.”

The soldiers who had once feared him when he first came to Hui'an Fort now looked reluctant to see him go.

Some of the boy soldiers who had only just enlisted back then had become bearded, middle-aged soldiers. Those who had been middle-aged were now old, and many of those who had already been old were no longer there at all.

Lee Hyun looked at them for a moment before cupping his hands.

“I owe you all a great deal for these past years. Stay safe, and live long lives.”

...

A few days later.

Fengtian Bureau, Yunjing.

Lee Hyun sat at a table in the Retainers Hall.

Across from him, Standing Retainer Lu Xiaoyan, who handled administrative affairs, checked his retainer badge and the ledger.

“You wish to exchange for the Barrier-Breaking Pill recipe?”

“Yes.”

“Five hundred merit points will be deducted. If you transmit or sell the contents of the pill recipe to outsiders, it could cause serious trouble.”

“Of course. I understand.”

Lee Hyun nodded.

A short while later, Lu Xiaoyan returned from somewhere carrying a small wooden box.

When she opened the lid, a thin booklet with no title written on it was revealed.

“Check it.”

Lee Hyun opened to the first page.

「Barrier-Breaking Pill recipe for one furnace batch.

The ages listed below refer to medicine age.

1 root of Spirit-Storing Ginseng, 50–70 years.

3 Meridian-Piercing Flowers, 40–60 years.

1 cap of Meridian-Protecting Lingzhi, 30–50 years.

3 nodes of Origin-Returning Vine, 30–45 years.

9 Triple-Layer Leaves, 20–35 years.

3 fully ripe Essence-Condensing Fruits borne by Essence-Condensing Trees aged 40–60 years.

12 Clear Void Seeds harvested from Clear Void Grass aged 15–25 years.

3 drops of Spirit-Stabilizing Stone Milk.」

“.......”

Lee Hyun stared down at the pill recipe for a long while.

‘This is no joke.’

Written in tiny script were not only the types of medicinal ingredients, but also when to harvest them, how to store and prepare them, and every step from Refining and Harmonizing to Pill Condensation.

Lee Hyun continued turning the pages.

「The medicine ages recorded in this pill recipe are based on spirit plants grown normally under standard conditions in a Tier 1 spirit field. Since the accumulation of medicinal potency varies depending on the environment of the spirit field, actual age alone must not be used as the criterion. Judge by also examining the color, fragrance, flow of spiritual qi, and outward signs described below.」

Lee Hyun’s expression brightened.

‘Good. The information is detailed.’

Lee Hyun closed the pill recipe.

“I’ve checked it.”

...

Earth Fire Cavern, Level C, No. 7.

“You really brought it.”

Wen Shenghe took the pill recipe, flipped through a few pages, then handed it back to Lee Hyun.

“My lord Wen. Do pill recipes normally require this many ingredients and such strict conditions?”

“Even so, it is only a Tier 1 pill recipe.”

“Even though it’s Tier 1?”

“Didn’t I tell you before? That is precisely why properly verified pill recipes are so valuable.”

Lee Hyun looked down at the pill recipe again before asking,

“By the way, how many spirit stones would it cost to obtain all these ingredients?”

“If you bought every ingredient needed for one furnace batch, you should expect to spend around seventy to one hundred twenty low-grade spirit stones.”

“That’s expensive. How many Barrier-Breaking Pills can one furnace batch produce?”

“Nine at most.”

“If it’s nine, then at least....”

“If the god of alchemy descends upon you, that is.”

“.......”

Wen Shenghe spoke as calmly as ever.

“If a Tier 1 alchemist like me, who has worked with this pill recipe for many years, uses medicinal ingredients in good condition, producing around three pills in a mix of low and mid grade would be a respectable result.”

“Then what about an alchemist who is just learning?”

“Once thoroughly familiar with the pill recipe, being able to consistently produce two low-grade Barrier-Breaking Pills would already be considered good.”

Lee Hyun held out his fingers.

Even if he obtained the ingredients at their cheapest, they would still cost seventy low-grade spirit stones.

And from that, two Barrier-Breaking Pills.

“...That’s thirty-five low-grade spirit stones per pill.”

“That is only the cost of the medicinal ingredients. There is also the cost of using the pill furnace and earth fire... not to mention the alchemist’s time and effort... Do you understand now?”

Wen Shenghe laughed heartily.

“A Qi Refining rogue cultivator who carelessly dabbles in alchemy will bankrupt himself.”

“.......”

Lee Hyun suddenly recalled the contents of the Fengtian Merit Register.

“So there was a reason everyone tries to obtain finished Barrier-Breaking Pills instead of refining them themselves.”

“There is a reason people buy them ready-made. Why do you think specialized fields and professions exist?”

“That certainly makes sense.”

But Lee Hyun had plenty of time.

‘I can just grow the ingredients myself and then refine the pills.’

Lee Hyun examined the pill recipe again before asking,

“But it says here to use Spirit-Storing Ginseng with a medicine age of fifty to seventy years, doesn’t it?”

“That’s right.”

“If I use one that’s around a hundred years old, would it produce a better Barrier-Breaking Pill?”

“In theory, yes. But you would have to revise the pill recipe. If the medicine age changes, not only the medicinal strength but also the speed and nature at which its medicinal potency is released during Refining will change.”

“Then couldn’t I simply use half as much hundred-year-old Spirit-Storing Ginseng?”

“You could make the total medicinal strength roughly equal, but the rate at which it harmonizes with the other medicinal ingredients would no longer match. Change the Spirit-Storing Ginseng, and you would have to adjust everything in turn, from the quantities of Meridian-Piercing Flower and Meridian-Protecting Lingzhi to the timing for adding the other medicinal ingredients.”

“So following the recipe exactly is best.”

“That’s right.”

Afterward, Lee Hyun watched from beside Wen Shenghe as he actually refined Barrier-Breaking Pills and learned a great deal.

Whenever Wen Shenghe refined a medicinal ingredient, he carefully pointed out each moment when its color, fragrance, and medicinal potency changed. Lee Hyun watched closely, comparing the changes in the actual medicinal ingredients with what was written in the pill recipe.

...

A few days later.

Wen Shenghe brought over a bamboo basket.

Inside were immature Spirit-Storing Ginseng that had failed to grow properly, Meridian-Piercing Flowers, small Meridian-Protecting Lingzhi, and cut sections of Origin-Returning Vine stems, all mixed together.

“Practice with these.”

“Is it all right even though their medicine ages are insufficient?”

“I’m not telling you to complete a Barrier-Breaking Pill. You need to develop a feel for Refining and Harmonizing the ingredients. Proper ingredients are far too expensive to use for practice.”

Lee Hyun picked up a root of Spirit-Storing Ginseng. Several fine roots had been severed, but the green leaves at the top were still intact.

“Do these come from the royal spirit fields too?”

“That’s right. They were culled because they grew too slowly or their roots were damaged. Leaving them there would only waste space and spiritual qi.”

Lee Hyun examined the other medicinal ingredients in the basket as well. The Origin-Returning Vines still had living buds, the Meridian-Piercing Flowers still had their roots, and the young Meridian-Protecting Lingzhi still had mycelium attached to pieces of rotting spirit wood.

‘Some of these might survive if I plant them properly.’

Lee Hyun’s gaze slowly swept across the basket.

“May I take a few of whatever remains after practice?”

“What do you intend to do with them?”

“I think growing them myself would help me learn how the medicinal ingredients develop and how their medicinal potency changes.”

“Hmm... I don’t see why not. They were going to be thrown away anyway.”

“Thank you.”

Afterward, Lee Hyun repeatedly practiced the Refining and Harmonizing processes using discarded medicinal ingredients. By taking a few of the better specimens after each lesson, he eventually obtained planting stock for every spirit plant used in the Barrier-Breaking Pill.

Spirit-Stabilizing Stone Milk, however, was a mineral spirit liquid rather than a spirit plant, so he would probably have to purchase it separately at a cultivator market later.

...

A month later.

Lee Hyun had learned most of what Wen Shenghe could teach him about the Barrier-Breaking Pill.

Although he had not yet personally refined a Barrier-Breaking Pill with ingredients matching the medicine ages listed in the pill recipe, Wen Shenghe judged that Lee Hyun had reached a level where he could successfully form a low-grade Barrier-Breaking Pill as long as he had good ingredients.

“Thank you for everything. I think it’s about time I left Yunze Kingdom. This is just a small token of my appreciation.”

Lee Hyun took two large Stone Honey Peaches from his storage pouch. A sweet, refreshing fragrance spread through the room.

“Spirit fruit?”

“They’re called Stone Honey Peaches. They taste quite good.”

“Stone Honey Peaches...? I’ve never heard that name before.”

Wen Shenghe examined the fruit for a while before taking a bite.

Crunch.

“......Huh.”

His eyebrows rose.

“It’s as sweet as honey, yet the flesh is cold as ice. Perhaps it’s because I’ve spent the last several days sitting in front of the pill furnace, but it feels as though all the pent-up heat in my chest has been swept away. Where did you obtain a spirit fruit like this?”

“I happened to find it at a cultivator market a long time ago. I went back later, but the seller had already left.”

“What a shame....”

Wen Shenghe placed the remaining Stone Honey Peach into his storage pouch.

“I’ll have to save this one.”

...

Fengtian Bureau, Formation Court.

Lee Hyun looked at the nine red formation stones arranged on the floor and the bronze pill furnace resting above them.

They were the same pill furnace and earth-fire formation that the Fengtian Bureau provided in every alchemy chamber of the Earth Fire Cavern.

“The Nine-Fire Flame-Storing Formation and the pill furnace designed to be used with it. Strictly speaking, they are only a Tier 1 low-grade magic tool and formation... Are you really going to spend merit points to buy these? I certainly don’t mind, but if you work for the Fengtian Bureau, you can use the Earth Fire Cavern anyway. There is hardly any need to purchase your own....”

“I intend to use them for private alchemy practice. I’ll look for somewhere with earth fire later.”

“Hmm. Don’t come asking to return them later. Refer to this booklet for how to connect the formation to earth fire, maintain the pill furnace, and so on.”

Lee Hyun placed the pill furnace, formation, and booklet into his storage pouch, then checked his retainer badge.

The little over one hundred merit points he had left after obtaining the Barrier-Breaking Pill recipe were now almost completely gone.

...

Before leaving Yunjing, Lee Hyun also stopped by Cuiyun Market.

While browsing the cultivator market, he found a stall selling seeds from Essence-Condensing Trees and Clear Void Grass.

Lee Hyun bought a small quantity of both kinds of seeds. He had already secured planting stock for everything, but he wanted spares in case some of them failed to take root properly.

He spent one low-grade spirit stone on them.

Lastly, at a shop dealing in spirit insects, he purchased a spirit-insect pouch capable of storing living spirit insects.

While he was there, a storage pouch displayed in one corner caught his eye.

Its internal space was several times larger than the one he currently used.

‘Now I have a pill furnace, and I’ll need to carry more spirit plants around in the future....’

After thinking it over for a moment, he bought that as well.

The two items together cost ten low-grade spirit stones.

After leaving the shop, Lee Hyun counted the spirit stones in his storage pouch.

He had exactly twelve low-grade spirit stones remaining.

‘Hmm... I’ll need to earn some spirit stones before long.’

...

Three days later.

Royal Palace of Yunze Kingdom.

Lee Hyun met Liu Zhenghui for the first time in a long while.

More than ten years ago, Liu Zhenghui had been a young Crown Prince wearing a golden crown, but now the crown of the King of Yunze Kingdom rested upon his head.

The previous King had passed away in the intervening years, and Liu Zhenghui had succeeded to the throne.

The youthful face that had once suited his dark purple robes so well now bore wrinkles around the eyes and a neatly trimmed short beard. He had never given a frivolous impression even in the past, but now he carried a far graver bearing befitting the King of a nation.

“I’ve lost count of how many times I’ve tried to persuade you to stay. You truly are leaving.”

“Yes.”

“You refused when I offered to double your stipend, refused when I offered to lend you part of the royal spirit fields, and even refused when I offered you an entire estate far better than Qingliang Villa.”

“I did consider the last offer for a moment.”

Liu Zhenghui’s eyes brightened.

“Then would you reconsider?”

“I still intend to leave.”

“.......”

Liu Zhenghui sighed.

“Where do you intend to go?”

“I haven’t decided.”

“So you have no destination. I envy you.”

Liu Zhenghui took a sip of tea.

“If I wandered around without a destination for even a single day, the ministers would come looking for me.”

A moment later, Liu Zhenghui spoke again.

“Will I be able to see you again?”

“Who knows.”

Lee Hyun suddenly thought of Zhang Ping, whom he had met in a Yunjing market more than three hundred years ago. When he had visited not long ago, a descendant who resembled Zhang Ping was selling Water Root Grass in the same spot.

Lee Hyun had only shut himself away in his tunnel for a while, yet Zhang Ping had already vanished from the world.

‘I see.’

A fact he had always known suddenly struck him anew. This would continue to happen in the future.

He would meet someone, go somewhere else for a while, and by the time he returned, that person would have grown old or died.

It was an issue he had never needed to think much about while spending hundreds of years alone in his tunnel.

Lee Hyun set down his teacup.

‘Well....’

That was no reason to stop meeting people.

Just because they would disappear someday did not mean the years they had spent together would vanish as well.

Lee Hyun rose from his seat.

“I should be going now.”

“There’s no point trying to stop you until the very end, is there?”

“That’s right.”

“Then I won’t try to stop you anymore.”

Liu Zhenghui cupped his hands.

“Thank you for all the help you’ve given Yunze Kingdom over the years.”

A few days later.

Lee Hyun left through Yunjing’s northern gate.

He followed the highway north, then turned toward the mountainous wilderness to the northwest once the road grew deserted.

...

A small mountain peak north of Yunjing.

Three men were watching Lee Hyun’s receding figure.

All three wore the retainer badges used by External Retainers of the Fengtian Bureau.

The middle-aged man standing at the front was named Wei Wendao. His face appeared to be around forty, and his expression revealed nothing. The aura of Qi Refining Stage 6 emanated from his body.

One step behind him stood Peng Ziliang, a gaunt man with sharp eyes and his arms folded. Qi Refining Stage 5.

The last was Han Xiaobai, the youngest of the three. Qi Refining Stage 3.

Han Xiaobai watched Lee Hyun in the distance for a while before speaking.

“Senior Brother Wei. Are we really making our move today?”

“Yes.”

“The rumors circulating outside aren’t entirely exaggerated. There are even records of him capturing several Profound Realm experts alive.”

Peng Ziliang snorted.

“Xiaobai. Are you frightened just because he captured a few martial artists from the mundane world?”

“I’m not frightened. I’m saying we should be cautious.”

“Did those martial grandmasters of the mundane world have mid-grade magic tools? Did they even have a Tier 1 low-grade talisman? No matter how powerful their martial arts were, they were ultimately only mortal means.”

“Ziliang, enough.”

Wei Wendao cut him off in a low voice.

“Xiaobai’s concerns are not wrong. For a Qi Refining Stage 3 rogue cultivator, that man’s record is far too impressive. That is why I came personally.”

“You thought it serious enough to come yourself, Senior Brother?”

“If we have decided to kill him, then we kill him properly. It will be too late to regret afterward that we should have been more careful.”

Wei Wendao’s tone remained calm.

Han Xiaobai hesitated for a moment before bringing up something else.

“Even so, the mission Steward gave us was to find a child with a single spiritual root. Can taking the pill recipe really make up for that?”

“That again?”

Irritation appeared on Peng Ziliang’s face.

“We’ve already been stuck in Yunze Kingdom for a year. Do you have any guarantee that a single spiritual root will suddenly turn up even if we comb through this place for another five years? Do you even understand what a single spiritual root is? It’s a talent difficult to find even among a million mortals. Why do you think it’s called a heavenly spiritual root?”

“That’s why I said from the beginning that if we used the authority of External Retainers just a little and gathered children from the county seats....”

“Xiaobai.”

Wei Wendao called his name.

Han Xiaobai fell silent.

“Do not bring that up again. This is not the Azure Cloud Sect’s sphere of influence. If the Biluo Sect or Danxiao Sect learned that we entered the territory of Kun Kingdom and tried to poach their talent, it would cause a far greater problem than failing to find a single spiritual root.”

“...I know.”

“We became External Retainers of the Fengtian Bureau so that we could travel throughout Yunze Kingdom without drawing attention, not so that we could use the Retainer name to gather children.”

Peng Ziliang clicked his tongue.

“Besides, you can barely cultivate properly in this wretched place. There isn’t even anywhere worthy of being called a spirit vein. I can’t stand staying here any longer.”

“Senior Brother Peng, you’ve been saying that since your very first month here.”

“...Xiaobai, you’ve gotten much more talkative lately. Have you lost your fear because I no longer beat you like before?”

“My apologies.”

The corner of Wei Wendao’s mouth moved ever so slightly before his face returned to its usual expressionlessness.

“If it is a new pill recipe, it should be enough of an achievement to make up for the mission of securing a disciple with a single spiritual root.”

Han Xiaobai asked,

“Doesn’t our sect already have the Meridian-Opening Pill?”

“Demand for Meridian-Opening Pills is high, and the prices of the spirit plants used as ingredients keep rising. Since this pill recipe has a different name, it must use different spirit plants. The purpose of securing a disciple with a single spiritual root was ultimately to gain promising juniors and strengthen the sect. If this pill recipe can help countless early Qi Refining disciples achieve their breakthroughs, Steward should recognize its value.”

“But are we certain that man really obtained the Barrier-Breaking Pill recipe?”

“After accumulating merit points for so many years, what else would he exchange for at the Retainers Hall besides the Barrier-Breaking Pill recipe? On top of that, after leaving the Retainers Hall, he visited the Earth Fire Cavern for over a month, and afterward I heard he even bought a pill furnace and formation for alchemy from the Formation Court.”

Peng Ziliang gave a faint laugh.

“What a ridiculous guy. What is a Qi Refining rogue cultivator doing learning pill recipes and alchemy...? Is that guy planning to found a cultivation clan himself?”

“Do not mock him. What sect master has never endured hard times like these in the beginning? You two have spent your lives in a great sect, so you do not understand. The difficulties faced by rogue cultivators are beyond imagination. Whatever they do, cultivators of great sects like us, who grew up in good environments, should not dismiss them lightly.”

Peng Ziliang picked his nose.

‘Senior Brother Wei really is ridiculous. Wasn’t he the one born into a good family and raised in comfort without hardship? Yet he talks as though he understands the suffering of rogue cultivators... How much longer is this sermon going to last?’

Wei Wendao looked at Peng Ziliang.

“More importantly, Ziliang. You said you never managed to find that man’s residence?”

“Yes. I followed him three times. Every time, I lost him near the far northwestern edge of Yunze Kingdom.”

“How did he disappear?”

“I wasn’t certain the first two times, but the third time I saw it clearly. While he was crossing a mountainside, his aura suddenly sank underground. It was definitely the Earth Escape Art.”

“He must have a cave abode.”

“That’s what I think too.”

Peng Ziliang took a folded map from inside his robes.

“Here.”

His finger pointed to a section of mountain range northwest of Yunjing.

“There is an area of solid bedrock along the route he always takes. If we surround him there, he won’t be able to escape.”

Wei Wendao slipped a hand into his robes and pulled out a yellow talisman.

“We also have this.”

“A talisman?”

“Yes. A Tier 1 mid-grade Spirit-Tracking Talisman. Even if we lose him, we can use this to track him. Once activated, it can follow the owner of a detected spiritual-power signature for two shichen (about four hours). If he remains within one hundred li (about 39 km) on the surface, it can tell us the direction he fled, and even if he goes underground, it won’t lose him as long as he stays within a depth of one li. With the spiritual power of Qi Refining Stage 3, how deep could he possibly descend using the Earth Escape Art? Eventually, he’ll have to come back up.”

“That certainly makes sense. But isn’t a Tier 1 mid-grade talisman too valuable to waste? I’ll kill him, so why not give me that talisman?”

“Stop talking nonsense and get on.”

Wei Wendao tapped his storage pouch, and light flashed.

Whoosh―

A small blue flying boat appeared in midair.

It was a little over two zhang (about 6.6 m) long.

Several formation inscriptions were carved across the surface of the pointed vessel.

The three men climbed aboard one after another.

Wei Wendao said,

“Ziliang, you steer first. Xiaobai, conserve your spiritual power.”

“Understood.”

Hummm―

The formation inscriptions beneath the flying boat lit up one after another, and in the next instant, it shot northwest, leaving a blue afterglow behind.

Chapter 27

It had been about a day since Lee Hyun left Yunjing.

He was crossing the mountain range in the northwestern part of Yunze Kingdom.

It was a route he had traveled countless times over the past dozen years.

He sped down a mountainside with the Reclining Escape Art before reaching a broad expanse of gray bedrock.

Once he crossed this area, he would be back in mountainous terrain covered in thick soil. Normally, he would have crossed it without a second thought.

'...What is it?'

Lee Hyun sensed something was off.

When he activated the Keen Hearing Art and Ground-Sense Art, even the faint presences of tiny creatures hiding in the cracks between the rocks entered his awareness one after another.

'There are far fewer insects than usual....'

That was when it happened.

Bang!

Tree roots burst from a crack in the bedrock beneath his feet amid a blue-green glow, coiling around Lee Hyun's ankles like snakes.

At the same time, savage waves of spiritual power erupted from three directions.

From directly ahead, a flying sword glowing with an eerie blue light shot toward the back of Lee Hyun's neck.

Clang!

A translucent Spirit Light Shield appeared and knocked the flying sword away.

Crack!

A thin fracture spread across the center of the Spirit Light Shield at the moment of impact.

The blade of the deflected blue flying sword was densely engraved with patterns no larger than grains of millet.

'A magic tool!'

The auras of three concealed figures entered his divine sense.

The middle-aged man in front was at Qi Refining Stage 6, the gaunt man on the right was at Qi Refining Stage 5, and the young man on the left, who had used the Wood Binding Art, was at Qi Refining Stage 3.

The sunlight above his head vanished.

A black square seal more than one zhang (about 3.3 m) across was descending as though it meant to crush Lee Hyun flat.

"Bind him!"

"Now!"

The three Qi Refining cultivators sealed off every direction.

From the front, the flying sword that had been knocked away curved back and twisted toward him. The black seal fell from above, while his ankles remained bound by the tough roots of the Wood Binding Art.

The moment Lee Hyun realized they truly intended to kill him, rage and killing intent awakened within him.

Boom!

The Qi Sphere Barrier burst outward from around Lee Hyun's entire body. The air blasted away in every direction, shattering the roots constricting his ankles. At the same instant, he followed with the Square-Inch Step. Lee Hyun's figure vanished like a ghost.

Rumble!

The black seal smashed down on the exact spot where he had been standing.

"What kind of speed is that...!"

Though startled, the attackers continued their assault.

The gaunt man sent black spikes flying in every direction to cut off his escape, while the young man tore two talismans apart, conjuring a massive curtain of flames and a wall of wind.

The Qi Refining Stage 6 cultivator in front changed his hand seal, splitting the blue flying sword into three phantom blades that targeted Lee Hyun's vital acupoints.

In response, a dazzling white orb of light bloomed above Lee Hyun's palm, and the tremendous wave of spiritual power made all three men blanch.

"Dodge!"

Booooom!

The fireball Lee Hyun hurled collided with the curtain of flames ahead, triggering a massive explosion. The curtain of flames and wall of wind collapsed from within, while the flying sword, spikes, and black seal were swept up by the blast and flung in every direction.

Flash!

The entire bedrock field was bathed in white light, and the tempest slammed into the three cultivators as though swallowing them whole.

Boom!

The gaunt man hurriedly pulled the black seal back to block the blast, but the violent impact sent him skidding more than ten chi (over 3.3 m) backward, both feet scraping across the bedrock. The young man, wrapped in a golden barrier, was hurled into the air and smashed into a boulder.

A plain iron sword slid from the sheath at Lee Hyun's waist as he stood amid the smoke.

Shrring–

A terrifying wave of spiritual power surged from the iron sword, and Spirit Aura imbued with an uncanny radiance sprang into existence.

The middle-aged man's pupils contracted sharply.

"Don't let him get close!"

Thump.

The moment Lee Hyun used the Square-Inch Step, his charging figure abruptly veered diagonally. The gaunt man hurriedly sent the black seal and spikes to block his path, but Lee Hyun slipped through the opening before the two attacks could converge.

By the time the gaunt man's eyes widened in disbelief, Lee Hyun had already reached the young man, who was protected behind layers of talismans and a bronze shield.

"Eek!"

The young man screamed as he wrapped himself in two layers of golden barriers and raised the bronze shield as a barricade.

But Lee Hyun's sword did not hesitate.

Flash!

Boom!

The first barrier tore apart helplessly, and even the second cracked. Immediately afterward, the Spirit Aura wrapped around the iron sword concentrated at a single point at its tip. Rather than smashing through the bronze shield head-on, the sword light of One Ultimate, Six Swords skimmed past its edge and traced a fleeting arc.

Slash!

"Aaaagh!"

The young man's left arm was severed at the shoulder, spraying blood through the air. The arm still clutching a talisman tumbled across the ground, and a hole opened in the trio's once-solid formation.

"Xiaobai! You bastard...!"

The gaunt man roared in fury as he dropped the black seal over Lee Hyun's head and thrust his spikes forward. The middle-aged man also condensed his blue flying sword and slashed toward the back of Lee Hyun's neck.

But Lee Hyun did not even look back as he stirred his mental intent.

Hum! Hum! Hum!

Holding nothing back with his Primordial True Qi, twelve Spirit Light Shields bloomed into existence at once. Three layers of shields precisely interposed themselves in front of the flying sword, spikes, and seal, while the remaining Spirit Light Shields rapidly revolved around Lee Hyun to cover every opening. The three magic tools hammered against the Spirit Light Shields one after another, yet not a single shield shattered.

'That's a Spirit Light Shield?'

Peng Ziliang felt as though he had been bewitched. Defensive techniques formed from condensed spiritual power were normally weaker than physical magic tools. Yet the Spirit Light Shields before him were withstanding even mid-grade magic tools without the slightest difficulty.

The toughness of the Spirit Light Shields created by this Qi Refining rogue cultivator was simply unbelievable.

Before his shock could fade, an iron nail shot from Lee Hyun's sleeve. It was the Spirit-Breaking Nail Wang Shao had given him long ago.

Launched with the Divine Finger-Flick Art, the Spirit-Breaking Nail carried an enormous amount of spiritual power as it struck Peng Ziliang's defensive enchanted robe head-on.

Craack!

The Spirit-Breaking Nail pierced through the enchanted robe's restriction and buried itself deep in his shoulder. Immediately afterward, cracks spread across the nail as it failed to withstand the immense Primordial True Qi.

Crackle!

The Spirit-Breaking Nail shattered outright, lodging fragments deep inside his shoulder.

'How can trash that's not even as good as a low-grade magic tool pierce my enchanted robe?'

While he staggered and struggled to steady himself, Lee Hyun closed the distance in an instant.

'No...'

Schk.

Sword light pierced through Peng Ziliang's forehead. He collapsed with his eyes rolling back, unable even to scream.

"Senior Brother Peng!"

Han Xiaobai screamed while clutching the shoulder that was pouring blood.

The situation had reversed in the blink of an eye. In only a few breaths, one man had lost an arm and another had become a corpse.

Wei Wendao's face turned deathly pale.

'Is this man truly a Qi Refining Stage 3 rogue cultivator?'

Without hesitation, Wei Wendao bit the tip of his tongue and spat crimson essence blood onto the blue flying sword.

Sizzle–

The blood-dyed flying sword swelled dramatically, radiating an ominous divine radiance.

Whoosh!

The flying sword screamed through the air toward Lee Hyun's chest. Razor-sharp sword qi shredded the surrounding bedrock.

But Lee Hyun remained calm.

Hum! Hum!

As though responding to Lee Hyun's mental intent, layers of Spirit Light Shields filled the air.

The blood-red flying sword pierced through three Spirit Light Shields in succession.

Crack! Craaack!

But there was no end to the shields behind them. Each time the flying sword pierced one, a new Spirit Light Shield immediately appeared to block its path.

Clatter.

At last, the flying sword lost its strength and fell to the ground.

"Impossible...."

Wei Wendao could not finish speaking as he coughed up blood.

Seeing the mid-grade magic tool he had empowered with his own essence blood stopped so completely by mere Spirit Light Shields made Wei Wendao feel as though all his cultivation until now had been rendered meaningless.

Boom!

Lee Hyun opened his palm, and a massive wave of force from the Qi Sphere Barrier slammed into Wei Wendao and Han Xiaobai at the same time. Both men screamed as they rolled across the ground.

Realizing there was no longer any chance of victory, Wei Wendao tapped his storage pouch and took out a blue flying boat.

Whoosh–

Wei Wendao tried to launch the flying boat and soar into the air, but Lee Hyun had already drawn the Earth Shovel Sword and leaped skyward.

Slash! Crack!

The sword light of the Azure Steel Sword Art came crashing down, shattering the side of the flying boat. The vessel spun like it was screaming and plummeted toward the ground.

Boom!

Wei Wendao was thrown from the flying boat and landed on his knees atop the bedrock.

Before he could even regain his posture, four streaks of Lee Hyun's Yang Metal Art precisely pierced the acupoints of his four limbs.

Schk! Schk-sch-sch!

"Ugh!"

Strength drained from Wei Wendao's limbs, and he collapsed to the ground.

...

Only the faint sound of fine stone grit rolling down the mountainside could be heard.

Lee Hyun silently looked down at the three fallen men.

The gaunt man was dead. The middle-aged man was coughing blood with all four limbs sealed, while the young man trembled in terror after losing his left arm.

The frightened young man suddenly seemed to come to his senses. He slammed his head against the ground and begged.

"We were wrong! Please spare our lives!"

Lee Hyun stared at him without a word.

"We're pitiful rogue cultivators too! We have no sect and wander from place to place cultivating. That fellow Daoist over there has a wife and children, and I have an elderly mother back home. We will never speak a word of what happened today."

"......."

"Take our storage pouches and magic tools, all of them. We don't need anything. Please...."

The young man's voice trembled miserably.

"Before that, let me ask you one thing. Why did you attack me?"

"Th-the pill recipe. We thought you obtained the Barrier-Breaking Pill recipe from the Fengtian Bureau... and we became greedy."

"How did you know that?"

"We knew you'd been saving merit points for a long time, and we saw you visiting the Earth Fire Cavern for more than a month after leaving the Retainers Hall. That's truly all!"

Lee Hyun silently stared at him.

The Barrier-Breaking Pill recipe was certainly something Qi Refining rogue cultivators would covet.

Now that the battle was over, the killing intent that had been boiling inside him moments ago was gradually subsiding.

If they truly were rogue cultivators without anyone behind them, he could consider taking their belongings and driving them far away.

By the time he emerged from hiding in his tunnel again, they would probably have died of old age anyway.

He was not afraid of the grudges of a few Qi Refining rogue cultivators. The world was too vast. Finding him would be difficult enough, never mind taking revenge.

Lee Hyun pondered briefly and was just about to speak.

Then a blue emblem caught the edge of his vision.

'Hm?'

The dead gaunt man's robe had been torn apart by the explosion, revealing an embroidered emblem on the inside.

A blue cloud.

Lee Hyun's gaze stopped.

'That....'

He had seen it somewhere before.

As he searched his memory, a scene from several hundred years ago surfaced in his mind.

Back when he had still been living as a woodcutter in White Wood Village in western Great Yan Kingdom, before entering the immortal path, he had once seen an Immortal's ship flying through the sky.

A blue cloud had been painted on its white sail, and the villagers had all rushed to bow, saying that the Immortal Masters of the Azure Cloud Sect had arrived.

"......."

'The Azure Cloud Sect?'

Lee Hyun checked the emblem once more, then looked at the young man and asked indifferently,

"You said you were rogue cultivators?"

"That's right! The three of us have traveled together for many years."

Lee Hyun lightly nodded.

"Strange. Your techniques looked quite familiar, so I thought you might be disciples of the Azure Cloud Sect. Long ago, a cultivator from the Azure Cloud Sect did me a great favor. If you were his fellow disciples, I might have spared you out of regard for that connection. But if you're not, I suppose there's no reason for me to do so."

The young man's eyes widened.

"Wait! We really are disciples of the Azure Cloud Sect!"

"Xiaobai!"

The middle-aged man shouted as he coughed blood.

"You idiot...!"

He tried to force his injured body upright, only to collapse again.

"What nonsense are you spouting?! How dare you impersonate cultivators of the Azure Cloud Sect just to bluff! We're rogue cultivators!"

"Ah......."

The face of the young man called Xiaobai turned deathly pale. Only then did he realize what he had said.

The middle-aged man squeezed his eyes shut. It was already too late.

Lee Hyun remained silent for a long while.

If they had truly been rogue cultivators, he might have made a different choice. Killing people felt horrible, so he wanted to avoid it whenever possible.

But if they were disciples of a cultivation sect, the situation was completely different.

He knew almost nothing about the Azure Cloud Sect.

But it was a sect that generously supplied even its Qi Refining disciples with good magic tools and talismans, and had sent people all the way to the remote White Wood Village in Great Yan Kingdom several hundred years ago to recruit disciples. And now, it seemed their disciples were active in Yunze Kingdom as well.

At the very least, it was not a force he could handle.

Which meant that, as nothing more than a Qi Refining Stage 3 rogue cultivator, he had now killed one disciple of a great sect and seriously wounded two others.

What if he let the remaining two go?

"......."

Great sects of the cultivation world placed tremendous importance on face. Even if the two surviving disciples did not seek revenge themselves, there was no chance the Azure Cloud Sect would simply let the matter go.

Now that things had come to this, he had to kill the two in front of him as well. Only by leaving no witnesses would he have even a chance of surviving.

"F-fellow Daoist."

The young man spoke in a trembling voice.

"It can't be helped. You brought this upon yourselves."

"What?"

Schk.

A small hole appeared in the young man's forehead. The light slowly faded from his wide-open eyes.

Thud.

Lee Hyun looked at the middle-aged man last. He seemed to understand that there was no point in saying anything.

The man closed his eyes without another word.

"Kill me."

Schk.

The man's body went limp.

Lee Hyun let out a short breath.

'I need to clean up the traces first.'

...

Lee Hyun used several detection arts to inspect the surroundings. He sensed no mortals or other cultivators nearby.

He first used the Soil-Turning Art and the Earth Shovel Sword's Soil-Softening Art to conceal the traces of battle. After softening and collapsing several cracked sections of bedrock, most of the rocks scorched by the Fireball Art, the marks left by the flying sword, the footprints, and the bloodstains disappeared beneath the fallen rubble.

Before long, the bedrock field looked less like a place where cultivators had fought and more like the site of a small landslide.

Lee Hyun removed everything the corpses carried, including their storage pouches and identity tokens, then gathered all the magic tools and other items scattered nearby into one place.

Afterward, he temporarily hid the bodies beneath rocks and entered the ground using the Earth Escape Art. When he spread the Ground-Sense Art through the surrounding strata, he detected several natural fissures and small caverns running between the deeper layers of bedrock.

He selected three deep fissures that were not connected to underground waterways.

Lee Hyun returned to the surface, dragged the bodies underground one by one, shoved each into a different fissure, then collapsed the entrances.

Rumble–

He did not believe he had erased every trace perfectly.

But this was the most he could do with his current abilities.

Now it was time to sort through the belongings.

...

Lee Hyun found a natural cavern far from the battle site and entered it.

He spread a cloth across the floor, then emptied the three men's storage pouches one after another.

First, he set aside the three Fengtian Bureau external retainer badges he had removed from their bodies.

Then came three white jade tokens. A blue cloud was engraved on the front of each, while a name was written on the back.

Wei Wendao.

Peng Ziliang.

Han Xiaobai.

"As expected...."

They certainly appeared to be identity tokens of the Azure Cloud Sect.

He pushed the identity tokens aside.

Next came the magic tools.

Wei Wendao's blue flying sword and the half-destroyed flying boat.

Peng Ziliang's black square seal and three spikes.

Han Xiaobai's bronze shield.

There were also several magic tools they had not used in battle, including a black dagger and several thin, needle-shaped implements.

Lee Hyun first picked up the blue flying sword and examined it closely.

"This is... wood."

During the fight, he had assumed it was made of metal because of its weighty power.

Looking closely, he saw that the entire blade had been carved from a spirit tree. Tiny spirit inscriptions forming its restrictions covered every inch of the surface.

It was the finest magic tool he had ever seen.

'It's a shame, but....'

Lee Hyun let go of his attachment.

He had no idea what kinds of restrictions were embedded in that sword.

There was no way to know whether it could alert his sect to its location after its owner's death, whether someone from the sect could sense the sword's position through a particular hand seal, or whether someone had already placed an unseen mark on it without his knowledge.

There was no guarantee the other magic tools were safe either.

'I should discard all the magic tools.'

No matter how expensive they were, they could not be worth more than his life.

He also pushed two gray beads, a black bronze plaque, and an enchanted robe bearing the Azure Cloud Sect's cloud emblem into the pile of dangerous items, along with anything else whose identity or function he could not determine.

On the other hand, items that could be obtained anywhere and were difficult to trace to a specific source could be kept.

First, the low-grade spirit stones.

"One, two...."

After a long while, Lee Hyun's lips curved slightly upward as he set down the last spirit stone.

"Three hundred and ninety."

Adding the twelve he already had gave him a total of four hundred and two.

'I won't have to worry about spirit stones for a while.'

Next came the talismans.

The three men had carried dozens of unused talismans. Among them was a single yellow talisman with denser spiritual qi and more intricate patterns than the others.

Talismans of which they had several copies were likely meant for common purposes, so he kept all of those.

Conversely, he unhesitatingly pushed any talisman of which there was only one, or which looked particularly unusual, into the dangerous pile.

He kept every bottle containing pills.

Some of the bottles had labels, while the contents of others were unknown, but since they were meant to be consumed by cultivators, they seemed unlikely to contain any tracking function.

Finally, he inspected the storage pouches.

The three men had possessed five in total.

After emptying them completely, he examined each one with the Aura-Reading Art. They were ordinary storage pouches commonly seen everywhere, with no sect markings either outside or within.

At least within the limits of Lee Hyun's current knowledge, there was nothing unusual about them.

He decided to keep the empty storage pouches.

Together with the two he already owned, he now had seven storage pouches in total.

There were also several books and documents.

An illustrated guide to demon beasts.

A book on basic talisman-crafting art.

Instructions for using several techniques.

Records the three men had kept during their cultivation.

There were also several jade slips, but those made him somewhat uneasy.

He would need to insert his divine sense to inspect the jade slips, and the divine sense of a Qi Refining Stage 3 cultivator was too weak to properly respond if any sort of trap had been placed inside.

'I should discard these too.'

He kept the paper books, since he could skim through them normally.

Among them, one item made Lee Hyun's hand pause.

Rustle.

A vast map of Kun Kingdom and the surrounding regions unfolded before him.

The borders of mortal nations, major cities, large mountain ranges, and rivers were all roughly marked.

And in the northern part of the map.

At the northeastern edge of Great Yan Kingdom, three blue characters were written.

Azure Cloud Sect.

'About thirty-six thousand li (about 14,100 km) from here. It's not close, but it still makes me uneasy....'

...

That night.

Lee Hyun buried the items he had deemed dangerous in multiple locations spread across several dozen li.

He did not keep the blue flying sword, black seal, half-destroyed flying boat, Azure Cloud Sect identity tokens, Fengtian Bureau retainer badges, enchanted robe, unidentified jade slips, and unusual talismans together in one place. Some he buried deep after using the Soil-Softening Art to soften the bedrock, then collapsed the surrounding stone over them.

Even after disposing of the final item, he did not immediately return to the surface.

He traveled underground for a long while with the Earth Escape Art until he had put enough distance behind him, only then emerging in the mountains. Even afterward, whenever the terrain seemed unfavorable or he sensed someone's presence, he changed direction or hid underground again.

In this way, he did everything he could to break his trail as he headed toward Tunnel No. 1.

...

One day later.

Tunnel No. 1.

Rustle–

Lee Hyun's head emerged from the soil.

"Phew...."

Just as his tension began to ease, he heard a familiar buzzing of wings.

Bzzzz–

Several fuzzbees flew over from the direction of the spirit field.

The moment they spotted Lee Hyun, they flew straight over his head as though delighted to see him.

Chirp.

The moment one landed on his shoulder, it pooped.

The small white lump, blocked by the Qi Sphere Barrier, slid down the transparent barrier and fell to the ground.

Tap.

"......."

Normally, Lee Hyun would have said something about it pooping on him yet again, but this time he did not even look at the fellow.

He stood in the center of the cultivation chamber without moving for a long time.

'I've done almost everything I can....'

But the unease in the corner of his mind refused to disappear.

'What if there's a method I don't know about?'

The techniques he knew were only a tiny fraction of those that existed throughout the cultivation world. It would not be strange if there were secret arts capable of tracking a culprit through nothing more than a corpse or blood.

And there was something else that bothered him even more.

Yesterday's ambush had not been a coincidence.

The three men had known the route he frequently used.

They had taken position in the bedrock field ahead of time and chosen a spot where escape would be difficult.

'They couldn't have seen me only once or twice.'

They might have watched him for days, perhaps even far longer.

If so, there was a possibility they had left traces behind in the Fengtian Bureau as well.

Three Azure Cloud Sect cultivators had suddenly vanished in Yunze Kingdom.

Moreover, all three had been External Retainers of the Fengtian Bureau. Someone around them was bound to remember their final movements.

If an investigation began, the name of a Retainer called Li Dongyi, who had left Yunjing around the same time, might surface as well.

If they dug deeper, they might even discover that for more than a dozen years, he had repeatedly taken leave and traveled in the same general direction.

If that happened, even if they did not know the exact location of Tunnel No. 1, they could narrow down the search area considerably.

"......."

Tunnel No. 1, which had felt familiar and safe until just recently, now looked entirely different.

Lee Hyun closed his eyes for a moment, then opened them again.

There was no longer any reason to hesitate.

"Let's move."

Chapter 28

Once he had made his decision, there was no reason to delay.

Lee Hyun first laid seven storage pouches out on the floor.

The sizes of their internal spaces varied.

The smallest was only about the size of a single room, while the one he had newly bought at Cuiyun Market and the storage pouch Wei Wendao had used were spacious enough to hold an entire storeroom.

‘Perfect. I can put the three Stone Honey Peach trees in the largest one.’

Lee Hyun first gathered the items already inside the storage pouches into one place. Spirit stones, talismans, pill bottles, books, records of techniques and cultivation arts, the formation stones of the Nine-Fire Flame-Storing Formation and the bronze pill furnace, the Earth Shovel Sword, clothing, and food.

Then Lee Hyun entered Spirit Field No. 1-1.

‘I should be able to move them while they’re still alive... right?’

Spirit beasts and spirit insects required dedicated containers such as spirit-beast pouches and spirit-insect pouches, but plants were different.

Even when he had worked with spirit plants at Qinghe Valley, he had often transported them in storage pouches.

The spirit plants he had used to establish the spirit fields here in the first place had been obtained from Qinghe Valley and brought over in storage pouches, so there was no doubt that putting spirit plants inside one would not kill them.

The problem was how long they could be stored.

Lee Hyun had seen Qinghe Rice and Hunger-Warding Pills that had been kept in storage pouches for many years lose a considerable amount of their spiritual qi.

Time inside a storage pouch flowed far more slowly than outside, almost as though it had stopped, but it was not completely frozen.

That was why cultivators transporting precious spirit plants used jade boxes containing spirit soil and spirit liquid suited to the plants’ attributes, then placed restrictions on them and even affixed talismans to keep their medicinal potency from leaking away.

But Lee Hyun had no specialized jade boxes, and there were far too many spirit plants to move.

‘I’ll take as much of the roots and surrounding soil as possible, then build Tunnel No. 2 quickly and transplant them. That should prevent any serious problems.’

Lee Hyun went through Spirit Fields No. 1-1 to No. 1-5 in order and began placing the spirit plants into storage pouches.

Whenever he spotted a fuzzbee along the way, he put it into the spirit-insect pouch.

The more he worked, the more practiced he became.

Lee Hyun operated the Ground-Sense Art and Aura-Reading Art simultaneously to examine the directions in which the spirit plants’ roots had spread, then used the Soil-Turning Art to separate the earth surrounding several plants at once into a huge clod.

Rrrrumble―

Whenever a clod more than one zhang (about 3.3 m) across slowly rose from the ground with dozens of spirit plants embedded in it, Lee Hyun opened a storage pouch.

Light spread out, and the enormous clod vanished without a trace.

“Good.”

Lee Hyun repeated the same process.

...

Spirit Field No. 1-6.

Lee Hyun first harvested the ripe lotus seeds separately.

Then he put not only the Yin Water Lotus flowers and leaves, but also the mud tangled with their rhizomes and even part of the pond created with the Spirit Rain Art into a storage pouch.

...

Spirit Field No. 1-7.

The three Stone Honey Peach trees had spread broadly sideways along the low ceiling.

Lee Hyun harvested only the fully ripened fruit, leaving the immature fruit on the branches.

Afterward, he first pruned the branches that had grown long enough to interfere with moving them. Since the cut branches could later be used for propagation by cuttings, he wrapped the cut ends in damp cloth and bundled them separately.

...

A long while later.

Three enormous clods containing the trees’ roots and surrounding soil lay in the middle of the spirit field.

Lee Hyun opened his largest storage pouch, enveloped the Stone Honey Peach trees in light one by one, and placed them inside in sequence.

“Whew... done. Now you’re the only ones left.”

Bzzzz―

Perhaps because of all the commotion around them, the remaining fuzzbees darted frantically around Lee Hyun.

Lee Hyun took out the spirit-insect pouch and collected every last one.

Then he packed up the facilities and tools.

He gathered the paper, lumber, hardware, and tools piled in the storeroom, then dismantled and packed away the bronze pipes, water tank, and axle of the automatic irrigation device. He also took every record he had made while inspecting the spirit fields, the wooden boards engraved with his handmade status screens, and the household items he had used for so long, leaving nothing behind.

...

The next day.

All traces of long habitation and every man-made object had vanished from Tunnel No. 1, leaving it like an empty shell.

Lee Hyun used various detection methods as he made a complete circuit of the tunnel, checking for anything he might have left behind, then either collected or erased everything he found.

Finally, he returned to the space he had used as his living quarters.

He lay comfortably for a moment in the place where he had always slept.

The cold sensation of the ground seeped into his back.

If he closed his eyes, he felt as though he might hear water dripping into the reservoir, leaves rustling, and the hum of fuzzbee wings.

“.......”

Lee Hyun sat up.

“I’ll just make Tunnel No. 2 even better.”

As Lee Hyun formed a hand seal with both hands, the Soil-Turning Art spread throughout the entire tunnel.

Rrrrrumble―

Spaces that had existed for hundreds of years filled with stone and earth. The air shafts and passageways were sealed one after another.

Once even the final cavern had been completely buried, the place looked like a natural layer of earth where nothing had ever existed, even when examined with the Ground-Sense Art.

“Farewell.”

Twenty days later.

A place 65,000 li (about 25,480 km) south of Tunnel No. 1 in a straight line.

A faint salty scent mingled with the wind.

Rustle.

Lee Hyun’s body slowly came to a halt as he slid down the mountainside.

He stood up, sat on a rock, and looked south.

A blue horizon stretched before him.

“The sea.”

It was the first time since coming to this world that he had seen a proper ocean.
