He made one final circuit of the entire tunnel, checking the locations of the bedrock supporting the major stone chambers and passageways.

He used the Soil-Turning Art to fill the side passages and smaller stone chambers with earth first.

Then he drew the Mountain-Suppressing Sword and cut through the bedrock supporting the tunnel.

Rrrrrrumble―

Having lost their support, the ceilings and walls collapsed one after another from the inside outward.

The spaces that had held the spirit fields, the storeroom, the cultivation chamber, the training cavern, and the rest all caved in.

Finally, the wall engraved with the words 「Tunnel No. 2」 tilted and disappeared beneath the falling rocks.

BOOOOM―

Once the vibrations subsided, even the Ground-Sense Art could no longer detect any regularly shaped empty spaces.

Lee Hyun descended to a depth greater than twenty li, then began moving north.

...

One month later.

Lee Hyun stopped while traveling underground.

“Hm?”

He caught a drop of water seeping between the rocks on his fingertip and touched it to his tongue.

It was salty.

“Am I near the coast already?”

He had seen the same thing before. Whenever he approached the coast, seawater would seep into underground aquifers and mix salt into the water.

Lee Hyun slowly ascended.

Ten li underground.

Three li underground.

At last, the moment he emerged through a secluded gap between the rocks, the familiar salty sea breeze brushed against his face.

A blue sea stretched before him.

This was not the southern coast of the Lan Kingdom bordering the Nanming Sea, but the northern coast of the Haiwu Kingdom, located in the northern part of the Lan Kingdom.

The thirty-thousand-li strait he had crossed more than five hundred years ago when traveling from Haimen City to Qingjin Port lay before him. This time, he would cross the same route in the opposite direction.

...

The next day.

Qingjin Port, Haiwu Kingdom.

Several hundred years had passed, but the port’s name had not changed.

Lee Hyun altered his appearance to resemble an ordinary traveling peddler in his mid-forties.

He searched for a ship heading across the strait to Haimen City in the Hailing Kingdom.

“Does this ship go to Haimen City?”

“Yes. The Canghai, which departs the morning after tomorrow, sails there directly. If the winds are favorable, it should arrive in around fifty days.”

...

Two days later.

Boom―

The beat of a drum announcing departure echoed across the harbor.

The ropes were cast off, and the folded sails were unfurled one after another.

Whump! Whump!

Catching the wind, the Canghai departed Qingjin Port.

...

During the voyage, Lee Hyun occasionally walked along the deck, watching the sailors, merchants, and children running about. In his cabin, he read the popular novels he had bought at Qingjin Port.

...

The night of the twentieth day.

The wind was calm.

Lee Hyun lay on the sparsely occupied stern deck and gazed up at the night sky.

Countless stars hung above him.

Each time the sea slowly swelled, the starlight reflected on the surface stretched into long streaks before breaking apart. Whenever the ship rode over a wave, the sky and sea seemed to tilt together.

It was a sight he could never see underground.

Lee Hyun lay still with his hands clasped behind his head.

The night sky looked almost no different from what he had seen while crossing this same sea more than five hundred years ago.

Cultivation sects rose and fell, and the borders of mortal kingdoms shifted, yet the starlight shimmered upon the sea as though none of it had anything to do with them.

“Not bad.”

...

The forty-seventh day after departure.

A vast port city came into view along the coastline.

Bwoooom―

“It’s Haimen City!”

The passengers began gathering their belongings.

...

Haimen City, at the southern tip of the Hailing Kingdom.

Lee Hyun disembarked and passed through customs.

Haimen City had grown larger than he remembered.

He immediately headed north.

The Lan Kingdom might have been drawn into the war against forces from beyond the Nanming Sea. But the Lan Kingdom covered a vast territory, and he had already crossed the sea, so there was no need to hurry.

He began leisurely observing the world as he traveled roughly a thousand li north each day.

...

Five days later.

A small county seat in northern Hailing Kingdom.

Lee Hyun entered an inn along the main road, partly to look around and see how the world had changed.

“What would you like?”

“A pot of tea and a bottle of wine.”

“Would you like anything to eat?”

“No.”

The attendant gave Lee Hyun a slightly strange look but asked no further questions.

A short while later, warm tea and a bottle of clear grain wine were placed on the table.

Lee Hyun drank a cup of tea, then poured himself a cup of wine. The sweetness of the grain wine mingled with the lingering bitterness of the tea in his mouth.

The people around him occasionally glanced at the man who had ordered no food and was alternating between tea and wine.

Just then, the inn door opened.

Creak―

Five martial artists carrying swords and sabers entered.

All five had a solid, disciplined bearing.

The middle-aged man in front had a long scar across his temple, while the four younger martial artists following him moved with measured strides and controlled breathing.

Lee Hyun paid them little attention and raised his teacup again.

At that moment, the spirit-insect pouch at his waist trembled ever so slightly.

Bzz.

The fuzzbees inside suddenly grew restless.

‘What’s gotten into them?’

Lee Hyun placed a hand on the spirit-insect pouch.

They were reacting much as they did when they discovered spirit insects or eggs inside the hunting tunnel.

It was almost as though they regarded the martial artists in front of him as prey.

‘Are they trying to eat people!? You terrifying little things... So you’ve finally revealed your true nature! I suppose bumblebees from the cultivation world really are different.’

Until now, the fuzzbees had never shown interest in anything other than spirit insects.

As he calmed them with his mental intent, the middle-aged martial artist in front suddenly stopped.

“...?”

He abruptly clutched his lower abdomen.

“Senior Brother, what’s wrong?”

“I don’t know. I suddenly have chills.”

The martial artists behind him also looked around.

“I feel strange too.”

“Doesn’t it feel as though someone is watching us?”

Their gazes swept across the inn and briefly stopped at Lee Hyun’s table.

Lee Hyun was merely drinking tea.

Even so, an inexplicable unease appeared on the martial artists’ faces.

The middle-aged martial artist spoke in a low voice.

“Let’s go somewhere else.”

“But―”

“Now.”

The five men left the inn almost as soon as they had entered.

Lee Hyun looked back and forth between the closing door and his spirit-insect pouch.

‘What was that?’

...

Two days later.

Lee Hyun was following the highway north through the Hailing Kingdom when he stopped.

Beside the road stood an enormous boundary stele three times the height of a man.

Golden characters had been carved deep into the surface of the black stone.

「Qianyang Kingdom, Nanmen Pass」

Beyond it, banners emblazoned with black suns fluttered atop the city walls.

“Qianyang Kingdom?”

Lee Hyun pulled an old map from inside his robe.

According to the route he remembered, he should have had to cross two more mortal kingdoms after leaving the Hailing Kingdom before reaching the Qianyang Kingdom.

Yet the border of the Qianyang Kingdom stood directly before him.

‘Did I take a wrong turn?’

But when he compared his position against the sun, the mountain ranges, and the nearby rivers, his direction was correct.

An old man selling tea near the boundary stele glanced at Lee Hyun’s worn map and burst out laughing.

“Pwahaha! Who sold you that map? Looks like you got swindled. Just how old is that thing?”

“Did the Qianyang Kingdom always extend this far south?”

“This far? It’s been more than two hundred years since this became Qianyang territory.”

“What happened to the two kingdoms that used to lie between here and there?”

“One lost a war, and the other opened its gates willingly. They’re both provinces of Qianyang now.”

“It seems the Qianyang Kingdom has grown considerably.”

The old man gave a disbelieving chuckle.

“Just how long ago are you talking about?”

Lee Hyun looked at the broad highway stretching beyond the boundary stele. He knew the Qianyang Kingdom was a great nation of the martial path that had been pressing the Yunze Kingdom to the north, but he had never imagined it had annexed two kingdoms to the south as well.

...

An inn near Nanmen Pass.

Lee Hyun spread his newly purchased map and a book titled 《Travelogue of the Northern Kun and Cang Regions》 across the table.

Far greater changes than he had expected had taken place in this region over the past several hundred years.

Chapter 41

The beginning of that change could be traced back to a martial artist born in Qianyang Kingdom roughly three hundred years ago.

Qianyang Divine Demon.

Though he was a mortal without a spiritual root, he reached the Profound Realm before the age of thirty, then continued advancing into a realm that no one had even been able to name.

In the end, he displayed the terrifying might to kill a Golden Core cultivator of Kun Kingdom!

A grandmaster of the martial path from the mundane world killed a Golden Core cultivator?

The news shook the cultivation worlds of Kun Kingdom and Cang Kingdom.

Even Nascent Soul cultivators from the Biluo Sect and Danxiao Sect, the great sects of Kun Kingdom, stepped forward to punish Qianyang Kingdom.

However, Wangu Sect, a great sect of southern Cang Kingdom with Nascent Soul cultivators and a reputation for spirit insects and gu arts, suddenly intervened.

No one knew what agreement had been reached among the Nascent Soul cultivators. All that was known was that afterward, the Biluo Sect and Danxiao Sect did not attack Qianyang Kingdom, while Wangu Sect likewise made no move northward.

Many speculated that the royal family of Qianyang Kingdom had formed close ties with Wangu Sect. There were even rumors that Qianyang Divine Demon had only been able to grow so powerful because of some secret inheritance or assistance from Wangu Sect.

In any case, Qianyang Kingdom rapidly expanded its territory.

To the south, it conquered two mortal kingdoms belonging to Cang Kingdom. To the north, it swallowed Yunze Kingdom and several nearby minor kingdoms belonging to Kun Kingdom.

Present-day Qianyang Kingdom had become a peculiar nation with vast territory spanning two Tier 4 cultivation nations, Kun Kingdom and Cang Kingdom.

It possessed power that made it difficult to call it a mere mundane kingdom.

Some cultivators even joked that Qianyang Kingdom ought to be regarded as an independent Tier 3 martial nation wedged between two Tier 4 cultivation nations.

Still, the prevailing belief was that no matter how strong Qianyang Divine Demon might be, he was no match for a Nascent Soul cultivator. For that reason, many regarded him as a powerhouse comparable to late Golden Core.

However, Qianyang Divine Demon had last appeared before the public several decades ago. Rumors circulated that he had already died and the royal family was concealing the truth, while others claimed he had entered secluded cultivation in hopes of glimpsing an even higher realm.

"Wait, Yunze Kingdom was annexed?"

Lee Hyun's gaze lingered on the northern part of the map.

The name Yunze Kingdom was nowhere to be found. In its place lay the vast territory of Qianyang Kingdom.

"So that's how it turned out...."

Lee Hyun briefly recalled his days in Yunze Kingdom.

"Well, by the time Qianyang Divine Demon was born, everyone I knew would already have been long dead. It doesn't mean much to me now."

His meeting with Liu Zhenghui, who had been the king of Yunze Kingdom, and the ambush a few days later by Wei Wendao, Peng Ziliang, and Han Xiaobai of the Azure Cloud Sect had all happened five hundred and forty years ago.

Even so, seeing the kingdom's very name erased from the map left him with a strange feeling.

...

Lee Hyun was more interested in how Qianyang Divine Demon and his disciples had transcended their limits and grown so powerful than in Qianyang Kingdom's expansion.

For several days, he visited bookstores, martial arts schools, and inns throughout Nanmen Pass, gathering information on Qianyang Kingdom's new martial path.

Books published in Qianyang Kingdom praised the New Martial Path, while books brought over from Kun Kingdom denounced it as a heretical path that planted insects inside human bodies.

Lee Hyun read accounts written from opposing perspectives and first extracted only the points on which both sides agreed.

The New Martial Path of present-day Qianyang Kingdom had split into several branches, but the mainstream among them was the Symbiotic Gu Path.

People shortened the name to the Gu Path, and martial artists who followed it were called gu warriors.

At the heart of the Gu Path was a symbiotic spirit insect known as the Life-Bound Gu.

「A suitable Life-Bound Gu larva is implanted into a martial artist's dantian, after which a special internal cultivation method and medicinal baths are used to link the life force of the human and the Life-Bound Gu into a single cycle.」

Unlike mortals, the Life-Bound Gu, as a spirit insect, could absorb heaven-and-earth spiritual qi!

The host mixed the spiritual qi absorbed and initially refined by the Life-Bound Gu with their own blood qi. The power produced in this way was known as Gu Origin True Qi.

Thanks to this, even mortals without spiritual roots could circulate Gu Origin True Qi, a type of spiritual power, through their meridians and incorporate it into martial arts.

In other words, the Life-Bound Gu functioned as both a living spiritual root and a dantian.

As the Life-Bound Gu grew, the host's lifespan increased along with it. The extent depended on the species and realm of the spirit insect, but it was hardly unusual for a powerful gu warrior to live for several hundred years. That was also why rumors that Qianyang Divine Demon was still alive never ceased.

The nature of Gu Origin True Qi also differed depending on the type of Life-Bound Gu.

Gu warriors who housed certain spirit insects possessed exceptionally strong body-protecting spirit light, while those bonded with venomous insects wielded poisonous spiritual power. Spirit insects with keen senses could even enhance their hosts' ability to detect danger.

There were also records of gu warriors whose wounds sprouted fine insect threads instead of bleeding, the threads stitching their flesh back together. How much of that was true and how much was exaggerated remained unclear.

No one knew how many varieties of Life-Bound Gu existed in total, and there were even rumors that their number continued to grow.

Qianyang Divine Demon himself was also known to be a gu warrior who carried a Life-Bound Gu.

However, records disagreed on who had first devised the method. One account claimed Qianyang Divine Demon had learned it from an unnamed eccentric in his youth, while another said a physician of the royal family had discovered the secret method in an ancient tomb.

The most widespread suspicion was that Wangu Sect had created the Gu Path while experimenting with spirit-insect implantation on Qianyang Kingdom's martial artists. Some even claimed that Qianyang Kingdom itself was a massive bulwark in the mundane world deliberately raised by Wangu Sect to test the possibilities of the Gu Path and expand its influence toward Kun Kingdom.

From what Lee Hyun had read so far, the Life-Bound Gu seemed capable of overturning the order of the cultivation world. After all, it allowed even mortals without spiritual roots to gain the power to fight cultivators.

But the reality was somewhat different.

The Life-Bound Gu merely substituted for the role of a spiritual root. Naturally, it could not produce spiritual qi on its own. For a gu warrior to become stronger, they had to rely on good spirit veins, pills, and spirit stones just like cultivators did.

And in the cultivation world of the present day, a good spirit vein was far rarer than a person with a spiritual root!

Even if Life-Bound Gu were distributed to ten thousand people, without the resources to cultivate, most would spend their entire lives at a realm comparable to early Qi Refining.

Moreover, to receive a Life-Bound Gu implant, one had to be a martial artist who had reached at least the Transformation Realm, with a sufficiently tempered dantian, meridians, and physical body. Otherwise, most died the moment the spirit insect was implanted.

But were Transformation Realm experts common?

Raising a single martial artist to the Transformation Realm was far more difficult than finding a child with an ordinary spiritual root.

Ultimately, the requirements were demanding in both resources and talent, making it impossible to mass-produce enough powerful gu warriors to overturn the order of the cultivation world.

Rather than a new path of cultivation, the Gu Path was closer to an expensive and dangerous detour toward immortal ascension, one open only to a small number of extraordinarily gifted mortals.

However, the mortal nations of this world possessed populations and territories beyond imagination. Among their people were many with terrifying talent who lacked nothing except a spiritual root.

In principle, the cultivation system of gu warriors was not inherently superior to cultivation.

Yet gu warriors who had first reached the Transformation Realm and then successfully achieved symbiosis with a Life-Bound Gu were actually stronger than ordinary cultivators at the same realm!

That alone meant the title of gu warrior carried considerable weight.

At present, the royal family of Qianyang Kingdom had established Gu-Rearing Institutes throughout the country to breed Life-Bound Gu.

The Gu-Rearing Institutes selected children with exceptional talent for the martial path at an early age, then tempered their bodies through martial arts and medicinal baths. Of those children, only those who reached the Transformation Realm and proved compatible with a Life-Bound Gu were permitted to receive an implant.

The outstanding gu warriors produced in this manner were assigned to the military, government offices, and armed units directly subordinate to the royal family.

Lee Hyun continued examining the materials.

「What are the disadvantages of gu warriors?

If compatibility is poor, the martial artist's body treats the Life-Bound Gu as a foreign object and rejects it. In mild cases, this results only in fever and damaged meridians, but in severe cases, both host and spirit insect die.

The quality and species of the Life-Bound Gu determine a gu warrior's future. Some who later attempt to replace an inferior spirit insect with a better Life-Bound Gu lose all their true qi or even their lives.

Cultivation costs are also considerable. Depending on the Life-Bound Gu, it may need to be fed specific medicinal ingredients, poisons, or demon beast blood. If food becomes scarce, it may instead consume its host's essence blood and life force.

Because the human and spirit insect share their lives, severe injury to one also shocks the other. If the Life-Bound Gu dies, the host's dantian often collapses, or the host descends into madness.

Above all, the Gu-Rearing Institutes that raise high-quality Life-Bound Gu are controlled by the royal family and major sects. Rare breeds are worth a fortune and cannot easily be obtained even with a cultivator's spirit stones.」

Lee Hyun closed the book in admiration.

"Live long enough, and you really do see all kinds of things."

At that moment, he recalled the martial artists he had encountered at the inn several days earlier.

The fuzzbees had grown excited as though they had discovered food the moment those people appeared, while the martial artists had abruptly left without knowing why.

"Wait... Did one of them have a Life-Bound Gu inside their body?"

Fuzzbees were predators specialized in devouring spirit insects and their eggs.

If one of the martial artists that day had possessed a symbiotic spirit insect in their dantian, it would explain the reactions of both the fuzzbees and the martial artists.

"So there was a gu warrior among them!"

...

"I have a rough idea of how the world has changed. Now it's time to choose a site for Tunnel No. 3."

Lee Hyun stacked the maps on the table atop one another.

Kun Kingdom, Cang Kingdom, and Qianyang Kingdom, which had grown between them. The shifts in power surrounding the three nations were interesting. But as someone who was still only at Qi Refining Stage 7, Lee Hyun had no reason to deliberately involve himself in the turmoil of great powers.

...

Fifteen days later.

An unnamed mountain valley near Pingling County, Shuoning Circuit, Anling Kingdom, in northwestern Kun Kingdom.

Lee Hyun sat halfway up a cliff, looking down over the surrounding mountains.

Rocky mountains stretched endlessly in every direction, and even the nearest mortal village lay more than three hundred li (about 118 km) away. There was no reason for anyone to go out of their way to come here.

Roughly six thousand li to the north lay Heiya Ridge and Qinghe Valley.

About one thousand and fifty years ago, this was one of the places Lee Hyun had passed through while fleeing Qinghe Valley and heading south past Heiya Ridge.

Over the past fifteen days, Lee Hyun had traveled throughout a radius of roughly a thousand li, marking mortal villages, highways, and minor local powers on his maps. Underground, he descended as far as twenty-five li to inspect the bedrock, water veins, and flow of earth fire, while also checking for traces of demon beasts or cultivators that had remained in the area for long periods.

There were no obvious dangers for the time being.

He had also discovered, around eighteen li beneath the valley, a bedrock layer containing several broad, stable caverns. Two narrow water veins flowed into the area from different directions.

"Tunnel No. 3 should work well here."

'And... it shouldn't be difficult to establish a second Qutian Society nearby.'

Lee Hyun intended to create a new Qutian Society here.

To establish a Qutian Society, he needed a nearby spirit vein to leech from.

To the north was Qinghe Valley's Tier 3 spirit vein, while sects and cultivation clans occupying Tier 2 spirit veins were scattered here and there around it.

Another place that caught Lee Hyun's attention was Qianyang Kingdom to the south of Anling Kingdom.

Since Qianyang Kingdom had swallowed several mortal kingdoms, it possessed several Tier 2 spirit veins within its territory. The major Gu-Rearing Institutes that cultivated Life-Bound Gu and trained gu warriors were likely built atop those spirit veins.

If Qianyang Divine Demon was a powerhouse comparable to late Golden Core, it would not have been strange for a Tier 3 spirit vein to exist there as well. However, none of the information Lee Hyun had obtained contained any evidence that Qianyang Kingdom possessed a Tier 3 spirit vein.

'Well, it doesn't matter. A Tier 2 spirit vein is enough for me anyway...'

Lee Hyun considered Qianyang Kingdom a suitable place for a Qutian Society to establish itself.

The cultivation clans of Nanli Kingdom had already suffered from rogue cultivator organizations like the Qutian Society, and over the years they had developed detection formations and patrol procedures while carefully monitoring the spiritual pressure of their spirit veins.

By contrast, the gu warriors of Qianyang Kingdom had only existed as an organized force for around three hundred years. They might have learned how to fight cultivators, but they likely had not yet felt the need to hunt down rogue cultivators hiding deep underground and secretly drawing off small amounts of spiritual qi.

That meant they would also lack experience operating the relevant detection formations.

Of course, if Wangu Sect truly was behind them, countermeasures might eventually appear. Even so, it was well worth testing.

Lee Hyun did not find gu warriors particularly frightening.

They were beings who used martial arts and spiritual power together.

They were like reflections of himself.

Lee Hyun had begun combining martial arts and spiritual power far earlier than they had, and he also surpassed them in the breadth and depth of the martial learning he had accumulated. Many of the martial arts passed down from earlier generations that Qianyang Kingdom's gu warriors drew upon belonged to lineages Lee Hyun had either encountered personally or whose inheritors he had fought.

Lee Hyun descended from the cliff.

Ssssss―

His body sank into the earth.

...

After descending eighteen li underground, Lee Hyun drew the Mountain-Suppressing Sword.

Scrrrape―

「Tunnel No. 3」

Lee Hyun first selected a flat cavern and laid out the magic tools he had obtained from the two Foundation Establishment cultivators of the Qingchao Merchant Alliance.

There were six bronze flying swords linked by matching ripple patterns, as well as a black-iron longspear with no seam between its shaft and spearhead.

The six bronze flying swords formed a set whose restrictions became complete only when all six were operated together. The black-iron longspear appeared simple, but intricate restrictions ran continuously through its entire spearhead and shaft, allowing spiritual power to flow through both at once. Both were worthy of being called high-grade magic tools.

Lee Hyun was still not well versed in the artifact-refining art. However, by combining the fundamentals of magic-tool bonding that he had learned through Introductory Guide on Telekinesis and Sword Control at Qinghe Valley with his knowledge of formation inscriptions from Changchun Sect, he had developed enough insight to examine the structure and restrictions of magic tools.

He spent several days inspecting the magic tools inside and out and confirmed that traces of spiritual power left by their deceased owners still clung to various parts of the core restrictions.

'I won't be able to do it immediately, but if I pour divine sense and spiritual power into them every day, I think I can gradually push out the previous owners' traces...'

Of the iron spheres that had emerged from the longspear, only two remained intact. One had been cut apart by the Mountain-Suppressing Sword.

The spirit materials used in the iron spheres were far lower in grade than those used in the longspear, and they were not connected to the spear's core restrictions. They were little more than auxiliary projectiles that could be enlarged with spiritual power and thrown, so Lee Hyun classified both the iron spheres and their fragments as items to be sold.

One year later.

Drip. Drip. Drip...

Drops of water gathered at the end of a bamboo pipe and fell.

The water traveled along the channels of Spirit Field No. 1-1 and seeped into grooves throughout the field. Once the soil became sufficiently moist, nearby formation inscriptions brightened, while the Water-Drawing Inscription that had been drawing in water dimmed instead.

The water flowing through the bamboo pipe stopped.

Lee Hyun headed toward the next spirit field.

Tunnel No. 3's irrigation system was another step ahead of the one he had built in Tunnel No. 2.

One level above the spirit fields was a large irrigation reservoir. Low stone walls divided the inside of the reservoir into several sections, so even if one side developed a crack, all the stored water would not drain away.

The water produced with the Spirit Rain Art was clean in itself. However, the reservoir had been carved directly from the bedrock, and Lee Hyun sometimes had to leave it unattended for years at a time, so stone dust or fine sand falling from the ceiling and walls could mix into the water. To prevent settled debris from entering the pipes, Lee Hyun positioned the openings of the bamboo pipes a handspan above the bottom of the reservoir.

Each spirit field was connected to its own independent bamboo pipe and formation inscriptions leading from the reservoir. When the water qi in the soil became insufficient, a basic formation inscription activated the Water-Drawing Inscription, allowing a small amount of water to flow through. Once the soil was sufficiently wet, the Water-Drawing Inscription deactivated and stopped water from entering the pipe.

It was a system Lee Hyun would have struggled to create before learning basic formation inscriptions at Changchun Sect.

Rather than relying on separate spirit stones, the formation inscriptions operated using the spiritual qi remaining in the reservoir water that Lee Hyun had produced with the Spirit Rain Art.

The formation inscriptions consumed a small amount of spiritual qi, but because water was now delivered only where and when it was needed, overall consumption actually decreased. The new irrigation system could maintain the spirit fields for three years even if Lee Hyun did not return.

'I could make it last longer by enlarging the reservoir, but expanding the caverns this far underground would be dangerous.'

Whenever Lee Hyun built tunnels, he made use of natural bedrock and caverns whenever possible.

That was because he had never studied civil engineering or architecture in his past life and could not calculate the loads and pressures the bedrock could withstand deep underground.

'It might be worth looking for relevant knowledge in this world later....'

Tunnel No. 3 consisted of four main levels. At the top were the cultivation chamber, storeroom, and resting room. Beneath them came the irrigation level and spirit-field level. At the very bottom was a drainage level designed to handle any unexpected influx of water from the underground aquifer into the spirit fields.

He did not create any broad air shafts that might leave visible traces on the surface. Instead, he connected narrow, winding natural fissures to the caves and bedrock caverns, allowing air to circulate, however slowly. In truth, breathing underground was not much of a problem for Lee Hyun, who possessed the Air-Clearing Art.

The spirit-field numbers remained the same as before.

The locations had changed, but the lineages and records of the spirit plants growing within them continued uninterrupted. If he changed their names as well, it would become confusing whenever he consulted cultivation ledgers spanning hundreds of years.

Lee Hyun recreated all twelve fields, from Spirit Field No. 1-1 through Spirit Field No. 1-7 and Spirit Field No. 2-1 through Spirit Field No. 2-5, inside the new bedrock. The test spirit field used for research into bone age manipulation was placed separately outside them.

Spirit Field No. 1-1 contained eighty-one Bone-Rot Flowers with an average medicine age of 349 years, 282 Yin Soul Grass plants, seventy-three Purple Poison Orchid bulbs, and fifty-two Earth Vein Flowers.

Spirit Field No. 1-2 through Spirit Field No. 1-5 contained a total of 432 Bone-Rot Flowers with an average medicine age of 315 years, 1,104 Yin Soul Grass plants, 292 Purple Poison Orchid bulbs, and 204 Earth Vein Flowers, divided among the four fields.

The oldest Yin Water Lotus in Spirit Field No. 1-6 and the three Stone Honey Peach trees in Spirit Field No. 1-7 had reached a medicine age of 295 years. The Yin Water Lotus he had divided and replanted after joining Changchun Sect and the three Stone Honey Peach trees grown from cuttings had also surpassed a medicine age of five years and were becoming well established.

Spirit Field No. 2-1 through Spirit Field No. 2-5 remained Spirit-Storing Ginseng fields. Five hundred and fifty-two Spirit-Storing Ginseng roots had reached a medicine age of 180 years, while another 915 roots had reached thirty-eight years.

"In another sixty years, the medicine age of those 552 roots will reach two hundred years. There must be countless Tier 2 pill recipes in the world that use Spirit-Storing Ginseng..."

Spirit-Storing Ginseng was a spirit plant with relatively neutral properties, and its primary function was to store spiritual power, so it was likely used in many different pill recipes.

Lee Hyun scooped up a handful of soil from the edge of the spirit field. Because he had moved the soil slabs intact during the relocation, almost none of the Spirit-Storing Ginseng roots had been damaged.

Bzzzzzz―

A fuzzbee flew over from somewhere and landed on the back of Lee Hyun's hand. White, sticky larval slime clung to its golden fur.

"You ate something weird again."

Plop.

As though offended by the accusation, the fuzzbee defecated, then threw itself onto the freshly packed dry soil.

Rrrrroll.

As the fellow rubbed its back against the dirt to wipe away the slime, three nearby fuzzbees followed suit and threw themselves onto the ground one after another.

"Do you like your new home?"

...

Tunnel No. 3's alchemy chamber lay around twenty-five li underground.

Its design was more advanced than the alchemy chamber in Tunnel No. 2. A separate passage in the ceiling allowed heat and smoke to escape, while one side of the stone wall had been carved thin so that if the pill furnace exploded, the pressure could vent into an empty cavern.

Nine red formation stones were embedded in the floor of the alchemy chamber, forming a wide circle. They were the Nine-Fire Flame-Storing Formation that Lee Hyun had recovered from Tunnel No. 2.

However, the size of the formation and the arrangement of its formation inscriptions were slightly different from before.

At the center stood not the pill furnace he had purchased from the Fengtian Bureau, but the Tier 1 pill furnace of supreme grade he had received from a steward of the Yang Fire Court when leaving Changchun Sect.

Lee Hyun widened the spacing between the formation stones to match the size of the new pill furnace and modified only the portions of the Nine-Fire Flame-Storing Formation's formation inscriptions that interacted with the restrictions on the furnace's surface. He had not created an entirely new formation, but after dozens of tests, he successfully expanded a proven formation to fit a different specification.

Fwoosh―

When Lee Hyun released his hand seal, the nine burners died down one after another.

When he opened the lid of the pill furnace, ivory-colored powder lay evenly settled across the bottom. Lee Hyun checked the powder's medicinal potency and impurities, then divided it evenly into six medicine packets.

It was Tier 1 Bone-Forging Powder.

Lee Hyun carried the packets to the storeroom. On one shelf sat three magic tools used to measure bone age, along with thick ledgers he had compiled over the past dozen or so years.

At present, after taking Bone-Forging Powder, Lee Hyun could adjust the bone age displayed by all three magic tools to anywhere between thirty-five and eighty-five. The discrepancy between the three tools was no more than two years.

He sorted the finished Bone-Forging Powder according to the target bone age and the timing of the examination.

「Bone age 35. Examination 10 to 20 days after taking.」

...

「Bone age 85. Examination 8 to 17 days after taking.」

Lee Hyun placed each medicine packet in a small jade casket and sealed it with a Tier 1 Spirit-Sealing Talisman. Jade caskets of identical size were neatly stacked along one side of his storage pouch.

...

After completing Tunnel No. 3, Lee Hyun changed his appearance under several different identities and traveled among cultivator markets in Anling Kingdom and Qianyang Kingdom. His purpose was to dispose of the items from the storage pouches of the two Foundation Establishment cultivators.

He kept the six bronze flying swords, the black-iron longspear, the two storage pouches, some healing pills meant for injuries, and a few general-purpose talismans. The iron spheres and the remaining pills, talismans, and spirit materials were divided up and sold across several cultivator markets.

The proceeds amounted to thirty-eight mid-grade spirit stones. He added those to his existing spirit stones and the spirit stones he had obtained from the two cultivators' storage pouches, then exchanged most of his low-grade spirit stones for mid-grade spirit stones to reduce their bulk. After settling everything, he had 145 mid-grade spirit stones and 100 low-grade spirit stones remaining.

"That takes care of everything I need to do for now. What's left is finding an environment with enough spiritual pressure to push the upper limit of my spiritual power even higher in late Qi Refining...."

He looked at the new map pinned to the wall. The spirit veins of Kun Kingdom and Qianyang Kingdom had been marked on it.

"Time to establish the Qutian Society."

Two hundred and eighty years later.

Anling Kingdom, a mortal kingdom in northwestern Kun Kingdom.

In the most remote alley of Huiyan Marketstood a shabby shop called Baiwu Shop

Its worn shelves were piled with low-quality spirit materials, empty jade bottles, and old fragments of magic tools whose purposes were impossible to identify. Most days, not a single customer entered the shop.

Late at night, a closed sign was hung on the door of Baiwu Shop. The rogue cultivator minding the store pushed aside a chest on the floor and pressed his identity token against a hidden formation inscription beneath it.

Grrrrrk―

A staircase leading underground appeared.

The rogue cultivator took a black crow mask from inside his robe, put it over his face, and descended the stairs.

Five cultivators had arrived before him and were waiting in masks inside Baiwu Shop's underground stone chamber. Their masks depicted a gray mountain goat, a yellow field mouse, a blue snake, a white owl, and a mole.

The rogue cultivator in the black crow mask took the last empty seat.

Just then.

Tap.

A small pebble jumped from the floor on one side of the stone chamber.

The solid floor soon rippled like water, and a cultivator in purple robes rose ghostlike from beneath the earth. A Badger mask covered his face.

Every member who witnessed the sight for the first time had much the same thought.

'What a terrifying technique! Is there really an Earth Escape Art in this world that can pass straight through granite? Society Head must surely be a Foundation Establishment cultivator, no... perhaps he might even be a Golden Core great cultivator!'

All six people rose at once and cupped their hands.

"Greetings, Society Head."

"Good. Begin your reports."

None of the members truly knew the origins of the 'Two Heavens Society'. They did not even know exactly when the organization had been founded.

If anything, not knowing the origin of the name only made the Two Heavens Society seem more mysterious and profound. Since no one knew what the "two heavens" in its name actually referred to, increasingly elaborate theories continued to emerge.

One member claimed that the name referred to drawing upon the spiritual qi of two "heavens", Kun Kingdom and Qianyang Kingdom.

Another insisted that the two heavens were the world aboveground and the world underground. Yet another speculated that there were actually two different people acting as the Badger Society Head, and that this was why the organization was called the Two Heavens Society.

It did not matter which interpretation, if any, was correct. Simply belonging to such a mysterious secret organization filled the members with pride, a sense of belonging, and even a certain sense of superiority.

Chapter 42

Black Crow was the first to take out a thick ledger.

“This is the year-end accounting of the spirit stones and spirit materials that passed through Baiwu Shop over the past year. All membership dues and vein-seat usage fees have been recorded in the ledger, and after deducting the maintenance expenses for each base, the remainder was exchanged for mid-grade spirit stones and stored.”

He placed a small storage pouch on the table along with the ledger.

“Would you like to check it yourself?”

“Leave the ledger. You keep the storage pouch.”

“Understood.”

After pushing the ledger forward, Black Crow took another storage pouch from his robes.

“And this is something I brought for you, Society Head.”

When the storage pouch opened, books appeared in neat stacks across the stone chamber floor.

Hardly any of them were old. The covers all bore the same title, but each had a different volume number.

A Poor Tenant Farmer's Chronicle of Returning Home with Longevity

Volumes 1 through 72. Complete.

Lee Hyun's gaze lingered on the books for a moment.

“They say it's currently the most popular work in the mundane world of Kun Kingdom. It begins with the son of a poor tenant farmer from a frontier commandery ravaged by war. He's conscripted into military service, then saves a wounded rogue cultivator on the battlefield and obtains an Immortal Ascension Token.”

Black Crow picked up one of the books.

“He starts as a lowly menial disciple, obtains cultivation resources and cultivation arts, then returns to his hometown a hundred years later still looking young. He punishes corrupt officials and restores his declining family. Toward the end, they say even the Emperor personally begs him to become the State Preceptor.”

He added,

“It was published steadily over ten years, and the series concluded last spring with Volume 72. The members who've read it also spoke highly of it.”

“I'll enjoy reading it.”

“I'm glad to hear that.”

Lee Hyun put the books into his storage pouch.

The other members had no idea why Society Head Badger collected popular novels from the mundane world.

...

Gray Mountain Goat was next.

He unfolded three maps marked with the spirit veins of Kun Kingdom near Baiwu Shop.

“The eleven vein seats on the Kun Kingdom side are mostly operating without issue. However, we closed Shihu Sect Vein Seat No. 2, nine thousand li (about 3,500 km) east of Huiyan Market.”

“Why?”

“Shihu Sect changed the detection method of its formations. Continuing to use the seat would have created too great a risk of discovery.”

“The members?”

“We divided them among nearby vein seats. It hasn't caused any significant disruption to their cultivation.”

“Well done.”

Gray Mountain Goat marked the closed vein seat on the map.

Then he took out a jade casket slightly larger than his palm.

Click.

Inside lay a blue-green bell about the size of a man's fist.

Wave-like patterns ran down its surface from top to bottom, but there was no visible clapper.

“A Protective Bell.”

Gray Mountain Goat infused it with spiritual power.

Hummm―

The fist-sized bell floated into the air.

Ding―

With a deep chime, the Protective Bell rapidly expanded.

Before long, it had grown to six chi (about 2 m) in height. It slowly descended and stopped about one cun (about 3.3 cm) above the floor.

“Mole, test it lightly.”

Mole nodded and extended a hand.

Whoosh!

A stone spike one ja (about 33 cm) long spun through the air toward the Protective Bell.

Boom!

Ding―

The stone spike shattered.

Dark blue ripples formed at the point of impact and spread in every direction across the bell's curved surface. The force carried by the stone spike was transformed into a deep chime and dispersed.

Hummm―

The Protective Bell shrank back to the size of a fist and settled onto Gray Mountain Goat's palm.

“They say it can withstand several attacks from a late Qi Refining cultivator. It can even take a single strike from an early Foundation Establishment cultivator, though the bell may be damaged in the process.”

“So it's a high-grade magic tool.”

“Correct. I was told it was cast with Mystic Resonance Copper, a Tier 2 mid grade spirit material, mixed into it.”

Lee Hyun turned the Protective Bell over several times in his palm, inspecting it, then placed it into his storage pouch.

“Well done.”

Gray Mountain Goat continued.

“I also managed to learn some of the uses of the Purple Poison Orchid, Bone-Rot Flower, and Yin Soul Grass that you asked about.”

“Let's hear it.”

“The Purple Poison Orchid is indeed one of the main ingredients of the Poison-Warding Pill. The nearest place known to refine Poison-Warding Pills is Qinghe Valley in the Great Yan Kingdom. However, I found no information indicating that Qinghe Valley uses Bone-Rot Flowers or Yin Soul Grass.”

Qinghe Valley was the sect where Lee Hyun had once been an outer disciple roughly 1,330 years ago.

'Using Purple Poison Orchids in alchemy makes sense. They were already growing them in the Withering Yin Field, after all. But they don't refine anything using Bone-Rot Flowers or Yin Soul Grass? Either the information is inaccurate, or Qinghe Valley lost those pill recipes as the years passed.'

Qinghe Valley's prominence was no longer what it had once been. At this point, Lee Hyun wasn't even sure whether the sect still had a Golden Core cultivator.

Yellow Field Mouse reported on the situation in the Great Yan Kingdom.

“We discovered four new residual-vein pockets in southern Great Yan Kingdom. However, we haven't established any vein seats yet.”

“Why?”

“Perhaps because the environment is harsher, the sects of the Great Yan Kingdom are much more sensitive about their territories than those in Kun Kingdom. The cultivation clans controlling the spirit veins also patrol frequently. I judged that hastily digging access passages could expose our other vein seats as well.”

“Well done.”

Yellow Field Mouse lowered his head, looking relieved.

“Instead, we're continuing to record only the spiritual pressure and patrol intervals. I'll observe them for another three years or so before reporting again.”

“Do that.”

Mole briefly reported that there were no particular problems with the vein seats under his supervision.

White Owl carefully took a jade casket from his robes.

Four jade bottles were neatly arranged inside.

“These are the Purple Essence Pills you ordered. Twelve pills in total.”

There were three pills in each bottle.

A Tier 1 Spirit-Sealing Talisman was affixed over each bottle's mouth, and the wax seal bore the Danxiao Sect's pill-inspection seal.

Lee Hyun took out one jade bottle and examined the Spirit-Sealing Talisman and wax seal.

“High grade again?”

“Yes. It's been less than half a year since they were released.”

Lee Hyun broke the seal and placed one Purple Essence Pill on his palm.

Fine fire patterns, resembling flames rising upward, remained on the surface of the faintly purple pill.

When he examined its interior with the Aura-Reading Art and his divine sense, he found that the refined medicinal strength had gathered evenly at the pill's center.

The Purple Essence Pill was a Tier 1 high grade pill taken by late Qi Refining cultivators to build up magical power.

It wasn't meant to break through the walls of a minor realm like the Essence-Raising Pill or Barrier-Breaking Pill, but its medicinal potency was gentle and pure, allowing a late Qi Refining cultivator to shorten the time needed for cultivation.

White Owl had supplied Lee Hyun with Purple Essence Pills for more than thirty years. Lee Hyun never relied solely on the Danxiao Sect's pill-inspection seal and personally inspected the pills every time, but he had never found a problem so far.

'As good as ever.'

Lee Hyun returned the pill to the jade bottle.

Thud.

A pouch filled with mid-grade spirit stones appeared on the table.

White Owl counted the spirit stones and tucked the pouch into his robes.

“Can you obtain more next time?”

“Purple Essence Pills have recently become more sought after even among Danxiao Sect disciples. I don't think I'll be able to acquire any for the time being.”

“Understood.”

Lee Hyun placed the jade casket containing the Purple Essence Pills into his storage pouch.

White Owl didn't know why Society Head Badger continued purchasing Purple Essence Pills.

'Does he attend another gathering? I've never seen him use Purple Essence Pills for trades at the gatherings I'm part of...'

White Owl was an outer disciple of the Danxiao Sect and a resident cultivator dispatched to the royal court of Anling Kingdom, far northwest of the sect's main mountain.

Anling Kingdom itself had no powerful cultivation forces. By the standards of the cultivation world, however, it was part of Kun Kingdom's territory.

The Danxiao Sect and Biluo Sect had established the Immortal Veneration Court within the Anling royal court and dispatched outer disciples there to supervise the rogue cultivators employed by the royal family, select children with exceptional spiritual roots, and sort out the tribute to be presented to the sects. Mediating disputes between rogue cultivators and small cultivation clans was also part of a resident cultivator's duties.

The title of resident cultivator sounded respectable, but from the perspective of the main mountain, it was closer to assigning distant miscellaneous duties to outer disciples who had fallen behind in the sect's internal competition. The cultivation resources they could receive were limited, and the spirit vein of the Anling royal family made it difficult to advance one's realm quickly.

White Owl had joined the Two Heavens Society after using one of its vein seats while traveling between the Danxiao Sect's main mountain and Anling Kingdom. Since his duties already kept him far from the main mountain, interacting with nearby rogue cultivators and Two Heavens Society members was relatively natural.

Once every three or four years, White Owl returned to the Danxiao Sect to escort a tribute procession or report on his assignments. On those occasions, he used purchase privileges received as rewards for external missions to buy various goods. The Purple Essence Pills requested by Lee Hyun were among them.

The timing of his supply was irregular, but the quality was reliable.

White Owl openly brought out pills bearing the Danxiao Sect's pill-inspection seal and made little effort to hide the fact that he was a disciple of a great sect. That status alone gave him a firm position within the Two Heavens Society.

...

Finally, Blue Snake unfolded a map of Qianyang Kingdom.

The map marked the Gu-Rearing Institute in northern Qianyang Kingdom, Tier 2 spirit veins, and fortresses garrisoned by gu warriors.

“Patrols around the spirit veins in northern Qianyang Kingdom have increased recently. Fortunately, none of the Two Heavens Society's vein seats have been discovered yet.”

“Keep watching, but don't take unnecessary risks.”

“Understood.”

Blue Snake hesitated briefly before continuing.

“There's also a member from the Qianyang Kingdom side who wishes to personally pay his respects to you, Society Head.”

“Who?”

“Black Sable. He joined three years ago and has provided information on the Gu-Rearing Institute's movements several times since then.”

Blue Snake added,

“He recently acquired something valuable and said he wished to present it to you, so I brought him here. He's waiting outside.”

“Have him come in.”

A short while later, a cultivator wearing a Black Sable mask descended the stairs into the stone chamber and knelt on both knees in its center.

“Greetings, Society Head.”

“Rise.”

“Thank you.”

He took a long wooden case from his robes.

“A Vein-Prospecting Ruler.”

Black Sable held up the wooden case.

“They say that if you place it against the ground and channel spiritual power into it, it will point toward the directions in which nearby spirit veins and residual veins extend. I thought it might help find new vein seats, so I wished to offer it to you, Society Head.”

“Bring it here.”

“Yes.”

Black Sable approached, carrying the wooden case with both hands. At that moment, the spirit-insect pouch at Lee Hyun's waist trembled almost imperceptibly.

“Here it is.”

He opened the wooden case.

Click.

Inside lay a metal ruler one chi long. A transparent bead was embedded in one end.

The moment Lee Hyun lowered his gaze,

transparent threads burst from Black Sable's fingertips, tearing through the air.

Half targeted Society Head Badger's dantian and chest, while the rest flew toward the major acupoints of his neck and limbs.

At the same time, thick black smoke erupted from the wooden case.

“Society Head―”

Before Blue Snake could finish shouting,

Shing.

As though time itself had stopped, a brief sword cry swept through the stone chamber.

The members didn't even see when the Society Head reached out.

All they saw were the transparent threads being cut uselessly into pieces before their eyes and scattering across the floor.

Shhk.

The black smoke surging forward to engulf their vision was likewise split cleanly to either side, as though a vast curtain had been torn apart.

From where Society Head Badger sat to directly in front of Black Sable's chest, a perfectly clean passage had been carved through the smoke.

But Black Sable didn't retreat.

Spiritual pressure suddenly exploded from his body.

Boom!

Blue Snake, who had been about to rush forward, froze.

The ledger and maps on the table whipped violently beneath the ferocious aura crushing down upon the stone chamber.

It wasn't the aura of Qi Refining.

Early Foundation Establishment.

And it wasn't the aura of a cultivator, but of a gu warrior!

Crack! Crunch!

Black Sable's long robe swelled as though it were about to burst. Carapace tore through his skin and spread across his right arm in an instant, grotesquely encasing it.

Black Sable threw aside the wooden case and lunged forward.

CRUNCH!

His right foot smashed down on the stone slab. The force began at his toes, traveled through his twisting waist and spine, then gathered all at once in his right fist.

Just seeing that single movement made Yellow Field Mouse's breath catch. The air before Black Sable's fist warped black beneath an aura that seemed capable of collapsing the stone chamber.

Whoosh―

The distance was far too close.

Black Sable's fist hurtled toward Society Head Badger's chest.

At that moment, through White Owl's eyes, the flow of the world seemed to slow.

Amid the storm-like fist wind, Society Head Badger's sleeve fluttered lightly.

A single streak of pure white sword light bloomed into dozens of branches like a spreading fan.

The light divided with the graceful beauty of plum blossoms bursting into full bloom beneath the night sky, only to condense back into a single point before anyone could blink.

Flash!

The ferocious fist force and Society Head Badger's sword light met head-on.

A chilling white line appeared through the center of the Gu Origin True Qi surrounding Black Sable's fist.

Along that line, the Gu Origin True Qi split neatly in two. The divided force swept past either side of Society Head Badger and slammed into the stone wall behind him.

BOOM!

The entire stone chamber shook.

Yellow Field Mouse reflexively squeezed his eyes shut, then opened them again.

Society Head Badger was still sitting calmly in his seat.

Only Black Sable stood frozen in the posture of throwing his punch.

The white line that had appeared on his fist continued down his forearm, shoulder, and chest, extending all the way to his lower abdomen.

Crack.

The black carapace and body-protecting spirit light split apart at the same time.

Splurt!

Dark red blood belatedly sprayed out.

Black Sable looked down in disbelief at the white line running across his body.

'How....'

Before his final thought could even finish, the sharp air-splitting shriek that had followed the sword light rang through the stone chamber.

Keeeeeng―

Thud.

Black Sable's body, split in two, collapsed to the floor.

Something writhed inside his lower abdomen.

Gurgle. Gurgle.

The skin around his dantian soon turned black, and slender protrusions resembling insect legs pushed outward from beneath it.

But the movement didn't last long. The Life-Bound Gu, which had been split apart by the sword light along with its host, twitched a few times before rapidly shriveling and turning to ash.

Mole stared at the corpse, his face pale.

“He was a gu warrior....”

Cold sweat ran down Blue Snake's face. He was the one who had personally brought Black Sable here.

In the Society Head's eyes, this ambush could easily look like something he and Black Sable had plotted together. If that was what the Society Head concluded, no one here would stop the next sword light even if it severed Blue Snake's neck.

Blue Snake hurriedly dropped to his knees.

“Society Head! I swear I was not in league with that man. I had no idea he was a gu warrior, nor did I know he was targeting you!”

The other members' gazes gathered on Blue Snake.

Lee Hyun flicked the blood from the Mountain-Suppressing Sword.

“I'll hear your excuses later.”

Blue Snake's shoulders flinched.

“First, search the corpse.”

“Yes!”

Only then did the six members snap back to their senses.

...

With trembling hands, Blue Snake removed Black Sable's mask and long robe.

Beneath the mask was the face of a man who appeared to be around forty. He had no conspicuous scars or other distinguishing features.

There was no token in his robes that could identify him.

But when they tore open the lining of his long robe, they found a small black iron plaque about two knuckles long.

A black sun was engraved on the front, while the back bore the image of an insect with its eyes closed.

Blue Snake's face grew even paler.

“The Black Sun Office.”

“What kind of organization is that?”

“It's an intelligence organization of the Qianyang royal family. They investigate the unauthorized distribution of Life-Bound Gu and plant spies among various factions outside the royal court.”

Blue Snake examined Black Sable's face again.

“This is my first time seeing someone from the Black Sun Office in person. I only knew their emblem.”

Mole found a black jade bead.

Thin red lines were intertwined inside it.

He examined the bead with the Aura-Reading Art, then abruptly stopped.

“This seems to be connected to something outside.”

“A voice-transmission magic tool?”

“I'm not certain.”

“Set it aside.”

The members spread everything found in Black Sable's robes and storage pouch across the table. The black iron plaque, jade bead, Vein-Prospecting Ruler from the wooden case, along with talismans and silver needles of unknown purpose, were classified as objects that might allow them to be tracked.

“I'll dispose of these.”

What remained were a little over thirty mid-grade spirit stones, medicinal pills for treating injuries, general-purpose talismans, and ordinary spirit materials. After confirming that none bore unusual markings or suspicious formation inscriptions, Lee Hyun moved them into his own storage pouch.

The members watched as though it were only natural.

The Society Head had killed the enemy, so the spoils belonged to him.

Lastly, they found a small spirit-insect pouch at Black Sable's waist.

Mole and Blue Snake inspected its exterior, but found no conspicuous tracking formation inscriptions.

“Let's open it.”

Lee Hyun removed the Spirit-Sealing Talisman and opened the mouth of the pouch.

A faint jade-colored glow leaked from within.

Inside, a white silkworm-like spirit insect about two knuckles long lay curled into a ball.

Its skin was translucent like jade, and fine blue veins ran through its body.

White Owl's eyes widened in surprise.

“A Meridian-Linking Jade Silkworm!”

“You know this spirit insect?”

“It's a Tier 2 Life-Bound Gu. I've heard it's exceptionally good at linking its host's meridians and life force, and that the process of accepting it is safer than with other Life-Bound Gu.”

“If it's a Tier 2 Life-Bound Gu... does that mean it's comparable to a Foundation Establishment cultivator?”

“It's only a larva right now. But once fully grown, it can coexist with a gu warrior in the Foundation Establishment realm, which is why it's classified as Tier 2.”

The Meridian-Linking Jade Silkworm didn't appear to have linked its life with anyone yet.

It was a separate spirit insect from the Life-Bound Gu that had died inside the man's body.

“Why would a Black Sun Office spy be carrying something like this?”

“He may have intended to recruit a local martial artist or implant it into a new informant. I don't know for certain either.”

Lee Hyun nodded.

He returned the Meridian-Linking Jade Silkworm to the spirit-insect pouch and kept the pouch as well.

Once the potentially traceable objects, ordinary spoils, and Meridian-Linking Jade Silkworm had all been sorted away, the table was clean once more.

...

After everything had been put away, Lee Hyun looked at Blue Snake.

“Where did you meet him?”

“Three years ago, at a vein seat in Heishi Ridge, Qianyang Kingdom.”

Blue Snake once again bowed until his forehead touched the floor.

“He was a rogue cultivator using that residual-vein pocket alone. I was the one who approached him first, and after testing him several times, I accepted him into the Two Heavens Society.”

“How did you test him?”

“I leaked false information at different locations and observed his reactions. I also inspected his storage pouch and the techniques he used. I detected no traces of Gu Origin True Qi or a Life-Bound Gu.”

“Were you also the one who brought him here today?”

“Yes.”

Blue Snake didn't dare raise his head.

“This was my failure. I'll accept whatever punishment you deem appropriate.”

“Raise your head.”

Blue Snake carefully straightened up.

“There was no easy way for you to know he was a gu warrior. If a Foundation Establishment gu warrior deliberately hides himself, how could someone at Qi Refining like you discover it? Moreover, if he truly belonged to the Black Sun Office, he was probably highly skilled at concealing his identity.”

“But I brought him all the way to the gathering place.”

“Yes. We won't use this place for the time being.”

Lee Hyun spoke to Black Crow.

“Continue operating Baiwu Shop as usual, but remove the formation gate leading to this underground stone chamber. I'll inform you separately of the next gathering place.”

“Understood.”

“Blue Snake, shut down the Heishi Ridge vein seat and every contact point that man visited. Scatter the members involved across different regions, and have them cut contact with one another for a while.”

“Yes.”

“From now on, we accept no new members.”

All six masks lowered their heads at once.

“Recheck the identities of all existing members and how they joined. Even if we begin accepting members again, they must have recommendations from two members and undergo at least ten years of observation. Anyone who has been a member for less than thirty years is not to be invited to central gatherings.”

“We'll keep that in mind.”

Blue Snake tried to speak again, but Lee Hyun raised a hand.

“If you had been working with him, you would have acted alongside him the moment the ambush failed. There's no need to explain yourself any further.”

“Thank you, Society Head.”

Lee Hyun gathered the items from the meeting, then burned Black Sable's corpse with the Fireball Art, erasing every trace.

“Today's gathering ends here.”

The six members cupped their hands in unison.

“We bid farewell to the Society Head.”

Lee Hyun's body slowly sank into the earth.

Ssssss―

The members remained motionless for a long while after he disappeared.

Yellow Field Mouse was the first to speak.

“Did anyone see him draw his sword?”

No one answered.

Gray Mountain Goat stared at the split stone wall and spoke in a low voice.

“Black Sable's strength was by no means ordinary either. If that strike had been aimed at us, not one person here would have survived.”

White Owl recalled the wound that had extended from Black Sable's fist to his lower abdomen.

“Then how did the Society Head...”

Mole stared at the solid granite floor into which Society Head Badger had vanished.

“His realm seems to be beyond anything we can fathom.”

...

Two shichen (about four hours) later.

After traveling to a point over a thousand li from Huiyan Market, Lee Hyun dug down to a depth of twenty-five li, where the earth-vein stratum began.

There, he took out the black iron plaque, jade bead, Vein-Prospecting Ruler, talismans of unknown purpose, and silver needles.

Lee Hyun tossed the objects one by one into a fissure where earth fire flowed.

Fwoooosh―

The black iron plaque glowed red-hot, while the red lines inside the jade bead snapped and burst one after another.

Crackle! Crack-crackle!

Lee Hyun watched until every object had lost its original form, then left.

...

The next day.

The cultivation chamber in Tunnel No. 3.

Lee Hyun lined up four jade bottles on the floor. Each bottle contained three Purple Essence Pills.

Twelve in total.

Over the past 280 years, he had cultivated only at the finest vein seats he could find, ranging from Tier 1 high grade all the way to supreme grade. Even so, the amount of cultivation required by the Primordial Body was absurdly high.

According to the calculations he'd made when reaching Qi Refining Stage 7, it would take six hundred years to reach Qi Refining Stage 9, then another four hundred years to reach Qi Refining Great Perfection.

Because of that, Lee Hyun had begun steadily purchasing cultivation pills roughly a hundred years ago.

He had unlimited time, but cultivation was tedious, and he had already read nearly all the popular novels he could obtain in the surrounding region.

Besides, centuries-old spirit plants had accumulated in his spirit field. At this point, spending several more centuries merely to save spirit stones would actually be a greater loss.

Among the cultivation pills available in the surrounding region, Purple Essence Pills were the most efficient. He had purchased more than seventy from White Owl alone over the years, and thanks to them, Lee Hyun had reached the very peak of Qi Refining Stage 8.

...

Lee Hyun placed a Purple Essence Pill in his mouth.

Gulp.

As the pill passed down his throat, gentle yet concentrated medicinal strength spread throughout his entire body.

Lee Hyun lay comfortably on the floor and circulated the Primordial One-Qi Art.

Whoooosh―

Primordial True Qi flowed through his meridians, rapidly absorbing the Purple Essence Pill's medicinal strength.

One shichen later.

He had completely absorbed the second Purple Essence Pill as well.

The newly absorbed medicinal strength pushed against the upper limit of his spiritual power.

Thump.

A faint shock spread through his meridians and his entire body.

...

The eighth Purple Essence Pill dissolved.

Primordial True Qi spun through his meridians like a storm.

Then, in a single instant, the Primordial True Qi circulating throughout his body expanded.

Whoooosh!

His brimming spiritual power forced open the final boundary.

Faint ripples spread beneath Lee Hyun's body.

Stone dust and tiny pebbles on the floor simultaneously floated into the air before falling again.

Rattle-rattle-rattle.

Qi Refining Stage 9!

Lee Hyun closed his eyes as he stabilized the flow of his Primordial True Qi.

...

The next day.

Lee Hyun finally rose to his feet.

His entire body felt refreshed.

“Good.”

For the first time in ages, Lee Hyun brought out the wooden board from the storeroom that he used as his handmade status window.

“Come to think of it, I haven't updated this in nearly three hundred years.”

He contemplated his own essence, qi and spirit for a moment, then used the Yang Metal Art to erase some of the existing characters and carve in new ones.

【Age: 1,393】

【Realm: Qi Refining Stage 9】

【Spiritual Power: 733 → 1,333】

【Constitution: Primordial Body, 9th Stage】

Lee Hyun stared at the wooden board for a long while.

Qi Refining Stage 9.

“So the next goal is the Foundation Establishment Pill...”

Foundation Establishment Pills were incomparably more precious than Essence-Raising Pills.

As far as Lee Hyun knew, the only faction in the surrounding region that refined and sold Foundation Establishment Pills was the Danxiao Sect of Kun Kingdom.

But even the Danxiao Sect rarely released Foundation Establishment Pills to outsiders.

Very few were sold externally. Most Foundation Establishment Pills went to true-inheritance disciples and inner disciples, and occasionally to outer disciples who had accumulated many years of contributions.

'I need at least fifty. But if I buy them a few at a time and stockpile them, the spiritual qi inside the pills I bought first will begin to dissipate....'

'If I can't secure a large quantity of Foundation Establishment Pills within a short period, it would be better to obtain the pill recipe and mother plants of the required spirit plants, grow them myself, and then refine the pills.'

'The problem is that the Foundation Establishment Pill recipe is advanced knowledge guarded closely even by great sects....'

Lee Hyun flopped onto his back.

'There's no need to rush. I only just reached Qi Refining Stage 9... For now, I'll steadily cultivate until Qi Refining Great Perfection and think about it along the way.'

Lee Hyun returned the wooden board to the storeroom.

Only then did he remember the Meridian-Linking Jade Silkworm he'd obtained from Black Sable.

“I should take a look at this too.”

...

Lee Hyun entered a separate underground space that the other fuzzbees didn't visit.

He had no intention of implanting the Meridian-Linking Jade Silkworm into himself. Selling a Life-Bound Gu that had come from the Black Sun Office was dangerous as well.

Most importantly, the fuzzbees had become unusually excited by the Meridian-Linking Jade Silkworm's presence, so he decided to feed it to them and observe what changes occurred.

First, he opened his own spirit-insect pouch and took out three fuzzbees. Thanks to their reaction when Black Sable approached, he had been prepared for the ambush in advance.

Bzz― Bzz-bzz―

The three fuzzbees flew a circle around Lee Hyun as soon as they emerged.

Squeak. Squeak-squeak.

“You want to eat it that badly?”

When Lee Hyun opened Black Sable's spirit-insect pouch, a faint jade glow spilled out.

Ssssss―

The Meridian-Linking Jade Silkworm emerged and slowly raised its head as though surveying its surroundings.

It tried to draw in the surrounding heaven-and-earth spiritual qi, but because it was still only a larva, its presence was faint.

At that moment, all three fuzzbees moved simultaneously.

Bzz!

The Meridian-Linking Jade Silkworm belatedly shrank back.

Squeak! Squeak-squeak!

Pshk! Pshk! Pshk!

Transparent liquid shot from the fuzzbees' mouths like bullets.

The sticky fluid struck the Meridian-Linking Jade Silkworm squarely on its head, torso, and tail.

The Meridian-Linking Jade Silkworm twisted its body, but the mucus only glued it more firmly to the floor.

Its jade-colored body was completely trapped inside the translucent slime.

The Meridian-Linking Jade Silkworm emitted a faint fluctuation of spiritual power, as though terrified.

It seemed to be searching for a host whose life it could link with its own.

But the only creatures around it were fuzzbees specialized in hunting and devouring spirit insects.

The three surrounded the Meridian-Linking Jade Silkworm.

Crunch. Crunch. Crunch...

The Meridian-Linking Jade Silkworm rapidly disappeared.

The fuzzbees shoved their heads against one another, each trying to get even one more bite.

Bzz-bzz! Squeak-squeak!

“Don't fight. Share.”

Before long, the Meridian-Linking Jade Silkworm was completely gone.

All three fuzzbees had round, swollen bellies.

They beat their wings unsteadily a couple of times before dropping one after another onto the dirt floor.

Thump. Thud.

All three lay sprawled spread-eagled on their backs.

Squeak....

“A food coma?”

Lee Hyun had never before seen fuzzbees so full that they couldn't move.

But upon closer inspection, he noticed regular fluctuations of spiritual power pulsing from their bodies.

“Hm?”

Lee Hyun placed one fuzzbee on his palm.

It was hotter than usual.

'Are they trying to break through?'

Lee Hyun immediately used the Soil-Softening Art to mold the granite into three small jars.

He placed one fuzzbee in each jar, then covered and sealed them with lids made using the Soil-Softening Art. He only pierced several tiny holes with the Yang Metal Art so air could pass through.

“Just in case, I'd better keep them separated.”

Lee Hyun moved the three jars into a small stone chamber adjoining the storeroom.

He considered the matter for a moment.

The fuzzbees followed Lee Hyun, but he had never established a formal master-servant contract with them using a secret art from an insect-control inheritance.

Their relationship was closer to one born from centuries of feeding, caring for, and growing accustomed to one another.

If the creatures transformed into Tier 2 spirit insects, there was no guarantee they would remain as obedient as they were now.

'I may need some sort of secret art for imprinting a master upon them.'

Chapter 43

A few days later.

Tunnel No. 3.

Lee Hyun lay comfortably on the floor, staring at the map he had attached to the ceiling.

The Two Heavens Society’s vein seats and contact points were marked on the map in different colors.

‘Did Black Sable investigate the Two Heavens Society on his own initiative?’

‘If the Black Sun Office considered the Two Heavens Society an important enemy, they wouldn’t have tried to attack the society head with just one early Foundation Establishment gu warrior.’

‘Either some branch assigned him a preliminary investigation, or Black Sable expanded the scope of the investigation on his own to earn merit...’

The Two Heavens Society had never raided the Gu-Rearing Institute or stolen Life-Bound Gu from Qianyang Kingdom. All it had ever done was siphon off small amounts of spiritual qi from Qianyang Kingdom’s spirit veins.

The Two Heavens Society was hardly a significant presence.

‘Still, if Black Sable reported regularly, some of the vein seats and members may already have been exposed.’

‘I shut down the places that needed shutting down and scattered the people. For now, all I can do is scale back the Two Heavens Society’s activities and watch what happens.’

Just then.

A faint flutter of wings came from somewhere.

Bzzzz―

The sound was coming from the small stone chamber attached to the storeroom.

“Already?”

It had only been five days since he put the fuzzbees that had eaten the Meridian-Linking Jade Silkworm into the jars.

‘They woke up before I could even obtain an insect control inheritance. These fellows... Don’t tell me they broke through to Foundation Establishment before I did?’

Swish.

Lee Hyun headed for the stone chamber.

...

The small stone chamber beside the storeroom.

Three granite jars stood apart from one another.

Bzzzzzz―

The fluttering of wings continued from inside the jars.

Taking care not to hurt the fuzzbee inside, Lee Hyun carefully used the Soil-Softening Art to break away one side of the jar.

Buzz!

A streak of golden light shot through the opening.

The fellow swiftly circled the stone chamber once before stopping in front of Lee Hyun’s eyes.

Bzzzzzz―

The fuzzbee’s appearance had not changed at all. Its round, fluffy body still had alternating bands of gold and black.

It stared at Lee Hyun for a moment before landing on the back of his hand.

“Looks like you remember me.”

Lee Hyun gently stroked the fuzzbee’s head with his index finger.

It did not shy away, merely moving its antennae back and forth.

Lee Hyun broke away one side of each of the other two jars in the same manner.

Buzz! Buzz!

Two streaks of golden light flew into the stone chamber.

The other two looked almost identical to the first one that had awakened. One landed on Lee Hyun’s other hand, while the last circled above his head.

Bzzzzzz―

“At least they don’t seem to have grown vicious.”

Lee Hyun examined the auras of the three one by one.

They certainly seemed stronger. However, their spiritual power had not undergone enough of a qualitative change for him to call them Tier-2 spirit insects.

“Is it because the three of you split one Tier-2 spirit insect between you? No, even if one ate the whole thing, there was never any guarantee it would become that much stronger. Still, you definitely seem stronger...”

At that moment, the abdomen of the fuzzbee still sitting on the back of his hand twitched slightly.

“Hm?”

The next instant.

Squeak!

Whoosh!

A small object shot out at terrifying speed.

Crack!

Something white flew into the granite wall and lodged there.

Lee Hyun slowly turned his gaze toward the stone wall.

A small hole a knuckle deep had been punched into the granite. Inside it, a white lump that appeared to be fuzzbee droppings was giving off steam.

“.......”

Lee Hyun looked at the fuzzbee on the back of his hand.

Having relieved itself, the fellow looked considerably more comfortable.

Then the other two turned around as well.

Squeak, squeak!

Whoosh! Whoosh!

Crack! Craack!

Two white projectiles embedded themselves in separate stone walls.

Lee Hyun inspected the three holes one after another.

“At this level... the power is about the same as when I first learned the Yang Metal Art....”

‘An early Qi Refining cultivator could get hurt if one of those hit them wrong.’

Lee Hyun stared at the fuzzbees with an indescribable expression.

The first change they displayed after eating the larva of a Tier-2 spirit insect was powerful, high-velocity poop.

...

Lee Hyun brought the three strengthened fuzzbees to where the rest of the fuzzbees were kept.

Bzzzzzzzz―

Dozens of fuzzbees took flight at once.

They circled the three mutated fuzzbees as though sniffing their scent.

Squeak. Squeak, squeak.

As though they had been waiting for this, the three beat their wings loudly.

BZZZZ!

A strong gust sprang up, pushing the surrounding fuzzbees backward.

The three mutated fuzzbees flew side by side around the cavern.

One landed on another fuzzbee’s head before quickly taking off again, while another shoved an approaching fuzzbee aside with its rear.

Tumble.

The fuzzbee that had been pushed rolled once across the floor.

Squeak!

It flew up angrily, but the mutated fuzzbee was already far away.

A short while later, when the three mutated fuzzbees took the lead, the ordinary fuzzbees naturally fell in behind them. The golden swarm circled several times.

Fortunately, they showed no sign of attacking or devouring their own kind.

Even the fuzzbee that had been shoved aside earlier was now following behind the three mutated fuzzbees.

‘Did their rank within the swarm rise? It seems fine for now... but will it still be fine once they become Tier-2 spirit insects?’

If they really grew into Tier-2 spirit insects, their intelligence could increase along with their ferocity.

‘Times like this make me regret not belonging to a great sect. Even without going all the way to the Wangu Sect in Cang Kingdom, a large sect’s Scripture Pavilion should at least have a basic inheritance in insect control...’

Lee Hyun suddenly thought of White Owl.

“The Danxiao Sect....”

Lee Hyun checked inside his storage pouch.

The jade caskets containing the Bone-Forging Powder he had made long ago to disguise his bone age were still there.

‘Hmm...’

Just then, one of the mutated fuzzbees landed on the back of Lee Hyun’s hand again.

Lee Hyun looked at it.

‘An insect control inheritance... Aside from that, what I need are a Foundation Establishment Pill and its pill recipe, and better inheritances in alchemy and spirit plants...’

Most of what he currently needed was likely to be found within the Danxiao Sect.

‘I was planning to put Two Heavens Society activities on hold for a while anyway... This works out nicely.’

Five years later.
